get.summary: Return the content of a file identified by an authorized file handle, for display in the client.
get.description:
Send the handle in the `X-CanDoItAll-File-Handle` request header. A handle is an opaque 43-character value issued by the application's file browsing and file opening features; no operation in this document issues one. It is valid for a short time (five minutes unless the host is configured otherwise), only for the operations it was issued for (viewing or downloading) and only for the identity, session and active database that obtained it. The route reads only the header: a `ref` query-string value, as found in some stored display addresses, is ignored.

The response body is the stored bytes of the file, with the file's stored media type as its `Content-Type` and without a download file name. Files larger than the host's file interaction limit (64 MiB unless configured otherwise) are refused. To receive the file as an attachment with its file name, use `GET /authorized-files/download`. `GET /storage/objects/preview` is an identical alias of this route.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a valid bearer token issued by this host, and the handle must have been issued for that token's subject and session. With authorization disabled (the development default), any caller of this host process can use a handle issued in it while the active database stays the same. Reading the file changes nothing.

200.description: The file content. The actual `Content-Type` is the stored media type of the file, which can differ from the declared `application/octet-stream`.

401.description: The `X-CanDoItAll-File-Handle` header is missing or blank. When API authorization is enabled, a missing or invalid bearer token is also rejected with 401, but with the general `errors` envelope (code `api.authorization-required`) instead of a problem document.

403.description: The handle does not authorize this request: it is malformed, unknown, expired or revoked, was issued for another caller, session or database, does not allow viewing, its storage source is unavailable, or the file exceeds the interaction limit. Obtain a new handle from the application.

get.summary: Reject a retired direct managed-file address; files are served only through authorized file handles.
get.description:
Addresses of the form `/managed-files/{path}` were once used to read workspace files by path. They are no longer served: every request that reaches this route is answered with HTTP 410, whatever the path, and no file is read. Use `GET /authorized-files/content` or `GET /authorized-files/download` with a handle obtained from the application instead.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a valid bearer token issued by this host is required before the 410 answer; without one the request is rejected with 401 and the general `errors` envelope.

410.description: Direct managed-file paths are no longer accepted; use an authorized file handle.

get.summary: Read the readiness, hot-reload and host-capability state of the running development host.
get.description:
Development diagnostics for local tooling. This route exists only when the host runs in the Development environment; it is never mapped in other environments and is not part of the versioned API, so its response can change without notice. It serves only loopback callers (the connection address and any forwarded client address must both be loopback) or, when API authorization is enabled, a caller whose bearer token has the exact `api.tokens.issue` scope. Any other caller receives HTTP 404, as if the route did not exist.

The JSON object has these members:

- `isReady`, `environmentName`, `summary`, `startedAtUtc`, `lastChangedAtUtc` and `activeUrls`: the host readiness snapshot; `summary` is `Starting` or `Ready`, or a failure summary.
- `watchIteration`: the `DOTNET_WATCH_ITERATION` environment variable as an integer, or null when the host was not started by `dotnet watch`.
- `hotReloadGeneration`: number of hot-reload updates applied to this process.
- `runtimePid`: operating-system process identifier of the host.
- `ownerKind`, `ownerId` and `serverInstanceId`: the `CanDoItAllMcpOwnerKind`, `CanDoItAllMcpOwnerId` and `CanDoItAllMcpServerInstanceId` configuration values set by the tooling that launched the host; null when not configured.
- `hostCapabilities`: the same host-capability snapshot as `GET /api/runtime/capabilities`.

The read has no side effects.

200.description: The current development runtime diagnostics.

Any other caller receives HTTP 404, as if the route did not exist.

The JSON object has these members:

- `id` and `runtimeProfileId`: identifier (GUID) of the database profile this process is using.
- `pendingRestartProfileId`: identifier of the persisted active profile when it differs from the running profile and takes effect only after a restart; null otherwise, and always null while the running profile is locked by a runtime override. `hasPendingRestartActivation` is true exactly when it is not null.
- `pendingRestartDisplayName` and `pendingRestartDescriptor`: display name and connection descriptor of that pending profile; empty strings when there is none.
- `displayName`, `providerKind` (JSON integer: 1 PostgreSql, 2 InMemory), `sourceKind` (JSON integer: 3 PostgresConnection, 6 InMemory), `fingerprint` (runtime fingerprint of the profile) and `workspaceRoot` (absolute workspace directory of the profile on this host) describe the running profile.

The read has no side effects. Use `POST /_dev/database/switch/{profileId}` to change the active profile.

200.description: The running database profile and any profile pending a restart.

post.summary: Create a PostgreSQL database profile for the development host, prepare its database and optionally activate it.
post.description:
Development diagnostics for local tooling. This route exists only when the host runs in the Development environment; it is never mapped in other environments and is not part of the versioned API, so its response can change without notice. It serves only loopback callers (the connection address and any forwarded client address must both be loopback) or, when API authorization is enabled, a caller whose bearer token has the exact `api.tokens.issue` scope. Any other caller receives HTTP 404, as if the route did not exist.

Every successful call saves a new profile with a new identifier, creates the database through the maintenance database when it does not exist yet (an existing database is reused), prepares the application schema and then, unless `activate` is false, switches the host to the new profile. A failure after the profile was saved leaves the saved profile and any created database in place.

The JSON object returned with HTTP 200 has `id` (identifier of the new profile), `displayName`, `providerKind` (JSON integer, 1 PostgreSql), `sourceKind` (JSON integer, 3 PostgresConnection), `fingerprint`, `workspaceRoot`, `descriptor` (`host:port/database`) and `switch`. The `switch` member is null when the profile was not activated; otherwise it has `generation`, `currentProfileId`, `runtimeProfileId`, `pendingRestartProfileId`, `requiresRestart`, `runtimeChangedInProcess` and `message`. When `requiresRestart` is true the process keeps using its current profile until the host restarts.

HTTP 400 returns a JSON array of human-readable messages: the database name or user name is missing, or saving or activating the profile failed. The password is stored with the profile; use only local development credentials.

requestBody.description: PostgreSQL connection settings and whether to activate the new profile.

200.description: The profile was saved and its database prepared; see `switch` for the activation.

post.summary: Run a test chat against an agent's provider and a real agent execution run, and report both outcomes.
post.description:
Development diagnostics for local tooling. This route exists only when the host runs in the Development environment; it is never mapped in other environments and is not part of the versioned API, so its response can change without notice. It serves only loopback callers (the connection address and any forwarded client address must both be loopback) or, when API authorization is enabled, a caller whose bearer token has the exact `api.tokens.issue` scope. Any other caller receives HTTP 404, as if the route did not exist.

The probe is not read-only: it sends a test chat to the agent's provider and then executes an agent run, which calls the model, can use the agent's tools with their effects, is recorded as an execution run and, with `persistTranscript` or `chatSessionId`, writes to a chat session. With `autoApprove` true, pending tool calls are approved automatically. Both calls can incur provider cost.

The JSON object returned with HTTP 200 has `agent`, `provider`, `resolver` (credential resolution, redacted), `providerProbe` (`succeeded`, the model, response length and token counts, or a failure type and redacted message) and `agentProbe` (the run settings, `succeeded`, the execution run and chat session identifiers, the response length and run metrics; on failure the failure type, a redacted message and, when the run exists, its state and last twelve log entries). A failed probe still returns HTTP 200; read `succeeded`. HTTP 404 with a JSON object that has an `error` message means the agent, its provider profile or, for the `latest-process-step-session` prompt mode, a recent process-step prompt was not found.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Identifier of the technical agent in the organization workspace.

parameters.name: promptMode
parameters.description: `ok` (the default when omitted or blank) sends the prompt `Reply with the single word OK.`; `latest-process-step-session` (compared case-insensitively) replays the most recent process-step prompt found in the agent's twelve most recently updated chat sessions.

parameters.name: persistTranscript
parameters.description: Required. When `chatSessionId` is omitted, true runs the agent probe in a chat session of the agent (an existing one or a new one) so that the exchange is kept, and false runs it without a chat session.

parameters.name: autoApprove
parameters.description: True approves pending tool calls automatically. Omitted means false.

parameters.name: chatSessionId
parameters.description: Identifier of an existing chat session of the agent to run the probe in.

parameters.name: sourceKind
parameters.description: Execution-context source kind recorded on the run. Optional.

parameters.name: sourceId
parameters.description: Execution-context source identifier recorded on the run. Optional.

parameters.name: correlationId
parameters.description: Execution-context correlation identifier recorded on the run. Optional.

parameters.name: causationId
parameters.description: Execution-context causation identifier recorded on the run. Optional.

parameters.name: requestedBy
parameters.description: Execution-context requester recorded on the run. Optional.

parameters.name: requestedByKind
parameters.description: Execution-context requester kind recorded on the run. Optional.

parameters.name: processRunId
parameters.description: Process run identifier recorded in the execution context. Optional.

parameters.name: processStepId
parameters.description: Process step identifier recorded in the execution context. Optional.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: Message identifier recorded in the execution context. Optional.

200.description: Both probes ran; read `providerProbe.succeeded` and `agentProbe.succeeded`.

It serves only loopback callers (the connection address and any forwarded client address must both be loopback) or, when API authorization is enabled, a caller whose bearer token has the exact `api.tokens.issue` scope. parameters.name: step
parameters.description: The step to run, compared case-insensitively after trimming: `repair`, `sync`, `workspace-agents`, `parties`, `summaries` or `roster`.

200.description: The step ran; the body reports its duration and results.

get.summary: Read the catalog of provider models that this host shares with other hosts.
get.description:
Returns the host's native shared-provider catalog: every published provider that is eligible for sharing, with its revision, purpose, health, default model and models (routing identifier, capabilities, public prices and reasoning support). Internal profile identifiers, credentials, private endpoint addresses and raw diagnostics are never included. Another CanDoItAll host uses this catalog to synchronize a shared-provider source; OpenAI-compatible clients can use `GET /api/shared-providers/openai/v1/models` instead. The read has no side effects.

Conditional reads: the response carries a strong `ETag`, the quoted `catalogRevision`, for example `"sha256:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08"`. Send a received entity tag in `If-None-Match` to get 304 without a body while the catalog is unchanged; `*` matches any catalog and weak tags match too. The header may hold at most 32 entity tags and 8,192 characters, and `*` only on its own.

Every response carries `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and `CanDoItAll-Request-Id`, which identifies the request for support. The optional `CanDoItAll-Access-Context-Ref` and `CanDoItAll-Access-Context-Type` headers are recorded for audit correlation only and never authorize anything. Failures use the general `errors` envelope.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.shared-providers.catalog.read` scope. Reading the catalog does not authorize invoking the models, which requires `api` or `api.shared-providers.invoke`.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Optional RFC 9110 entity-tag list used for conditional catalog retrieval.

parameters.name: CanDoItAll-Access-Context-Ref
parameters.description: Optional opaque access-context correlation reference; it does not authorize the request.

parameters.name: CanDoItAll-Access-Context-Type
parameters.description: Optional canonical type for the access-context reference, for example project or erp.company-project. Requires the reference header.

200.description: The catalog; its `ETag` header is the quoted catalog revision.

ETag.description: Strong entity tag for the canonical public catalog representation.

304.description: The catalog still matches an entity tag sent in `If-None-Match`; no body. The current `ETag` is repeated.

ETag.description: Strong entity tag for the canonical public catalog representation.

400.description: `If-None-Match` is malformed, too long or lists too many entity tags (`shared-provider.catalog.if-none-match-invalid`), or an access-context header is invalid (`api.access-context-invalid`).

401.description: API authorization is enabled and no valid bearer token was sent (`shared-provider.catalog.unauthorized`).

403.description: The token lacks the catalog scope (`shared-provider.catalog.forbidden`).

503.description: The catalog could not be built (`shared-provider.catalog.unavailable`). Nothing was changed; try again later.

get.summary: List the shared models in the OpenAI model-list format.
get.description:
Returns every model of every shared publication as an OpenAI-style list, so that an OpenAI-compatible client configured with the base address `/api/shared-providers/openai/v1` can discover the routing identifiers to send as `model`. The list includes models that consumers do not suggest in pickers and carries only the routing identifiers; publications, capabilities and prices are in `GET /api/shared-providers/v1/catalog`. The read has no side effects.

Conditional reads work as for the catalog: the `ETag` is the quoted catalog revision, and a matching `If-None-Match` gets 304 without a body. The header may hold at most 32 entity tags and 8,192 characters, and `*` only on its own.

Every response carries `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and `CanDoItAll-Request-Id`. The optional `CanDoItAll-Access-Context-Ref` and `CanDoItAll-Access-Context-Type` headers are recorded for audit correlation only. Failures use the OpenAI error envelope.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.shared-providers.catalog.read` scope. Listing models does not authorize invoking them, which requires `api` or `api.shared-providers.invoke`.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Optional RFC 9110 entity-tag list used for conditional catalog retrieval.

parameters.name: CanDoItAll-Access-Context-Ref
parameters.description: Optional opaque access-context correlation reference; it does not authorize the request.

parameters.name: CanDoItAll-Access-Context-Type
parameters.description: Optional canonical type for the access-context reference, for example project or erp.company-project. Requires the reference header.

200.description: The model list; its `ETag` header is the quoted catalog revision.

ETag.description: Strong entity tag for the canonical public catalog representation.

304.description: The catalog still matches an entity tag sent in `If-None-Match`; no body. The current `ETag` is repeated.

ETag.description: Strong entity tag for the canonical public catalog representation.

400.description: `If-None-Match` is malformed, too long or lists too many entity tags (`shared_provider_invalid_if_none_match`), or an access-context header is invalid (`shared_provider_access_context_invalid`).

401.description: API authorization is enabled and no valid bearer token was sent (`shared_provider_unauthorized`).

403.description: The token lacks the catalog scope (`shared_provider_insufficient_scope`).

503.description: The catalog could not be built (`shared_provider_catalog_unavailable`). Nothing was changed; try again later.

post.summary: Create a model response through a shared provider, using the OpenAI Responses request format.
post.description:
Relays a stateless OpenAI Responses request to the shared model named by `model`, a routing identifier from `GET /api/shared-providers/v1/catalog` or `GET /api/shared-providers/openai/v1/models`; it never falls back to another model or provider. The request must fit the strict subset in the request schema: unknown or duplicate members, remote URLs, files, hosted tools, stored responses, background mode and `previous_response_id` are rejected. `store` is treated as false when omitted and may only be false; `background` may only be false. Every feature the request uses (streaming, function tools, structured output, image input, a reasoning effort) must be supported by the model.

Without `stream`, or with false, the body is the provider's completed response object as JSON, with `model` replaced by the routing identifier; a response that is not completed or carries an error is reported as HTTP 502 instead. With `stream` true, the body is `text/event-stream`: the provider's server-sent events, relayed with `model` replaced. Once the stream has started the status stays 200 even if the provider fails: the host then aborts the connection without a terminal event. Treat a stream that ends without its terminal event as failed and never use its partial output as a complete answer.

Each call is a new, separately recorded invocation (caller, publication, model, usage and the prices in effect) and can be charged; there is no idempotency key. After HTTP 502, 503 or 504, and after an aborted stream, the provider may still have processed the request. Responses carry `Cache-Control: private, no-store, no-cache`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `CanDoItAll-Request-Id`, which identifies the invocation for support. Failures use the OpenAI error envelope; branch on `error.code`.

post.summary: Create a chat completion through a shared provider, using the OpenAI Chat Completions request format.
post.description:
Relays an OpenAI Chat Completions request to the shared model named by `model`, a routing identifier from `GET /api/shared-providers/v1/catalog` or `GET /api/shared-providers/openai/v1/models`; it never falls back to another model or provider. The request must fit the strict subset in the request schema: unknown or duplicate members, remote image URLs and hosted tools are rejected. Every assistant tool call must be answered by a `tool` message with its `tool_call_id` before the next other message; `stream_options` is accepted only with `stream` true; at most one of `max_tokens` and `max_completion_tokens`. Every feature the request uses (streaming, function tools, structured output, image input, a reasoning effort) must be supported by the model.

Without `stream`, or with false, the body is the provider's chat completion object as JSON, with `model` replaced by the routing identifier; a response that carries an error is reported as HTTP 502 instead. With `stream` true, the body is `text/event-stream`: the provider's server-sent events, relayed with `model` replaced, ending with `data: [DONE]` when the provider sends it. Once the stream has started the status stays 200 even if the provider fails: the host then aborts the connection without a terminal event. Treat a stream that ends without its terminal event as failed and never use its partial output as a complete answer.

Each call is a new, separately recorded invocation (caller, publication, model, usage and the prices in effect) and can be charged; there is no idempotency key. After HTTP 502, 503 or 504, and after an aborted stream, the provider may still have processed the request. Responses carry `Cache-Control: private, no-store, no-cache`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `CanDoItAll-Request-Id`, which identifies the invocation for support. Failures use the OpenAI error envelope; branch on `error.code`.

post.summary: Generate images through a shared image-generation provider, using the OpenAI Images request format.
post.description:
Relays an OpenAI image generation request to the shared model named by `model`, a routing identifier of an `image-generation` publication from `GET /api/shared-providers/v1/catalog`; it never falls back to another model or provider. The request must fit the strict subset in the request schema; unknown or duplicate members are rejected. Images are returned only as base64 data (`response_format` may only be `b64_json`), never as URLs, and this operation cannot stream.

The JSON body has a `data` array with one object per image, holding `b64_json` and, when the provider returns it, `revised_prompt`, plus `created` when the provider reports a creation time. It holds 1 to 16 images, each at most 8 MiB decoded and 32 MiB in total; a larger or malformed result is reported as HTTP 502.

Each call is a new, separately recorded invocation (caller, publication, model and the prices in effect) and can be charged; there is no idempotency key. After HTTP 502, 503 or 504 the provider may still have generated the images. Responses carry `Cache-Control: private, no-store, no-cache`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `CanDoItAll-Request-Id`, which identifies the invocation for support. Failures use the OpenAI error envelope; branch on `error.code`.

get.summary: Read the runtime host profile and the availability of each host capability.
get.description:
Returns a fresh snapshot of the resolved host profile (for example `WindowsHeadless`), the operating system, whether the host is interactive, the readiness of each application purpose root and one entry per host capability. `isReady` is true when every mandatory capability is available; optional capabilities, such as desktop file opening on a headless host, can be unavailable on a ready host. For the deployment support manifest and the database readiness in one response, use `GET /api/runtime/operations`.

Each read probes the application purpose roots again by creating and deleting a small temporary file in each root; it changes no application data. The response contains no paths, connection strings or secret values.

Authority: this route is outside the authorized `/api` route group. It requires no bearer token, even when API authorization is enabled, and it is mapped even when `Api:Enabled` is false.

200.description: The current host capability snapshot.

get.summary: Read the operational state of the host: readiness, deployment support and host capabilities.
get.description:
Use this read after an installation, upgrade or restart to confirm that the host finished starting. The response combines `state` (`Starting`, `Ready` or `Unavailable`), whether the database and its migrations are ready, the deployment support manifest embedded in this build (supported publish targets, host profiles, prerequisites and pending validations) and the host capability snapshot also returned by `GET /api/runtime/capabilities`. A successful HTTP response does not mean the host is ready: check `state` and `databaseAndMigrationsReady`.

Each read probes the application purpose roots again by creating and deleting a small temporary file in each root; it changes no application data. The response contains no paths, connection strings or secret values.

post.summary: Create a root project.
post.description:
Creates a new top-level project with the sent values and returns its summary. Its `id` identifies the project in the other operations, and its structure starts with the project root node `project:{id}`. To place a project under another one, attach it with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{parentProjectId}/subprojects`, or extract existing nodes into a new subproject with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/nodes/move-to-new-subproject`. Creation is not idempotent: repeating the request creates another project. No lease is involved.

put.summary: Replace the values of an existing project.
put.description:
Replaces the project's name, description, objective, current phase, status and target date with the sent values and returns the updated summary. Omitted members are not kept: send the current value of everything you keep. The update also removes the project's phases and option selections, which this request cannot carry. The project structure and the project hierarchy are not changed.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON, or a member of the wrong JSON type such as a status name instead of its integer) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Make a project a subproject of another project, as an additional parent or in place of a current parent.
post.description:
Without `currentParentProjectId`, adds the route's project as a parent of `childProjectId` and keeps the child's other parents; adding a parent the child already has succeeds without a change. With `currentParentProjectId`, replaces that parent of the child with the route's project. A change that would make a project its own parent or create a cycle is rejected. Only the project hierarchy changes; the structures of the projects are not modified. Read the result with `GET /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/hierarchy`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. The lease is taken on the child project, not on the parent: send `leaseToken` to work under your own lease on the child; without it the operation uses the lease your identity already holds on the child, or else takes a five-minute lease on it for its own duration; if another identity holds that lease, it waits when the lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Read the nodes and links of a project structure, with optional filters and sections.
post.description:
Returns the current stored structure of the project: the selected nodes, the links between them when requested, and `expectedProjectAdmission`, the project write admission that task writes and managed-file deletions send back. Read it before changing anything, to obtain node identifiers (`nodes[].id`) and the current values that edits are checked against. The node catalog lists the kinds of node that can be created.

Send `{}` to get every node with the basic members only. Set `includeMetadata` to get `metadataJson` (task edits need it), `includeLinks` for links, and `includeNotes`, `includeLayout` or `includeAssets` for the other optional members. `nodeIds` and `subtreeRootIds` select nodes (their union); the other filters narrow the selection. Nodes are ordered by title, and `take` cuts the list with a warning. Only the current structure can be read over HTTP: `source` 1 (InvocationSnapshot) belongs to in-process agent invocations and is rejected.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope (reads require the same scope).

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the project, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/project-structure/projects` or by project creation.

requestBody.description: Structure read request: which nodes of the project to return and which optional sections to fill. Every member is optional; the empty object `{}` returns all nodes without notes, metadata, layout and file fields and without links. `nodeIds` and `subtreeRootIds` are combined (union); every other filter must also match. Nodes are ordered by title, ignoring case. Send one JSON object as `application/json` or `application/*+json`. The Project Structure reader rejects other content types with HTTP 415 `ProjectStructureContentTypeUnsupported`, a body larger than 262,144 bytes with HTTP 413 `ProjectStructureRequestBodyTooLarge`, and malformed JSON or members of the wrong JSON type with HTTP 400 `ProjectStructureRequestInvalid`.

200.description: The selected part of the structure as currently stored. Keep `expectedProjectAdmission` for admission-checked writes; it becomes stale when the project is replaced or deleted.

projectId.description: Identifier of the project that was read.

projectName.description: Name of the project at the time of the read.

id.description: String node identifier, unique within the project; use it in node routes and requests. Nodes created through this API have the form `custom:` followed by 32 hexadecimal characters, for example `custom:3f2504e04f8911d39a0c0305e82c3301`. Nodes kept in sync with other records use other prefixes followed by that record's identifier, for example `project:{projectId}` for the project root, `project-child:{projectId}` for a subproject or `phase:{phaseId}`. Treat it as opaque and compare it exactly; it is not a GUID.

parentId.description: Identifier of the parent node in the hierarchy; null for a top-level node such as the project root.

objectType.description: Kind of project object the node represents. Returned as the object type name, for example `WorkItem`.

objectSubtype.description: Lower-case subtype that refines the object type, for example `task` for a WorkItem or `pdf` for a File; empty when none. A WorkItem with subtype `task` is a canonical task, changed only through the task operations.

subtitle.description: Secondary display text; may be empty.

status.description: Free-text status, for example Draft, Active or Done. Progress and the finished state are derived from words in it (see `progressMode`).

notes.description: Free-text notes; in a structure read, null unless `includeNotes` was true.

route.description: Application route that shows the node or its artifact in the web UI; informational.

artifactKind.description: Kind of record the node represents, for example `project` for project nodes or the object type name for ordinary nodes; informational.

artifactId.description: Identifier of the external record the node is bound to, for example the project id of a project node; null when the node has no external record.

mediaRelativePath.description: Location of the node's stored file within the application's managed storage; empty when the node has no file. In a structure read, null unless `includeAssets` was true. Not a path on the client's machine.

mediaContentType.description: Content type of the stored file, for example `application/pdf`; empty when there is none. In a structure read, null unless `includeAssets` was true.

mediaOriginalFileName.description: Original file name of the stored file; empty when there is none. In a structure read, null unless `includeAssets` was true.

badges.description: Display labels derived from the node, for example Synced (kept in sync with another record), Scheduled (has a planned start), a subtype label, Uploaded (has an uploaded file), Subproject, Parent or Shared parent. For display only; do not parse them.

progressMode.description: How progress is expressed: `complete`, `started`, `progress` or `na` (not applicable); empty when progress is not tracked, as for project hierarchy nodes. A status change resets the mode and percentage from the status text.

progressPercent.description: Progress from 0 through 100, or -1 when it is not tracked. Unless set explicitly, it follows the status: for example 28 for draft, planned, pending or queued, 62 for active, running or blocked, 78 for review or testing, and 100 for done, complete, approved, ready or final.

markerIcon.description: Icon token of the node's primary marker; empty when the node has no marker.

markerTone.description: Tone (color) token of the node's primary marker; empty when there is none.

markerLabel.description: Label of the node's primary marker; empty when there is none. A node can carry several markers; only the primary one is returned.

priority.description: Priority set on the node itself: 0 means none; smaller positive values are more urgent.

effectivePriority.description: Priority used for ordering and filtering, from 0 (none) through 6: the node's own priority or, unless the node is finished, paused or stopped, the most urgent nonzero priority among it and its descendants. Node creation and change responses return the node's own priority here.

startUtc.description: Planned start as an instant with offset; null when the node is not scheduled.

endUtc.description: Planned end as an instant with offset; null when the node is not scheduled.

metadataJson.description: Node metadata as a JSON string that contains a JSON object; parse it before use. In a structure read, null unless `includeMetadata` was true. Its sections are named after the object type, for example `workItem` for tasks (with `expectedEffortHours`, `expectedEffortUnit`, `executionState` and `directAssignmentRevision`) or `projectBlock`. Enum values inside it are camel-case strings such as `"hours"` or `"notStarted"`, unlike the integers used in request bodies.

projectRole.description: Role of the node in the project hierarchy, as a JSON integer: 0 None, 1 ActiveProject, 2 Subproject, 3 ParentProject, 4 AdditionalParentProject.

relatedProjectId.description: Project id that a project hierarchy node stands for (project root, subproject or parent project); null for other nodes.

parentProjectCount.description: For a subproject node, the number of project nodes in this structure that contain it; 0 for other nodes.

x.description: Horizontal canvas position in the structure editor; in a structure read, null unless `includeLayout` was true.

y.description: Vertical canvas position in the structure editor; in a structure read, null unless `includeLayout` was true.

durationSeconds.description: Stored planned duration in seconds; null when none is stored.

post.summary: Compute the plan summary of a project from its canonical tasks.
post.description:
Computes, as of `asOfUtc` (now by default), how the project's canonical tasks are distributed over plan states, their schedule span, total effort, task- and effort-weighted progress, expected cost per currency, remaining cost per resource group and date, resource coverage, previews of running, blocked and waiting tasks, and counts of tasks with missing or unusable data. Nothing is stored or changed. Costs are totalled per currency and never converted. It uses POST because the query travels in the body.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope (reads require the same scope).

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Create a canonical project task with its planned interval and optional estimate and resource.
post.description:
Creates a canonical task (a WorkItem with subtype `task`) in the project's main backlog block, which is created when missing, with execution state NotStarted. With a resource the owner attaches it (a person or agent becomes the direct assignee) and prices the estimate from it; the task is then placed in the Gantt row order after `afterTaskNodeId` or at the end. Generic node creation rejects tasks; change the task later with `PUT /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}`.

Requires the `expectedProjectAdmission` from the latest structure read. When resource attachment or row ordering fails after the task was written, the owner deletes the task again: HTTP 409 `ResourceAttachmentFailed` or `RowOrderingFailed` means nothing remains, while HTTP 500 `ResourceAttachmentCompensationFailed` or `RowOrderingCompensationFailed` means the task could not be removed; `details.taskNodeId` names it in both cases. Creation is not idempotent: repeating a request creates another task, so read the structure before retrying after an unclear failure.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. The body carries no lease token: the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type, such as an enum name instead of its integer) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

put.summary: Update a canonical project task using the task state previously read by the caller.
put.description:
Changes the title, progress, estimate, planned schedule, execution state or direct assignee of a canonical task (one created with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/tasks`). Generic node operations reject canonical tasks; workflow and process resources are attached with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}/resource` instead.

Read, modify, write:

1. Call `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/structure/read` with `{ "includeMetadata": true }` and keep its `expectedProjectAdmission`.
2. Take the task from `nodes` by its `id` and copy `title`, `progressPercent`, `startUtc` and `endUtc`.
3. Parse the task's `metadataJson` string. Under `workItem`: `expectedEffortHours`, `expectedEffortUnit`, `expectedCostAmount` and `expectedCostCurrencyCode` form the current estimate; `executionState`, `actualStartedAtUtc` and `actualEndedAtUtc` the current execution; `expectedCostBasis` the current cost basis; `directAssignmentRevision` the current direct-assignment revision. A member missing there is null, and a missing revision is 0.
4. Send every current value unchanged and change only the proposed values you intend to change.
5. Read the structure again to see the stored result.

`metadataJson` writes enums as camel-case text (for example `"manDays"` or `"notStarted"`), but this request expects the JSON integers listed on each enum schema. Always include `currentCostBasis`, using null when the read had none.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. The body must also carry the project write admission from the read; it carries no lease token.

Failures handled by the operation use the Project Structure error envelope. HTTP 409 means the task, its assignments or the project changed after your read, or the admission is missing or stale: read again and reapply the intended change; never resend an obsolete body with only its preconditions refreshed. A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON, a wrong JSON type such as text for an integer enum, or a missing `currentCostBasis` member) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Attach a workflow or process definition to a canonical task and reprice the task for it.
post.description:
Attaches the workflow (at its exact version, with optional run input settings) or the process definition to the task and recalculates the task's expected cost from that resource's price. The result reports the pricing and the node created for the resource, if any. Persons and agents are not attached here: set them as the direct assignee with `PUT /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}`.

Read, modify, write: read the structure with `includeMetadata`, keep `expectedProjectAdmission`, and send the task's execution state from its `metadataJson` (`workItem.executionState` and the actual timestamps) as `currentExecution`. When pricing fails after the resource was attached, the attachment is rolled back and the response is HTTP 409 `TaskResourceAttachmentPricingConflict`; read the task again and retry. HTTP 500 `TaskResourceAttachmentCompensationFailed` means the rollback failed: read the task and resolve its resource before editing it again.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. The body carries no lease token; where the owner needs a project lease, it uses the one your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON, a member of the wrong JSON type, or a missing `resource` or `currentExecution`) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Create a generic node, such as a block, note, decision, link or runtime node, in a project structure.
post.description:
Creates one node under `parentNodeKey` (the project root when omitted) and returns it with every optional member filled. Choose `objectType` and `objectSubtype` from `GET /api/project-structure/node-catalog`. Use `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/tasks` for canonical tasks (WorkItem with subtype `task`) and `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/assets` for File nodes and `mermaid` subtypes; this operation rejects them. The node is placed on the canvas automatically near its parent.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`. Metadata folders of runtime nodes and delivery blocks must lie inside the managed workspace.

The whole body stays under the host's request limit of 30,000,000 bytes by default: a larger body is rejected with HTTP 400 `ProjectStructureRequestInvalid` (or HTTP 413 when its declared length exceeds the reader's limit). The creation is not idempotent: repeating a request creates another node, so read the structure before retrying after an unclear failure.

parameters.description: Identifier of the project, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/project-structure/projects` or by project creation.

requestBody.description: Node creation request: the kind of node, its display fields and an optional parent, schedule, file, metadata and canvas position. put.summary: Replace the display fields, schedule and metadata of a generic node, optionally changing its kind.
put.description:
Writes the sent values over the node's subtitle, notes and schedule, so read the node first and send the current values of everything you keep: an omitted `subtitle` or `notes` is cleared, and omitted schedule members clear the planned interval unless the node is also reclassified. A blank `title` keeps the title, and blank metadata keeps the stored metadata. A new `objectType` or `objectSubtype` reclassifies the node when that change is supported. Status, progress, markers, priority, position and parent have their own operations.

Canonical tasks are rejected; change them with `PUT /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}`. Nodes kept in sync with other records (badge Synced) cannot be updated and are reported as not found.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

post.summary: Change the object type or subtype of a generic node, keeping its other values.

Reclassifies the node while keeping its title, subtitle, notes, metadata and schedule. Supported changes are a subtype change within the same family of node kinds, promoting a Note to a kind that accepts promotion, and switching between runnable runtime kinds (script, runtime environment, Docker); other changes are rejected. Changes only the node's canvas coordinates in the structure editor; its parent, links and schedule stay the same. Use the reparent operations to move a node in the hierarchy. An unknown node identifier is ignored and the response is still `{ "ok": true }`, so read the structure with `includeLayout` to confirm the new position.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Automatically re-lay out the descendants of a node on the structure canvas.

post.summary: Move the node named in the route under another parent in the project hierarchy.
post.description:
Makes `parentNodeKey` the node's parent (the project root when null or blank); its descendants move with it and its links other than parent links are kept. Sending the current parent changes nothing. The new parent cannot be the node itself or one of its descendants. Nodes kept in sync with other records (badge Synced) cannot be moved and are reported as not found. `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/nodes/reparent` does the same with the node identifier in the body.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the project, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/project-structure/projects` or by project creation.

parameters.name: nodeId
parameters.description: String identifier of the node to move, as returned in `nodes[].id` by the structure read.

requestBody.description: New parent node identifier and an optional lease token.

200.description: The committed node with its new `parentId`, with every optional member filled.

id.description: String node identifier, unique within the project; use it in node routes and requests. Nodes created through this API have the form `custom:` followed by 32 hexadecimal characters, for example `custom:3f2504e04f8911d39a0c0305e82c3301`. Nodes kept in sync with other records use other prefixes followed by that record's identifier, for example `project:{projectId}` for the project root, `project-child:{projectId}` for a subproject or `phase:{phaseId}`. Treat it as opaque and compare it exactly; it is not a GUID.

parentId.description: Identifier of the parent node in the hierarchy; null for a top-level node such as the project root.

objectType.description: Kind of project object the node represents. Returned as the object type name, for example `WorkItem`.

objectSubtype.description: Lower-case subtype that refines the object type, for example `task` for a WorkItem or `pdf` for a File; empty when none. A WorkItem with subtype `task` is a canonical task, changed only through the task operations.

subtitle.description: Secondary display text; may be empty.

status.description: Free-text status, for example Draft, Active or Done. Progress and the finished state are derived from words in it (see `progressMode`).

notes.description: Free-text notes; in a structure read, null unless `includeNotes` was true.

route.description: Application route that shows the node or its artifact in the web UI; informational.

artifactKind.description: Kind of record the node represents, for example `project` for project nodes or the object type name for ordinary nodes; informational.

artifactId.description: Identifier of the external record the node is bound to, for example the project id of a project node; null when the node has no external record.

mediaRelativePath.description: Location of the node's stored file within the application's managed storage; empty when the node has no file. In a structure read, null unless `includeAssets` was true. Not a path on the client's machine.

mediaContentType.description: Content type of the stored file, for example `application/pdf`; empty when there is none. In a structure read, null unless `includeAssets` was true.

mediaOriginalFileName.description: Original file name of the stored file; empty when there is none. In a structure read, null unless `includeAssets` was true.

badges.description: Display labels derived from the node, for example Synced (kept in sync with another record), Scheduled (has a planned start), a subtype label, Uploaded (has an uploaded file), Subproject, Parent or Shared parent. For display only; do not parse them.

progressMode.description: How progress is expressed: `complete`, `started`, `progress` or `na` (not applicable); empty when progress is not tracked, as for project hierarchy nodes. A status change resets the mode and percentage from the status text.

progressPercent.description: Progress from 0 through 100, or -1 when it is not tracked. Unless set explicitly, it follows the status: for example 28 for draft, planned, pending or queued, 62 for active, running or blocked, 78 for review or testing, and 100 for done, complete, approved, ready or final.

markerIcon.description: Icon token of the node's primary marker; empty when the node has no marker.

markerTone.description: Tone (color) token of the node's primary marker; empty when there is none.

markerLabel.description: Label of the node's primary marker; empty when there is none. A node can carry several markers; only the primary one is returned.

priority.description: Priority set on the node itself: 0 means none; smaller positive values are more urgent.

effectivePriority.description: Priority used for ordering and filtering, from 0 (none) through 6: the node's own priority or, unless the node is finished, paused or stopped, the most urgent nonzero priority among it and its descendants. Node creation and change responses return the node's own priority here.

startUtc.description: Planned start as an instant with offset; null when the node is not scheduled.

endUtc.description: Planned end as an instant with offset; null when the node is not scheduled.

metadataJson.description: Node metadata as a JSON string that contains a JSON object; parse it before use. In a structure read, null unless `includeMetadata` was true. Its sections are named after the object type, for example `workItem` for tasks (with `expectedEffortHours`, `expectedEffortUnit`, `executionState` and `directAssignmentRevision`) or `projectBlock`. Enum values inside it are camel-case strings such as `"hours"` or `"notStarted"`, unlike the integers used in request bodies.

projectRole.description: Role of the node in the project hierarchy, as a JSON integer: 0 None, 1 ActiveProject, 2 Subproject, 3 ParentProject, 4 AdditionalParentProject.

relatedProjectId.description: Project id that a project hierarchy node stands for (project root, subproject or parent project); null for other nodes.

parentProjectCount.description: For a subproject node, the number of project nodes in this structure that contain it; 0 for other nodes.

x.description: Horizontal canvas position in the structure editor; in a structure read, null unless `includeLayout` was true.

y.description: Vertical canvas position in the structure editor; in a structure read, null unless `includeLayout` was true.

durationSeconds.description: Stored planned duration in seconds; null when none is stored.

canRunNormally.description: True when the node's runtime plan can be executed directly on the server.

canRunAsAdministrator.description: True when the runtime plan can be started with elevation on the server.

canOpenInFileExplorer.description: True when an existing file or folder of the node, inside the configured workspace root, can be shown in the server's system file browser.

canOpenInNewTab.description: True when the node is IPFS-backed and opens in a separate browser tab.

runtimeDisplayName.description: Display name of the node's runtime plan; empty when there is none.

runtimeDisplayCommand.description: Always empty in this API: runtime commands are not disclosed over HTTP.

runtimeWorkingDirectory.description: Always empty in this API: working directories are not disclosed over HTTP.

openInNewTabRoute.description: Route opened in a new tab when `canOpenInNewTab` is true; otherwise empty.

storageProvider.description: Name of the storage provider holding the node's stored object; empty when the node has no stored object.

storageLocatorKind.description: Name of the kind of `storageLocator`; empty when there is no stored object.

storageLocator.description: Provider-specific locator of the stored object (its syntax depends on the provider and locator kind); empty when there is no stored object. Do not treat it as a path on the client's machine.

actionId.description: Stable action identifier, for example `runtime:open`, `runtime:terminal`, `runtime:admin`, `runtime:stop`, `open-local`, `open-new-tab` or `browse-files`.

surface.description: Where the structure editor offers the action, as display text.

description.description: What the action does, as display text.

items.description: One action the application offers for a node in its structure editor, for example running a script node or showing a file in its folder. Descriptive only: the HTTP API does not execute these actions.

actions.description: Actions the structure editor offers for the node.

guidance.description: Display notes about the actions, including why a runtime action is unavailable on this host.

oneOf.description: What the server can do with the node on its own machine; null when nothing applies.

value.description: The intent identifier; never the all-zero GUID.

intentId.description: Business intent of the process step that created the asset.

nativeObjectId.description: Identifier of the created project object record.

nodeId.description: Identifier of the created node, as in `nodes[].id`.

post.summary: Copy one or more subtrees of a project structure under another parent in the same project.
post.description:
Copies each source node with all its descendants under `destinationParentNodeId`, together with the caller-created links between copied nodes; the response maps every source node to its copy and lists the caller-created links that crossed the copied set and were left out. The copy fails as a whole, before anything is saved, when a subtree contains a canonical task, a source is not editable or not finished with deferred work, or the destination is missing or a synced project node. Copying is not idempotent: repeating a request creates another set of copies.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Create a subproject of the project and move selected nodes into its structure.
post.description:
Creates a new project under the route's project (status Active and current phase Execution unless sent) and moves the selected nodes into it, by default with all their descendants. Moved nodes keep their identifiers; those whose parent stays behind become children of the new project's root. With `includeDescendants` false, children that stay are attached to the moved node's former parent. Links between moved nodes move with them; links between a moved node and one that stays are deleted and listed in `removedBoundaryLinks`. Identifiers that are not editable nodes of the project (unknown ids, the project root, synced nodes) are ignored with a warning. The operation is not idempotent: repeating it creates another subproject.

The subproject is created first and the nodes move afterwards. When the move fails, the empty subproject is removed again (HTTP 400 `SelectedNodesTransferUnavailable` or HTTP 500 `SubprojectTransferFailed`). When the nodes moved but reconciling their task assignments failed, the change stays committed and HTTP 409 `ProjectStructureTransferPartialCommit` is returned: do not repeat the move.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own lease on the route's project. Without it the operation uses the lease your identity already holds on that project, or else takes a five-minute lease on it for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON, or a member of the wrong JSON type such as a status name instead of its integer) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Move all descendants of a node into another existing project.
post.description:
Moves the descendants of the route's node, except synced nodes and anything below them, into `targetProjectId`, which can be any other existing project. The node itself stays; its former children become children of the target project's root and deeper descendants keep their parents. Moved nodes keep their identifiers. Links between moved nodes move with them; links between a moved node and one that stays are deleted and listed in `removedBoundaryLinks`. A node without descendants, or an identifier that is not in the project, returns a result with empty lists and changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Both projects are leased: send `leaseToken` for your lease on the route's project and `targetLeaseToken` for your lease on the target project. For each token omitted, the operation uses the lease your identity already holds on that project, or else takes a five-minute lease on it; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Resolve the page or artifact a node opens, creating a prompt node's Prompt Gallery prompt when needed.
post.description:
Returns a reference to what the node opens in the web application: the project overview for the project root, the managed file preview for file and media nodes, the Prompt Gallery prompt for a prompt node bound to one, and the project structure page for ordinary nodes. Command 3 (Test) returns the project's Test Lab for any existing node. Commands 0 (Open) and 1 (Wizard) on a PromptFlow, PromptSession or PromptStep node without a prompt first create a draft Prompt Gallery prompt and bind the node to it; that is the only case that writes. The other commands only resolve the reference.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Although most commands only read, the operation needs the project lease: send `leaseToken` to work under your own lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON, or a member of the wrong JSON type such as a command name instead of its integer) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Link a node to a process definition, so that process starts for the node launch that definition.
post.description:
Creates a Uses link from the node to the definition's node `process-definition:{processDefinitionId}`. `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/nodes/{nodeId}/process/start` then launches this definition when it is called without `processDefinitionId`. The definition's existence is not checked here. Canonical tasks are rejected; attach a process to a task with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}/resource`. The result echoes the link and `changed` is true also when it already existed.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Launch a process run for a project structure node.
post.description:
Launches `processDefinitionId`, or else the definition the node represents or is linked to, for the node, and links the created run back to the node. The call returns when the launch is prepared, not when the process finishes. `stage` Running with a `runId` means a run exists; with `execute` true it is also queued for execution by the process runtime. `stage` Blocked means readiness findings stopped the launch and no run was created. Follow a run with `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}`.

Every call launches again; there is no idempotency key, so after an unclear failure look for the run before retrying. This operation does not take a project lease and ignores `leaseToken`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Preview the workflow definitions and run input for a workflow node under a parent node.
post.description:
Lists every workflow definition (active ones first) with whether it can be selected, resolves the preselected workflow and version, normalizes the input settings and previews the input that a workflow node under `nodeId` would pass to its runs. Nothing is created or changed; create the node with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/nodes/{nodeId}/workflow-definition`. It uses POST because the settings travel in the body.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope (reads require the same scope).

Nodes kept in sync with other records use other prefixes followed by that record's identifier, for example `project:{projectId}` for the project root, `project-child:{projectId}` for a subproject or `phase:{phaseId}`. post.description:
Creates a WorkflowDefinition node under `nodeId`, bound to the workflow definition and version, with the run input settings in its metadata. The definition must exist and be active. Canonical task parents are rejected; attach a workflow to a task with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}/resource`. Preview the choices first with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/nodes/{nodeId}/workflow-add-options` and start runs later with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/nodes/{workflowNodeId}/workflow/start`. Repeating a request creates another node.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

parameters.description: Identifier of the project, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/project-structure/projects` or by project creation.

projectId.description: Identifier of the project that contains the node.

id.description: String node identifier, unique within the project; use it in node routes and requests. Nodes created through this API have the form `custom:` followed by 32 hexadecimal characters, for example `custom:3f2504e04f8911d39a0c0305e82c3301`. Nodes kept in sync with other records use other prefixes followed by that record's identifier, for example `project:{projectId}` for the project root, `project-child:{projectId}` for a subproject or `phase:{phaseId}`. Treat it as opaque and compare it exactly; it is not a GUID.

parentId.description: Identifier of the parent node in the hierarchy; null for a top-level node such as the project root.

objectType.description: Kind of project object the node represents. Returned as the object type name, for example `WorkItem`.

objectSubtype.description: Lower-case subtype that refines the object type, for example `task` for a WorkItem or `pdf` for a File; empty when none. A WorkItem with subtype `task` is a canonical task, changed only through the task operations.

subtitle.description: Secondary display text; may be empty.

status.description: Free-text status, for example Draft, Active or Done. Progress and the finished state are derived from words in it (see `progressMode`).

notes.description: Free-text notes; in a structure read, null unless `includeNotes` was true.

route.description: Application route that shows the node or its artifact in the web UI; informational.

post.summary: Launch a run of a workflow node's workflow, once per launch intent.
post.description:
Admits a launch of the workflow bound to the node: reserves a run for `intentId`, builds the run input from the node's settings and starts the run on the requested backend. HTTP 200 means the launch was admitted, not that the run finished: poll `GET /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/nodes/{nodeId}/workflow/status` or `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}`.

Send a new `intentId` for each launch you intend and repeat the same one to retry: a retry returns the launch it created instead of starting another run, and an intent that belongs to another node, source or project lifetime is rejected with HTTP 409 `WorkflowAdmissionConflict`. Without `intentId` every call starts another run.

When the launch was admitted but a later step, such as execution or delivery to the node, failed, the response is still HTTP 200 with the retained run, `status.delivery` Pending and a warning; repeat the request with the same `intentId` or poll the status to reconcile.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. The launch runs under the caller's workflow authority (the token's subject until the token expires, or the local operator when authorization is disabled); HTTP 403 `WorkflowAuthorityDenied` means that authority does not allow the launch. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

get.summary: Read the status of the latest run of a workflow node.
get.description:
Returns the status of the node's current launch (or, for nodes launched before launch admissions were recorded, its last run): run state, the status the node shows, step position, message, an execution summary with artifacts and created items, up to 12 recent events, and how far the result was delivered to the node. Before the first launch `runId` is null. Poll it until `state` is final (4 Completed, 5 Failed or 6 Cancelled); 2 WaitingForInput means the run waits for a response. Nothing is changed.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope (reads require the same scope).

post.summary: Delete a node with all its descendants, or finish the pending cleanup of an earlier deletion of that node.
post.description:
Without `durableMutationId`, removes the node and its whole subtree from the structure and then cleans up related records and managed files as `managedStorageDisposition` says. This requires the `expectedProjectAdmission` from the latest structure read. Files that cannot be deleted are kept and reported in `deletionWarnings`. Repeating a deletion that already completed returns its recorded result again, so a retry after an unclear failure is safe.

When the structure change is committed but the cleanup cannot finish, the response is HTTP 409 `ProjectStructureDeletionBatchPartialCommit`: the nodes are gone, and `details` lists the pending cleanups. Finish each one by calling this operation again with its `durableMutationId` and the same `managedStorageDisposition` (the admission is then not required), or list them later with `GET /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/deletion-cleanups`. Never start a new deletion of the same root instead.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.
