post.summary: Record an approval request as a Decision node in a project structure.
post.description:
Creates a Decision node with subtype `approval-request` under `parentNodeKey` (the project root when omitted) and returns it. Unless `metadataJson` is sent, its metadata records the requested operation, the estimated minutes and the requesting identity and time under `approvalRequest`. The node only records the request: nothing is blocked, paused or started by it. Repeating a request creates another node.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the project, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/project-structure/projects` or by project creation.

requestBody.description: Title, requested operation and optional parent, details, estimate and metadata.

200.description: The committed Decision node, with every optional member filled.

id.description: String node identifier, unique within the project; use it in node routes and requests. Nodes created through this API have the form `custom:` followed by 32 hexadecimal characters, for example `custom:3f2504e04f8911d39a0c0305e82c3301`. Nodes kept in sync with other records use other prefixes followed by that record's identifier, for example `project:{projectId}` for the project root, `project-child:{projectId}` for a subproject or `phase:{phaseId}`. Treat it as opaque and compare it exactly; it is not a GUID.

parentId.description: Identifier of the parent node in the hierarchy; null for a top-level node such as the project root.

objectType.description: Kind of project object the node represents. Returned as the object type name, for example `WorkItem`.

objectSubtype.description: Lower-case subtype that refines the object type, for example `task` for a WorkItem or `pdf` for a File; empty when none. A WorkItem with subtype `task` is a canonical task, changed only through the task operations.

subtitle.description: Secondary display text; may be empty.

status.description: Free-text status, for example Draft, Active or Done. Progress and the finished state are derived from words in it (see `progressMode`).

notes.description: Free-text notes; in a structure read, null unless `includeNotes` was true.

route.description: Application route that shows the node or its artifact in the web UI; informational.

artifactKind.description: Kind of record the node represents, for example `project` for project nodes or the object type name for ordinary nodes; informational.

artifactId.description: Identifier of the external record the node is bound to, for example the project id of a project node; null when the node has no external record.

mediaRelativePath.description: Location of the node's stored file within the application's managed storage; empty when the node has no file. In a structure read, null unless `includeAssets` was true. Not a path on the client's machine.

mediaContentType.description: Content type of the stored file, for example `application/pdf`; empty when there is none. In a structure read, null unless `includeAssets` was true.

mediaOriginalFileName.description: Original file name of the stored file; empty when there is none. In a structure read, null unless `includeAssets` was true.

badges.description: Display labels derived from the node, for example Synced (kept in sync with another record), Scheduled (has a planned start), a subtype label, Uploaded (has an uploaded file), Subproject, Parent or Shared parent. For display only; do not parse them.

progressMode.description: How progress is expressed: `complete`, `started`, `progress` or `na` (not applicable); empty when progress is not tracked, as for project hierarchy nodes. A status change resets the mode and percentage from the status text.

progressPercent.description: Progress from 0 through 100, or -1 when it is not tracked. Unless set explicitly, it follows the status: for example 28 for draft, planned, pending or queued, 62 for active, running or blocked, 78 for review or testing, and 100 for done, complete, approved, ready or final.

markerIcon.description: Icon token of the node's primary marker; empty when the node has no marker.

markerTone.description: Tone (color) token of the node's primary marker; empty when there is none.

markerLabel.description: Label of the node's primary marker; empty when there is none. A node can carry several markers; only the primary one is returned.

priority.description: Priority set on the node itself: 0 means none; smaller positive values are more urgent.

effectivePriority.description: Priority used for ordering and filtering, from 0 (none) through 6: the node's own priority or, unless the node is finished, paused or stopped, the most urgent nonzero priority among it and its descendants. Node creation and change responses return the node's own priority here.

startUtc.description: Planned start as an instant with offset; null when the node is not scheduled.

endUtc.description: Planned end as an instant with offset; null when the node is not scheduled.

metadataJson.description: Node metadata as a JSON string that contains a JSON object; parse it before use. In a structure read, null unless `includeMetadata` was true. Its sections are named after the object type, for example `workItem` for tasks (with `expectedEffortHours`, `expectedEffortUnit`, `executionState` and `directAssignmentRevision`) or `projectBlock`. Enum values inside it are camel-case strings such as `"hours"` or `"notStarted"`, unlike the integers used in request bodies.

projectRole.description: Role of the node in the project hierarchy, as a JSON integer: 0 None, 1 ActiveProject, 2 Subproject, 3 ParentProject, 4 AdditionalParentProject.

relatedProjectId.description: Project id that a project hierarchy node stands for (project root, subproject or parent project); null for other nodes.

parentProjectCount.description: For a subproject node, the number of project nodes in this structure that contain it; 0 for other nodes.

x.description: Horizontal canvas position in the structure editor; in a structure read, null unless `includeLayout` was true.

y.description: Vertical canvas position in the structure editor; in a structure read, null unless `includeLayout` was true.

durationSeconds.description: Stored planned duration in seconds; null when none is stored.

canRunNormally.description: True when the node's runtime plan can be executed directly on the server.

canRunAsAdministrator.description: True when the runtime plan can be started with elevation on the server.

canOpenInFileExplorer.description: True when an existing file or folder of the node, inside the configured workspace root, can be shown in the server's system file browser.

canOpenInNewTab.description: True when the node is IPFS-backed and opens in a separate browser tab.

runtimeDisplayName.description: Display name of the node's runtime plan; empty when there is none.

runtimeDisplayCommand.description: Always empty in this API: runtime commands are not disclosed over HTTP.

runtimeWorkingDirectory.description: Always empty in this API: working directories are not disclosed over HTTP.

post.summary: List the unfinished work of a project, most urgent first.
post.description:
Returns the project's unfinished nodes, except project nodes and, unless `includePaused` is true, paused or stopped nodes. Items are ordered by effective priority (nodes without a priority last) and then by title, and each lists its unfinished prerequisites: ancestors below the project root, DependsOn targets and Blocks sources. A node counts as finished when its progress mode is `complete` or its progress is 100, or when its status contains done, complete, approved, ready, final or archived. Nothing is changed.

Use the dependency query for the full analysis including finished nodes and dependents, and the structure read for all node members.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope (reads require the same scope).

parameters.description: Identifier of the project, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/project-structure/projects` or by project creation.

requestBody.description: Checklist query: filters for the list of open work in a project. Every member is optional; the empty object `{}` returns every unfinished node except project nodes (the project root, subprojects and parent projects) and paused or stopped nodes, most urgent first. Send one JSON object as `application/json` or `application/*+json`. The Project Structure reader rejects other content types with HTTP 415 `ProjectStructureContentTypeUnsupported`, a body larger than 262,144 bytes with HTTP 413 `ProjectStructureRequestBodyTooLarge`, and malformed JSON or members of the wrong JSON type with HTTP 400 `ProjectStructureRequestInvalid`.

post.summary: Analyze the prerequisites, dependents and durations of project nodes.
post.description:
For each selected node (every node when `nodeIds` is omitted) returns its prerequisites (ancestors below the project root, the targets of its DependsOn links and the sources of Blocks links to it), its dependents, whether it can start now (`canExecute`) and its known and effective duration. Items are ordered by title. Nothing is changed. Create and remove dependencies with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/dependencies/link` and `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/dependencies/unlink`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope (reads require the same scope).

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Create a directed link of a chosen kind between two nodes of a project.
post.description:
Records that the source node depends on, uses, validates, tests, blocks or derives from the target node. The operation succeeds with `changed` true also when the same link already exists. Hierarchy kinds (Contains, BelongsTo) are rejected: change the parent instead. A Uses link from a canonical task is rejected: attach task resources with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}/resource`. Dependencies can also be created with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/dependencies/link`; cycles of DependsOn links are not detected.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Create a File, ImageAsset or VideoAsset node and store its content as a managed file.
post.description:
Creates the asset node under `parentNodeKey` (required) and stores its content, taken from the first source present: inline `media`, a file in the server's managed workspace (`sourceWorkspacePath`) or a download from a public http or https address (`sourceUrl`). This is the only way to create File nodes and `mermaid` subtypes. Change an existing asset's content by creating a revision with `POST /api/project-structure/projects/{projectId}/assets/{nodeId}/revisions`. Repeating a request creates another asset.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

Content is limited to 25 MiB. With inline `media` the whole JSON body must also stay under the host's default request limit of 30,000,000 bytes, which base64 encoding reaches with files of about 21 MiB; a larger body is rejected with HTTP 400 `ProjectStructureRequestInvalid`. Use `sourceWorkspacePath` or `sourceUrl` for larger files.

requestBody.description: Asset creation request: a new File, ImageAsset or VideoAsset node under an explicit parent, with its content taken from exactly one source, in this order of precedence: `media` (inline base64), `sourceWorkspacePath` (a file in the server's managed workspace) or `sourceUrl` (a download from a public web address). The content is stored as a managed file of the project. Send one JSON object as `application/json` or `application/*+json`. The Project Structure reader rejects other content types with HTTP 415 `ProjectStructureContentTypeUnsupported`, a body larger than 36,001,112 bytes with HTTP 413 `ProjectStructureRequestBodyTooLarge`, and malformed JSON or members of the wrong JSON type with HTTP 400 `ProjectStructureRequestInvalid`.

Nodes created through this API have the form `custom:` followed by 32 hexadecimal characters, for example `custom:3f2504e04f8911d39a0c0305e82c3301`. Nodes kept in sync with other records use other prefixes followed by that record's identifier, for example `project:{projectId}` for the project root, `project-child:{projectId}` for a subproject or `phase:{phaseId}`. Treat it as opaque and compare it exactly; it is not a GUID.

parentId.description: Identifier of the parent node in the hierarchy; null for a top-level node such as the project root.

subtitle.description: Secondary display text; may be empty.

status.description: Free-text status, for example Draft, Active or Done. Progress and the finished state are derived from words in it (see `progressMode`).

notes.description: Free-text notes; in a structure read, null unless `includeNotes` was true.

route.description: Application route that shows the node or its artifact in the web UI; informational.

artifactKind.description: Kind of record the node represents, for example `project` for project nodes or the object type name for ordinary nodes; informational.

artifactId.description: Identifier of the external record the node is bound to, for example the project id of a project node; null when the node has no external record.

post.summary: Create a revision of an asset: a new asset node with new content, linked to the original.
post.description:
Stores the new content as a new asset node of the same type under the original asset and links it to the original with DerivedFrom; the result's `revisionParentNodeId` names the original. The original node and its content stay unchanged. Omitted subtype and metadata are copied from the original. Always send `media`: a null value creates a revision node without content and then fails with HTTP 400 `AssetRequired`, leaving that node in the structure. Repeating a request creates another revision.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. Send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or a member of the wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Import an outline (Mermaid, Word, XMind or JSON) as new nodes of a project structure.
post.description:
Creates a container ProjectBlock titled `title` under `parentNodeKey` (by default the project root), stores `sourceAsset` in it as a File node when one is sent, and creates one node per outline item below the container: items with children become ProjectBlock nodes (subtype `containerBlockSubtype`) and leaves become WorkItem nodes (subtype `leafWorkItemSubtype`, by default `task`, which makes them canonical tasks). Mermaid flowchart edges become DependsOn links. The new nodes are then laid out automatically. The import is not idempotent: repeating it creates another container.

The import is not atomic. Each node is saved separately, and the source is read only after the container and the source file node were created. A failure after that point, including most HTTP 400 errors below, leaves the nodes created so far in the structure: read the structure and delete the partial container before retrying.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. The lease is on the body's `projectId`: send `leaseToken` to work under your own project lease. Without it the operation uses the project lease your identity already holds, or else takes a five-minute project lease for its own duration; if another identity holds the lease, it waits when that lease ends within 30 seconds and otherwise fails with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict`.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON, or a member of the wrong JSON type such as a source kind name instead of its integer) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Acquire or extend a lease on a project, a project node or a repository branch for the calling identity.
post.description:
A lease tells other writers that a scope is being changed. For a Project lease, send the returned `leaseToken` as `leaseToken` with that project's mutations to make several changes under one lease. Mutations sent without a token take a five-minute project lease for their own duration and release it afterwards; they fail with HTTP 409 `LeaseConflict` while another identity holds the project lease. ProjectNode and RepoBranch leases only coordinate callers that look for them.

When the calling identity already holds the active lease on the scope, the lease is extended from now, its reason is replaced and the same token is returned; otherwise a new lease with a new token is created. Released or expired leases are never revived. The holder is the calling identity (the bearer token's subject, or the shared identity `local-api-operator` when API authorization is disabled), so every caller with that identity can use the lease.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.project-structure.write` scope. A lease is neither an authorization nor a project write admission.

Renew the lease with `POST /api/project-structure/leases/renew` before `expiresAtUtc` and release it with `POST /api/project-structure/leases/release` when done. A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON or an unknown `scopeKind`) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

post.summary: Read the log of recent Project Structure operation calls, newest first.
post.description:
Every call of a Project Structure operation, successful or failed, is recorded when it finishes: reads included, calls made by in-process agent tools included, and calls of this query itself included. Filter by project, operation name, caller identity and outcome; the filters combine. At most 200 entries are returned and there is no paging.

The log is not limited to the caller: every caller with access sees all entries, and their request and response bodies can contain notes, metadata, inline file content, lease tokens and internal failure messages. Treat the response as sensitive.

get.summary: Read the database runtime context that every other storage placement recovery request must carry.
get.description:
Storage placement recovery resolves stable storage placements whose outcome was left open: a planned write of an asset to a storage provider that was not confirmed, or a completed write whose owner (the process step or workflow that produced the asset) did not record it. Every recovery request carries this context, which names the host's active database profile and its generation. Call this operation first, and again after any 409 `StaleContext`: the context changes when the host switches its database profile, and requests with an old context are rejected. The read has no side effects.

Failures return a JSON object with a single `failure` member.

Authority: usable only while API authorization is enabled; otherwise every request is refused with 403 (`Denied`). The bearer token must hold the exact scopes `api` and `api.storage-placement-recovery.read`. The check is repeated during the request, so a token revoked or narrowed meanwhile gets 403.

200.description: The current database runtime context.

403.description: `Denied`: authorization is disabled, or the token is missing, invalid, revoked or lacks a required scope.

409.description: `StaleContext`: the host switched its database profile during the read; call this operation again.

503.description: `Unavailable`: the context could not be read. Nothing was changed; try again later.

get.summary: List stable storage placements whose write is unresolved, oldest first, one page at a time.
get.description:
Returns placements in the storage states `Prepared`, `Dispatching`, `Uncertain` and `Conflict`, ordered by creation time and then by intent identifier. Completed and deleted placements are not listed; for completed placements whose owner has not recorded them, use `GET /api/storage-placement-recovery/pending-continuations`. Each item says which action, if any, the caller may take (`availableAction`) or why none is possible (`block`). The items contain no content, storage addresses or paths. The read has no side effects.

Paging is offset-based: send `offset` = `nextOffset` of the previous page until `nextOffset` is null. After a 409 `StaleContext`, read the context again and restart from offset 0.

Failures return a JSON object with a single `failure` member. A missing or malformed `databaseProfileId` or `generation` is rejected by the framework with 400 before the operation runs, without that object.

Authority: usable only while API authorization is enabled; otherwise every request is refused with 403 (`Denied`). The bearer token must hold the exact scopes `api` and `api.storage-placement-recovery.read`. Without the write scopes, a placement that could otherwise be reconciled shows `block` `ReadOnlyAuthority` instead of an action.

parameters.name: offset

get.summary: List completed storage placements whose owner has not finished recording them, one page at a time.
get.description:
The storage write of these placements completed (storage state `Completed`, or `Deleted` after a later deletion), but the owner that produced the asset (a process step's agent run or a workflow run) has not finished recording it; `phase` says which step is missing. Use `GET /api/storage-placement-recovery/{intentId}/owner-continuation` on an item to see whether a continuation can finish it. The items contain no content, storage addresses or paths. The read has no side effects.

Paging is offset-based over the owners' candidate records: `take` bounds the candidates examined, so a page can hold fewer items than `take`, or none, while `nextOffset` is not null. Continue with `offset` = `nextOffset` until it is null. After a 409 `StaleContext`, read the context again and restart from offset 0.

Failures return a JSON object with a single `failure` member. A missing or malformed `databaseProfileId` or `generation` is rejected by the framework with 400 before the operation runs, without that object.

Authority: usable only while API authorization is enabled; otherwise every request is refused with 403 (`Denied`). The bearer token must hold the exact scopes `api` and `api.storage-placement-recovery.read`.

get.summary: Read the recovery state of one stable storage placement by its intent identifier.
get.description:
Returns the placement's storage state, whether its storage and owner receipts exist, and which recovery action the caller may take (`availableAction`) or why none is possible (`block`). Read it before any recovery command and again after one, because a command's response can be followed by further changes. The item contains no content, storage addresses or paths. The read has no side effects.

Failures return a JSON object with a single `failure` member. A missing or malformed `databaseProfileId` or `generation` is rejected by the framework with 400 before the operation runs, without that object.

Authority: usable only while API authorization is enabled; otherwise every request is refused with 403 (`Denied`). The bearer token must hold the exact scopes `api` and `api.storage-placement-recovery.read`. Without the write scopes, a placement that could otherwise be reconciled shows `block` `ReadOnlyAuthority` instead of an action.

parameters.name: intentId
parameters.description: Identifier (GUID) of the placement intent, as `identity.intentId.value` in the list operations. Must not be the empty GUID.

parameters.name: databaseProfileId
parameters.description: `databaseProfileId` of the context returned by `GET /api/storage-placement-recovery/context`.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description: `generation` of the context returned by `GET /api/storage-placement-recovery/context`.

403.description: `Denied`: authorization is disabled, or the token is missing, invalid, revoked or lacks a required scope.

post.summary: Reconcile an unresolved stable storage placement by reading back its exact original target.
post.description:
Use it when a read shows `availableAction` `Reconcile`. The host re-reads the exact target that was prepared for the placement and compares its length and SHA-256 hash with the planned content. It never uploads the content again, never chooses another target and never deletes what it finds. The original project must still exist in the lifetime it had when the placement was planned.

HTTP 200 means that reconciliation ran, not that the placement is complete: the body is the item read after the attempt, and `storageState` tells the result.

- `Completed`: the content was verified at the target and the storage receipt recorded.
- `Uncertain`: the outcome still could not be verified; the target is kept. Do not treat it as stored and do not write the content elsewhere; reconcile again later or investigate the storage.
- `Conflict`: the target holds different content, which was preserved and not overwritten.

A write to FTP without a completion acknowledgment cannot be reconciled until an operator attests that its server-side dispatch stopped; the item then shows `availableAction` `VerifyExternalTermination`.

Repeating the request is another read-back of the same target and never writes content, but a failure response does not prove that nothing changed: after 403, 409 or 503 read the item again before deciding the next step.

Failures return a JSON object with a single `failure` member.

Authority: usable only while API authorization is enabled; otherwise every request is refused with 403 (`Denied`). The bearer token must hold the exact scopes `api`, `api.storage-placement-recovery.read`, `api.project-structure.write` and `api.storage-placement-recovery.reconcile`.

requestBody.description: The context and the intent of the placement to reconcile.

200.description: Reconciliation ran; `storageState` of the returned item tells whether the placement completed.

400.description: `InvalidRequest`: the context is invalid.

403.description: `Denied`: authorization is disabled, or the token is missing, invalid, revoked or lacks a required scope.

404.description: `NotFound`: no placement intent has this identifier in the active database.

409.description: `Blocked`: reconciliation is not available for the placement now (read the item for `block` and `availableAction`), or `StaleContext`: the context is not the host's current one.

503.description: `Unavailable`: the request could not complete, and it may have stopped after changing the placement. Read the item again before any further step; do not repeat blindly.

post.summary: Record an operator's attestation that an unacknowledged FTP upload has stopped, then reconcile the placement.
post.description:
Use it only when a read shows `availableAction` `VerifyExternalTermination`: an FTP upload was dispatched but its completion was never acknowledged, so the host cannot tell whether the server is still receiving data. Send the request only after verifying outside the host, for example on the FTP server, that no further data can arrive for that upload. The attestation is recorded durably and cannot be withdrawn through this API. The host then reconciles the placement as `POST /api/storage-placement-recovery/reconcile` does, reading back the exact target without uploading again.

HTTP 200 means that the attestation was recorded and reconciliation ran; `storageState` of the returned item tells the result (`Completed`, `Uncertain` or `Conflict`). A failure response does not prove that nothing changed: after 403, 409 or 503 read the item again before deciding the next step.

Failures return a JSON object with a single `failure` member.

Authority: usable only while API authorization is enabled; otherwise every request is refused with 403 (`Denied`). The bearer token must hold the exact scopes `api`, `api.storage-placement-recovery.read`, `api.project-structure.write`, `api.storage-placement-recovery.reconcile` and `api.storage-placement-recovery.verify-external-termination`. Grant the last scope only to operators who can verify the FTP server.

requestBody.description: The context, the intent and the explicit attestation.

200.description: The attestation was recorded and reconciliation ran; `storageState` of the returned item tells the result.

400.description: `InvalidRequest`: `verifiedExternalDispatchStopped` is not true, or the context is invalid. Nothing was recorded.

403.description: `Denied`: authorization is disabled, or the token is missing, invalid, revoked or lacks a required scope.

404.description: `NotFound`: no placement intent has this identifier in the active database.

409.description: `Blocked`: the placement does not need or allow the attestation now (read the item for `block` and `availableAction`), or `StaleContext`: the context is not the host's current one.

503.description: `Unavailable`: the request could not complete, and it may have stopped after recording the attestation or changing the placement. Read the item again before any further step; do not repeat blindly.

get.summary: Read whether the owner of a completed storage placement recorded it, and which continuation can finish it.
get.description:
Applies to placements listed by `GET /api/storage-placement-recovery/pending-continuations`: the storage write completed, but the owner that produced the asset may not have recorded it. The observation returns the placement (`storage`), the owner's state (`state`) and the continuation the caller may run (`availableAction`):

- `ReconcileCancelledRunReceipts`: run `POST /api/storage-placement-recovery/reconcile-cancelled-run-receipts`.
- `RecordWorkflowAssetReceipt` or `CompletePreparedWorkflowAsset`: run `POST /api/storage-placement-recovery/continue-workflow-asset` with that action and the returned `workflowIntent`.
- `None`: nothing can be run now; `state` says why.

The read has no side effects.

Failures return a JSON object with a single `failure` member. A missing or malformed `databaseProfileId` or `generation` is rejected by the framework with 400 before the operation runs, without that object.

Authority: usable only while API authorization is enabled; otherwise every request is refused with 403 (`Denied`). The bearer token must hold the exact scopes `api` and `api.storage-placement-recovery.read`; without the write scopes `state` is `ReadOnlyAuthority` where an action would otherwise be offered.

parameters.description: Identifier (GUID) of the placement intent, as `storage.identity.intentId.value` in `GET /api/storage-placement-recovery/pending-continuations`. Must not be the empty GUID.

post.summary: Reconcile the tool receipts of a cancelled agent run so that it records the process asset it placed in storage.
post.description:
Use it when `GET /api/storage-placement-recovery/{intentId}/owner-continuation` shows `availableAction` `ReconcileCancelledRunReceipts`: a process step's agent run was cancelled after its asset was placed in storage, and the run did not record the asset. The host reconciles the cancelled run: it records the tool effect only when the owner confirms it with a receipt, and it never runs the tool again or writes the content again.

The body is the observation read after the attempt; read `state`. `ReceiptRecorded` means the asset is now recorded. `NativeReceiptNotObserved` means no receipt was found yet; the action stays available and the effect remains uncertain, because an earlier transaction of the owner could still commit. Other states, such as `OwnerReceiptUnconfirmed`, `CurrentReadDenied` or `ContinuationUnavailable`, mean the receipt could not be reconciled this way. When the owner state is neither `Ready` nor `ReceiptRecorded`, the request changes nothing and returns the current observation, still with HTTP 200.

A failure response does not prove that nothing changed: after 403, 409 or 503 read the owner continuation again before deciding the next step.

Failures return a JSON object with a single `failure` member.

post.summary: Finish a workflow asset whose storage placement completed, using the continuation the owner offers.
post.description:
Use it when `GET /api/storage-placement-recovery/{intentId}/owner-continuation` shows `availableAction` `CompletePreparedWorkflowAsset` (create the workflow's prepared asset node in the project structure from the completed placement) or `RecordWorkflowAssetReceipt` (the node exists; record the workflow's receipt). Send that action and the `workflowIntent` of the same read unchanged as `expectedIntent`. The host checks both against the current state; when anything changed after your read, the request is rejected with 409 `Blocked` and nothing is continued. The content is never written again.

The body is the observation read after the attempt; read `state` and `availableAction`. `ReceiptRecorded` means the asset is recorded. `WorkflowManifestPending` means the asset is in the project structure but the workflow has not yet acknowledged it; after a new read, run the operation again with `RecordWorkflowAssetReceipt`.

A failure response does not prove that nothing changed: after 403, 409 or 503 read the owner continuation again before deciding the next step.

Failures return a JSON object with a single `failure` member.

get.summary: Read how the HTTP API of this host is configured: enabled surfaces, authorization and token lifetimes.
get.description:
Use this read to discover whether a bearer token is needed before calling other operations, and which issuer, audience and lifetimes a token issued by `POST /api/access/tokens` gets. The response contains no signing key and no token.

Authority: anonymous. The route never requires a bearer token, even when API authorization is enabled. It exists only while `Api:Enabled` is true, so `apiEnabled` is always true in a response.

200.description: The current API access configuration.

post.summary: Issue a signed bearer token for this host's HTTP API with the requested scopes and lifetime.
post.description:
Creates a new managed API token: an HS256-signed JSON Web Token with this host's configured issuer and audience, the requested subject and scopes, and an expiry. The token is registered with the host, which checks the registration on every request, so a revoked, deleted or expired token is rejected even while its signature is still valid. Every call issues a new, separate token; nothing is replaced.

Send the returned `token` as `Authorization: Bearer {token}`. The token value is returned only in this response and cannot be read again; store it as a secret and keep it out of URLs, logs and source control. Operations that require a specific scope check the scope names exactly and case-sensitively, and a scope name that no operation uses grants nothing.

Tokens can be issued only while API authorization is enabled (`Api:Authorization:Enabled`); otherwise the request fails with HTTP 400. Read `GET /api/access/status` first to check this and the lifetime limits.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the exact `api.tokens.issue` scope; the general `api` scope is not enough. Grant that scope only to administrators, because a caller that holds it can issue tokens with any scope.

400.description: The token was not issued (`api.token-invalid`): API authorization is disabled or misconfigured, the subject is blank, the lifetime is zero, negative or above the configured maximum, or no non-blank scope was given.

401.description: API authorization is enabled and no valid bearer token was sent (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: The bearer token lacks the `api.tokens.issue` scope (`api.authorization-forbidden`).

get.summary: List all projects with their status, hierarchy counts and main participants.
get.description:
Returns every project, most recently updated first; the list is not paged or filtered. A project is the Projects-owned business record; its task and node hierarchy is read through `/api/project-structure`. Each summary carries the status, current phase, number of phases, number of parent and child projects, and the parties that take part in the project as a whole (not only in one of its tasks) together with the resulting primary customer, delivery unit and owner names.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

post.summary: Create a project, or overwrite the editable fields, phases and options of an existing project.
post.description:
Without `id` a new project with a new identifier is created; every such call creates another project. With `id` the project with that identifier is updated: all editable fields are overwritten with the values sent, phases and options missing from the request are deleted, entries whose `id` matches a stored entry are updated and the other entries are added. Start from `GET /api/projects/{projectId}` and send the complete object. Phases are stored in array order; option entries with an empty name and empty notes are skipped.

Send `expectedLifetimeId` from the read: when the project was deleted and recreated with the same identifier since then, the save is rejected with `projects.lifetime-changed`. Without it the save applies to the current project with that identifier. There is no other concurrency check; the last save wins. Subproject links are changed with the subproject operations, not with this request.

The project is saved first; the search index and the activity feed are updated afterwards, and failures of those updates are logged without changing the response.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

400.description: The project was not saved: `validation` (blank name) or `projects.lifetime-changed` (`expectedLifetimeId` names an earlier lifetime of the project; read it again). A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

404.description: No project has the sent `id` (`projects.not-found`), for example because it was deleted. Omit `id` to create a project.

get.summary: List the identifier and name of every project, ordered by name.
get.description:
A lightweight alternative to `GET /api/projects` for pickers: one item per project with only its identifier and name, ordered by name. It lists every project and is not filtered by the caller.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

get.summary: List every parent-child link between projects.
get.description:
Returns all links of the project hierarchy, ordered by parent and then child project identifier. A project can have several parents and several children; the attach and reconnect operations reject links that would create a cycle. Use `GET /api/projects/{projectId}/hierarchy` for the direct parents and children of one project with their summaries.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

200.description: All hierarchy links; an empty array when no project has a parent.

get.summary: Read the editable fields of a project, or a blank template when no project has the identifier.
get.description:
Returns the project's name, description, objective, status, current phase, target date, phases and technology options, and `expectedLifetimeId`, the identifier of the project's current lifetime. Change the values and send the whole object to `POST /api/projects` to update the project.

When no project has the identifier the response is still 200: a blank template for a new project whose `id` and `expectedLifetimeId` are null. Check `id` before treating the response as an existing project.

`options` always contains an entry for each of the categories Language, Database, Ui, ExternalApi, Storage, Deployment and Testing; an entry without a stored value has a null `id` and an empty name.
