parameters.description: Identifier of the project, as returned by `GET /api/projects`.

200.description: The project's editable fields, or a blank template with a null `id`.

delete.summary: Delete a project and have the other modules clean up the data they keep for it.
delete.description:
Deletes the project record with its phases, options and hierarchy links, retires its lifetime and removes its search entries and storage routing. Then every registered deletion participant cleans up its own data for the project: currently `workbench` (Project Structure nodes and managed media) and `agent-project-structure-access` (agents' access to the project). Subprojects are kept; only their links to this project are removed.

Outcomes:

- 200: the project is deleted and every participant finished. `warnings` lists objects that were kept, such as managed media retained by a storage provider, with remediation text.
- 409 with `projects.delete-cleanup-pending`: the project is deleted, but at least one participant did not finish. The deletion is not rolled back. Retry each entry of `recovery.failures` with `POST /api/projects/{projectId}/deletion-cleanups/{participantId}/{recoveryId}/retry`, using its exact `participantId.value` and `recoveryId`; do not delete the project again to finish the cleanup.

Deleting an identifier that has no project still runs the participant cleanups for it and returns the same outcomes.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the project to delete, as returned by `GET /api/projects`.

200.description: The project is deleted (or did not exist) and all cleanup finished; `warnings` lists retained objects.

409.description: The project is deleted but cleanup is incomplete (`projects.delete-cleanup-pending`); `recovery` lists the participant cleanups to retry.

get.summary: List the project-deletion cleanups that have not finished.
get.description:
After a project is deleted, each deletion participant cleans up its own data for it (currently `workbench` for Project Structure nodes and managed media and `agent-project-structure-access` for agents' access to the project). This read returns one item for each participant cleanup that has not finished, across all projects, ordered by project, participant and recovery identifier.

Retry an item with `POST /api/projects/{projectId}/deletion-cleanups/{participantId}/{recoveryId}/retry`, using its `projectId`, `participantId.value` and `recoveryId`. When `canRetryNow` is false, another attempt is running and holds the cleanup until `retryAvailableAtUtc`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

200.description: The unfinished cleanups; an empty array when nothing is pending.

get.summary: List the finished project-deletion cleanups and the objects they kept.
get.description:
Returns one notice for each finished participant cleanup of a project deletion, and for each finished cleanup of deleted Project Structure nodes that kept objects, across all projects, ordered by project, participant and recovery identifier. `warnings` lists managed media that was kept, for example by an immutable storage provider, with remediation text. Reading the notices does not remove them.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

200.description: The completion notices; an empty array when there are none.

post.summary: Retry one unfinished participant cleanup of a deleted project.
post.description:
Runs again the cleanup identified by the project, participant and recovery identifiers, taken from `recovery.failures` of a 409 deletion response or from `GET /api/projects/deletion-cleanups`. Use the exact identifiers; deleting the project again does not finish an earlier cleanup. When the cleanup has already finished, the response is 200 with the warnings recorded for it, so repeating a successful retry is safe.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the deleted project.

parameters.name: participantId
parameters.description: Text identifier of the deletion participant, the `participantId.value` of the cleanup, for example `workbench`. Surrounding whitespace is ignored; the rest must match exactly.

parameters.name: recoveryId
parameters.description: Recovery identifier of the cleanup, from the same source as the participant.

200.description: The cleanup has finished, now or earlier; `warnings` lists retained objects.

400.description: The participant identifier is blank (`projects.delete-cleanup-participant-invalid`).

404.description: No unfinished or finished cleanup matches the project, participant and recovery identifiers (`projects.delete-cleanup-not-found`).

409.description: The cleanup is still incomplete (`projects.delete-cleanup-pending`); the project stays deleted. Retry later with the identifiers in `recovery.failures`.

get.summary: Read the direct parent and child projects of a project.
get.description:
Returns the summaries of the projects directly above and directly below the project in the project hierarchy, each list most recently updated first. A project can have several parents. When no project has the identifier, both lists are empty and the response is still 200.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the project, as returned by `GET /api/projects`.

200.description: The project's direct parents and children; empty lists when it has none.

post.summary: Make an existing project a subproject of another existing project.
post.description:
Adds a parent-child link between two projects. A project can have several parents, so the child's other parent links are kept; use `POST /api/projects/{childProjectId}/reconnect-subproject` to move a subproject from one parent to another. Attaching a link that already exists succeeds without a change. A link that would make a project its own ancestor is rejected.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: parentProjectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the project that becomes the parent.

parameters.name: childProjectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the project that becomes the subproject.

200.description: The link exists.

400.description: Nothing was changed (`validation`): both identifiers are equal, the parent or the subproject was not found, or the link would create a cycle. The message says which.

delete.summary: Remove the link between a parent project and one of its subprojects.
delete.description:
Deletes only the parent-child link; both projects and the subproject's other parent links are kept. Detaching a link that does not exist fails.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: parentProjectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the parent project.

parameters.name: childProjectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the subproject to detach.

200.description: The link was removed.

400.description: Nothing was changed (`validation`): the link does not exist, or one of the projects no longer exists.

post.summary: Move a subproject from its current parent project to another parent project.
post.description:
Removes the link from `currentParentProjectId` and adds a link from `newParentProjectId` in one save. When the subproject is already linked to the new parent, only the old link is removed. The subproject's other parent links are kept. A move that would make the subproject an ancestor of its new parent is rejected.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: childProjectId
parameters.description: Identifier of the subproject to move.

requestBody.description: The current and the new parent project.

200.description: The subproject was moved.

400.description: Nothing was changed (`validation`): both parents are the same, the subproject is not linked to `currentParentProjectId`, one of the three projects was not found, or the move would create a cycle. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

get.summary: List the agent definitions of the current workspace, ordered by name.
get.description:
Returns the technical agent definitions, the configuration and identity an agent execution run uses, in case-insensitive name order and without paging. Agents of every lifecycle status (Draft, Active, Suspended, Archived) are included; template agents are left out unless `includeTemplates` is true. The CRM/HR party that represents an agent is a projection maintained from these definitions; change the agent here, not the party.

Each item is the stored definition, including its `configurationJson` string and its allowed secret references (identifiers and display names only, never secret values). To change an agent, read its editable form with `GET /api/agents/{agentId}`, which also carries the concurrency revision.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: includeTemplates
parameters.description: True to include template agents. Omitted or false returns only agents that are not templates.

200.description: The matching agents; an empty array when there are none.

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: Only when API authorization is enabled and an authenticated token is refused by an operation policy (`api.authorization-forbidden`). This operation accepts any valid token, so it does not currently return this status.

post.summary: Create an agent definition, or replace an existing one using the revision the caller last read.
post.description:
A save stores the complete agent from the body: every member is taken from the request, and an omitted member falls back to its default (for example status Draft, default permissions, no capabilities, no access settings), so always send the whole editor form. Do not send JSON null for text, list or object members: it is not translated into the error envelope and fails with a generic HTTP 500.

To create an agent, send `id` and `expectedUpdatedAtUtc` as null. To update one:

1. Read `GET /api/agents/{agentId}`.
2. Change only the members you intend to change; keep `id` and `expectedUpdatedAtUtc` as read.
3. Send the whole form, then read the agent again for the stored values and the new revision.

When `expectedUpdatedAtUtc` is present it must equal the stored revision exactly; otherwise nothing is saved and the request is rejected with HTTP 400. When it is null, an existing agent is overwritten without a concurrency check. An `id` that does not exist yet creates the agent with that identifier.

The server trims text, derives the template key from `templateKey` or, when blank, from `name`, drops unknown capability identifiers and duplicate tags, replaces `permissions.allowedSecrets` with `allowedSecretReferences`, and writes each typed access setting over its key in `configurationJson` (a value that is not a JSON object is replaced by an empty object). Saved configuration never attaches runtime tools by itself: each run still applies the agent's permissions, capabilities, access settings and invocation policy.

The agent is committed before the CRM/HR directory projection is refreshed. If that refresh fails, the request fails with a generic HTTP 500 although the agent is saved; list the agents before retrying, because a repeated create is then rejected for its already used template key.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The complete agent form.

200.description: The agent was saved. The body is the agent identifier as a JSON string (a GUID); read the agent to get the stored values and its new revision.

400.description: Nothing was saved (`agents.request-invalid`). Causes: `expectedUpdatedAtUtc` differs from the stored revision or names an agent that does not exist; the template key has no letter or digit or already belongs to another agent or template; the provider profile does not exist; the model is not allowed by a shared provider or has no price row on the provider profile; the thinking effort is not supported by the provider and model; a project that does not exist is granted for the first time; or an access setting is invalid. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without an envelope.

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: Only when API authorization is enabled and an authenticated token is refused by an operation policy (`api.authorization-forbidden`). This operation accepts any valid token, so it does not currently return this status.

get.summary: Read the data needed to open the agent chat page: the agent list and the workspace of the initially selected agent.
get.description:
Returns the agents as short catalog items in case-insensitive name order (templates only when `includeTemplates` is true), the agent to select first (the one with the most recently updated chat session, otherwise the first listed agent) and that agent's chat workspace. It only reads. For one agent's chat workspace use `GET /api/agents/{agentId}/chat-workspace`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: includeTemplates
parameters.description: True to include template agents in the list. Omitted or false lists only agents that are not templates.

200.description: The agent list, the initially selected agent and its workspace; the agent and workspace are null when there are no agents.

get.summary: Read an agent definition as the editable form accepted by `POST /api/agents`.
get.description:
Returns the agent's stored settings in editor form: the definition's fields, the typed access settings parsed from its `configurationJson`, the selected capability identifiers and `expectedUpdatedAtUtc`, the concurrency revision to send back when saving. This is the read step of an agent update: change only the members you intend to change and send the whole form to `POST /api/agents`.

An unknown agent identifier, or stored access or thinking-effort configuration that cannot be parsed, is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Identifier of the agent, as returned by `GET /api/agents`.

200.description: The editable form of the agent, including its current revision.

delete.summary: Delete an agent definition together with its chat sessions, execution history and memory notes.
delete.description:
Removes the agent definition, its chat sessions, its execution runs with their log, metrics, approvals, artifacts, checkpoints and tool receipts, its workspace memory notes, its team memberships and its external-key bindings. This cannot be undone; export the agent first (`GET /api/agents/{agentId}/export`) when a copy is needed. The CRM/HR party that represented the agent is kept, with its binding to the agent marked as missing.

Deleting an identifier that does not exist succeeds, so a repeated delete is harmless. The all-zero identifier is not translated into the error envelope and fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Identifier of the agent to delete.

200.description: The agent no longer exists (it was deleted or never existed). The body is `{ "ok": true }`.

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: Only when API authorization is enabled and an authenticated token is refused by an operation policy (`api.authorization-forbidden`). This operation accepts any valid token, so it does not currently return this status.

409.description: The agent was not deleted: it is managed by the product and cannot be deleted (`agents.delete-managed-seed`), or one of its runs is still preparing, running, waiting on a tool or persisting, or has tool effects that are not resolved (`agents.delete-active-execution`). Let the run finish or resolve it, then delete again.

post.summary: Create a new agent definition that copies an existing agent or template.
post.description:
Creates an agent that is not a template, with a new identifier, the name `cloneName` and a template key derived from that name. Everything else is copied from the source: its status (an archived source gives an archived clone), provider and model, instructions, permissions and allowed secret references, capability assignments with their proof state, access settings, tags and avatar. Chat sessions, runs, memory notes, team memberships and external-key bindings are not copied. Cloning a template is how a template becomes a working agent; change the clone afterwards through `GET /api/agents/{agentId}` and `POST /api/agents`.

An unknown source, a name without any letter or digit, or a name whose derived template key already belongs to another agent is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500 and nothing is created. The clone is committed before the CRM/HR directory projection is refreshed; if that refresh fails, HTTP 500 is returned although the clone exists, so list the agents before retrying.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Identifier of the agent or template to copy.

requestBody.description: Name of the new agent.

200.description: The clone was created. The body is the new agent's identifier as a JSON string (a GUID).

post.summary: Create a template agent from an existing agent, leaving the source agent unchanged.
post.description:
Despite its route, this does not convert the agent in place: it adds a new template agent with a new identifier, the name of the source followed by " template" and the given template key, copying the source's other settings. The source agent and its history are unchanged. Create working agents from the template with `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/clone`.

The template key is normalized to lower-case letters and digits separated by hyphens and must not already belong to another agent or template. A blank key falls back to the source name, which normally collides with the source agent's own key, so send an explicit key. An unknown agent or an unusable or duplicate key is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500 and nothing is created. The template is committed before the CRM/HR directory projection is refreshed; if that refresh fails, HTTP 500 is returned although the template exists, so list the agents with `includeTemplates=true` before retrying.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Identifier of the agent to copy into a template.

requestBody.description: Template key of the new template.

200.description: The template was created. The body is the new template's agent identifier as a JSON string (a GUID).

get.summary: Write an export package of an agent on the server and return the package's server path.
get.description:
Although this is a GET, every call writes a new ZIP package into the workspace's export folder on the server and returns its absolute server-side path. The package itself is not returned, and this API offers no download of it; the path is meant for `POST /api/agents/import` on the same host or for an operator with file access. Repeated calls create additional packages.

The package contains the agent definition, its chat sessions, its execution runs with their log, metrics, approvals, artifacts, checkpoints and tool receipts, its memory notes, its own provider profile and its assigned capabilities. Secrets appear only as references, and protected run state is removed or redacted.

An unknown agent identifier is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Identifier of the agent to export.

200.description: The package was written. The body gives its server path and a short summary.

post.summary: Import an agent from an export package file that already exists on the server.
post.description:
Reads the ZIP package at `packagePath`, a path in the server's file system such as one returned by `GET /api/agents/{agentId}/export`, and stores its agent under the agent's original identifier together with its chat sessions, runs and their evidence, and memory notes. Its provider profile and capabilities are matched to existing ones by identifier or identity and otherwise added to the agent catalog. To upload a package from the client instead, use `POST /api/agents/import-package`.

If an agent with the same identifier exists, it is replaced without any check for active runs: its chat sessions, runs, evidence and memory notes are replaced by the package's copies, and its external-key bindings are deleted because packages carry none (bind it again with `PUT /api/agents/by-external-key/{externalNamespace}/{key}`). Team memberships are kept. Treat an import over an existing agent as destructive.

The package must use schema version 1.0, contain only the known entries (at most 64), stay within 32 MiB compressed and 128 MiB expanded, and contain no raw secret values. A missing file, an invalid package, an ambiguous provider or capability match or a conflicting template key is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500. The agent is committed before the CRM/HR directory projection is refreshed; if that refresh fails, HTTP 500 is returned although the import is stored.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: Server path of the package to import.

200.description: The agent was imported. The body is its identifier as a JSON string (a GUID), the identifier stored in the package.

post.summary: Import an agent package file to create, replace or clone an agent bound to an external identity.
post.description:
Reads a ZIP agent package, as produced by the agent export, and adds its agent to the current workspace in one of three modes. The resulting agent is bound to an external identity (namespace and key) that `GET /api/agents/by-external-key/{externalNamespace}/{key}` resolves afterwards. To provision an agent from a JSON definition instead of a package, use `PUT /api/agents/by-external-key/{externalNamespace}/{key}`.

Send `multipart/form-data` with the file part `package` and the text fields `mode`, `externalKey` and, optionally, `externalNamespace`, `expectedPackageSha256` and `expectedAgentVersion`, together with the `Idempotency-Key` header. The package may have at most 32 MiB (33554432 bytes), expand to at most 128 MiB and contain only the entries `manifest.json` (package schema version 1.0, at most 8 MiB), `agent.md`, `instructions.txt`, `memory.json`, `sessions.json` and `metrics.json`. Symbolic links, executable entries and raw secret values in the manifest (a non-empty `apiKey`, `accessToken`, `bearerToken`, `clientSecret`, `password`, `privateKey` or `refreshToken` property) are rejected. A whole request larger than 33 MiB is rejected before the operation runs, without an error envelope.

Modes:

- `create`: adds the packaged agent under its own identifier, together with its packaged chat sessions, execution runs, memory and metrics. Fails if an agent with that identifier exists.
- `replace-exact-version`: replaces the existing agent with the packaged identifier, whose current revision must equal `expectedAgentVersion`. Its chat sessions, execution runs, memory, metrics and other run records are deleted and replaced by the packaged ones.
- `clone`: adds only the packaged definition, under a new identifier, as a non-template agent with a new template key. No history is copied.

Provider and capability references are matched to this workspace by identifier or by a unique identity; unmatched ones are dropped and listed in the receipt's `unresolvedPrerequisites`. Secret references are always removed. Read the agent with `GET /api/agents/{agentId}` afterwards and configure what is missing. A rejected request imports nothing. An HTTP 500 can follow a completed import when the CRM/HR directory refresh after the save fails; resend the identical request with the same `Idempotency-Key` to receive the stored receipt.

Idempotency: repeating the request with the same `Idempotency-Key`, package, mode, external key and expected version returns the stored receipt with `replayed` true and imports nothing again; the same key with different values is rejected with `agent-package.idempotency-conflict`. The last 2048 imports of the workspace are remembered.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required. Client-chosen key of this import, 1 to 200 characters after trimming, compared exactly. Repeating the same request with the same key returns the stored receipt instead of importing again; reusing the key with different values is rejected with agent-package.idempotency-conflict.

requestBody.description: The multipart form: the package file part `package` and the import mode, external identity and optional preconditions as text fields.

200.description: The agent was replaced (`replace-exact-version`), or the request repeated an earlier import with the same `Idempotency-Key` (`replayed` is true and nothing was imported again). The body is the receipt.

201.description: A new agent was imported (`create` or `clone`). The body is the receipt; the `Location` header is `/api/agents/{agentId}` of the new agent.

400.description: Nothing was imported. The request is incomplete or invalid: `agent-package.file-required`, `agent-package.too-large`, `agent-package.mode-invalid`, `agent-package.idempotency-key-invalid` (missing, blank or longer than 200 characters), `agent-package.external-key-invalid`, `agent-package.external-identity-invalid` (namespace or key format) or `agent-package.expected-version-required`. Or the package is not acceptable: `agent-package.expected-hash-invalid`, `agent-package.hash-mismatch`, `agent-package.invalid-archive`, `agent-package.empty`, `agent-package.too-many-entries`, `agent-package.entry-not-allowed`, `agent-package.duplicate-entry`, `agent-package.symlink-not-allowed`, `agent-package.executable-not-allowed`, `agent-package.expanded-size-exceeded`, `agent-package.manifest-missing`, `agent-package.manifest-too-large`, `agent-package.manifest-invalid`, `agent-package.schema-version-unsupported`, `agent-package.raw-secret-material`, `agent-package.runtime-admission-not-portable` (a packaged run carries a tool admission journal) or `agent-package.agent-invalid` (the packaged agent has no identifier or name).

409.description: Nothing was imported because it conflicts with the workspace: `agent-package.idempotency-conflict` (the key was used with different values), `agent-package.external-key-conflict` (the external identity is already bound and this is not a `replace-exact-version` of that same agent), `agent-package.agent-already-exists` (`create` of an existing agent), `agent-package.agent-not-found` (`replace-exact-version` without an agent to replace) or `agent-package.template-key-conflict` (another agent uses the packaged template key).

412.description: Nothing was imported: `expectedAgentVersion` does not equal the current revision of the agent to replace (`agent-package.version-conflict`). Read the agent again and decide whether to replace it.

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: An authorization policy rejected the authenticated caller (`api.authorization-forbidden`). This operation itself requires only a valid bearer token.

get.summary: Read which agent an external identity (namespace and key) is bound to.
get.description:
Resolves a caller-defined external identity to the agent bound to it by `PUT /api/agents/by-external-key/{externalNamespace}/{key}` or by a package import (`POST /api/agents/import-package`), and returns the binding's configuration version, also as the quoted `ETag` response header. Send that value as `If-Match` with the next `PUT` or `DELETE` through this identity. Read the agent itself with `GET /api/agents/{agentId}`.

The namespace and key are trimmed and lowered before the lookup; each must then be 1 to 100 characters of lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, starting and ending with a letter or digit. Deleting the agent with `DELETE /api/agents/{agentId}` also removes its bindings.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: externalNamespace
parameters.description: Namespace of the external identity, chosen by the caller when provisioning (`package-import` for package imports without a namespace), for example `erp-sync`.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key of the external identity within the namespace, for example `invoice-assistant`.

200.description: The binding: the bound agent, the recorded configuration version (also in the `ETag` header), whether the agent is archived and when the binding last changed.

400.description: The namespace or key has an invalid format (`agents.external-key-invalid`).

404.description: No agent is bound to the identity in this workspace (`agents.external-key-not-found`), or the binding points to an agent that no longer exists (`agents.external-key-agent-not-found`).

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: An authorization policy rejected the authenticated caller (`api.authorization-forbidden`). This operation itself requires only a valid bearer token.

put.summary: Create or update the agent bound to an external identity, idempotently and with optimistic concurrency.
put.description:
Provisions an agent under a caller-defined external identity (namespace and key), so that an external system can manage it by its own key. When no agent is bound to the identity, a new agent is created and bound (HTTP 201). Otherwise the bound agent's configuration is replaced by the body (HTTP 200): the body is the complete desired configuration, not a patch, and omitted members take their default values. Use `POST /api/agents` to save an agent without an external identity.

The body has the shape that `POST /api/agents` accepts, with these rules: `id` and `expectedUpdatedAtUtc` must be omitted or null (the server owns the identity and revision); `name` must not be blank; `allowedSecretReferences` and `permissions.allowedSecrets` must be empty; `selectedCapabilityIds` and `tags` must not be null; `configurationJson` must be empty or valid JSON without raw secret values (a non-empty string `apiKey`, `accessToken`, `bearerToken`, `clientSecret`, `password`, `privateKey` or `refreshToken` member, also inside string members whose names end in `Json`). Capability identifiers that do not exist in the workspace are ignored.

Concurrency: omit `If-Match` when creating. When updating, send the configuration version from the last `GET` or receipt as `If-Match`; a missing or stale value is rejected with HTTP 412 and nothing is written. If the new configuration equals the recorded one, nothing is changed and the receipt's `warnings` say so. The response's `ETag` header carries the resulting configuration version in quotes.

Idempotency: `Idempotency-Key` is required. Repeating the same request (identity, `If-Match` and body) with the same key returns the stored receipt with `replayed` true and the original status, and writes nothing again; the same key with a different request is rejected with HTTP 409. Keys are shared with `DELETE` on this route, and the last 2048 writes of the workspace are remembered. An HTTP 500 can follow a stored change when the CRM/HR directory refresh after the save fails: resend the identical request with the same key to receive the stored receipt (the replay does not repeat the refresh).

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: externalNamespace
parameters.description: Namespace of the external identity, chosen by the caller, for example `erp-sync`. It is trimmed and lowered; it must then be 1 to 100 characters of lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Key of the external identity within the namespace, for example `invoice-assistant`, in the same format as the namespace.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required. Client-chosen key of this write, 1 to 200 characters after trimming, compared exactly. Repeating the same request with the same key returns the stored receipt; reusing the key for a different request, including a DELETE on this route, is rejected with agents.external-key-idempotency-conflict.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Configuration version the update is based on, from the ETag or configurationVersion of the last read or receipt: 64 hexadecimal digits, surrounding quotes allowed. Omit it when the identity is not bound yet; required when updating.

requestBody.description: The complete agent definition to store under this identity, following the rules above.

200.description: The bound agent was updated, or already had this configuration (see `warnings`), or the request repeated an earlier update (`replayed` true). The body is the receipt; the `ETag` header carries its configuration version.

201.description: A new agent was created and bound to the identity, or the request repeated that creation (`replayed` true). The `Location` header is this route with the normalized namespace and key; the `ETag` header carries the configuration version.

400.description: Nothing was written. The identity or headers are invalid (`agents.external-key-invalid`, `agents.external-key-idempotency-key-invalid` for a missing, blank or longer than 200 characters key, `agents.external-key-version-invalid` for an `If-Match` that is not 64 hexadecimal digits), or the body breaks a rule above (`agents.external-key-agent-invalid`, `agents.external-key-server-identity-only`, `agents.external-key-secret-reference-forbidden`, `agents.external-key-configuration-json-invalid`, `agents.external-key-secret-material-forbidden`). A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no error envelope.

409.description: Nothing was written: the `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a different request (`agents.external-key-idempotency-conflict`), the binding points to an agent that no longer exists (`agents.external-key-agent-missing`), or the definition breaks an agent rule, for example a template key that another agent uses, an unsupported thinking-effort override or a model without a price row on its provider profile (`agents.external-key-configuration-conflict`, explained in the message).

412.description: Nothing was written: `If-Match` was sent for an identity that is not bound yet (`agents.external-key-create-version-conflict`), is missing for a bound identity (`agents.external-key-version-required`) or is stale (`agents.external-key-version-conflict`). Read the binding again, then decide whether to reapply the change.

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: An authorization policy rejected the authenticated caller (`api.authorization-forbidden`). This operation itself requires only a valid bearer token.

delete.summary: Archive the agent bound to an external identity.
delete.description:
Changes the status of the agent bound to the external identity to archived. The agent, its history and the binding are kept: `GET` on this route still resolves it, with `isArchived` true, and a later `PUT` can change its status again. To remove an agent permanently use `DELETE /api/agents/{agentId}`, which also removes its bindings.

`If-Match` is required and must equal the binding's current configuration version; a missing or stale value is rejected with HTTP 412 and nothing is written. The response's `ETag` header carries the configuration version after archiving. Archiving an agent that is already archived succeeds again and keeps the same configuration version.

Idempotency: `Idempotency-Key` is required. Repeating the same request (identity and `If-Match`) with the same key returns the stored receipt with `replayed` true and writes nothing again; the same key with a different request is rejected with HTTP 409. Keys are shared with `PUT` on this route. An HTTP 500 can follow a stored change when the CRM/HR directory refresh after the save fails: resend the identical request with the same key to receive the stored receipt (the replay does not repeat the refresh).

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required. Client-chosen key of this archive request, 1 to 200 characters after trimming, compared exactly. Repeating the same request with the same key returns the stored receipt; reusing the key for a different request, including a PUT on this route, is rejected with agents.external-key-idempotency-conflict.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Required. Current configuration version of the binding, from the ETag or configurationVersion of the last read or receipt: 64 hexadecimal digits, surrounding quotes allowed.

200.description: The agent is archived. The receipt has `archived` true and the configuration version, also in the `ETag` header; `replayed` is true for a repeated request.

400.description: Nothing was written: the namespace or key has an invalid format (`agents.external-key-invalid`), the `Idempotency-Key` is missing, blank or longer than 200 characters (`agents.external-key-idempotency-key-invalid`), or `If-Match` is not 64 hexadecimal digits (`agents.external-key-version-invalid`).

get.summary: List all agent teams of the current workspace, ordered by name.
get.description:
An agent team is a named group of agent definitions used to organize agents; an agent can belong to several teams. A team does not grant capabilities or tools and does not change how its member agents run. Teams are returned in case-insensitive name order, each with its member agent identifiers. Use a team's `id` with the other `/api/agents/teams/{teamId}` operations.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: Every team of the workspace; an empty array when none exist.

post.summary: Create an agent team, or replace the team whose identifier the body carries.
post.description:
With `id` null or omitted the server creates a team with a new identifier. With an `id` the stored team with that identifier is replaced (its creation time is kept); if none exists, a team is created with that identifier. Prefer `PUT /api/agents/teams/{teamId}` for updates so the identifier comes from the route. There is no concurrency check: the last save wins.

The name is trimmed and must be non-blank and unique among teams, ignoring case. The description is trimmed. An icon outside the supported set becomes `groups`. Member agent identifiers must name existing agents; empty identifiers and duplicates are dropped, and members are stored in agent-name order.

These validation failures (blank or duplicate name, unknown agent) are not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500 and nothing is saved.

A success does not always mean the values were kept: teams shipped with the product are reset to their shipped content on every catalog write, and a team sent with the all-zero identifier is discarded. Read the team back with `GET /api/agents/teams/{teamId}` to confirm the stored result.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The complete team to store.

200.description: The team was saved. The body is the team identifier as a JSON string (a GUID); read the team to see the stored values.

Returns the stored team. To edit it, read `GET /api/agents/teams/{teamId}/editor` and save the changed form with `PUT /api/agents/teams/{teamId}`; to see the member agents' definitions, use `GET /api/agents/teams/{teamId}/agents`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

put.summary: Replace an agent team's name, description, icon and members.
put.description:
Stores the body as the complete team, using the route identifier and ignoring any `id` in the body. If no team has this identifier, a team is created with it. Every member is replaced by `agentIds`; to change only the members, use `PUT /api/agents/teams/{teamId}/members`. There is no concurrency check: the last save wins.

The name is trimmed and must be non-blank and unique among teams, ignoring case. An icon outside the supported set becomes `groups`. Member agent identifiers must name existing agents; empty identifiers and duplicates are dropped. These validation failures are not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500 and nothing is saved.

Teams shipped with the product are reset to their shipped content on every catalog write, so changes to them report success but are not kept; the all-zero identifier is likewise discarded. Read the team back to confirm the stored result.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

Removes the team record only; the member agent definitions, their runs and their memberships in other teams are unchanged. Deleting an identifier that does not exist also succeeds, so a repeated delete is harmless. Teams shipped with the product are restored by the same catalog write, so deleting one reports success but the team remains.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

Returns the team's name, description, icon and member agent identifiers in the shape expected by `PUT /api/agents/teams/{teamId}` and `POST /api/agents/teams`. The team save operations have no concurrency check: the last save wins.

An unknown team identifier is not translated into the error envelope; the request fails with a generic HTTP 500. Use `GET /api/agents/teams/{teamId}` first when you need a 404 for a missing team.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: The editable form of the team.

get.description:
Returns the full definitions of the team's member agents in case-insensitive agent-name order, the same shape as `GET /api/agents`. Template agents are members like any other agent but are left out unless `includeTemplates` is true, so a team of templates can yield an empty array. The team and the agents are read separately, so a concurrent change can make the result differ from the team's `agentIds`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

Behaves exactly like `PUT /api/agents/teams/{teamId}/members`: the team's members become the agents in `agentIds`, and agents not listed are removed from the team. This is a replacement, not an append; an empty list leaves the team without members. The team's name, description and icon are unchanged, and the member agents themselves are not modified.

Every identifier must name an existing agent; empty identifiers and duplicates are dropped, and members are stored in agent-name order. An unknown team or agent is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500 and the team is unchanged.

Teams shipped with the product are reset to their shipped members on every catalog write; for them the response shows the requested members although the stored team keeps its shipped members. Read the team back to confirm.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

post.summary: Check whether an unconfirmed provider-profile write took effect.
post.description:
Use it after a provider operation answered HTTP 409 with code `agents.provider-write-unconfirmed`: send that response's `attempt` object unchanged as the body. The server compares the receipt with the stored provider profile and reports `Committed`, `DefinitelyNotCommitted` or `StillUnconfirmed`. The check only reads: it never repeats or undoes the write, and it can be called again.

Next step: after `Committed`, read the profile with `GET /api/agents/providers/{providerId}/editor` and continue from its stored state; after `DefinitelyNotCommitted`, read the profile and submit the intended change again if it is still wanted; after `StillUnconfirmed`, verify again later instead of writing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The receipt from the unconfirmed-write response, unchanged.

200.description: The verification result. It reflects the stored profile at the time of the check and is never cached.

400.description: The receipt has an all-zero `attemptId` or `providerId` or an undefined `kind` (`agents.provider-receipt-invalid`). The body has `code` and `message` members, not the `errors` envelope. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without this body.

get.summary: List the model provider profiles that agents can use.
get.description:
A provider profile is a configured connection to a model provider (OpenAI-compatible, Azure OpenAI, Ollama or ComfyUI) that an agent references through `providerProfileId`; the model an agent uses is a separate string within the profile. Returns every local profile, enabled or not, and every profile imported from a shared provider source (`isSourceManaged` true), including imports that are currently unavailable (`isEnabled` false, `healthStatus` naming the reason), ordered by name. A built-in fallback profile for a remote Ollama server is included unless the host disables it. Publishing a local profile to other hosts (a shared-provider publication) is managed elsewhere and is not shown here.

API keys are never returned: `apiKeyEnvironmentVariable` holds at most a reference to a stored secret. The stored `configurationJson` is returned as saved apart from that reference.

A profile that cannot be read makes the whole list fail with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: The provider profiles.

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: Only when API authorization is enabled and an authenticated token is refused by an operation policy (`api.authorization-forbidden`). This operation accepts any valid token, so it does not currently return this status.

post.summary: Create a provider profile, or replace a local one using the concurrency token the caller last read.
post.description:
To create a profile, send `id` null (the server assigns one) or a new identifier, with `expectedConcurrencyToken` null; send the all-zero GUID as `expectedConcurrencyToken` instead to make the create fail with HTTP 409 when a profile with that `id` already exists. To update one, read `GET /api/agents/providers/{providerId}/editor`, change what you intend to change and send the whole form with its `expectedConcurrencyToken`; a stale token is rejected with HTTP 409. Profiles imported from a shared provider source cannot be saved.

The server checks the kind, transport and purpose (Ollama requires the ChatCompletions transport), the name (not blank), the base URL (an absolute http or https URL without user information, query or fragment), the credential reference (`apiKeyEnvironmentVariable` is empty or `secret:` followed by the identifier of a stored secret; OpenAI and Azure OpenAI profiles require one), `configurationJson` (a JSON object), the model prices and the thinking-effort capabilities. A blank default model becomes the connector's default model. `notes`, `preferFrameworkManagedChatHistory` and `supportsBackgroundResponses` are not stored.

HTTP 200 means the profile is stored, including when only the follow-up reconciliation after the commit failed (header `CDA-Provider-Outcome: committed-reconciliation-pending`); do not send it again. When the outcome of the write is unknown, HTTP 409 carries an unconfirmed-write receipt instead of the `errors` envelope: code `agents.provider-write-unconfirmed`, members `providerId`, `attempt`, `automaticReplaySafe` (false), `verificationPath` and `message`, and the header `CDA-Provider-Outcome: unconfirmed-verification-required`. Send `attempt` to `POST /api/agents/providers/mutations/verify` before any retry.

Some invalid thinking-effort capability entries and over-long model lists are not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500 before anything is written.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The complete provider profile form.

200.description: The profile is stored. The body is the provider profile identifier as a JSON string (a GUID).

400.description: Nothing was saved (`agents.provider-request-invalid`): a validation rule failed, the identifier is the all-zero GUID, or the profile is imported from a shared provider source. The response does not say which rule failed. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without an envelope.

409.description: The profile changed since it was read, or a profile with the requested identifier exists although the create demanded none (`agents.provider-concurrency-conflict`): read the editor again and reapply the change. Or the outcome is unknown and the body is an unconfirmed-write receipt (code `agents.provider-write-unconfirmed`) to verify first.

get.summary: Read a provider profile as the editable form accepted by `POST /api/agents/providers`.
get.description:
Returns the profile's settings together with `expectedConcurrencyToken`, the token to send back when saving a change. Profiles imported from a shared provider source can be read here but cannot be saved.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: providerId
parameters.description: Identifier of the provider profile, as returned by `GET /api/agents/providers`.

200.description: The editable form of the profile, including its concurrency token.

404.description: No provider profile has this identifier, or the link of an imported profile to its source is broken (`agents.provider-not-found`).

503.description: The profile is imported from a shared provider source and its import is retired (`agents.provider-unavailable`).

delete.description:
Deletes the profile. Agents that referenced it keep their definitions but lose the reference (`providerProfileId` becomes null), so their runs fail until another profile is selected. A profile that is or ever was published as a shared provider, or that is imported from a shared provider source, cannot be deleted. Deleting an identifier that does not exist also succeeds.

HTTP 200 is also returned when only the follow-up reconciliation after the delete failed (header `CDA-Provider-Outcome: committed-reconciliation-pending`). When the outcome is unknown, HTTP 409 carries an unconfirmed-write receipt (see `POST /api/agents/providers`) to send to `POST /api/agents/providers/mutations/verify` before any retry.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: providerId
parameters.description: Identifier of the provider profile to delete.

200.description: The profile no longer exists (it was deleted or never existed). The body is `{ "ok": true }`.

409.description: The profile was not deleted because it is referenced by a shared-provider publication or import (`agents.provider-reference-conflict`) or changed concurrently (`agents.provider-concurrency-conflict`); or the outcome of the delete is unknown and the body is an unconfirmed-write receipt (code `agents.provider-write-unconfirmed`) to verify first.

post.summary: Run a health check against a provider profile and store the result on the profile.
post.description:
Calls the provider with the profile's connection settings, for example by listing its models and sending a short chat request (which the provider may bill) for an OpenAI-compatible chat profile, or by listing the models and sending a chat request to an Ollama server. Local profiles are tested even when disabled, and the result is stored on the profile: `healthStatus` becomes Healthy or Unhealthy, `lastCheckedAtUtc` is set, the suggested models are replaced by the discovered ones and, for Ollama, discovered thinking-effort capabilities are stored. Storing the result changes the profile's concurrency token. Profiles imported from a shared provider source are checked without storing anything, and an unavailable import reports a failure without calling it.

A provider that answers with an error yields HTTP 200 with `success` false. The check is recorded in the provider request history as a diagnostic.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: providerId
parameters.description: Identifier of the provider profile to test.

200.description: The check finished; `success` tells whether the provider answered as expected. For a local profile the result is stored.

202.description: The result was stored, but the follow-up reconciliation did not finish (header `CDA-Provider-Outcome: committed-reconciliation-pending`). The check result itself is not returned; read the profile list for the stored health.

400.description: The result could not be stored because the stored profile no longer passes validation, for example because its secret was deleted (`agents.provider-request-invalid`).

404.description: No provider profile has this identifier (`agents.provider-not-found`).

409.description: Storing the result conflicted with a concurrent change (`agents.provider-concurrency-conflict`), or its outcome is unknown and the body is an unconfirmed-write receipt (code `agents.provider-write-unconfirmed`, kind 3 HealthPersistence) to verify with `POST /api/agents/providers/mutations/verify`.

502.description: The health check itself could not be completed (`agents.provider-diagnostic-unavailable`); nothing was stored.

post.summary: Send a test chat request through a provider profile and return the model's reply.
post.description:
Sends the system prompt, the earlier messages and the prompt to the provider with the profile's settings and returns the reply. It involves no agent, chat session or execution run. The call is a real provider request that the provider may bill; it does not change the profile, but it is recorded in the provider request history with the HTTP caller as the requester.

The model defaults to the profile's default model, then its first suggested model. A request without prompt and messages, a provider error or timeout, a provider that cannot chat (ComfyUI) or a model not published by a shared provider is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: providerId
parameters.description: Identifier of the provider profile to use.

requestBody.description: The conversation to send.

200.description: The provider's reply, the model used and the token counts it reported.

404.description: No provider profile has this identifier (`agents.provider-not-found`).

503.description: The profile is disabled or its shared provider import is unavailable (`llm-chat.provider-unavailable`).

post.summary: Create or update a model on an Ollama server and make it the provider profile's default model.
post.description:
Asks the profile's Ollama server to create the model `targetModel` from `baseModel` with the given system prompt and context length (the equivalent of an Ollama Modelfile), then updates the profile: its default model becomes `targetModel`, the model is added to the suggested models and `healthStatus` shows the server's status message. The model is created on the server before the profile is updated, so a failure of the profile update leaves the model in place.

Only local Ollama profiles are supported. Missing values, a context length outside 2048 to 262144 and profiles of another kind are not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: providerId
parameters.description: Identifier of a local Ollama provider profile.

requestBody.description: The model to create and its settings.

200.description: The model was created or updated and the profile updated. The body describes the model.

202.description: The model was created and the profile update stored, but the follow-up reconciliation did not finish (header `CDA-Provider-Outcome: committed-reconciliation-pending`).

400.description: The profile is imported from a shared provider source, or the updated profile does not pass validation (`agents.provider-request-invalid`).

404.description: No provider profile has this identifier (`agents.provider-not-found`).

409.description: The profile update conflicted with a concurrent change (`agents.provider-concurrency-conflict`), or its outcome is unknown and the body is an unconfirmed-write receipt (code `agents.provider-write-unconfirmed`, kind 4 ModelMaintenancePersistence) to verify first. The model already exists on the server.

503.description: The profile is disabled (`agents.provider-unavailable`).

get.summary: List the capability catalog of the current workspace.
get.description:
Returns every catalog capability, the ones shipped with the product and the custom ones, ordered by kind (McpServer, Skill, Tool, Plugin, Rag, AiContext) and then by name, without paging. A catalog capability is a declaration only: it reaches an agent when it is selected in the agent's `selectedCapabilityIds` (`POST /api/agents`), and even then each run attaches tools only as the runtime's permissions and invocation policy allow. The proof fields are catalog-level results of the latest verification.

Each item includes its `configurationJson` exactly as stored, without redaction.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: The catalog capabilities.

post.summary: Create a catalog capability, or replace one using the fingerprint the caller last read.
post.description:
Create: send `id` and `expectedFingerprint` as null; the server assigns the identifier. Update: read `GET /api/agents/capabilities/{capabilityId}/editor`, change the members you intend to change, and send the whole form with its `id` and `expectedFingerprint`. With a fingerprint the save is rejected when the stored capability changed since the read; without one the update overwrites without a check. The proof fields are kept. Changing the kind or key also updates every agent's assignment of the capability and advances those agents' revisions.

The key is normalized (letters and digits lower-cased, other characters collapsed to hyphens) and must be unique per kind. Name, description and endpoint are trimmed; tags are trimmed, lower-cased and de-duplicated. The kind Memory is retired and rejected. Skill configuration must be a JSON object; the configuration of other kinds is stored as sent and is not validated.

Every rejection, including a fingerprint mismatch, an unknown `id`, a fingerprint sent on create, a duplicate key or a null text member, is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500 and nothing is saved. Capabilities shipped with the product are restored to their shipped definition when the catalog is written, so edits to them can report success without being kept. Read the editor form again after every save.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The complete capability form.

200.description: The save completed. The body is the capability identifier as a JSON string (a GUID); read the editor form for the stored values and the new fingerprint.

get.summary: Read a catalog capability as the editable form accepted by `POST /api/agents/capabilities`.
get.description:
Returns the capability's definition together with `expectedFingerprint`, the concurrency fingerprint to send back when saving a change. The form carries no proof fields; read them from `GET /api/agents/capabilities`.

An unknown capability identifier is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

Removes the capability from the catalog and its assignment from every agent, advancing those agents' revisions; assignments do not block the delete. Deleting an identifier that does not exist succeeds, so a repeated delete is harmless. Capabilities shipped with the product are restored by the same catalog write, so deleting one reports success but it remains.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

post.summary: Run the verification diagnostic for a capability assigned to an agent and publish its proof.
post.description:
Checks that the capability is assigned exactly once to the agent, runs the capability's local proof checks with the agent's current provider profile (for an HTTP endpoint this includes a GET request with a 10 second timeout), and, when the agent, the capability and the provider did not change meanwhile, stores the proof (status, notes and check time) on the agent's capability assignment and on the catalog capability. The diagnostic invokes no runtime tool and grants nothing: attaching tools to runs stays governed by the runtime.

HTTP 200 means the proof was published, not that it passed: read `GET /api/agents` (with `includeTemplates=true` for a template) and inspect the agent's entry in `capabilities`, whose `proofStatus` can be Failed. Publishing advances the agent's `updatedAtUtc` revision, so an agent editor form read before the verification is stale.

Failures return a `CapabilityVerificationApiResponse`, not the general `errors` envelope. Its `automaticReplaySafe` is always false: do not retry automatically. After `Unconfirmed` the proof may already be stored; read the agent before deciding whether to verify again as a new, deliberate request.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Identifier of the agent whose capability assignment is verified.

parameters.name: capabilityId
parameters.description: Identifier of the catalog capability assigned to the agent.

200.description: The proof was published on the agent's assignment and on the catalog capability. The body is `{ "ok": true }`; read the agent to see the proof status, which can be Failed.

400.description: Outcome `Rejected`: the agent or capability does not exist, the capability is not assigned exactly once to the agent, or the agent's provider profile cannot be resolved. No diagnostic ran and nothing was written.

409.description: No proof was published. Outcomes: `InfrastructureUnavailable` (the catalog or provider state could not be read), `DiagnosticInterrupted` (the diagnostic failed), `Superseded` (the agent, capability or provider changed during the diagnostic), `PublicationNotStarted` (the catalog could not be read after the diagnostic), `Unconfirmed` (the publication write failed and may or may not be stored), `CanceledBeforeDiagnostic` or `PublicationCanceled` (the request was cancelled). Read the agent before deciding whether to verify again.

post.summary: Test a tool capability definition by calling the external process or HTTP endpoint it describes once.
post.description:
Validates the tool definition in `capability` and then calls it once with `jsonInput`: it starts the configured process on the server host with the input on standard input, or sends the input as the body of a request to the configured HTTP endpoint. The definition does not have to be saved, nothing is written to the catalog, and the tool's output is not returned; the result reports success and diagnostics only.

This runs the configured command or request from the server, with the server's identity and network access. The executable allow-list defaults to the command's own file name. Keep API authorization enabled on any host this operation can be reached on, and test only definitions you trust.

The tool is read from `capability.configurationJson`: `toolKind` (`externalProcess`, the default, or `externalHttp`); for a process `externalProcess.command` (required), `arguments`, `workingDirectory`, `allowedExecutableNames`, `timeoutSeconds` (default 30) and `maxOutputBytes` (default 4096); for HTTP `externalHttp.endpoint` (an absolute URL), `method` (default POST), `headers`, `timeoutSeconds` and `maxResponseBytes`. The capability kind in the request is ignored, and secret bindings and secret-bearing arguments are rejected.

Invalid definitions and failed calls are reported in the result's `diagnostics` with HTTP 200. An empty `jsonInput`, a null `capability` or `tags`, or an invalid HTTP method is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The tool definition to test and the input to send.

200.description: The test finished: `isSuccess` tells whether the call succeeded, and `diagnostics` explain a failure.

post.summary: Test an MCP server capability definition by starting or connecting to the server and listing its tools.
post.description:
Validates the MCP server definition in `capability`, then starts the local server process (stdio transport) or connects to the remote endpoint (HTTP transport), performs the MCP handshake, lists the server's tools, checks them against the definition's allowed tools and stops. The definition does not have to be saved and nothing is written to the catalog.

This starts a process on the server host or connects from it. A local server command must be one of `dotnet`, `node`, `npx`, `powershell`, `pwsh`, `python`, `python3`, `uv` or `uvx`, and header bindings of a remote server are resolved from the server's environment variables and sent to the configured endpoint. Keep API authorization enabled on any host this operation can be reached on, and test only definitions you trust.

The server is read from `capability.configurationJson`: `transport` (`stdio` for a local process; `http`, `sse` or `remote-http` for a remote server; when absent, a `command` implies stdio and an `endpoint` implies HTTP), `command`, `arguments`, `workingDirectory`, `endpoint`, `allowedTools` (required for stdio), `approvalMode` (`NeverRequire` or `AlwaysRequire`; required for stdio), `timeoutSeconds` and `headerBindings`. Raw environment variables and raw headers are rejected. The capability kind in the request is ignored.

Invalid definitions and connection or listing failures are reported in the result's `diagnostics` with HTTP 200. Other failures, such as an out-of-range timeout, are not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500 and the started server may not be stopped.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The MCP server definition to test.

200.description: The test finished: `isSuccess`, the discovered and allowed tools, diagnostics and whether the server was stopped cleanly.

post.summary: Preview which capabilities an access policy would allow, without saving anything.
post.description:
Builds the candidate capabilities from saved catalog capabilities (`capabilityIds`, or all of them when empty) and unsaved `draftCapabilities`, compiles `policy`, evaluates it against the candidates and the `requiredCapabilities`, and returns which candidates would be allowed with the reasons for those that are suppressed. It reads the catalog and writes nothing. It previews the policy only; it does not describe what a particular agent run will receive.

Evaluation: a matching Deny rule wins; with the default effect DenyAll, a candidate needs a matching Allow or Require rule; a Require rule that matches no candidate produces a diagnostic. When any candidate or the policy is invalid, `validationResult` lists the issues, the effective set is empty and no row is allowed; with an empty `capabilityIds` a single invalid saved capability therefore invalidates the whole preview.

Note the two capability kind numberings in one request: `draftCapabilities[].kind` uses the catalog kind (2 is Tool), while `requiredCapabilities[].kind` uses the identity kind (1 is Tool).

A null list in the request is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500; send empty arrays instead.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: Candidates, the policy to evaluate and the required capabilities.

200.description: The preview: validation issues, the effective allowed set and one row per candidate.

get.description:
Returns the agent's workspace memory notes, which are simple title and content records kept in the agent catalog. They are not the memory providers configured through the agent's `memoryAccess` settings or `/api/memory-providers`, and they are not injected into agent runs: the runtime lists them only as an excluded context source. An agent without notes, or an unknown agent identifier, yields an empty array.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

post.summary: Create a workspace memory note for an agent, or replace the note whose identifier the body carries.
post.description:
With `id` null or omitted a new note is created with a new identifier; with an `id` the note with that identifier is replaced as a whole (its creation time is kept) or, if none exists, created with it. There is no concurrency check, and a replacement may move the note to another agent. Text members are trimmed; kind, importance and metadata are stored as sent without further validation. The note is not injected into agent runs (see `GET /api/agents/{agentId}/memory`).

Notes shipped with the product (source `seed`) are restored whenever they are missing, so changing the title or source of such a note leaves the shipped note next to the changed copy.

A note for an agent that does not exist (including an omitted `agentId`), or a null text member, is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

Removes the note with this identifier. Deleting an identifier that does not exist also succeeds, so a repeated delete is harmless. Notes shipped with the product (source `seed`) are restored by the same catalog write, so deleting one reports success but the note remains. Memory held by memory providers is not affected.

Sending a message without a session (`POST /api/agents/{agentId}/chat`) also creates one, so this operation is only needed to prepare a session in advance.

The session named by `preferredSessionId` is selected when it exists and belongs to the agent; otherwise the most recently updated session is selected. post.summary: Send a prompt to an agent in a chat session and wait for the agent's reply.
post.description:
Starts a chat-backed agent execution run: the prompt is added to the session transcript, the agent runs with the session history, and the request returns when the run completes, fails or stops to wait for tool approvals. Without `chatSessionId` a new session is created and titled from the prompt. A chat session is not an execution run: every message starts its own run in the session. To run the agent without a transcript, or with a structured-output contract, use `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/execution-runs`; to receive progress events in the response itself, use `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/chat/stream`.

Tool calls that need approval stop the run with `state` 3 WaitingOnTool; approve or reject them with `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/pending-approvals`. Only the agent's own automatic approval setting applies here. Sending a message grants no tools: the agent's permissions, capabilities, access settings and the runtime policy decide which tools the run receives.

Each command is admitted as an activity operation, identified by `activityOperationId` or a server-generated identifier and returned in the `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` response header. Progress can be followed with `GET /api/agents/execution-operations/{operationId}/events/stream` while the request runs (it answers 404 until the operation is admitted). The identifier is not an idempotency key: use a new one for every attempt.

The request waits for the run; cancelling the request cancels the run, which is then stored as failed with the outcome Cancelled. After any response, read `GET /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}` for the stored state and evidence. An unknown agent or session, a session of another agent, a session that is busy with another run, an agent without a usable provider profile or an invalid attachment is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

post.summary: Continue an interrupted agent execution run in place from its saved original input.
post.description:
Recovery continues the same execution run, after re-checking current permissions, from the original input the server saved when the run was admitted. It does not start a new conversation or a new run, and it never repeats a tool call whose outcome is unknown. Only runs started from the product's chat page or by governed process steps can be recovered: runs started through this HTTP API keep no recovery record and are rejected with HTTP 400 `tool-admission.legacy-run`.

The server rechecks the run and the current authority before resuming. A run that waits for approvals, was cancelled, still has effects to reconcile, belongs to an agent that is no longer Active, or whose authority or context changed is rejected with HTTP 400 and a `tool-admission.` code. A cancelled run needs `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/reconcile-cancellation` first; pending approvals are answered with `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/pending-approvals`. A completed run returns its stored result after a read-authority check.

The command is admitted as an activity operation (`activityOperationId` or a server-generated identifier, returned in the `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` header; follow it with `GET /api/agents/execution-operations/{operationId}/events/stream`). Use a new identifier for every attempt. An unknown run identifier is not translated into the error envelope and fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the exact `api` scope; tokens with only other scopes are refused. With authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

Or the resumed run failed because the provider rejected the request as incompatible (`agents.provider-request-incompatible`).
