post.summary: Determine, from owner receipts, which tool effects of a cancelled agent execution run took place.
post.description:
For a run whose outcome is Cancelled, examines every tool call the run proposed: calls that were never sent had no effect, read-only calls changed nothing, and for sent calls the owning service's receipt is read where the tool offers one. A confirmed receipt records the effect as committed; without one the effect stays unknown, because a transaction started earlier could still commit. The operation runs no tool and calls no model provider; it only records the resolution and adds a log entry. It does not undo effects.

Use the response to decide what needs manual follow-up: `hasUnknownEffects` true means at least one effect could not be confirmed either way. Only runs with a recoverable tool-admission journal (runs admitted by the interactive chat interface or by governed process steps) can be reconciled; other runs are rejected with HTTP 400 `tool-admission.legacy-run`, and a run that was not cancelled with `tool-admission.denied`.

The command is admitted as an activity operation (`activityOperationId` or a server-generated identifier, returned in the `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` header). Use a new identifier for every attempt. An unknown run identifier is not translated into the error envelope and fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the exact `api` scope; tokens with only other scopes are refused. With authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

post.summary: Approve or reject the pending tool calls of an agent execution run and continue the run.
post.description:
Read the run's pending approvals first (`GET /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/approvals` or the run detail) and then send exactly one decision per pending approval in `decisions`. A set with a missing, unknown or repeated approval identifier is rejected (`agents.approval-decision-mismatch`) and nothing is decided. When `decisions` is omitted or empty, the single value `approved` is applied to every approval pending when the request is handled. The decisions are recorded, the run continues with the approved calls executed and the rejected ones refused, and the request returns when the run completes, fails or stops for new approvals.

`autoApprovePendingToolCalls` true, together with approving every pending call, also approves later approval requests of this run automatically; any rejection clears that setting. A run with nothing pending returns its stored result unchanged when it is completed or failed, and ignores the decisions.

The command is admitted as an activity operation (`activityOperationId` or a server-generated identifier, returned in the `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` header; follow it with `GET /api/agents/execution-operations/{operationId}/events/stream`). Use a new identifier for every attempt; `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/pending-approvals/stream` streams the progress instead. An unknown run, a run that is already being continued, or a run with nothing pending that is neither completed nor failed is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open. Approving a call here does not widen the agent's tool access; the call still runs under the run's policy.

post.summary: Start an agent execution run for the agent named in the body and wait for its result.
post.description:
Runs the agent on `prompt` as a new agent execution run and returns when the run completes, fails or stops to wait for tool approvals. Without `chatSessionId` the run has no chat transcript (no assistant message is stored); with it, the run is added to that existing session of the agent. An agent execution run is not a workflow run or a process run. `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/execution-runs` is the same operation with the agent in the route, and `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/stream` streams progress instead of waiting.

Optional `structuredOutput` asks the model for JSON that matches a JSON Schema; the result then carries the parsed data and its validation status, and output that fails validation ends the run as Failed with HTTP 200. `context` labels the run's origin for later filtering (see `GET /api/agents/execution-runs`). `autoApprovePendingToolCalls` true runs tool calls that would need approval without asking.

Tool calls that need approval stop the run with `state` 3 WaitingOnTool; answer them with `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/pending-approvals`. Starting a run grants no tools: the agent's permissions, capabilities, access settings and the runtime policy decide which tools it receives.

The command is admitted as an activity operation (`activityOperationId` or a server-generated identifier, returned in the `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` header; follow it with `GET /api/agents/execution-operations/{operationId}/events/stream`). It is not an idempotency key: use a new identifier for every attempt. Cancelling the request cancels the run, which is then stored as failed with the outcome Cancelled. After any response, read `GET /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}`.

An unknown agent or session, a session of another agent, a session busy with another run or waiting for approvals, an agent without a usable provider profile, an invalid attachment or an inconsistent `context` for process steps is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

Or the run failed because the provider rejected the request as incompatible (`agents.provider-request-incompatible`; the body names the run).

Returns the agent execution runs that match every given filter, ordered by last update (newest first) and limited to `Take` results; there is no paging cursor, so narrow the filters or the time range to see older runs. Text filters match the stored value exactly, ignoring case; time ranges include their bounds. Without filters, the most recently updated runs of all agents are returned. For one agent's runs you can also use `GET /api/agents/{agentId}/execution-runs`.

The items are summaries; read `GET /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}` for the log, metrics, approvals, artifacts, checkpoints and tool receipts of a run.

post.summary: Start an agent execution run for the agent in the route and wait for its result.
post.description:
Same operation as `POST /api/agents/execution-runs`, with the agent taken from the route instead of the body: runs the agent on `prompt` as a new agent execution run and returns when the run completes, fails or stops for tool approvals. Without `chatSessionId` the run has no chat transcript; with it, the run is added to that existing session of the agent. `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/execution-runs/stream` streams progress instead of waiting.

Optional `structuredOutput` asks for JSON that matches a JSON Schema; output that fails validation ends the run as Failed with HTTP 200. Tool calls that need approval stop the run with `state` 3 WaitingOnTool; answer them with `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/pending-approvals`. Starting a run grants no tools.

The command is admitted as an activity operation (`activityOperationId` or a server-generated identifier, returned in the `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` header; follow it with `GET /api/agents/execution-operations/{operationId}/events/stream`). Use a new identifier for every attempt. Cancelling the request cancels the run. An unknown agent or session, a busy session, an agent without a usable provider profile or an invalid attachment is not translated into the error envelope: the request fails with a generic HTTP 500.

get.summary: Stream the retained activity of an agent execution operation as server-sent events.
get.description:
Opens a `text/event-stream` response that replays and then follows the activity of one agent execution operation: a chat message, an execution run, an approval response, a recovery or a cancellation reconciliation started through the `/api/agents` operations. Use it to follow an operation from another connection or to catch up after a dropped connection; the streaming commands (the `POST` operations under `/api/agents` whose route ends with `/stream`) already deliver the same activity events. The operation identifier is the `activityOperationId` sent with the command or, when none was sent, the value of the command's `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` response header.

Activity is held only in the memory of this server process, for the current database profile: at most the last 256 events of each operation, kept for up to 10 minutes after the operation finished (less when many other operations finish in the meantime). It is not a durable record: read the execution run for results.

To resume, send the `id` of the last event received in the `Last-Event-ID` header or in the `after` query parameter (a non-negative integer; each at most once; when both are sent they must be equal). Only events with a larger `id` follow. Without a cursor the stream starts at the first retained event, after a `stream.gap` when earlier events were already discarded.

Events; each `data:` line is one JSON object with camel-case members and camel-case string enum values:

- `agent.activity`, `agent.approval.waiting`, `agent.activity.completed`, `agent.activity.failed` and `agent.activity.cancelled`: one activity, with `id:` set to its sequence number (1 for the first activity of the operation). Data: `operationId`; `phase` (`accepted`, `capturingContext`, `resolvingPreparation`, `resolvingProvider`, `resolvingSession`, `creatingExecution`, `preparingInput`, `preparingCapabilities`, `preparingRuntime`, `waitingForProvider`, `streaming`, `usingTool`, `awaitingApproval`, `persistingResult`, `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`); `occurredAtUtc`; `agentId`; `message` (human-readable progress text, at most 2048 characters); `chatSessionId` and `executionRunId` (null until known); `terminalOutcome` (`succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `suspended`; null before the last activity); `errorCode` (only on failure, for example `agent-execution-unhandled`).
- `stream.gap`: events between the cursor and the oldest retained event were discarded. Data: `operationId`, `requestedFromInclusive` and `availableFromInclusive`. Its `id:` is the sequence just before the oldest retained event, which follows.
- `stream.evicted`: the finished operation's events were discarded. Data: `operationId`, `reason` (`terminalRetentionExpired`, `terminalCapacityExceeded` or `partitionCapacityPressure`) and `evictedAtUtc`. Nothing follows.

While no event arrives, a comment line `: heartbeat` followed by a UTC timestamp is sent every heartbeat interval (15 seconds by default). The server ends the response after the activity whose `terminalOutcome` is set (`suspended` means the run waits for tool approval) or after `stream.evicted`; a cursor at or after the last activity of a finished operation gives an empty stream. If the connection closes before that, reconnect with the last `id` received or read the execution run. This stream never carries the command's result or failure details: read them with `GET /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; the stream is not limited to the caller that started the operation. Reading it does not change the operation.

parameters.name: operationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the agent execution operation (not the empty GUID): the `activityOperationId` sent with the command or the value of its `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` response header.

200.description: The `text/event-stream` of the operation's activity described above. It stays open until the operation reaches its last activity or the client disconnects.

400.description: Rejected before streaming: the empty GUID as operation identifier (`agents.execution-operation-invalid`), a malformed, repeated or conflicting cursor (`sse.cursor-invalid`), or the largest 64-bit integer as cursor (`sse.cursor-exhausted`).

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: An authorization policy rejected the authenticated caller (`api.authorization-forbidden`). This operation itself requires only a valid bearer token.

404.description: No activity is known for this operation (`agents.execution-operation-not-found`): the identifier is wrong, the operation ran in another server process or under another database profile, or its events were discarded and the record of that discard has also been dropped (at the latest 15 minutes later). Read the execution run instead.

post.summary: Send a chat message to an agent and stream the command's progress and result as server-sent events.
post.description:
Streaming form of `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/chat`: the same request body and the same chat command, but the response is a `text/event-stream` that reports the command's activity while it runs and ends with its result, instead of one JSON object after the command finished. The message is added to the given chat session, or to a new session when `chatSessionId` is omitted, and runs as an agent execution run.

Before the stream starts the request is checked and the command is admitted; a rejection is returned as JSON with one of the error statuses below. After HTTP 200, every outcome, including a failure, arrives as an event. The stream and the 409, 410, 422, 500 and 503 responses carry the command's activity operation identifier in the `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` header: the `activityOperationId` from the body, or a new one when none was sent. Use a new GUID for every command.

Events, in order; each `data:` line is one JSON object with camel-case members, and enum values are camel-case strings even where the JSON operations write integers:

- Activity events with `id:` set to their sequence number (1, 2 and so on): `agent.activity` while the command progresses, `agent.approval.waiting` when the run waits for tool approval, and last `agent.activity.completed`, `agent.activity.failed` or `agent.activity.cancelled`. The data is the activity object described for `GET /api/agents/execution-operations/{operationId}/events/stream`; the activity whose `terminalOutcome` is set is the last one (`suspended` when the run waits for approval).
- `stream.gap` or `stream.evicted`, as described for that operation, only when this connection falls behind the 256 retained activity events.
- `agent.approval.required`, without `id:`, when the run waits for tool approvals. Data: `operationId`, `executionRunId` and `approvals`, each with `approvalId`, `toolName`, `toolKind` and `requestedAtUtc`. Answer them with `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/pending-approvals` or its streaming form.
- Last, without `id:`, either `agent.command.completed` with `operationId` and `result` (the object that `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/chat` returns) or `agent.command.failed` with `operationId`, `code`, `message`, `correlationId`, `agentId`, `executionRunId`, `chatSessionId` and `providerFailureCategory`. A run that started and then failed reports `agents.run-failed`, or for a provider failure `agents.provider-request-incompatible`, `agents.provider-configuration-invalid`, `agents.provider-quota-unavailable`, `agents.provider-rate-limited` or `agents.provider-failed` with the matching `providerFailureCategory`. Any other failure, including a request rejected after the stream started such as an unknown agent or chat session, reports `agents.command-failed` without further detail.

While no activity arrives, a comment line `: heartbeat` followed by a UTC timestamp is sent every heartbeat interval (15 seconds by default). The server closes the response after the last event.

The command runs only while this response is open: closing the connection cancels it, and work that already completed, such as tool calls, is not undone. The last events are not replayable. After a dropped connection, read the run with `GET /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}` (its identifier appears in the activity events) before sending the message again.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Identifier of the agent that receives the message (not the empty GUID), as listed by `GET /api/agents`.

requestBody.description: The chat message, the same body as for `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/chat`: `prompt` (required, not blank); `chatSessionId` of an existing chat session of this agent, or omitted to start a new session; optional `attachmentPaths` with up to 8 image paths returned by `POST /api/agents/attachments/images`; optional `activityOperationId`, a new GUID that identifies this command's activity.

200.description: The `text/event-stream` described above. Unless the client disconnects it ends with `agent.command.completed` or `agent.command.failed`.

400.description: Rejected before the stream started (`agents.request-invalid`): the empty GUID as agent or chat session identifier, or a blank prompt. A body the framework cannot bind, for example malformed JSON or an `activityOperationId` that is not a non-empty GUID string, is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no error envelope.

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: An authorization policy rejected the authenticated caller (`api.authorization-forbidden`). This operation itself requires only a valid bearer token.

409.description: The `activityOperationId` belongs to an operation whose activity is still retained (`agents.execution-operation-duplicate`). Nothing was started; send a new GUID.

410.description: The `activityOperationId` belongs to an earlier operation whose activity was discarded (`agents.execution-operation-evicted`). Nothing was started; send a new GUID.

422.description: The run failed before the stream started because the provider profile is not usable (`agents.provider-configuration-invalid`). Run failures normally arrive in the stream instead.

500.description: The run failed before the stream started (`agents.run-failed`). Run failures normally arrive in the stream instead; read the run named in `executionRunId` before retrying.

503.description: The server is tracking too many unfinished operations (`agents.execution-operation-capacity-exhausted`; nothing was started, retry later), or the run failed before the stream started because the provider was unavailable (`agents.provider-quota-unavailable`, `agents.provider-rate-limited` or `agents.provider-failed`).

post.summary: Send one chat completion request to a provider profile and stream its status and answer as server-sent events.
post.description:
Calls the provider profile directly, outside any agent, chat session or execution run, and reports the call as a `text/event-stream`. It is the streaming form of `POST /api/agents/providers/{providerId}/test-chat` and is meant for checking a provider profile: the answer arrives once, in the last event, not token by token.

The request is validated and the provider profile is looked up before the stream starts; those rejections are returned as JSON with the error statuses below. After HTTP 200 the outcome arrives as an event.

Events; each has an `id:` and one JSON `data:` line with camel-case members:

- `provider.chat.accepted` (`id: 1`): `operationId`, a new identifier of this stream only, and `providerId`.
- `provider.chat.running` (`id: 2`): the same members; the provider call has started.
- `provider.chat.completed` (`id: 3`): `operationId`, `providerId` and `result` with `model` (the model that answered, as reported), `responseText`, `inputTokens` and `outputTokens`.
- `provider.chat.failed` (`id: 3`): `operationId`, `providerId`, `code` (`providers.chat-completion-failed`) and `message`. No failure detail is disclosed: a disabled provider profile, a provider error and an empty answer all report this event.

While the provider call runs, a comment line `: heartbeat` followed by a UTC timestamp is sent every heartbeat interval (15 seconds by default). The server closes the response after `provider.chat.completed` or `provider.chat.failed`. The stream cannot be resumed: the `Last-Event-ID` header is ignored and no other operation accepts its `operationId`. Closing the connection cancels the provider call. The call can be recorded in provider request history under the calling identity.

Stores one image in the managed workspace and returns its workspace-relative path. Send that path in `attachmentPaths` of `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/chat` or in `inputAttachmentPaths` of the execution-run operations, or of their streaming forms, to give the image to the agent; one request can attach up to 8 images. Uploading sends nothing to an agent or provider.

Send `multipart/form-data` with one file part named `file`: a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image of at most 10 MiB (10485760 bytes). The image type is taken from the file name extension (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif` or `.webp`); a part content type, when sent, must match it (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif` or `image/webp`). The image content itself is not inspected. A whole request larger than the image limit plus 64 KiB is rejected before the operation runs, without an error envelope.

Every upload creates a new file under `artifacts/chat-attachments/` in the workspace, with a unique name derived from the uploaded file name; uploading the same image again stores another copy.

post.summary: Open an agent recruiting interview that assesses a candidate agent's current configuration.
post.description:
Creates an interview, the container of assessment evidence for one candidate agent. The interview is fenced to the candidate's configuration at creation: readiness counts only interviews whose recorded configuration version equals the agent's current one, so evidence gathered before the agent's configuration changes stops counting afterwards. This is not a CRM/HR recruitment interview of a person (`POST /api/crm-hr/recruiting/interviews`).

Typical sequence:

1. Read `GET /api/agent-recruiting/candidates/{agentId}/readiness` and send its `currentConfigurationVersion` as `candidateConfigurationVersion`.
2. Run the assessment as an agent execution run, workflow run or process run in which the candidate takes part, and wait until the run has finished.
3. Record the result with `POST /api/agent-recruiting/interviews/{interviewId}/attempts`.
4. Have a human reviewer approve or reject the attempt with `POST /api/agent-recruiting/interviews/{interviewId}/reviews`.
5. Read the readiness again.

An interview changes only by appending attempts and reviews; there is no update or delete operation. Each request creates another interview, so after a lost response list the candidate's interviews before retrying. Recruiting evidence never activates or changes the agent. Text limits count UTF-16 code units after trimming.

A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no error envelope.

409.description: `candidateConfigurationVersion` is not the candidate's current configuration version (`agent-recruiting.candidate-version-conflict`). Read the readiness again and use its `currentConfigurationVersion`.

post.summary: Append an assessment attempt, the recorded result of a finished run, to an agent recruiting interview.
post.description:
Records one attempt of the candidate: the run whose result is assessed (`target`), the challenge and rubric used, integrity hashes of input and output, the automated evaluation and an optional structured analysis. The server checks that the target run exists in the current workspace and that the interview's candidate took part in it: as the run's agent (`agent-execution-run`), as the agent of a workflow node that executed in the run (`workflow-run`) or as a recorded participant of the run (`process-run`). It stores the supplied hashes and evaluation without recomputing them.

Missing evidence does not reject the attempt: it is stored with `completeness` `Incomplete` and `missingEvidence` naming what is missing, and it stays incomplete. Only complete attempts count for readiness. Append the attempt after the target run has finished (an agent execution run completed or failed; a workflow or process run completed, failed or cancelled); an attempt recorded while the run is still active is incomplete (`terminal-execution-target`). To replace an incomplete attempt, append a new one.

Attempts are numbered 1, 2 and so on per interview in append order and cannot be changed or deleted. Each request appends another attempt, so after a lost response read the interview before retrying. Text limits count UTF-16 code units after trimming.

An approval qualifies the attempt for readiness only when it carries both `authorizationReference` and `authorizationEvidenceHash`; otherwise it is stored with `qualifiesForReadiness` false and `missingEvidence` naming what is missing. Readiness uses the latest review of the latest attempt for the candidate's current configuration, so a new review of an attempt supersedes its earlier reviews, which stay in the history. Reviews cannot be changed or deleted, and each request appends another review; after a lost response read the interview before retrying.

Send a bearer token issued by this host whose scopes include `agent-recruiting.review`; the `api` scope alone is not enough. The stored reviewer identity comes from the token: `reviewerActorId` is the token subject and `reviewerDisplayName` its name claim, or the supplied name when the token has none.

- `Provider` and `Model` keep items that declare a matching supported model (case-insensitive) and items that declare no supported models.
- `Consumer` keeps items that declare that consumer and items that declare no consumers.

post.summary: Create a Prompt Gallery item or save a new draft of an existing item.

Tags, supported models and supported consumers are replaced by the lists sent; an omitted or null list clears them.

A draft is not a version. Saving sets the item's status to Draft and restores an archived item; existing versions and the current version number do not change. Create an immutable version with `POST /api/prompt-gallery/items/{promptId}/versions` to make the item Final again.

All request problems are reported together in `errors`. The response carries the new `updatedAtUtc`; use it for the next save or version.

post.summary: Check whether a Prompt Gallery item can be used by a consumer with a given provider and model.
post.description:
Evaluates the item against the consumer context without changing anything. The result lists the issues found; `canUse` is false when any issue has severity Error.

- Archived: the item is archived; always an error.
- MissingFinalVersion: the item has no version while the context needs one (purpose Execution or `requiresFinalVersion` true); an error.
- ConsumerNotSupported: the item declares supported consumers and the context consumer is not one of them; an error.
- ItemKindMismatch: `requiredKind` differs from the item's kind.
- ProviderModelNotSupported: a provider or model is given, the item declares supported models and none matches (case-insensitive).

The last two are warnings for purpose Selection, where a saved suppression for the consumer marks them `isSuppressed`, and errors for purpose Execution, where they cannot be suppressed.

post.summary: Start a production run of a workflow addressed in the route and wait until it stops.
post.description:
Same operation as `POST /api/workflows/runs/start`, with the workflow identifier taken from the route. A `workflowId` in the body is optional but, when present, must equal the route value.

Without `versionId` the latest Active version runs; this requires the current version to be Draft or Active. With `versionId` that exact version runs; it must itself be Active and the workflow's current version must be Draft or Active. The definition must pass validation, the chosen backend must be registered and runnable, and a definition that requires durable production runs cannot run on a non-durable backend.

The request waits while the run executes and returns when it stops: completed, failed, cancelled, waiting for an external response (see `pendingExternalRequests`) or idle. Closing the connection before the response arrives cancels the run in this host. The response is the safe run projection with its events, artifacts, pending external requests and checkpoints; `detailsComplete` false means the run was admitted but its detail could not be read, so read it with `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/detail`.

Idempotency: send an `Idempotency-Key` to make retries safe. The first request with a key creates the run and records the key; a later request with the same key and the same request returns that original run (`replayed` true, `idempotencyDisposition` ReplayedExistingRun) instead of starting another one, and a concurrent duplicate waits for the first to finish. In a replay, `run` shows the state recorded when the original start returned; read `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}` for the current state. A key is compared after trimming and is global across all API callers of this host. Reusing it for another workflow, version choice or request content is rejected with HTTP 409. When the original start failed without admitting a run, the key is released and can be used again. After a lost response, read `GET /api/workflows/runs/by-idempotency-key/{key}` or resend the same request with the same key. Without a key every request starts a new run, so a request whose response was lost cannot be retried safely; look for the run in `GET /api/workflows/runs` first.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; its subject becomes the run's actor. With authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open and the run is attributed to the local operator.

parameters.description: Identifier of the workflow to run, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/workflows/definitions`.

parameters.description: Optional client-chosen key, 1 to 256 characters after trimming, that identifies this start request, for example `invoice-4711-review`. Send the header at most once and without commas. A repeated request with the same key and the same content returns the original run instead of starting another. Keys are global across API callers, so include something unique to your client.

A body the framework cannot bind, including an unknown member, is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no error envelope.

post.summary: Request cancellation of a workflow run.
post.description:
Asks the runtime to stop a run that has not finished. What happens depends on the run:

- A run executing in this host whose backend supports cancellation is signalled; it becomes Cancelled shortly after the response, which may still show its earlier state.
- A run waiting for an external response is cancelled at once: its pending request is cancelled and the response shows the Cancelled run.
- A run that is already Completed, Failed or Cancelled, that is not executing in this host (for example after a restart or on another host), or whose pending request is being answered is not changed.

Every outcome returns the same body; branch on `outcome` and read the run again with `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}` to confirm its final state. Repeating the request is safe: once the run is terminal, it returns HTTP 409 with `AlreadyTerminal`.

The `run` in the body is the stored run record without the public safe projection, including the backend run identifier and the run's launch origin.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

409.description: `AlreadyTerminal` (the run already finished), `NotActive` (the run is not executing in this host, or its pending request is being answered) or `TransitionRejected` (the waiting run could not be cancelled consistently). Nothing was changed.

422.description: `BackendNotCancellable`: the run executes on a backend that does not support cancellation.

parameters.description: Only for `GET /api/workflows/runs/page`: number of runs per page; values outside 1 through 100 are clamped to that range. Omitted means `Take`, or 50 when that is omitted too. Ignored by `GET /api/workflows/runs`.

get.summary: Read one page of workflow runs, most recently updated first.
get.description:
Returns the runs that match every supplied filter, ordered by last update (newest first, ties by run identifier), as safe run projections with the total number of matches. Paging is zero-based: request the next page while `hasNextPage` is true. The page size is `PageSize`, else `Take`, else 50, limited to 1 through 100; the response states the page index and size actually used. Pages are computed per request, so runs updated between two requests can move between pages.

`Search` here is a case-sensitive substring of the run summary or backend run identifier; it does not match the run identifier, unlike `GET /api/workflows/runs`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: Backend
parameters.description: Only runs executed on this runtime backend, as an integer: 0 InProcess, 1 DurableTask, 2 AzureFunctions.

parameters.name: Search
parameters.description: Text filter; surrounding whitespace is ignored and omitted or blank applies no filter. For `GET /api/workflows/runs` it is a case-insensitive substring of the run summary, backend run identifier or run identifier. For `GET /api/workflows/runs/page` it is a case-sensitive substring of the run summary or backend run identifier only.

parameters.description: For `GET /api/workflows/runs`: the maximum number of runs returned, default 50; values outside 1 through 500 are clamped to that range. For `GET /api/workflows/runs/page`: the page size used when `PageSize` is omitted.

parameters.description: Only for `GET /api/workflows/runs/page`: zero-based page number, default 0; a negative value is treated as 0. Ignored by `GET /api/workflows/runs`.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Only for `GET /api/workflows/runs/page`: number of runs per page; values outside 1 through 100 are clamped to that range. Omitted means `Take`, or 50 when that is omitted too. Ignored by `GET /api/workflows/runs`.

200.description: The requested page. An empty `items` array means no run matched or the page is beyond the last page.

Returns the safe projection of the run: its identity, the workflow and version it runs, its state, backend, bounded summary and timestamps. Poll this operation, or subscribe to `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/events/stream`, to follow a run; read `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/detail` for its events, artifacts, pending requests and checkpoints.

Returns the same detail a start operation returns: the run, every event in time order, the artifact metadata, the external requests that still have no response, and the checkpoint metadata. All parts are safe projections: event payloads, artifact storage paths and content, raw external request and response JSON, checkpoint payload references and hashes and the run's launch origin are never included, and texts are bounded and redacted. The parts are read one after another, so a run that is still executing can show a slightly newer part next to an older one. Read artifact content with `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/content`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

Internal provider-read evidence records are not listed. For long runs use `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/events/page`; to be notified of new events use `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/events/stream`.

An unknown run identifier returns an empty array, not HTTP 404.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.description: Identifier of the run whose events are listed.

200.description: The events of the run; an empty array for a run without events or an unknown run.

Returns the run's events, oldest first (ties by event identifier), as safe projections with the total number of events. Paging is zero-based: request the next page while `hasNextPage` is true. Internal provider-read evidence records are not counted or listed. An unknown run identifier returns an empty page, not HTTP 404.

get.summary: List the artifacts recorded by a workflow run.
get.description:
Returns the metadata of every artifact of the run, oldest first: its kind, node, name, content type and bounded summary. Artifacts hold node outputs, tool receipts, preview simulations, payloads too large to keep inline, and files written by file operations. The storage location and the content are not included; read the content with `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/content`.

An unknown run identifier returns an empty array, not HTTP 404.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the run whose artifacts are listed.

200.description: The artifacts of the run; an empty array when there are none.

get.summary: Download the text content of one artifact of a workflow run.
get.description:
Returns the stored content as text, with the artifact's recorded `contentType` as the response `Content-Type`. Payload artifacts (node outputs, receipts, preview simulations and payloads too large to keep inline) use `application/json`, `text/plain` or `application/octet-stream`, and their content is the complete payload after credential-like values were redacted. File artifacts return the current text of the workspace file the run wrote, read at request time, and only when their content type is textual (for example `text/plain` or `text/markdown`); other File artifacts, such as spreadsheets and downloads, have no content here. The content is not bounded like the metadata projections and can be large.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the run that recorded the artifact.

parameters.name: artifactId
parameters.description: Identifier of the artifact, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/artifacts`.

200.description: The artifact content as text, with the artifact's content type.

404.description: The run has no artifact with this identifier (`workflows.artifact-not-found`), or the artifact has no readable content (`workflows.artifact-content-not-found`), for example because its file was removed or is not text.

get.summary: List the checkpoints recorded for a workflow run.
get.description:
Returns the metadata of every checkpoint of the run in the order they were created: where and why the runtime recorded it, whether it holds trusted runtime state, and whether the run can be resumed from it. Checkpoint payload references, hashes and backend identifiers are never returned. Checkpoints are informational for clients: resuming a run that waits for input happens through `POST /api/workflows/external-requests/{requestId}/response`, not through a checkpoint operation.

An unknown run identifier returns an empty array, not HTTP 404.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the run whose checkpoints are listed.

200.description: The checkpoints of the run; an empty array when there are none.

get.summary: List the external requests of a workflow run that have no recorded response yet.
get.description:
Read this before answering a human-input or approval request. Each item carries the request identity, kind, node, current `version`, `state`, a bounded and redacted `prompt` and the `responseContract` that a response must satisfy. Only an item whose `state` is Pending accepts a response: submit it with `POST /api/workflows/external-requests/{requestId}/response`, sending `version` as `expectedRequestVersion`.

The projection deliberately never returns the request's prior-node context, the raw request JSON, its authorization policy, executor arguments or checkpoint material. Do not derive a user interface from artifact file names; use `prompt` and `responseContract`. Items are ordered by creation time. An unknown run identifier returns an empty array, not HTTP 404.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open. Answering a request requires the separate `api.workflows.respond` scope.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the run whose open external requests are listed.

200.description: The external requests without a response; an empty array when there are none.

get.summary: Find the workflow run that a start request with a given `Idempotency-Key` created.
get.description:
Use this after a start request whose response was lost to learn, without starting anything, whether the key was recorded and which run it belongs to. The evidence names the original run, the workflow and version selection, the resolved version and backend, whether the start completed, the run's current state and how often the key was replayed. It returns hashes of the key and of the request, never the key itself or the run input.

Only keys sent to the HTTP start operations are found. Keys are global across all API callers of this host, so the lookup can find a start made by another caller with the same key. `claimState` Pending means the original start is still in progress: read again later, or resend the same start request with the same key, which waits for it and then returns the same run. When the original start failed before admitting a run, its key was released and this operation returns HTTP 404. Read the run itself with `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}` using `originalRunId`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The `Idempotency-Key` value sent to the start operation, for example `invoice-4711-review`. It is trimmed and then compared exactly; URL-encode reserved characters.

200.description: The key was recorded; the body describes the start request it belongs to.

400.description: The key is blank or longer than 256 characters after trimming (`workflows.idempotency-key-invalid`).

404.description: No HTTP start request recorded this key (`workflows.idempotency-key-not-found`). Nothing was started with it, or its start failed before a run was admitted; it is safe to send the start request with this key.

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: Reserved for a bearer token that does not authorize the operation (`api.authorization-forbidden`). The `/api` group currently accepts any valid token, so this route does not return it today.

get.summary: List the workflow definitions, or find the one bound to an external identity.
get.description:
Without query parameters this returns one catalog item for every workflow: the metadata of its current version, whatever its status, most recently updated first. There is no paging.

With `externalNamespace` and `externalKey` it returns only the workflows bound to that external identity: an empty array when none is, and normally at most one item because an external identity is unique. Supply both parameters or neither. To learn whether the identity can be started and which version would run, use `GET /api/workflows/definitions/by-external-key/{externalNamespace}/{externalKey}` instead, which also reports the resolution status.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: externalNamespace
parameters.description: Optional namespace of an external identity, for example `partner.system`. Required together with `externalKey`. It is trimmed and lower-cased; at most 100 characters of ASCII letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, period and colon.

parameters.name: externalKey
parameters.description: Optional key of an external identity within the namespace, for example `invoice:review`. Required together with `externalNamespace`. It is trimmed and lower-cased; at most 200 characters of the same characters.

200.description: The catalog items; an empty array when nothing matches.

400.description: Only one of the two parameters was supplied (`workflows.external-identity-incomplete`), or a value is too long or contains another character (`workflows.stable-identity-invalid`).

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: Reserved for a bearer token that does not authorize the operation (`api.authorization-forbidden`). The `/api` group currently accepts any valid token, so this route does not return it today.

post.summary: Create a workflow definition or store a new version of an existing one.
post.description:
Without `id` a new workflow is created with a server-generated identifier. With `id` the body becomes the new current version of that workflow; an unknown `id` creates a workflow with that identifier. Every successful save stores a new version with a new `versionId`; earlier versions stay readable. The body replaces the definition content: send the complete graph, runtime policy and input parameters, not a patch.

To edit safely, read the definition, change it and send the `versionId` you read as `expectedVersionId`; the save is rejected if another save happened in between. Without `expectedVersionId` the last save wins.

The new version must pass validation whatever its `status`, so an invalid draft cannot be stored; check a draft first with `POST /api/workflows/validate`. The requested `status` is stored as sent, so saving with Active publishes the new version directly. For LLM call nodes that reference a component, an empty provider, model or instructions value is filled from the component when the version is stored. The name and description are trimmed.

Stable identity: `externalNamespace` and `externalKey` must be sent together; they are stored lower-cased and must be unique across workflows. Leaving both empty keeps the identity of the current version, so this operation cannot remove an identity. Template provenance cannot be set here.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The complete definition content to store and the optional concurrency precondition.

200.description: The version was stored. The body is the stored definition with its new `versionId`.

400.description: Nothing was stored (`workflows.request-invalid`; the message gives the reason): a blank name, a missing graph or runtime policy, a stale `expectedVersionId`, an incomplete, malformed or already used external identity, a validation failure (the message lists the issues), or a component or Prompt Gallery binding that cannot be resolved. Read the current version before retrying a stale save. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no error envelope.

get.summary: Resolve the workflow installed from a template key to the version that would run.
get.description:
Looks up the workflows whose template provenance carries this template key and reports the outcome in `status`; every outcome is returned with HTTP 200, so always check `status`:

- Resolved: exactly one workflow matches and `runnableVersionId` names the version a latest-Active start would run.
- NotFound: no workflow was installed from this template.
- Ambiguous: several workflows carry the key; nothing is selected until the catalog is repaired.
- Stale: one workflow matches but it has no runnable Active version.

`materializations` lists every matching workflow in all cases. A template key identifies where a workflow came from; it is not unique and it is not the workflow identifier. Start the resolved workflow with `POST /api/workflows/runs/start` using `workflowId`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: templateKey
parameters.description: Template key to resolve, for example `billing.review`. It is trimmed and lower-cased before matching; at most 200 characters of ASCII letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, period and colon.

200.description: The resolution, whatever its `status`.

400.description: The key is blank, too long or contains another character (`workflows.stable-identity-invalid`).

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: Reserved for a bearer token that does not authorize the operation (`api.authorization-forbidden`). The `/api` group currently accepts any valid token, so this route does not return it today.

get.summary: Resolve the workflow bound to an external identity to the version that would run.
get.description:
Looks up the workflow whose external identity is the given namespace and key (set with `POST /api/workflows/definitions`) and reports the outcome in `status`; every outcome is returned with HTTP 200, so always check `status`:

- Resolved: exactly one workflow matches and `runnableVersionId` names the version a latest-Active start would run.
- NotFound: no workflow is bound to this identity.
- Ambiguous: several workflows match; nothing is selected until the catalog is repaired.
- Stale: the workflow exists but has no runnable Active version.

Use this instead of storing workflow identifiers when an external system knows workflows by its own names. Start the resolved workflow with `POST /api/workflows/runs/start` using `workflowId`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: externalNamespace
parameters.description: Namespace of the external identity, for example `partner.system`. It is trimmed and lower-cased; at most 100 characters of ASCII letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, period and colon.

parameters.name: externalKey
parameters.description: Key within the namespace, for example `invoice:review`. It is trimmed and lower-cased; at most 200 characters of the same characters. URL-encode it when it contains reserved characters.

200.description: The resolution, whatever its `status`.

400.description: A value is blank, too long or contains another character (`workflows.stable-identity-invalid`).

401.description: API authorization is enabled and the request has no valid bearer token (`api.authorization-required`).

403.description: Reserved for a bearer token that does not authorize the operation (`api.authorization-forbidden`). The `/api` group currently accepts any valid token, so this route does not return it today.

post.summary: Answer a pending human-input or approval request of a waiting workflow run.
post.description:
Submits one response to an external request that a run is waiting for, validates it against the request's persisted response contract and resumes the run. This is the only HTTP way to answer an external request.

Before submitting, read the request with `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/pending-requests` or `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/detail`: its `state` must be Pending, send its `version` as `expectedRequestVersion`, and build `response` from its `responseContract`.

The body is a JSON object with exactly two members, `expectedRequestVersion` (a positive integer) and `response` (a JSON value, not a string containing encoded JSON). Member names are case-sensitive; unknown, duplicate or missing members, comments, trailing commas, nesting deeper than 32 levels and bodies larger than 70 KiB are rejected before anything changes. The `response` must also fit `responseContract.maximumPayloadBytes` (UTF-8 bytes of its JSON text):

- Approval and tool-approval requests: an object with the boolean `approved` and optionally a `message` string of at most 4,096 characters, for example `{ "approved": true, "message": "Reviewed and approved." }`. `approved` false denies the request and the governed step is not executed.
- Human-input requests: a JSON value that satisfies `responseContract.schema`, which is checked strictly.

Idempotency: the `Idempotency-Key` header is required. An external request accepts one answer attempt, identified by its key and caller. Resending the same body with the same key returns that attempt (`replayed` true) and continues it when it was accepted but not finished or failed with a retryable error; the request is never answered twice. The same key with a different response, or another key or caller for a request that already has an attempt, is rejected with HTTP 409.

Outcomes: HTTP 200 when the run completed, waits for another request (`nextPendingRequest`) or the approval was denied; HTTP 202 while the run is still resuming. Read the attempt later with `GET /api/workflows/external-response-operations/{operationId}` and the run with `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}`. Every response of this operation, success or failure, uses the same allowlisted body; branch on `outcome`. The body never contains the raw request or response JSON, event payloads, checkpoint references or hashes, artifact storage paths, the idempotency key, leases or authorization material.

Authority: the caller must be authenticated with a bearer token issued by this host that carries a subject and the exact `api.workflows.respond` scope; the broad `api` scope is not enough. The token's subject is recorded as the responder and must equal the request's intended approver when the request names one. The request must belong to the current database profile and to a workspace scope the caller may answer. With API authorization disabled (the development default) no caller is authenticated, so this operation always returns HTTP 401: it is not open.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: Identifier of the external request, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/pending-requests` or in `nextPendingRequest.id`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key for this answer attempt, required: exactly one value, not blank, without commas and at most 256 characters after trimming, for example `approval-7f3c-attempt-1`. It is scoped to the external request. Resend the same key with the same body to retry safely; a different body under the same key is rejected with HTTP 409.

requestBody.description: The expected request version and the response value, as a JSON object with exactly these two members. Take `expectedRequestVersion` from `version` of the pending request and build `response` from its `responseContract`.

expectedRequestVersion.description: `version` of the pending request as last read, a positive JSON integer. When the request has moved to another version, the submission is rejected with HTTP 409 (`outcome` 10 RequestVersionMismatch).

response.description: Any JSON value. The member that uses it describes the expected shape.

schema.description: Body of `POST /api/workflows/external-requests/{requestId}/response`: the request version the caller read and the response value. Exactly these two members are accepted, with these case-sensitive names; unknown, duplicate or missing members are rejected with HTTP 400 before anything changes.

expectedRequestVersion.description: `version` of the pending request as last read, a positive JSON integer. When the request has moved to another version, the submission is rejected with HTTP 409 (`outcome` 10 RequestVersionMismatch).

response.description: Any JSON value. The member that uses it describes the expected shape.

schema.description: Body of `POST /api/workflows/external-requests/{requestId}/response`: the request version the caller read and the response value. Exactly these two members are accepted, with these case-sensitive names; unknown, duplicate or missing members are rejected with HTTP 400 before anything changes.

200.description: The response was accepted and processed: `outcome` 0 Completed (the run completed), 1 WaitingAgain (the run waits for `nextPendingRequest`) or 2 Denied (the approval was denied and the governed step was not run).

202.description: `outcome` 3 Resuming: the response was accepted and the run is still resuming. Poll `GET /api/workflows/external-response-operations/{operationId}` until it reports a final outcome.

400.description: `outcome` 6 InvalidResponse: the `Idempotency-Key` header, the body or the `response` value was rejected (for example a schema mismatch or a response over the payload limit). Nothing was recorded; correct the request and send it again.

401.description: No authenticated caller: `outcome` 4 Unauthenticated, including every call while API authorization is disabled, or a token without a subject or with invalid timestamps. With API authorization enabled, a request without a valid bearer token is rejected before this operation runs with the general error envelope (`api.authorization-required`) instead of this body.

403.description: The caller may not answer this request: `outcome` 5 Forbidden (another database profile, workspace scope or intended responder, a missing response capability, an expired authentication, or an autonomous actor approving) or 18 AuthorizationContextUnavailable (the request's stored authorization context is incomplete). A token without the `api.workflows.respond` scope is rejected before this operation runs with the general error envelope (`api.authorization-forbidden`) instead of this body.

404.description: `outcome` 7 RequestNotFound or 8 RunNotFound: the request or its run does not exist.

409.description: The request cannot take this response now; nothing new was recorded: `outcome` 10 RequestVersionMismatch (read the request again and use its current `version`), 11 RequestNotPending (it was already answered), 12 RunNotWaiting, 13 IdempotencyConflict (the key was used with a different response) or 14 ActiveOperationConflict (the request already has an attempt under another key or caller; read that attempt with `operationId` when it is returned, instead of answering again).

410.description: `outcome` 15 Cancelled or 16 Superseded: the request or the attempt was cancelled, or a newer request replaced it. Do not retry; read the run's pending requests.

422.description: The run's stored state cannot be resumed with this response: `outcome` 17 LegacyNonResumable, 19 CheckpointMissing, 20 CheckpointCorrupt, 21 CheckpointIncompatible, 22 TopologyMismatch, 23 WorkflowVersionMismatch or 24 RequestMismatch. Retrying does not help.

500.description: `outcome` 27 TerminalFailure: the attempt failed for an unclassified reason; the message is redacted. Read the operation, if one was returned, and the run before deciding what to do.

503.description: `outcome` 25 BackendUnavailable or 26 RetryableFailure: a temporary failure. Resend the same body with the same `Idempotency-Key` later; the recorded attempt continues instead of starting a second one.

get.summary: Read the current status of an accepted external-response attempt.
get.description:
Returns the operation that a submission to `POST /api/workflows/external-requests/{requestId}/response` recorded, with its state, final outcome, run state and the next pending request when the run waits again. Use it to follow a submission that returned HTTP 202 or whose response was lost. Reading never changes the operation and never continues it: when it stays Resuming or reports a retryable failure, resend the original submission with the same `Idempotency-Key`, which continues the recorded attempt.

The body and the status mapping are the same as for the submission, with `replayed` always false. The caller is authorized again against the request's current policy, so any caller allowed to answer the request can read its operations. The body never contains the raw request or response JSON, event payloads, checkpoint references or hashes, artifact storage paths, the idempotency key, leases or authorization material.

Authority: the caller must be authenticated with a bearer token issued by this host that carries a subject and the exact `api.workflows.respond` scope; the broad `api` scope is not enough. With API authorization disabled (the development default) no caller is authenticated, so this operation always returns HTTP 401.

parameters.name: operationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the attempt, as returned in `operationId` by the submission.

200.description: The attempt finished: `outcome` 0 Completed, 1 WaitingAgain (see `nextPendingRequest`) or 2 Denied.

202.description: `outcome` 3 Resuming: the attempt was accepted and has not finished. Read again later.

400.description: `outcome` 6 InvalidResponse: the operation identifier is the empty GUID.

401.description: No authenticated caller: `outcome` 4 Unauthenticated, including every call while API authorization is disabled. With API authorization enabled, a request without a valid bearer token is rejected before this operation runs with the general error envelope (`api.authorization-required`) instead of this body.

403.description: The caller may not read this attempt: `outcome` 5 Forbidden or 18 AuthorizationContextUnavailable. A token without the `api.workflows.respond` scope is rejected before this operation runs with the general error envelope (`api.authorization-forbidden`) instead of this body.

404.description: `outcome` 9 OperationNotFound, 7 RequestNotFound or 8 RunNotFound: the attempt, its request or its run does not exist.

409.description: Part of the status map shared with the submission route; reading an attempt does not return it.

410.description: `outcome` 15 Cancelled: the attempt or its request was cancelled.

422.description: The attempt ended because the run's stored state could not be resumed: `outcome` 17 LegacyNonResumable, 19 CheckpointMissing, 20 CheckpointCorrupt, 21 CheckpointIncompatible, 22 TopologyMismatch, 23 WorkflowVersionMismatch or 24 RequestMismatch.

500.description: `outcome` 27 TerminalFailure: the attempt failed for an unclassified reason, or reading it failed; the message is redacted.

503.description: `outcome` 25 BackendUnavailable or 26 RetryableFailure: the attempt failed temporarily. Resend the original submission with the same `Idempotency-Key` to continue it.

get.summary: List the routes of the workflow API family together with a short boundary note.
get.description:
Returns a fixed list of `METHOD /route` strings for this family and one sentence about where agent capability setup is validated. The list is informational: it does not reflect authorization, configuration or runtime state, and this OpenAPI document stays the exact contract for parameters, bodies and responses.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: The route list and the boundary note.

get.summary: Read the workflow settings document of this host.
get.description:
Returns the single settings document shared by all workflows: the recorded default runtime policy, the payload and artifact capture policy, the human-in-the-loop policy and the agent voice settings. When no settings were saved yet, the built-in defaults are returned: the in-process backend, 64,000 inline payload characters with node-output capture, human input allowed with a 240-minute default timeout, and voice input and output disabled. Change the document with `POST /api/workflows/settings`, which replaces it as a whole.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: The saved settings, or the built-in defaults when none were saved.

post.summary: Replace the workflow settings document.
post.description:
Stores the body as the complete settings document and returns it; nothing is merged with the stored document. Read the current document with `GET /api/workflows/settings`, change the members you need and send all of them: an omitted `voiceSettings` is stored as null, which resets agent voice input and output to their disabled defaults.

Checks before anything is stored:

- `artifactPolicy.maxInlinePayloadCharacters` and `humanInLoopPolicy.defaultRequestTimeoutMinutes` must be greater than zero.
- The preferred backend of `defaultRuntimePolicy` must be registered and runnable in this host (see `GET /api/workflows/runtime-backends`).
- The two Azure Functions exposure flags may be true only when an Azure Functions backend is runnable; none is registered by default.

The new settings apply to later work. Setting `humanInLoopPolicy.allowHumanInputNodes` to false makes every definition that contains a human-input node fail validation, so it can no longer be saved, published or launched until the setting is restored.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The complete settings document to store. Send every member.

200.description: The settings were stored; the body is the stored document.

400.description: A check failed (`workflows.request-invalid`, the message names the check) and nothing was stored. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no error envelope.

get.summary: List the workflow runtime backends this host knows and whether each one can run workflows.
get.description:
Returns one entry for each backend kind (InProcess, DurableTask and AzureFunctions) with its capabilities and availability. By default only the in-process backend is registered and runnable; the others are listed as planned. Use the list to choose `requestedBackend` when starting a run or `runtimePolicy.preferredBackend` for a definition: a backend that is not registered and runnable is rejected when a run starts and makes a definition that prefers it fail validation.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: Every known backend, runnable or not.

get.summary: List the executors that executor nodes of a workflow definition can use, with their current availability.
get.description:
Returns the built-in and plugin-provided executors known to this host. Each entry gives the executor identifier to put in `settings.executorId` of an Executor node, its input and result shapes, its settings schema and default settings, its default execution policy, its source and trust level, its side effects, the permissions and approval it requires, and whether it can run now. Availability is evaluated while the list is read, so an executor can be listed but not runnable, for example when its plugin is disabled or not configured.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: The executor catalog.

get.summary: Read the current version of a workflow definition with a fresh validation result.
get.description:
Returns the workflow's current version, whatever its lifecycle status, and a validation result computed now against the current components, providers, Prompt Gallery bindings, runtime backends and workflow settings, so a definition that was valid when saved can become invalid later. A workflow keeps its `workflowId` across versions; every save, import and status change stores a new version with a new `versionId`. Read an earlier version with `GET /api/workflows/definitions/{workflowId}/versions/{versionId}`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Identifier of the workflow, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/workflows/definitions` or by a save.

200.description: The current version and its validation result.

404.description: No workflow has this identifier (`workflows.definition-not-found`).

delete.summary: Permanently delete a workflow definition and all its versions.
delete.description:
Removes the workflow and every stored version; this cannot be undone except by importing an earlier export. Runs of the workflow, with their events, artifacts and checkpoints, are not deleted and stay readable through the run operations. LLM call components are not deleted. To stop new runs but keep the definition, archive or suspend it instead.

The operation is idempotent: deleting an unknown or already deleted workflow also returns `{ "ok": true }`. There is no concurrency precondition.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Identifier of the workflow to delete.

200.description: The workflow no longer exists; `{ "ok": true }`.

get.summary: Read one stored version of a workflow definition with a fresh validation result.
get.description:
Returns the exact version, which may be older than the current one, and a validation result computed now. Version identifiers come from `versionId` of a definition, a catalog item or a run. A version identifier is only found under the workflow it belongs to.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Identifier of the workflow that owns the version.

parameters.name: versionId
parameters.description: Identifier of the stored version of that workflow.

200.description: The requested version and its validation result.

404.description: The workflow or the version does not exist (`workflows.definition-not-found`).

get.summary: Export a workflow definition version as a portable envelope.
get.description:
Returns the current version, or the version named by `versionId`, wrapped with the exchange format `CanDoItAll.WorkflowDefinition/v1`, its validation result at export time and the export time. Send the envelope unchanged in `envelope` of `POST /api/workflows/definitions/import` to recreate the workflow on this or another host. The envelope holds the whole definition, including node instructions and executor settings, so handle it like the definition itself. Exporting changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Identifier of the workflow to export.

parameters.name: versionId
parameters.description: Optional identifier of the version to export. Omit it to export the current version.

200.description: The export envelope.

404.description: The workflow or the requested version does not exist (`workflows.definition-not-found`).

post.summary: Import a workflow definition from an export envelope.
post.description:
Stores the definition inside an envelope produced by `GET /api/workflows/definitions/{workflowId}/export`. Only the definition of the envelope is used; its validation result and export time are ignored. The imported version is validated like a save and stored with the requested status, Draft when `status` is omitted.

With `preserveWorkflowId` false the import creates a new workflow with a new identifier and without the source's external identity or template provenance. With true it keeps the source's workflow identifier, external identity and template provenance; if that workflow already exists here, the import becomes its new current version without any concurrency check.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The export envelope and the import options.

200.description: The definition was stored. The body is the stored version.

400.description: Nothing was stored (`workflows.request-invalid`): the envelope or its definition is missing, the envelope format is not `CanDoItAll.WorkflowDefinition/v1`, the definition fails validation, or its external identity is already used by another workflow. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no error envelope.

post.summary: Publish the current version of a workflow definition by storing it as a new Active version.
post.description:
Validates the workflow's current version and stores a copy of it with status Active as the new current version (a new `versionId`). Production runs started with `POST /api/workflows/runs/start` without a `versionId` use the latest Active version. Publishing does not affect runs that already exist.

Send the `versionId` you last read as `expectedVersionId` so that the change is rejected when the workflow changed in between; without it the change applies to whatever version is current.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Identifier of the workflow to publish.

parameters.name: expectedVersionId
parameters.description: Optional `versionId` of the current version as last read. When it no longer is the current version, the change is rejected with HTTP 400.

200.description: The new Active version.

400.description: Nothing was stored (`workflows.request-invalid`): the current version fails validation (the message lists the issues) or `expectedVersionId` is stale. Read the definition again before retrying.

404.description: No workflow has this identifier (`workflows.resource-not-found`).

post.summary: Suspend a workflow definition by storing its current version as a new Suspended version.
post.description:
Stores a copy of the current version with status Suspended as the new current version (a new `versionId`). While the current version is Suspended, no version of the workflow can be started by the start operations: latest-Active starts find no runnable version and exact-version starts are rejected. Runs that already exist continue. Publish again to make the workflow runnable.

The stored copy is validated like any save, so a definition that no longer validates cannot be suspended until it is fixed. Send the `versionId` you last read as `expectedVersionId` to detect concurrent changes.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Identifier of the workflow to suspend.

parameters.name: expectedVersionId
parameters.description: Optional `versionId` of the current version as last read. When it no longer is the current version, the change is rejected with HTTP 400.

200.description: The new Suspended version.

400.description: Nothing was stored (`workflows.request-invalid`): the definition fails validation or `expectedVersionId` is stale.

404.description: No workflow has this identifier (`workflows.resource-not-found`).

post.summary: Archive a workflow definition by storing its current version as a new Archived version.
post.description:
Stores a copy of the current version with status Archived as the new current version (a new `versionId`). Archiving keeps the workflow and its versions but, like suspending, stops the start operations from starting it; runs that already exist continue. It does not delete anything: use `DELETE /api/workflows/definitions/{workflowId}` for that.

The stored copy is validated like any save, so a definition that no longer validates cannot be archived until it is fixed. Send the `versionId` you last read as `expectedVersionId` to detect concurrent changes.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Identifier of the workflow to archive.

parameters.name: expectedVersionId
parameters.description: Optional `versionId` of the current version as last read. When it no longer is the current version, the change is rejected with HTTP 400.

200.description: The new Archived version.

400.description: Nothing was stored (`workflows.request-invalid`): the definition fails validation or `expectedVersionId` is stale.

404.description: No workflow has this identifier (`workflows.resource-not-found`).

post.summary: Validate the current version of a stored workflow definition.
post.description:
Runs the same validation as a save or a start against the workflow's current version and the current components, providers, backends and settings, and returns the issues. Nothing is changed. An empty `issues` list means the version is valid now.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Identifier of the workflow whose current version is validated.

200.description: The validation result; issues are returned with HTTP 200 too.

404.description: No workflow has this identifier (`workflows.definition-not-found`).

post.summary: Validate an unsaved workflow definition.
post.description:
Checks a complete definition, for example an edited draft, with the same rules a save applies, without storing it: graph structure, node settings, component, executor and provider references, runtime policy and the workflow settings. Nothing is stored and the identifiers in the body are not looked up, so any non-empty identifiers can be sent. An empty `issues` list means that a save of this content would pass validation at this moment.
