Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The complete definition to validate.

200.description: The validation result; issues are returned with HTTP 200 too.

get.summary: List the chat model providers that LLM call components and nodes can use.
get.description:
Returns the chat-purpose provider profiles configured in this host, enabled ones first and then by name, with their default and suggested models and capability flags. Use `providerProfileId` and one of `modelOptions` in a component or an LLM call node. The list contains no credentials. An empty list means no chat provider is configured.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: The provider options.

get.summary: List the reusable LLM call components.
get.description:
Returns every LLM call component ordered by name. A component is a reusable model call (provider, model, instructions, input and result shapes, permissions) that LLM call nodes reference by `componentId`. Its instructions are kept as a Prompt Gallery prompt version, identified by `promptArtifactId` and `promptVersionId`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: The components; an empty array when none exist.

post.summary: Create or replace an LLM call component and record its instructions in the Prompt Gallery.
post.description:
Without `id` a new component is created; with `id` the stored component with that identifier is replaced (an unknown `id` creates it). The name, model and instructions are trimmed and must not be blank, and the component must pass the component validation and the provider checks: the provider must exist, be enabled and be a chat provider, support vision for Vision or Multimodal modality and structured output when JSON output is required, and have a price row for the model.

The instructions are stored as a Prompt Gallery prompt version, which is a side effect of this call:

- With `promptVersionId`, that version's content becomes the instructions and the sent `instructions` are not stored.
- With `promptArtifactId` (or an existing binding) and changed instructions, a new version of that prompt is created.
- Without any binding, a new Prompt Gallery prompt is created for the component.

Nodes that reference the component copy its provider, model and instructions when their definition is saved, so saved definitions keep the values they copied.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

requestBody.description: The complete component to store.

200.description: The component was stored. The body shows the stored instructions and the Prompt Gallery binding.

400.description: The component was rejected (`workflows.request-invalid`; the message lists the reasons): a blank name, model or instructions, a validation or provider check failure, or a Prompt Gallery item or version that is missing, mismatched or incompatible. A Prompt Gallery prompt created before a later check failed can remain. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no error envelope.

get.summary: Read one LLM call component.
get.description:
Returns the component with its instructions resolved from its Prompt Gallery prompt version.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: componentId
parameters.description: Identifier of the component, as returned in `id` by `GET /api/workflows/components` or a save.

200.description: The component.

404.description: No component has this identifier (`workflows.component-not-found`).

delete.description:
Removes the component. Stored definition versions keep the provider, model and instructions they copied from it, but a definition whose LLM call node still references the deleted component fails validation when it is validated, saved, published or started. Its Prompt Gallery prompt is not deleted.

The operation is idempotent: deleting an unknown component also returns `{ "ok": true }`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: componentId
parameters.description: Identifier of the component to delete.

200.description: The component no longer exists; `{ "ok": true }`.

post.summary: Validate a workflow, or run it once in preview mode, and wait for the outcome.
post.description:
Tests either an unsaved draft (`draftDefinition`, which must have status Draft) or an exact stored version (`workflowId` and `versionId`). With `validateOnly` the definition is only validated and no run is created.

Otherwise a real preview run is created and executed before the response is sent: it is stored like any run, appears in the run lists and executes its nodes, including executors with external effects, except the nodes replaced by `previewSimulationPlan`. Preview runs do not require an Active version but must be allowed by the definition's runtime policy. There is no idempotency key: repeating the request creates another run.

The run succeeds when it ends Completed, WaitingForInput or Idle. Unlike the start operations, this response returns the stored run records without the public safe projection, including event payloads, artifact storage paths, external request and response JSON, checkpoint references and the run's launch origin. Use it only for trusted authoring clients.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open. The authenticated subject, or the local operator when authorization is disabled, becomes the preview run's actor.

requestBody.description: What to test, the run input and the preview options.

200.description: Validation passed (`validateOnly`) or the preview run ended Completed, WaitingForInput or Idle.

400.description: The test did not succeed; the body has the same shape and explains why in `validation` and `errorMessage`: no definition was identified, the definition failed validation, the launch was rejected, or the preview run failed or was cancelled (then `run` is present). A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs and has no envelope.

get.summary: Aggregate workflow definition, run, duration and model-usage figures.
get.description:
Computes a snapshot at request time. Definition counts cover the current version of each workflow (all of them, or the one named by `WorkflowId`). Run figures cover the runs that match every supplied filter: `WorkflowId`, `State`, `Backend` and `Search` (a case-insensitive substring of the run summary, backend run identifier or run identifier). `Take` limits only `recentRuns`; `runs` lists every matching run, so filter large catalogs.

Usage figures add up the model usage recorded for the matching runs; a cost is included only when a price was known, and the counts of known and unknown observations say how complete the totals are. Durations of runs still in progress are measured up to the snapshot time.

Like the cancellation and test-run results, the run entries are the stored run records without the public safe projection, including the backend run identifier and the run's launch origin.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: WorkflowId
parameters.description: Identifier of one workflow to analyze. Omitted means all workflows; an unknown identifier gives zero counts.

parameters.name: State
parameters.description: Count only runs in this state, as an integer: 0 NotStarted, 1 Running, 2 WaitingForInput, 3 Idle, 4 Completed, 5 Failed, 6 Cancelled. It filters the run figures only, not the definition counts.

parameters.name: Backend
parameters.description: Count only runs executed on this runtime backend, as an integer: 0 InProcess, 1 DurableTask, 2 AzureFunctions. It filters the run figures only.

parameters.name: Search
parameters.description: Text matched case-insensitively as a substring of each run's summary, backend run identifier or run identifier. Surrounding whitespace is ignored; omitted or blank applies no text filter.

parameters.name: Take
parameters.description: Number of most recently updated runs to return in `recentRuns`, from 1 through 500. Omitted means 8; a value outside the range is rejected with HTTP 400. It does not limit the counts or the `runs` list.

200.description: The analytics snapshot. Filters that match nothing give zero counts and empty lists.

400.description: `Take` is outside 1 through 500, or a stored run cannot be measured (`workflows.request-invalid`).

get.summary: Subscribe to change notifications of all workflow runs as server-sent events.
get.description:
Opens a `text/event-stream` response that stays open and sends a notification each time an event is recorded for any workflow run of this host. A notification tells which run changed and how, not the details: read the run or its events when you need them. Use it to keep a run list or dashboard current; follow a single run with `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/events/stream`.

Frames are UTF-8 text separated by a blank line:

- A notification: `id: {position}`, `event: workflow.run.changed` and `data:` with one JSON object: `eventId` (the event's `id` in the run event lists), `runId`, `category` (`started`, `progress`, `needsAttention`, `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`), `kind` (the event kind as a camel-case token, for example `executorCompleted` or `waitingForInput`), `nodeId` (null for run-level events), `occurredAtUtc`, `isTerminal` (the run completed, was cancelled or failed as a whole) and `needsAttention` (input is awaited, or a warning or failure occurred).
- A gap notice: `event: stream.gap` when notifications before the requested position were discarded or the position lies ahead of the stream. Its `data` has `reason` (`cursorBeforeRetention` or `cursorAheadOfStream`), `requestedAfterSequence`, `firstAvailableSequence`, `lastAvailableSequence`, `resumeAfterSequence` and `snapshotUrl` (null here); its `id` is the position the stream continues from. Changes in the gap were missed, so re-read the runs you follow.
- A heartbeat comment, `: heartbeat {time}`, every 15 seconds by default while nothing else is sent.

To resume after a disconnect, send the last received position as the `Last-Event-ID` header (browsers do this automatically) or as the `after` query parameter; if both are sent they must be equal. Without either, the stream first repeats the retained notifications (the last 1,024 by default) and then continues live. Notifications are held only in memory: a host restart starts the positions over, and a change of the active database profile closes open streams and discards the retained notifications. The durable record is `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/events`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

200.description: The event stream (`text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`). It stays open until the client disconnects or the host closes it.

400.description: The `after` query parameter or `Last-Event-ID` header is not a single non-negative integer, or the two differ (`sse.cursor-invalid`). No stream is opened.

get.summary: Subscribe to change notifications of one workflow run as server-sent events.
get.description:
Opens a `text/event-stream` response that stays open and sends a notification each time an event is recorded for this run. A notification tells what changed, not the details: read `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}` or the run's events when you need them. The stream does not end when the run finishes; close it after a notification whose `isTerminal` is true. An unknown run identifier is accepted, and the stream then sends only heartbeats and gap notices.

Frames are UTF-8 text separated by a blank line:

- A notification: `id: {position}`, `event: workflow.run.changed` and `data:` with one JSON object: `eventId` (the event's `id` in the run event lists), `runId`, `category` (`started`, `progress`, `needsAttention`, `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`), `kind` (the event kind as a camel-case token, for example `executorCompleted` or `waitingForInput`), `nodeId` (null for run-level events), `occurredAtUtc`, `isTerminal` (the run completed, was cancelled or failed as a whole) and `needsAttention` (input is awaited, or a warning or failure occurred).
- A gap notice: `event: stream.gap` when notifications before the requested position were discarded or the position lies ahead of the stream. Its `data` has `reason` (`cursorBeforeRetention` or `cursorAheadOfStream`), `requestedAfterSequence`, `firstAvailableSequence`, `lastAvailableSequence`, `resumeAfterSequence` and `snapshotUrl` (null here); its `id` is the position the stream continues from. Changes in the gap were missed, so re-read the run.
- A heartbeat comment, `: heartbeat {time}`, every 15 seconds by default while nothing else is sent.

Positions (`id`) belong to the host-wide notification stream, so they are increasing but not consecutive for one run. To resume after a disconnect, send the last received position as the `Last-Event-ID` header (browsers do this automatically) or as the `after` query parameter; if both are sent they must be equal. Without either, the stream first repeats the retained notifications of the run (from the last 1,024 notifications of the host by default) and then continues live. Notifications are held only in memory: a host restart starts the positions over, and a change of the active database profile closes open streams and discards the retained notifications. The durable record is `GET /api/workflows/runs/{runId}/events`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; with authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the run to follow, as returned in `run.runId` by a start operation. It must not be the empty GUID.

200.description: The event stream (`text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`). It stays open until the client disconnects or the host closes it.

400.description: The run identifier is the empty GUID (`workflows.run-id-invalid`), or the `after` query parameter or `Last-Event-ID` header is not a single non-negative integer or the two differ (`sse.cursor-invalid`). No stream is opened.

get.summary: Search the durable records of ended process runs, newest end first, one cursor page at a time.
get.description:
A run record is created when a run ends (it completes, fails, is cancelled or becomes blocked) and is then completed in the background: first the hard facts (steps, usage, costs, evidence), then a generated narrative. Active runs have no record yet; use `GET /api/processes/live` or `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}` for them. Records of child runs (subprocesses) are listed as well, and a record's totals include the child runs of its run. A run that is reactivated, for example by step rework, has no record until it ends again.

Records are ordered by `metrics.endedAtUtc` descending and then by run identifier descending. To page, send the returned `nextCursor` as `cursor` with the same filters until `nextCursor` is null. The cursor is opaque and does not carry the filters, so always repeat them.

Filters are combined with AND. `projectId`, `definitionId` and `participantId` become known only when a record's facts are assembled (`factsStatus` Completed); records without facts never match them. `rootRunId`, `disposition`, `fromUtc` and `toUtc` apply as soon as a record exists.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host, and every record is visible to that caller; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Only records of runs launched for this project. The all-zero GUID is rejected.

parameters.name: definitionId
parameters.description: Only records of runs of this process definition (`definitionId` of the launch response). The all-zero GUID is rejected.

parameters.name: rootRunId
parameters.description: Only records whose top-level run is this run: the run's own record and the records of its child runs. The all-zero GUID is rejected.

parameters.name: disposition
parameters.description: Only records that ended this way: `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Cancelled` or `Blocked`, matched case-insensitively; numbers are not accepted. `Escalated` is also accepted but is not currently produced.

parameters.name: participantId
parameters.description: Only records whose run involved this participant: an executor identifier of a step assignment or the identifier of an agent that executed a step (agent identifiers are GUID strings). Exact match after trimming; 1 to 256 characters.

parameters.name: fromUtc
parameters.description: Only runs that ended at or after this instant (inclusive). When both bounds are given, it must be earlier than `toUtc`.

parameters.name: toUtc
parameters.description: Only runs that ended before this instant (exclusive).

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Page size, from 1 through 200. Omitted means 50.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `nextCursor` of the previous page, unchanged; omit it for the first page.

200.description: One page of records, newest end first. An empty `records` array means that nothing matched.

400.description: A filter is invalid (`process.run_record_query_invalid`): `take` outside 1 through 200, a malformed cursor, an unknown `disposition`, an all-zero GUID, a blank or longer than 256 character `participantId`, or `fromUtc` not earlier than `toUtc`. A value of the wrong type, such as text for `take`, is rejected by the framework with HTTP 400 without this envelope.

get.summary: Aggregate the durable records of process runs that ended within a time window.
get.description:
Counts and sums the run records (see `GET /api/processes/runs`) whose run ended at or after `fromUtc` and before `toUtc` and that match the optional filters. The window defaults to the 30 days ending now; either bound can be given alone. `fromUtc` must be earlier than `toUtc`, and the window can be at most 366 days long.

The record counts cover every matching record. Durations, token counts, costs and the activity counts are summed only over records whose facts are available (`factsAvailableRunCount`); compare it with `matchingRunCount` before drawing conclusions. Child runs have their own records, which are counted too, while the totals of a parent's record already include its child runs: sums over a window that contains both therefore count the child runs' usage more than once, and filtering by `rootRunId` still returns both the root record and its children's records. For exact figures of one run tree, read the root run's own record. There is no disposition filter; the breakdown is in `dispositions`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Only records of runs launched for this project; matches only records with assembled facts. The all-zero GUID is rejected.

parameters.name: definitionId
parameters.description: Only records of runs of this process definition; matches only records with assembled facts. The all-zero GUID is rejected.

parameters.name: rootRunId
parameters.description: Only records whose top-level run is this run: its own record and those of its child runs. The all-zero GUID is rejected.

parameters.name: participantId
parameters.description: Only records whose run involved this participant (an executor or agent identifier, see `GET /api/processes/runs`); matches only records with assembled facts. 1 to 256 characters.

parameters.name: fromUtc
parameters.description: Inclusive start of the window. Omitted means 30 days before `toUtc`.

parameters.name: toUtc
parameters.description: Exclusive end of the window. Omitted means now.

200.description: The aggregates for the effective window, which is echoed in `fromUtc` and `toUtc`.

400.description: A filter is invalid (`process.run_record_query_invalid`): `fromUtc` not earlier than `toUtc`, a window longer than 366 days, an all-zero GUID, or a blank or longer than 256 character `participantId`.

get.summary: Read the durable record of one ended process run: summary, a page of hard facts, and the narrative.
get.description:
Returns the record that the server keeps for a run that has ended (completed, failed, cancelled or blocked). The record is created when the run ends and is completed in the background: hard facts are assembled first and a narrative is then generated by a process manager agent, each with its own status, attempt count and retry time in `summary`. `facts` is null until `summary.factsStatus` is Completed, and `narrative` is null until `summary.narrativeStatus` is Completed. A missing or failed narrative does not invalidate facts that are available; check `summary.completeness` and `summary.evidence` before relying on totals.

The facts cover the run and every child run it launched (see `facts.steps[].owningRunId`). Steps and per-minute event buckets are paged separately with zero-based item offsets: `stepOffset` and `stepTake` (1 through 200, default 100), and `runtimeEventMinuteOffset` and `runtimeEventMinuteTake` (1 through 200, default 200). Each page object reports `totalCount` and `hasMore`. Other identifier lists show at most 200 entries next to their stored count.

For a run that is still active, use `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}`: this record does not exist until the run ends, and it is withdrawn while a reactivated run runs again. Use `/graph` for step dependencies.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the ended process run, for example from `GET /api/processes/runs` or from the launch response. The all-zero GUID is rejected.

parameters.name: stepOffset
parameters.description: Number of steps to skip, zero-based. Omitted means 0; must not be negative.

parameters.name: stepTake
parameters.description: Number of steps to return, from 1 through 200. Omitted means 100.

parameters.name: runtimeEventMinuteOffset
parameters.description: Number of per-minute event buckets to skip, zero-based. Omitted means 0; must not be negative.

parameters.name: runtimeEventMinuteTake
parameters.description: Number of per-minute event buckets to return, from 1 through 200. Omitted means 200.

200.description: The record with the requested pages.

400.description: A paging value is out of range, or the run identifier is the all-zero GUID (`process.run_record_query_invalid`). Paging is checked before the record is looked up.

404.description: There is no current record for this run (`process.run_record_not_found`): the run does not exist, has not ended, its end has not been processed yet, or it was reactivated and is running again.

get.summary: Read the step dependency graph of an ended process run, one page of steps at a time.
get.description:
Returns the record summary (as in `/summary`), one page of steps as nodes, and the dependency edges between steps of that page. Nodes include the steps of child runs (see `owningRunId`) and follow the stored step order: the run's own steps first, then those of its child runs. An edge from `sourceStepInstanceId` to `targetStepInstanceId` means that the target step depends on the source step. An edge is returned only when both steps are on the returned page, so request pages that together cover every step to see every edge. While the record's facts are not assembled, the graph is empty (`nodePage.totalCount` 0).

Paging: `stepOffset` is a zero-based number of steps to skip (default 0) and `stepTake` the page size, from 1 through 200 (default 100).

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the ended process run. The all-zero GUID is rejected.

parameters.name: stepOffset
parameters.description: Number of steps to skip, zero-based. Omitted means 0; must not be negative.

parameters.name: stepTake
parameters.description: Number of steps to return, from 1 through 200. Omitted means 100.

200.description: The graph page.

400.description: A paging value is out of range, or the run identifier is the all-zero GUID (`process.run_record_query_invalid`).

404.description: There is no current record for this run (`process.run_record_not_found`): the run does not exist, has not ended, its end has not been processed yet, or it was reactivated and is running again.

get.summary: List the HTTP routes of the process API.
get.description:
Returns a fixed list of the process routes that this host serves, as `METHOD /path` text, and a short informational note. The list is compiled into the server: it does not depend on authorization, configuration or runtime readiness and says nothing about request or response shapes, which this OpenAPI document describes. The operation reads and changes no process state.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

200.description: The route list and the informational note.

post.summary: Prepare a process launch for review and save it, without creating a run.
post.description:
Selects the process definition and live-run profile, compiles an immutable launch plan (steps, assigned agents or workflows, branch gates) and evaluates its readiness, then saves the result as a durable preparation. No run is created and nothing is dispatched, even when `execute` is true. Use it to review what a launch would do; `POST /api/processes/launch` is the operation that accepts a run.

Results, all with HTTP 200:

- Prepared: `stage` `Planned`, `runId` null, and `observation` with the `admissionId` of the saved preparation (`continuationState` `Prepared`). Keep the admission identifier for `GET /api/processes/launch/{admissionId}`; only a repeated check or launch with the same intent and input returns it again.
- Blocked: `stage` `Blocked`, `observation` null, and the reasons in `warnings` and `launchPlan.readinessFindings`. Nothing was saved.
- Already launched: when the preparation identified by `callerIntentId` or `preparedAdmissionId` has since been launched, the response reports its run (`runId`, `stage`) instead of preparing again.

Retries: generate a `callerIntentId` once per intended launch and send it with the check, the launch and every retry. A repeated check with the same intent and identical input returns the same preparation; a launch with the same intent and input then accepts exactly this reviewed plan. Different input under the same intent is rejected with HTTP 409. Without an intent, every check saves a new preparation with a new plan.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host. The preparation is bound to the token's subject: only the same subject can launch or observe it, and the launch must happen before the token used here expires. With authorization disabled, every API caller acts as the same local operator. A `projectId` must name an existing project.

requestBody.description: The launch request: definition, optional profile, project and node, variables, readiness option and retry identifiers.

200.description: The preparation was saved (`stage` `Planned`), readiness blocked it (`stage` `Blocked`, nothing saved), or the identified preparation had already been launched.

403.description: Launch authority was rejected: the bearer token has no `sub` or `exp` claim, or the project named by `projectId` does not exist. No JSON error envelope; the host may return its HTML status page.

400.description: The launch could not be prepared (`process.launch_check_failed`; the cause is logged on the server, not returned). Typical causes: an unknown `definitionKey` or `liveRunProfileKey`, a profile of another definition, an unknown `projectNodeId`, an all-zero identifier, an unknown `preparedAdmissionId`, or a `callerIntentId` or `preparedAdmissionId` that belongs to another caller. A body the framework cannot bind (missing, malformed or not JSON) is rejected with HTTP 400 without this envelope.

409.description: `process.launch_intent_conflict`: the `callerIntentId` or `preparedAdmissionId` already identifies a preparation with different input. Nothing new was saved. Resend the original input, or use a new intent for a different launch.

post.summary: Accept a process run, preparing the launch first or reusing a reviewed preparation.
post.description:
Prepares the launch exactly like `POST /api/processes/launch/check`, or reuses the preparation identified by `callerIntentId` or `preparedAdmissionId`, and then commits the run: run state, immutable plan, step assignments and the first runtime events are saved together and the admission becomes accepted. After the commit the run is activated and its ready steps are scheduled.

- `execute` true also queues the accepted run for background dispatch. The response does not wait for any step to execute.
- `execute` false (the default) accepts and activates the run without queuing it. When the host runs its background dispatch recovery scan, an active run with ready steps can still be dispatched later, so do not use it to keep a run paused; use the check operation to review a launch without a run.

Results, all with HTTP 200: `runId`, `route` and `observation` describe the accepted run. `stage` is usually `Running`. `Planned` means that the run was accepted but activation and scheduling are still pending; the host's continuation worker or a retry with the same intent completes them. `Failed` means that the commit was rejected (`runId` null) or that the run could not be activated. `Blocked` means that readiness blocked the launch and nothing was saved. `warnings` carries the reasons.

Retries: a launch repeated with the same `callerIntentId` (or `preparedAdmissionId`) and identical input returns the same run and creates nothing new. Different input, or a different `execute` value after the run was accepted, is rejected with HTTP 409. Without these identifiers every call creates a new preparation and a new run, and after a lost response you cannot tell whether a run was created: retry only with the same intent, or read `GET /api/processes/launch/{admissionId}` when you have the admission identifier. An HTTP 400 or 403 does not prove that no preparation was saved.

Next: follow the run with `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}`, `GET /api/processes/live` or `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}/events/stream`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host. The preparation is bound to the token's subject, and the authority saved with it (including the expiry of the token that created it) is checked again when the run is accepted. With authorization disabled, every API caller acts as the same local operator. A `projectId` must name an existing project whose lifetime has not changed since the preparation.

requestBody.description: The launch request: definition, optional profile, project and node, variables, readiness option, the `execute` choice and retry identifiers.

200.description: The run was accepted (`runId` set), or the result explains why not (`stage` `Blocked` or `Failed`).

403.description: Launch authority was rejected: the bearer token has no `sub` or `exp` claim, the project named by `projectId` does not exist, or the authority saved with the preparation is no longer valid (for example its token expired or the API authorization settings changed). No JSON error envelope; the host may return its HTML status page.

400.description: The launch could not be completed (`process.launch_failed`; the cause is logged on the server, not returned). Typical causes: an unknown `definitionKey` or `liveRunProfileKey`, a profile of another definition, an unknown `projectNodeId`, an all-zero identifier, an unknown `preparedAdmissionId`, an intent or admission of another caller, or a project whose lifetime changed after the preparation. A body the framework cannot bind (missing, malformed or not JSON) is rejected with HTTP 400 without this envelope.

409.description: `process.launch_intent_conflict`: the `callerIntentId` or `preparedAdmissionId` already identifies a preparation with different input, or an accepted run with a different `execute` value. Nothing new was saved. Resend the original input, or use a new intent for a different launch.

get.summary: Read whether a launch preparation was accepted and how far its continuation got.
get.description:
Returns the saved state of a preparation created by `POST /api/processes/launch/check` or `POST /api/processes/launch`: whether a run was accepted (`acceptedRunId`), how far activation and scheduling got (`continuationState`), the Project Structure link delivery state, and the current runtime status of the accepted run. It is a pure read: it launches, resumes, dispatches and relinks nothing. Use it after a lost launch response or to confirm an acceptance; use `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}` for the run itself.

Only the caller that prepared the launch can read it: another token subject, or with authorization disabled a preparation made in the user interface, gets HTTP 403.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host, with the preparation's subject; otherwise the route is open to the local operator.

parameters.name: admissionId
parameters.description: Identifier of the preparation: `observation.admissionId` from the check or launch response.

200.description: The saved launch state.

403.description: The preparation belongs to another caller or its saved state could not be read. No JSON error envelope; the host may return its HTML status page.

404.description: No preparation has this identifier (`process.launch_not_found`).

post.summary: Execute the ready steps of a process run synchronously, inside this request.
post.description:
Drives one run in the foreground: activates a run that has not started, expires lapsed step claims, and then claims and executes every ready step one after another. It repeats while further steps become ready (at most 200 passes), so a single call can run a whole sequence of steps. The call returns when no step is ready any more, when the run is blocked or has ended, or when a step is handed over to a workflow run or child run that continues on its own. Each agent or workflow step is awaited, bounded by the host's step execution timeout (60 minutes by default; host setting `Processes:RuntimeDispatch:StepExecutionTimeout`), so the request can take a long time.

Use it only when the run has ready work that nothing is progressing, for example a current step in status `Ready` in `GET /api/processes/live` on a host without the background dispatch worker. The call does not go through that worker's queue and does not take its per-run lock, so do not call it while the worker is progressing the same run.

Nothing is executed for a run that has ended (Completed, Failed, Cancelled), is Blocked or is CancelRequested; the response then just reports its current state. An active run with no runnable path left is marked Blocked, and the runtime may then attempt its automatic blocked-run recovery. A step failure is reported in the body (for example `status` Failed), not as an HTTP error.

Completed work is not executed again, but every call can execute newly ready steps, so a repeat is not free of effects: read the run before calling again. If the client disconnects, the step being executed is cancelled and its claim released; effects that the step had already caused are not rolled back. An unexpected runtime failure, such as a stored plan that no longer matches the run, is not mapped to an error envelope.

Before responding, the server projects one bounded batch of pending runtime events into the read models. Read `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}` and `/history` afterwards; that read-back, not this response, is the evidence of what happened.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the process run, for example `runId` returned by `POST /api/processes/launch`.

requestBody.description: Optional label of the caller. The JSON object is required: send `{}` to use the default label.

200.description: The dispatch finished. `stage` and `status` describe the run afterwards and `diagnostics` explain what happened.

404.description: No process run has this identifier (`process.run_not_found`).

post.summary: Cancel a process run, including its child runs.
post.description:
Cancels within this request rather than queuing a request. For a top-level run: the run becomes CancelRequested, every step that has not finished is cancelled together with its open claims, agent executions of the run that are active in this server are told to stop, the child runs (subprocesses) are cancelled, and the run finally becomes Cancelled. A child run is cancelled on its own, without its parent or siblings. Cancellation does not roll back what agents, workflows or tools have already done.

Once the run exists, the outcome is reported in the body with HTTP 200:

- `Applied`: the run is now Cancelled.
- `Rejected`: nothing more was done. The run had already ended (Completed, Failed or Cancelled), concurrent changes kept the cancellation from being saved, or a child run could not be cancelled yet; in the last case the top-level run stays CancelRequested, `diagnostics` name the child runs, and you can call again.

The `reason` is not stored with the run. Before responding, the server projects one bounded batch of pending runtime events into the read models; confirm the result with `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}` and, when the run record exists, `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}/summary`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the process run to cancel, for example `runId` returned by `POST /api/processes/launch`. For a child run, only that run is cancelled.

requestBody.description: Optional caller label and reason. The JSON object is required: send `{}` to use the defaults.

200.description: The request was processed. Check `outcome`: only `Applied` means that the run was cancelled.

404.description: No process run has this identifier (`process.run_not_found`).

post.summary: Send one step of a process run back for rework, with an instruction for its executor.
post.description:
Resets the step to Ready and makes the run Active again within this request. A run that had failed or was blocked is reactivated; a Completed or Cancelled run cannot be reworked. Only the named step is reset: steps that depend on it are not reset. The `reason` becomes the step's rework instruction and is given to the agent or workflow that executes the step next, so write a concrete correction and never include secrets. The step is then queued for background dispatch; it is not executed inside this request.

Once the run exists, the outcome is reported in the body with HTTP 200:

- `Applied`: the step was reset for rework.
- `Duplicate`: the step was already Ready in an active run; the instruction was still updated and the step queued.
- `Rejected`: nothing changed, and `diagnostics` say why: the step is not part of this run or is not executable, the run has completed or was cancelled, the step is claimed or running, the step is not Waiting, Blocked or Failed, its prerequisites are not satisfied, or another step of the run holds an open claim.

Before responding, the server projects one bounded batch of pending runtime events into the read models; follow the step with `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}` and `/history`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the process run that owns the step, as shown in `runId` of the step in the run's detail or live projection.

parameters.name: stepInstanceId
parameters.description: Identifier of the step within the run: `stepInstanceId` from the launch plan, the current step of `GET /api/processes/live` or the run's diagnostics and lineage.

requestBody.description: Optional caller label and the rework instruction. The JSON object is required; send a specific `reason`.

200.description: The request was processed. Check `outcome`: `Applied` and `Duplicate` mean that the step is queued for rework; `Rejected` means that nothing changed.

404.description: No process run has this identifier (`process.run_not_found`).

get.summary: List process runs with recent activity, including their current step, from the live projection.
get.description:
Returns the live projection of the process runs whose last runtime event occurred within the last `windowMinutes`, most recent activity first, at most `take` runs. Runs that have ended are included while their last event is inside the window. Child runs (subprocesses) are separate entries with their own `runId` and the `rootRunId` of their tree. For each run it shows the status, up to 20 recent events, the step that is being worked on or is next, the child runs it waits for, and current diagnostics.

The live projection is updated as runtime events are projected and can lag behind the runtime; see `freshness`. It is not a durable run record: use `GET /api/processes/runs` for ended runs outside the window, and `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}` for one run with its result lineage. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host, and every run is visible to that caller; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Maximum number of runs, from 1 through 500. Omitted means 50; values outside the range are clamped.

parameters.name: windowMinutes
parameters.description: How long ago, in minutes, the last event of a run may have occurred, from 1 through 43,200 (30 days). Omitted means 240 (4 hours); values outside the range are clamped.

200.description: The runs, most recent activity first. An empty `runs` array means that no run had an event within the window.

get.summary: Read the live detail of one process run: status, recent events, current diagnostics and result lineage.
get.description:
Returns the projected detail of a run of any age, including a child run: its status, first and last event times, up to 20 most recent events, the current diagnostics (from the latest results of steps that are now Blocked or Failed), and the lineage of every applied step result with its produced artifacts and recovery decision. Use it to follow a run after launch, dispatch, cancellation or rework. For an ended run, `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}/summary` returns the durable record (hard facts, usage, costs and narrative); `/history` returns the event timeline and `/graph` the step dependencies.

The detail is a projection, updated as runtime events are projected; `freshness` shows how current it is. A run that was just accepted can be missing until its first events are projected. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the process run: `runId` from `POST /api/processes/launch`, a `runs[].runId` of `GET /api/processes/live`, or a `childRunId` of a waiting step.

200.description: The run detail.

404.description: No projected detail exists for this identifier (`process.run_not_found`): the run does not exist, or its first events have not been projected yet.

get.summary: Read the projected runtime events of one process run within a time window, oldest first.
get.description:
Returns the events of this run whose `occurredAtUtc` is at or after `fromUtc` and before `toUtc`, in ascending `globalSequence` order. Events of child runs are not included; read each child run separately. By default the window is the 24 hours before now.

At most `take` events are returned, and they are the oldest ones in the window. There is no continuation value: when `take` events are returned, more can exist, so request again with `fromUtc` set to the `occurredAtUtc` of the last event you received and skip events you already have by `eventId`.

Restricted events are included with a generic summary. An unknown run returns an empty list, not HTTP 404. `freshness` is derived from the last returned event. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the process run, for example `runId` from `POST /api/processes/launch`.

parameters.name: fromUtc
parameters.description: Inclusive start of the window, an instant with offset (converted to UTC). Omitted means 24 hours before `toUtc`. It must be earlier than `toUtc`; otherwise the request currently fails with a generic HTTP 500 that has no error envelope.

parameters.name: toUtc
parameters.description: Exclusive end of the window, an instant with offset. Omitted means now.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Maximum number of events, from 1 through 1,000. Omitted means 100; values outside the range are clamped.

200.description: The events in the window, oldest first. An empty `events` array means that there were none, or that the run is unknown.

get.summary: Stream lifecycle change signals of all process runs as server-sent events.
get.description:
Opens a long-lived `text/event-stream` response. Each time this server has projected a runtime event of any process run into its read models, it sends one `process.run.changed` event. The event is a signal, not the state: after receiving one, read the current state with `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}` (live detail), `GET /api/processes/live` or `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}/history`. Use `GET /api/processes/runs/{runId}/events/stream` to receive the events of a single run only.

Frames (LF line endings; each JSON object on a single `data:` line):

- A change signal: `id: 1287`, `event: process.run.changed`, `data: {JSON object}`. The `id` is a sequence number of this stream in this server process, not the event's `globalSequence`. It increases while the process runs and starts again at 1 after a restart.
- A gap notice: `event: stream.gap` with `data` members `reason`, `requestedAfterSequence`, `firstAvailableSequence`, `lastAvailableSequence`, `resumeAfterSequence` and `snapshotUrl` (always null here). `cursorBeforeRetention` means that older events were dropped and replay continues with the oldest retained one; `cursorAheadOfStream` (for example after a server restart) means that only new events follow. After a gap, read the state again instead of relying on the missed events.
- A heartbeat comment, `: heartbeat` followed by the current UTC instant, while no event is pending (every 15 seconds by default; host setting `Api:ServerSentEvents:HeartbeatIntervalSeconds`).

The `data` of `process.run.changed` is a camel-case JSON object with these members:

- `eventId`, `rootRunId`, `runId`: objects of the form `{"value":"GUID"}`, not plain strings. `rootRunId` is the top-level run of a subprocess tree and equals `runId` for a top-level run.
- `globalSequence`: position of the runtime event in the durable event log across all runs. `rootSequence`: 1-based position of the event within its root run.
- `category`: `started` (run created, activated or reactivated), `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled` (the run reached that terminal state), `needsAttention` (the run or a step is blocked, step rework was requested, or the process manager raised an incident, escalated a loop budget, denied a recovery or rejected a branch decision) or `progress` (every other event, including a failed step attempt and a cancellation request).
- `eventType`: the runtime event type name, for example `ProcessRunCompleted`, or `RestrictedRuntimeEvent` when the event is restricted. `sensitivity`: `normal` or `restricted`.
- `occurredAtUtc`: instant of the runtime event. `isTerminal`: true for completed, failed and cancelled. `needsAttention`: true for needsAttention and failed.

Example `data`: `{"eventId":{"value":"6f1d2c3b-8a4e-4f0b-9c55-2b7e1a9d4c10"},"globalSequence":90412, "rootSequence":37,"rootRunId":{"value":"0b8e6f3a-5d2c-4e71-a1f9-7c3d2e4b5a60"}, "runId":{"value":"0b8e6f3a-5d2c-4e71-a1f9-7c3d2e4b5a60"},"category":"completed", "eventType":"ProcessRunCompleted","sensitivity":"normal","occurredAtUtc":"2026-09-19T08:15:30.1234567+00:00", "isTerminal":true,"needsAttention":false}`

Resuming: send the last received `id` in the `Last-Event-ID` header (browser `EventSource` clients do this when they reconnect) or in the `after` query parameter; if both are sent they must be equal. Retained events with a larger `id` are replayed first, then live events follow. Without a cursor, every retained event is replayed first. The server retains the most recent events of all runs together (1,024 by default; host setting `Api:ServerSentEvents:ReplayCapacity`).

Delivery is best effort. Events are kept only in the memory of this server process; an event whose publication fails is skipped; an event can occasionally arrive twice (de-duplicate on `eventId`); a switch of the active database profile ends the response, so reconnect. The stream does not end by itself, not even after a terminal event.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host, and the stream then shows every run to that caller; otherwise the route is open.

200.description: The open event stream (`text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`, not cached). It stays open until the client disconnects or the server ends it.

400.description: The cursor is invalid (`sse.cursor-invalid`): `Last-Event-ID` or `after` is repeated, is not a non-negative integer, or the two values differ. Returned as a JSON error envelope before the stream starts.

get.summary: Stream lifecycle change signals of one process run as server-sent events.
get.description:
Same stream as `GET /api/processes/events/stream`, filtered to events whose `runId` equals the route value. Events of child runs (subprocesses) are not included: a child run shares the parent's `rootRunId` but has its own `runId`, so subscribe to it separately or use the all-runs stream.

The run is not checked for existence. An unknown identifier gets an open stream with heartbeats and possibly `stream.gap` frames, but never a `process.run.changed` event. Frame `id` values of this stream have gaps, because events of other runs are skipped; resume with the last `id` you received.

Frames, the `data` object, resuming with `Last-Event-ID` or `after`, delivery guarantees and the recommended read-back are exactly as described for `GET /api/processes/events/stream`. A terminal event (`isTerminal` true) does not close this stream; close it yourself when you no longer need it.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: Identifier of the process run to observe, for example `runId` from `POST /api/processes/launch` or from `GET /api/processes/live`. The all-zero GUID is rejected.

200.description: The open event stream (`text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`). It stays open until the client disconnects or the server ends it.

400.description: Rejected before the stream starts, as a JSON error envelope: `processes.run-id-invalid` (the all-zero GUID) or `sse.cursor-invalid` (`Last-Event-ID` or `after` is repeated, is not a non-negative integer, or the two values differ).

get.summary: List all configured memory provider profiles.
get.description:
Experimental API: memory providers are an experimental integration and this contract can still change.

Returns every memory provider profile the host knows, enabled or not, ordered by display name (ignoring letter case) and then by provider identifier. The list is not paged. An empty array means that no provider is configured, which is a valid deployment. Each item has the same shape as `GET /api/memory-providers/{providerId}`; transport settings name credential environment variables but never contain credential values. The read has no side effects.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.memory-providers.read` scope.

200.description: All memory provider profiles; an empty array when none is configured.

get.summary: Read one memory provider profile by its provider identifier.
get.description:
Experimental API: memory providers are an experimental integration and this contract can still change.

Returns the configuration, advertised capabilities, limits and last recorded health of the profile. Transport settings name credential environment variables but never contain credential values. The read has no side effects and does not contact the provider.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.memory-providers.read` scope.

parameters.name: providerId
parameters.description: Identifier of the provider profile, as chosen when it was saved with `PUT /api/memory-providers/{providerId}` and returned as `providerId`. Surrounding whitespace is ignored; at most 256 characters without control characters.

200.description: The provider profile.

400.description: The identifier is blank, longer than 256 characters or contains control characters (`memory-provider.request-invalid`).

404.description: No profile has this identifier (`memory-provider.not-found`).

put.summary: Create a memory provider profile or replace the configuration of an existing one.
put.description:
Experimental API: memory providers are an experimental integration and this contract can still change.

Upsert by provider identifier: when no profile has the identifier, a new profile is created; otherwise its configuration is replaced by the request. There is no concurrency check, so the last write wins. Sending the same body again stores the same configuration. The operation stores configuration only; it does not contact the provider or check that it is reachable, so `healthState` keeps its last recorded value (`Unknown` for a new profile).

What the request replaces: the display name, driver kind, enabled flag, fallback behavior, provider kind, selection tags, the three query and status capabilities, and the transport of the driver kind. Saving through this operation also turns off the ingestion, feedback and event capabilities of the profile, because this API cannot configure them, and removes the stored settings of the other transport when the driver kind changes. The user-interface capabilities, provider limits and protocol version of an existing profile are kept; the workspace scope is always all workspaces.

Rules checked before anything is saved (HTTP 400, `memory-provider.request-invalid`):

- `Http` and `NativeRemote` drivers need `http` and no `mcp`; `Mcp` needs `mcp` and no `http`; `Mock` takes neither.
- Each driver runs only some capabilities: `Http`, `NativeRemote` and `Mock` support synchronous queries only; `Mcp` supports synchronous queries, asynchronous queries and operation status.
- Asynchronous queries require operation-status support, because polling is the only completion path.
- An MCP profile with a query capability needs `contextQueryTool`, and with asynchronous queries or operation status also `operationStatusTool`.
- Endpoints are absolute HTTPS addresses, or HTTP to a loopback address, without user information, query or fragment; credentials are referenced by environment-variable name, never sent as values.

A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON, an unknown member or a wrong JSON type) is rejected with HTTP 400 before the operation runs, without the `errors` envelope.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.memory-providers.write` scope. Read the result back with `GET /api/memory-providers/{providerId}` when needed.

parameters.name: providerId
parameters.description: Identifier of the profile to create or replace, chosen by the caller, for example `provider.team-memory`. Surrounding whitespace is removed; at most 256 characters without control characters. It is the profile's permanent identity: use it in every later memory-provider request.

requestBody.description: The complete configuration of the profile.

200.description: The configuration was saved; the body is the stored profile.

400.description: Nothing was saved (`memory-provider.request-invalid`): the identifier or a value is invalid, or the driver, capabilities and transport do not fit together. The message names the rule.

post.summary: Query one memory provider for context, synchronously or as an asynchronous operation.
post.description:
Experimental API: memory providers are an experimental integration and this contract can still change.

Sends the query text to exactly the provider named in the route; no other provider is used as a fallback. The provider must exist, be enabled and support the capability of the requested mode: `context.query.sync` for `Synchronous` or `context.query.async` for `Asynchronous`. Before calling the provider the host records an operation in its memory operation ledger; that operation belongs to the caller: the bearer token's subject when API authorization is enabled, otherwise one local identity shared by all callers.

The status code follows `status` in the body, which always has the same shape:

- 200 (`Completed`): `contextPack` holds the retrieved context.
- 202 (`Accepted`): the provider started an asynchronous operation. Poll `GET /api/memory-providers/operations/{operationId}` with `acceptedOperation.operationId`, waiting at least `pollAfterSeconds` between reads, until the operation ends or `expiresAtUtc` passes.
- 403 and 404: the provider was not selected and nothing was dispatched (`driverDispatchAttempted` is false); `selection` explains why.
- 409: the query cannot run. Usually the provider was not selected and nothing was dispatched (for example `ProviderDisabled`); `UnsupportedOperation` means the provider was called and reported that it does not support the query.
- 502 and 504: dispatch failed or timed out; `driverDispatchAttempted` tells whether the provider was contacted, and `operation` records the failure.

Every call creates a new operation; a retry is a new query and never resumes an earlier operation. Retry a 502 or 504 only as a new query.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.memory-providers.query` scope.

parameters.name: providerId
parameters.description: Identifier of the provider profile to query, as returned by `GET /api/memory-providers`. Surrounding whitespace is ignored; at most 256 characters without control characters.

requestBody.description: The query text and the query mode.

200.description: The query completed; `contextPack` holds the result.

202.description: The provider accepted an asynchronous operation; poll it through `acceptedOperation`.

403.description: Selection denied the provider (`status` `ProviderDenied` or `CapabilityDenied`), for example because the profile is bound to a single workspace, which the host cannot verify. A 403 whose body is the general `errors` envelope instead (`memory-provider.identity-missing`) means the bearer token has no subject.

404.description: No profile has this identifier (`status` `ProviderNotFound`).

409.description: The query cannot run: usually the provider was not selected and nothing was dispatched, for example `ProviderDisabled` or `CapabilityUnavailable` (the profile does not advertise the capability of the mode); `UnsupportedOperation` means the provider was called and rejected the query as unsupported.

502.description: The query failed (`DriverUnavailable`, `DriverFailed` or `Failed`), for example because the provider could not be reached or returned an invalid result.

504.description: The provider did not answer in time (`TimedOut`).

400.description: The request was rejected before any operation was recorded (`memory-provider.request-invalid`): the query is blank or longer than 32,768 characters after trimming, the identifier is invalid, or the mode is unknown. A body the framework cannot bind (malformed JSON, an unknown member or a wrong JSON type) is also rejected with 400, without the `errors` envelope.

get.summary: Read the progress of a memory operation that the caller created with a provider query.
get.description:
Experimental API: memory providers are an experimental integration and this contract can still change.

Use it to poll an asynchronous query accepted by `POST /api/memory-providers/{providerId}/queries`. It returns the host's ledger record of the operation (`operation.status`, retry and transition counts and timestamps); it does not contact the provider and it returns no context pack. The record advances only when the host updates it, for example when its memory background workers are enabled and poll the provider, so a record can stay `Accepted` or `Running` when those workers are disabled. Stop polling when `operation.status` is `Completed`, `Failed`, `TimedOut`, `Cancelled`, `Expired` or `Forgotten`.

Only the caller that created the operation can read it: the same bearer token subject when API authorization is enabled, otherwise the shared local identity. The provider that ran the operation must still exist, be enabled and advertise `operations.status`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the `api` or `api.memory-providers.read` scope.

parameters.name: operationId
parameters.description: Identifier (GUID) of the operation, from `acceptedOperation.operationId` or `operation.operationId` of the query response. A value that is not a GUID does not match this route.

200.description: The operation record (`status` `Completed` means the read succeeded).

403.description: The operation belongs to another caller (`status` `AccessDenied`) or its provider was denied by selection; `operation` is null. A 403 with the general `errors` envelope instead (`memory-provider.identity-missing`) means the bearer token has no subject.

404.description: The operation does not exist (`NotFound`) or its provider profile no longer exists (`ProviderNotFound`).

409.description: The operation's provider cannot report status now, for example `ProviderDisabled` or `CapabilityUnavailable` (it no longer advertises `operations.status`).

400.description: The identifier is the empty GUID (`memory-provider.request-invalid`).

get.summary: List the plugins that this host provides, with their installation state.
get.description:
Returns every plugin that a current source provides (plugins bundled with the host and plugins of installed packages), plus plugins recorded as installed that no current source provides any more (`availability` 1 Unavailable), ordered by display name. Packages in the server's catalogue folder that are not installed are not listed here; see `GET /api/plugins/packages/catalog`. Each item contains the full manifest in `descriptor`: workflow executors, settings forms, connection kinds and the public OAuth configuration, never secrets. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

200.description: The plugins, ordered by display name.

get.summary: List the plugin packages that are available to install or already installed on this host.
get.description:
Lists the `.zip` plugin packages in the server's catalogue folder and the installed package folders, one entry per package identifier (a catalogue file takes precedence over an installed folder), ordered by display name. Plugins bundled with the host are not packages and are not listed. Install a catalogue package with `POST /api/plugins/packages/catalog/{packageId}/install`, or upload a package with `POST /api/plugins/packages/upload`. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

200.description: The packages, ordered by display name.

get.summary: Download the icon file of an installed plugin package.
get.description:
Returns the icon file that the manifest of an installed plugin package declares, as binary content. The media type follows the file extension: `.svg` image/svg+xml, `.png` image/png, `.jpg` and `.jpeg` image/jpeg, `.webp` image/webp, anything else application/octet-stream. The response carries a `Last-Modified` header. Only installed packages have icons here: packages that are only in the catalogue folder and plugins bundled with the host get HTTP 404. Plugin icons of kind 2 (PackageAsset) refer to this operation.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: packageId
parameters.description: Identifier of the installed package, for example `candoitall.docker.package`; letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, matched case-insensitively.

200.description: The icon file.

404.description: No installed package has this identifier, or its icon file is missing. No JSON error envelope; the host may return its HTML status page.

400.description: The identifier contains other characters (`plugins.package-id-invalid`).

get.summary: List the newest plugin installation and runtime log entries.
get.description:
Returns the 100 newest entries of the plugin log, newest first, optionally filtered by stream, plugin and package; the filters combine with AND and match exact identifiers. The log records package uploads and installations, plugin installation, enabling and disabling, restart requirements, and the runs and events of plugin workflow executors, with secrets redacted from messages and details. There is no paging: narrow the filters to reach older entries. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: streamKind
parameters.description: Only entries of this stream, as an integer: 0 Installation or 1 Runtime. The names `Installation` and `Runtime`, with exactly this casing, are also accepted. Omitted means both streams.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Only entries of this plugin, for example `gmail.mail`; letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, compared after lower-casing. Omitted or blank means all plugins.

parameters.name: packageId
parameters.description: Only entries of this package, for example `candoitall.docker.package`; same format as `pluginId`. Omitted or blank means all packages.

200.description: The entries, newest first; at most 100.

400.description: An identifier contains characters other than letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_` (`plugins.plugin-id-invalid` or `plugins.package-id-invalid`). A `streamKind` that is neither a number nor a member name is rejected by the framework with HTTP 400 without this envelope.

post.summary: Install a plugin package from the server's package catalogue.
post.description:
Finds the `.zip` package in the server's catalogue folder whose manifest declares this package identifier, validates it, extracts it into the installed packages folder, records the plugin as installed (enabled unless `enable` is false) and writes installation log entries. An existing installation of the same package is replaced without a version comparison. The hash and signature declared by the manifest are not verified.

The plugin appears in `GET /api/plugins/catalog` at once, but when the package contains .NET assemblies or declares that it needs a restart, its code (for example its workflow executors) runs only after the host restarts: `restartRequired` is then true, and `POST /api/plugins/runtime/restart` requests the restart. Installing grants no capabilities; decide them with `PUT /api/plugins/{pluginId}/grants`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: packageId
parameters.description: Identifier of the package, as listed by `GET /api/plugins/packages/catalog`; letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, matched case-insensitively.

requestBody.description: Installation options. The JSON object is required; send `{}` for the defaults.

200.description: The package was installed; check `restartRequired`.

400.description: The package was not installed: `plugins.package-id-invalid` (invalid identifier characters), `plugins.package-not-found` (no catalogue package declares this identifier), `plugins.package-invalid` (missing or invalid manifest, missing icon or assembly, unsafe path, or too large), or a manifest validation code.

post.summary: Upload a plugin package file and install it.
post.description:
Accepts a `.zip` plugin package as the form field `file` of a `multipart/form-data` body and installs it like a catalogue package: validation, extraction into the installed packages folder (replacing an existing installation of the same package identifier), installation record and log entries. The archive must contain `plugin.package.json` at its root with the plugin and package metadata, a display name, a version and an icon path; a package cannot declare itself bundled or trusted at application level. The hash and signature declared by the manifest are not verified, and the uploaded file name is used only in messages.

Size: the file and its extracted content may each be at most 100 MiB by default (host setting `PluginPackages:MaxPackageBytes`); the web server's request body limit also applies and can be lower.

`restartRequired` true means that the package's code runs only after a host restart (`POST /api/plugins/runtime/restart`). Installing grants no capabilities.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: enable
parameters.description: False installs the plugin disabled. Omitted or true installs it enabled.

requestBody.description: The plugin package file (`.zip`), sent as the form field `file`. It must not be empty.

file.description: The plugin package file (`.zip`). It must not be empty.

200.description: The package was installed; check `restartRequired`.

400.description: The package was not installed: `plugins.package-upload-empty` (empty file), `plugins.package-upload-invalid` (the upload could not be stored or exceeds the size limit), `plugins.package-invalid` (not a valid package) or a manifest validation code. A request without the `file` form field is rejected by the framework with HTTP 400 without this envelope.

get.summary: Read whether the host must restart to activate installed plugin packages.
get.description:
Returns the plugin restart state kept on the server: whether an installed package needs a host restart and whether a restart was requested. The state is cleared when the host starts, so after a restart `isRestartRequired` is false again and `processId` is that of the new host process. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

200.description: The restart state; every flag is false when nothing is pending.

post.summary: Stop the host so that it restarts with the installed plugin packages.
post.description:
Allowed only while a restart is required (`isRestartRequired` true). It records the request and, about 0.75 seconds after responding, stops the host application. This API does not start the host again: it comes back only when a process supervisor, such as a service manager or a container runtime, restarts it. Stopping the host interrupts every user and all running work of the host, so request it deliberately.

After the host is back, read `GET /api/plugins/runtime/restart-status` (a new `processId`) and `GET /api/plugins/catalog`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

requestBody.description: The JSON object is required; send `{}`.

200.description: The restart was requested; the host stops shortly after this response.

400.description: No installed package requires a restart (`plugins.restart-not-required`).

post.summary: Install a plugin that a current source provides, enabled or disabled.
post.description:
Records the plugin as installed from its manifest in the plugin catalog (a bundled plugin or a plugin of an installed package), enabled unless `enable` is false. Installing again replaces the saved manifest and the enabled state and keeps the original installation time. Installing grants no capabilities: the plugin can use a capability only after `PUT /api/plugins/{pluginId}/grants` grants it. To add a new package, use the package operations first.

After success the host also refreshes its managed example workflow definitions when example seeding is enabled (host setting `Workflows:ExampleSeed:Enabled`), so plugin-based examples can appear.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the plugin, as listed by `GET /api/plugins/catalog`, for example `gmail.mail`.

requestBody.description: Installation options. The JSON object is required; send `{}` for the defaults.

200.description: The plugin is installed; the body is its updated catalog entry.

400.description: Not installed: `plugins.plugin-id-invalid` (invalid identifier characters), `plugins.not-found` (no current source provides the plugin; this API reports it with HTTP 400) or a manifest validation code.

post.summary: Enable an installed plugin.
post.description:
Marks the installed plugin as enabled. It takes effect for the next capability evaluation, without a restart. Enabling grants nothing: the plugin can use a capability only when it is also granted. Repeating the call is harmless but updates `updatedAtUtc` and writes a log entry. After success the host refreshes its example workflow definitions when example seeding is enabled.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the installed plugin, for example `gmail.mail`.

requestBody.description: The JSON object is required; send `{}`.

200.description: The plugin is enabled; the body is its updated catalog entry.

400.description: Not enabled: `plugins.plugin-id-invalid` (invalid identifier characters) or `plugins.not-installed` (install the plugin first).

post.summary: Disable an installed plugin.
post.description:
Marks the installed plugin as disabled. From the next evaluation on, its workflow executors and OAuth operations are refused; saved grants and connections are kept, so enabling it again restores them. Code of an installed package stays loaded until the next host restart. Repeating the call is harmless.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the installed plugin, for example `gmail.mail`.

requestBody.description: The JSON object is required; send `{}`.

200.description: The plugin is disabled; the body is its updated catalog entry.

400.description: Not disabled: `plugins.plugin-id-invalid` (invalid identifier characters) or `plugins.not-installed`.

get.summary: Read the settings view of one plugin: catalog entry, grants, connections, host tool recipes and OAuth metadata.
get.description:
Combines, for one plugin, its catalog entry, its effective grants (including synthesized undecided entries), its saved connections, the host tool recipes it can request, the connection kinds it declares and its public OAuth configuration. Connection settings are returned as saved; OAuth tokens and client secrets are never returned. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the plugin, for example `gmail.mail`.

200.description: The settings view.

400.description: `plugins.plugin-id-invalid` (invalid identifier characters) or `plugins.not-found` (no current source provides the plugin; this API reports it with HTTP 400).

get.summary: List the effective capability grants of a plugin.
get.description:
Returns one entry per capability that the plugin declares and per host tool recipe that it offers, each either the saved decision or a synthesized undecided entry (state 0 Requested), followed by any other saved grants, ordered by capability value and then recipe. At runtime a capability is allowed only when the plugin is installed and enabled, declares the capability, and has a plugin-scope grant in state 1 Granted for exactly that capability; a host tool recipe needs its own grant and the HostCommand grant. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the plugin, for example `gmail.mail`.

200.description: The effective grants.

400.description: `plugins.plugin-id-invalid` (invalid identifier characters) or `plugins.not-found` (no current source provides the plugin).

put.summary: Save a capability grant decision for a plugin.
put.description:
Creates, or replaces the decision of, the grant identified by `capability`, `recipeId`, `scopeKind` and `scopeKey`, and records `api` as the actor. The decision applies from the next evaluation, without a restart. Only the state is validated: whether the plugin exists, whether it declares the capability, whether the recipe exists and whether the scope fits are not checked, and only plugin-scope grants of a single declared capability take effect. Read `GET /api/plugins/{pluginId}/grants` first and send one of its entries with the new state.

After success the host refreshes its example workflow definitions when example seeding is enabled.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open. Grants apply to the whole host, not to one caller; a HostCommand grant lets the plugin run its reviewed host commands.
