parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the plugin, for example `candoitall.docker`.

requestBody.description: The grant identity and decision. Send `capability` and `state`.

200.description: The decision was saved; the body is the saved grant.

400.description: Not saved: `plugins.plugin-id-invalid` (invalid identifier characters) or `plugins.grant-state-invalid` (state 0 Requested or 4 Unavailable).

get.summary: List the saved connections of a plugin.
get.description:
Returns the plugin's saved connections, ordered by connection key and then display name, with their settings exactly as saved. OAuth state is read with `GET /api/plugins/{pluginId}/oauth/status`; tokens are never returned. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the plugin, for example `gmail.mail`.

200.description: The connections; empty when there are none.

400.description: `plugins.plugin-id-invalid` (invalid identifier characters) or `plugins.not-found` (no current source provides the plugin).

post.summary: Create a plugin connection, or replace the display name, settings and enabled flag of an existing one.
post.description:
Without `id`, creates a connection of the given connection kind. With `id`, replaces the display name, settings and enabled flag of that connection of this plugin and keeps its connection key; an `id` that no connection of this plugin has creates a connection with that identifier. The server does not check the plugin or the connection key against the catalog and stores `settingsJson` without validating it, so read `connectionDescriptors` of `GET /api/plugins/{pluginId}/settings` first and send a declared key and the fields of its settings form. Settings are returned unredacted: never put secrets in them. OAuth connections are authorized afterwards with `POST /api/plugins/{pluginId}/oauth/start`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the plugin, for example `gmail.mail`.

requestBody.description: The connection to create or replace.

200.description: The connection was saved; the body is the saved connection with its identifier.

400.description: Not saved: `plugins.plugin-id-invalid` (invalid identifier characters) or `plugins.connection-display-name-required` (blank display name).

get.summary: List the OAuth state of a plugin's connections.
get.description:
Returns one entry per connection of this plugin that has OAuth state, ordered by connection key. OAuth state is created when an authorization callback completes or fails and is reset by a disconnect. A connected entry whose stored token lacks a scope that the plugin requires is reported as 2 ReconnectRequired with `lastErrorCode` `oauth-scope-missing`. Tokens are never returned. An unknown plugin returns an empty list. The read changes nothing.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the plugin, for example `gmail.mail`.

200.description: The OAuth state entries; empty when there are none.

400.description: The identifier contains invalid characters (`plugins.plugin-id-invalid`).

post.summary: Start the OAuth authorization of a plugin connection and return the address where the user signs in.
post.description:
Prepares an OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for the connection kind named by `connectionKey`: selects or creates the connection (a new one is saved before the user signs in), creates a one-time `state` and, when the plugin uses PKCE, a code verifier, and returns `authorizationUrl`. Open that address in the user's browser. After sign-in the identity provider sends the browser to `GET /api/plugins/oauth/callback`, which stores the tokens and redirects to `returnPath`. The pending authorization expires after 10 minutes and can be completed once.

Prerequisites: the plugin is in the catalog, declares OAuth for this connection kind, is installed and enabled, and has the OAuth2 capability (128) granted. The OAuth client identifier comes from the connection setting `clientId` or from the plugin. The callback also needs the client secret in the server environment variable that the plugin's OAuth configuration names.

Next: after the browser returns, read `GET /api/plugins/{pluginId}/oauth/status`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the plugin, for example `gmail.mail`.

requestBody.description: Connection kind, optional connection, return path, scopes and redirect address.

200.description: The authorization was prepared; open `authorizationUrl`.

400.description: Not started: `plugins.plugin-id-invalid`, `plugins.not-found` (not in the catalog), `plugins.oauth-descriptor-missing` (no OAuth for this connection key), `plugins.oauth-grant-denied` (not installed, not enabled, or OAuth2 not granted), `plugins.connection-not-found` (`connectionId` is not a connection of this plugin) or `plugins.oauth-client-id-missing`. A connection created by this request remains when the client identifier is missing.

post.summary: Delete the stored OAuth tokens of a plugin connection.
post.description:
Deletes the connection's stored tokens and sets its OAuth state to 0 NotConnected. It does not revoke the tokens at the identity provider and keeps the connection and its settings; authorize again with `POST /api/plugins/{pluginId}/oauth/start`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host; otherwise the route is open.

parameters.name: pluginId
parameters.description: Identifier of the plugin, for example `gmail.mail`.

parameters.name: connectionId
parameters.description: Identifier of the connection: `id` of a saved connection or `connectionId` of an OAuth state entry.

200.description: The tokens were deleted; `status` is 0 NotConnected.

400.description: `plugins.plugin-id-invalid` (invalid identifier characters) or `plugins.oauth-connection-not-found` (the connection has no OAuth state).

get.summary: Complete an OAuth authorization when the identity provider sends the user's browser back.
get.description:
This is the redirect target registered with the identity provider, not an operation for API clients: the browser arrives here after sign-in with `state` and either `code` or `error`. The server checks the one-time `state` created by `POST /api/plugins/{pluginId}/oauth/start`, exchanges the code for tokens at the provider's token endpoint, keeps the tokens in its secret store (never in a response) and marks the connection as connected.

It always answers with a redirect, a relative path in the `Location` header, to the start request's `returnPath` with the query parameters `oauth` (`connected` or `failed`), `connectionId` and, on failure, `reason`: for example `state-used`, `expired`, `missing-code`, the provider's error code, or a token exchange failure code such as `plugins.oauth-client-secret-missing`. A missing or unknown `state` redirects to `/plugins?oauth=failed` with `reason` `missing-state` or `invalid-state`.

Authority: anonymous. The route accepts requests without a bearer token even when API authorization is enabled, because the browser returns from the identity provider without one; the single-use `state` ties the callback to the pending authorization.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: One-time state value that the start operation put into the authorization address.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Authorization code issued by the identity provider after a successful sign-in.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Error code sent by the identity provider when sign-in failed or was declined.

parameters.name: error_description
parameters.description: Error description sent by the identity provider.

302.description: Redirect to the return path with the outcome in its query string. Failures are reported in the same way, never with an error status.

get.summary: List CRM/HR parties that match optional text, tag and party-type filters, one page at a time.
get.description:
Returns people, organizations, organization units and AI agents recorded as CRM/HR parties, ordered by display name and then party identifier. Archived parties are excluded unless `IncludeArchived` is true. Use the returned `id` with the other `/api/crm-hr/parties/{partyId}` operations; a party identifier is not a login account, workforce-profile or recruitment-application identifier.

Sensitive parties are listed with their display name, type and status, but their external code, summary and tags are returned empty, their external code and summary are not searched and they never match a tag filter.

Paging is zero-based: request the next page with `PageIndex` + 1 while `pageIndex` + 1 is less than `totalPages`. Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: Search
parameters.description: Text matched case-insensitively as a substring of the display name and, for parties that are not sensitive, of the external code and summary. Surrounding whitespace is ignored; at most 200 characters. Omitted or empty applies no text filter.

parameters.name: Tags
parameters.description: Tags a party must all have (whole-tag, case-insensitive match). Repeat the parameter for several tags, for example `?Tags=vip&Tags=partner`. Blank values are ignored and duplicates merged; at most 20 distinct tags. Sensitive parties never match a tag filter.

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.description: Party types to include, as a flags value: 1 People, 2 Organizations, 4 OrganizationUnits, 8 AiAgents; add the values to combine types (for example 3 for people and organizations). Omitted means all types (15). A value with no supported type, or with other bits, is rejected.

parameters.name: PageIndex
parameters.description: Zero-based page number. Omitted means 0; must not be negative.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Number of parties per page, from 1 through 100. Omitted means 24.

parameters.name: IncludeArchived
parameters.description: True to include archived parties. Omitted or false excludes them.

200.description: The requested page. An empty `items` array means no party matched.

400.description: A filter is out of range (`crmhr.party.query-invalid`): negative page index, page size outside 1 through 100, search text longer than 200 characters, more than 20 tags, or a party-type scope without a supported type.

post.summary: Create a CRM/HR party together with its roles, public contact points and addresses.
post.description:
Every successful call creates a new party with a new identifier; this operation cannot update an existing party and is not idempotent. The external code is stored as sent and is not checked for uniqueness. To avoid duplicates, search with `GET /api/crm-hr/parties` before creating, and search again before retrying after a timeout or server error: the party is saved before the search index and the activity feed are updated, so a failed response can follow a saved party.

Request rules:

- `displayName` is required. Text values are trimmed.
- Tags are trimmed; blank tags and case-insensitive duplicates are dropped.
- Every entry of `publicContacts` is stored as a contact point with the public flag set. The flag is a data classification; it does not make the party or the contact readable without authorization. At most one contact point per contact type can be primary.
- Confidential notes cannot be created through this operation.
- `isSensitive` true withholds the external code, summary and tags from directory reads and keeps the party out of the application search index.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host. The change is recorded as made by `crm-hr-api`.

requestBody.description: The party to create: identity, classification, roles, public contacts and addresses.

200.description: The party was created. The body is its new identifier as a JSON string (a GUID); use it as `partyId` in the other CRM/HR operations.

400.description: The party was not created: `crmhr.party.display-name-required` (blank display name) or `crmhr.party.multiple-primary-contacts` (more than one primary contact point of the same contact type). A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

get.summary: Read the directory summary of one CRM/HR party.
get.description:
Returns, for one party identifier, the summary that the party list returns, whether or not the party is archived. Use it to check that a party exists and to read its type and lifecycle status before you reference it from relationships, workforce records or recruitment applications. It does not include roles, contact points or addresses.

For a sensitive party the external code, summary and tags are returned empty.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: partyId
parameters.description: Identifier of the party, as returned in `items[].id` by `GET /api/crm-hr/parties` or by `POST /api/crm-hr/parties`.

200.description: The party summary.

404.description: No party has this identifier (`crmhr.party.not-found`).

get.summary: List every relationship in which a CRM/HR party is the source or the target.
get.description:
Each item describes the relationship from the point of view of the party in the route: `relatedPartyId` is the other party, and `isOutgoing` is true when the route party is the source. A relationship reads source, kind, target: with `isOutgoing` true and kind MemberOf, the route party is a member of the related party. Items are ordered by the related party's display name (case-insensitive), then by relationship kind, related party identifier and relationship identifier.

Read this list before `PUT /api/crm-hr/parties/{partyId}/relationships`: that operation replaces the whole list, in both directions.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: partyId
parameters.description: Identifier of the party whose relationships are listed, as returned by `GET /api/crm-hr/parties`. Archived parties are accepted.

200.description: The party's relationships; an empty array means it has none.

404.description: No party has this identifier (`crmhr.party.not-found`).

put.summary: Replace the complete set of relationships of a CRM/HR party.
put.description:
This is a full replacement, not a patch. The server deletes every existing relationship in which the route party is the source or the target, including relationships created from the other party's side and the manager, buddy and mentor relationships saved by `POST /api/crm-hr/recruiting/support-assignments`, and then stores exactly the submitted list. An empty `relationships` array, or a body without that member, removes all relationships of the party. Send an array, never null. Every stored relationship gets a new identifier on each call.

Read, modify, write:

1. Call `GET /api/crm-hr/parties/{partyId}/relationships`.
2. Copy every item you want to keep into the request with the same `relatedPartyId`, `relationshipKind`, `isOutgoing`, `isPrimary`, dates and `notes`, then add or remove items.
3. Send the complete list and read it again.

Each item must reference another existing party, and the same source, target and kind can appear only once. When any item is rejected nothing is changed. There is no concurrency check: a replacement saved by another client after your read is overwritten.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: partyId
parameters.description: Identifier of the party whose relationships are replaced, as returned by `GET /api/crm-hr/parties`.

requestBody.description: The complete intended list of the party's relationships.

200.description: The relationships were replaced. Read them back with `GET /api/crm-hr/parties/{partyId}/relationships` to get their new identifiers.

400.description: Nothing was changed: `crmhr.party.relationship-invalid` (an item has no related party or points to the route party itself) or `crmhr.party.relationship-duplicate` (the same source, target and kind twice). A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

404.description: Nothing was changed: the route party does not exist (`crmhr.party.not-found`) or one or more related parties do not exist (`crmhr.party.relationship-party-not-found`; the message lists their identifiers).

get.summary: List CRM/HR parties of the workforce population, one page at a time.
get.description:
Returns the same party summaries as `GET /api/crm-hr/parties`, limited to the workforce population: every person and organization unit, plus organizations that have a workforce profile or the DeliveryUnit role. AI agent parties are never included, and a listed party does not necessarily have a workforce profile. Read `GET /api/crm-hr/workforce/{partyId}` for the profile, skills and capacity of one party.

Search, tag, sensitivity and paging rules are those of the party list: items are ordered by display name and then party identifier, archived parties are excluded unless `IncludeArchived` is true, search text matches the display name and, for parties that are not sensitive, the external code and summary, sensitive parties return an empty external code, summary and tags, and paging is zero-based.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: Search
parameters.description: Text matched case-insensitively as a substring of the display name and, for parties that are not sensitive, of the external code and summary. Surrounding whitespace is ignored; at most 200 characters. Omitted or empty applies no text filter.

parameters.name: Tags
parameters.description: Tags a party must all have (whole-tag, case-insensitive match). Repeat the parameter for several tags, for example `?Tags=backend&Tags=remote`. Blank values are ignored and duplicates merged; at most 20 distinct tags. Sensitive parties never match a tag filter.

parameters.name: PageIndex
parameters.description: Zero-based page number. Omitted means 0; must not be negative.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Number of parties per page, from 1 through 100. Omitted means 24.

parameters.name: IncludeArchived
parameters.description: True to include archived parties. Omitted or false excludes them.

200.description: The requested page. An empty `items` array means no party matched.

400.description: A filter is out of range (`crmhr.workforce.query-invalid`): negative page index, page size outside 1 through 100, search text longer than 200 characters or more than 20 tags.

get.summary: Read the workforce workspace of a CRM/HR party: profile, skills, capacity blocks and project allocations.
get.description:
Combines, for one person, organization or organization unit: the party summary, its workforce profile, the whole skill catalog, the party's skills, its capacity blocks, its project allocations and a capacity summary calculated for the current UTC date. When no profile was saved yet, `profile` holds default values and its `id` is null. Use `profile` as the starting point for `POST /api/crm-hr/workforce/profiles`.

Project allocations are the party's project participations and task work assignments that carry an allocation percentage, including past ones. Only allocations bound to the current, not retired lifetime of their project count in the capacity summary. An allocation whose project no longer exists, or was recreated with the same identifier, shows an empty project name.

For a sensitive party the primary email and phone are returned empty; the summary and the other fields are returned. The response contains personal and HR data: do not log it.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: partyId
parameters.description: Identifier of the party, as returned by `GET /api/crm-hr/workforce` or `GET /api/crm-hr/parties`; not a workforce profile identifier.

200.description: The workforce workspace of the party.

404.description: No person, organization or organization unit has this identifier (`crmhr.workforce.party-not-found`). AI agent parties have no workforce workspace.

post.summary: Create or replace the workforce profile of a CRM/HR party.
post.description:
A workforce profile holds the work classification, reporting line, employment dates, rates and weekly capacity of a party; it is not a person identity or a login account. A party has at most one profile, found by `partyId`: the first save creates it and every later save overwrites all of its fields with the values sent. Start from `profile` in `GET /api/crm-hr/workforce/{partyId}` and send every field.

Rules checked before saving:

- People cannot use the DeliveryUnit workforce kind; organizations and organization units must use it.
- `managerPartyId` must identify another existing person, and `homeUnitPartyId` an existing organization or organization unit other than the party itself.
- Rates cannot be negative and `rateCurrencyCode` must consist of three letters A to Z after trimming and upper-casing (a format check only; blank means USD).

The save also gives the party the role that matches the workforce kind (Employee, Contractor, Freelancer or DeliveryUnit) when it is missing. The search index and the activity feed are updated after the profile is saved, so after a server error read the workspace before retrying.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

requestBody.description: All fields of the party's workforce profile.

200.description: The profile was saved. The body is the workforce profile identifier as a JSON string (a GUID), which is not the party identifier; read `GET /api/crm-hr/workforce/{partyId}` for the stored values.

400.description: The profile was not saved: `crmhr.workforce.party-required`, `crmhr.workforce.self-manager`, `crmhr.workforce.self-home-unit`, `crmhr.workforce.rate-negative`, `crmhr.workforce.rate-unit-invalid`, `crmhr.workforce.rate-currency-invalid`, `crmhr.workforce.person-delivery-unit`, `crmhr.workforce.organization-kind`, `crmhr.workforce.manager-invalid` or `crmhr.workforce.home-unit-invalid`. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

404.description: The party does not exist (`crmhr.workforce.party-not-found`).

get.summary: List the workforce skill catalog.
get.description:
Returns every skill definition, active ones first, then ordered by category and name. A skill definition is a catalog entry that party skills refer to by `skillId`; it is not an agent skill or capability. The list is not paged. The workforce workspace returns the same catalog in `skillCatalog`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

200.description: All skill definitions, including inactive ones; an empty array when the catalog is empty.

post.summary: Create or update a skill definition in the workforce skill catalog.
post.description:
The definition to update is found by `id` and, when `id` is omitted or unknown, by the same trimmed name. When neither matches, a new definition with a new identifier is created; a sent `id` is never used as the new identifier. All fields are overwritten with the values sent. Skill names are unique in the catalog, so renaming a definition to the name of another one fails with a server error. Setting `isActive` to false keeps the definition and the party skills that refer to it.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

requestBody.description: The skill definition fields.

200.description: The definition was saved. The body is its identifier as a JSON string (a GUID); use it as `skillId` of a party skill.

400.description: The name is blank (`crmhr.skills.name-required`). A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

post.summary: Record or update a CRM/HR party's proficiency in a catalog skill.
post.description:
A party skill links a party to a skill definition from `GET /api/crm-hr/workforce/skills` with a proficiency level, years of experience and certification details. A party has at most one record per skill. The record to update is found by `id` and otherwise by the `partyId` and `skillId` pair; when neither matches, a new record with a new identifier is created. All fields, including the party and the skill, are overwritten with the values sent. Negative years of experience are saved as 0.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

requestBody.description: The party, the skill and the proficiency details.

200.description: The party skill was saved. The body is its identifier as a JSON string (a GUID); read it back in `skills` of `GET /api/crm-hr/workforce/{partyId}`.

400.description: `partyId` or `skillId` is missing (`crmhr.skills.party-required`, `crmhr.skills.skill-required`). A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

404.description: The party (`crmhr.skills.party-not-found`) or the skill definition (`crmhr.skills.skill-not-found`) does not exist.

post.summary: Create or update a capacity block that reduces the availability of a CRM/HR party for a date range.
post.description:
A capacity block records leave, unavailability, a reservation or a tentative hold as a percentage of the party's capacity between two dates. It is not a task or a project assignment; a related project is informational. Blocks active on the current UTC date reduce `availablePercent` in the workforce workspace.

The block is found by `id`; without `id`, or when no block has it, a new block with a new identifier is created. All fields are overwritten with the values sent. `startDate` and `endDate` are required, the end date cannot be before the start date and `percentage` must be greater than 0 and at most 100.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

requestBody.description: The party, the block kind, the date range, the percentage and an optional project.

200.description: The block was saved. The body is its identifier as a JSON string (a GUID); read it back in `capacityBlocks` of `GET /api/crm-hr/workforce/{partyId}`.

400.description: The block was not saved: `crmhr.capacity.party-required`, `crmhr.capacity.date-required`, `crmhr.capacity.date-range-invalid` or `crmhr.capacity.percentage-range`. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

404.description: The party (`crmhr.capacity.party-not-found`) or the related project (`crmhr.capacity.project-not-found`) does not exist.

get.summary: List recruitment applications that match optional text and stage filters, one page at a time.
get.description:
A recruitment application is a candidate party's application for a role; its identifier is not the candidate's party identifier. Items are ordered by last update, newest first, then by application identifier. Search text matches, case-insensitively as a substring, the desired role, the source, the display names of the candidate, recruiter, hiring manager and target unit, and the candidate's public email addresses.

Paging is zero-based and `totalCount` counts all matches: request the next page while (`pageIndex` + 1) multiplied by `pageSize` is less than `totalCount`. Items carry the candidate's primary public email and phone, also for sensitive candidates.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: Search
parameters.description: Text matched case-insensitively as a substring of the desired role, the source, the display names of the candidate, recruiter, hiring manager and target unit, and the candidate's public email addresses. Surrounding whitespace is ignored; at most 200 characters. Omitted or empty applies no text filter.

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.description: Stage to include, as the case-sensitive member name (for example `Interviewing`) or its integer value: 0 All, 1 Applied, 2 Screening, 3 Interviewing, 4 Offer, 5 Hired, 6 Rejected, 7 Withdrawn. Omitted means All.

parameters.name: PageIndex
parameters.description: Zero-based page number. Omitted means 0; must not be negative.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Number of applications per page, from 1 through 100. Omitted means 12.

200.description: The requested page. An empty `items` array means no application matched.

400.description: A filter is out of range (`crmhr.recruiting.query-invalid`): negative page index, page size outside 1 through 100, search text longer than 200 characters or an unknown stage scope.

post.summary: Create or update a recruitment application, creating the candidate party when needed.
post.description:
Candidate: send `partyId` of an existing person or AI agent party, or omit it and send `candidateName` (with optional `candidateEmail`, `candidatePhone` and `candidateSummary`) to create a new person party with lifecycle status Candidate, the Candidate role and public contact points. The candidate fields are ignored when `partyId` is sent. When updating, always send the `partyId` from the read: without it a new candidate party is created and the application is moved to it.

Application: the application is found by `id`; without `id`, or when no application has it, a new application with a new identifier is created. All application fields are overwritten with the values sent, so start from `application` in `GET /api/crm-hr/recruiting/applications/{applicationId}`. Stage and decision are stored as sent; no transition order is enforced. `stageNotes` is recorded in the stage history only when the application is created or its stage changes.

The steps are saved separately: a new candidate party is saved before the recruiter, hiring manager and target unit are checked, so a 400 response can follow a created party, and the search index and activity feed are updated after the application is saved. After a failure, search for the candidate and the application before retrying.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

requestBody.description: The application fields and either the candidate party or the new candidate's details.

200.description: The application was saved. The body is the recruitment application identifier as a JSON string (a GUID), not the candidate's party identifier; read the workspace for the candidate's `partyId`.

400.description: The application was not saved: `crmhr.recruiting.role-required`, `crmhr.recruiting.candidate-invalid` (the party is not an existing person or AI agent), `crmhr.recruiting.candidate-required` (neither `partyId` nor `candidateName`), `crmhr.recruiting.recruiter-invalid`, `crmhr.recruiting.hiring-manager-self`, `crmhr.recruiting.hiring-manager-invalid` or `crmhr.recruiting.target-unit-invalid`. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

get.summary: Read the recruitment workspace of one application, with its candidate, history, interviews, tasks and support.
get.description:
Returns the application, the candidate's name, summary and primary public contacts, the stage history of the application (newest first), its interviews (by scheduled time), the candidate party's lifecycle tasks and support assignments, and a conversion request prepared from the application and any existing workforce profile. Lifecycle tasks and support assignments are stored per party, not per application.

Use it as the source of the recruiting writes: send `application` back to `POST /api/crm-hr/recruiting/applications` after changing it, and review `conversion` before `POST /api/crm-hr/recruiting/conversions`.

The response contains personal data, including the contact values and summary of sensitive candidates: do not log it.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the recruitment application, as returned by `GET /api/crm-hr/recruiting/applications` or `POST /api/crm-hr/recruiting/applications`; not the candidate's party identifier.

200.description: The application workspace; `hasSelectedApplication` is true.

404.description: No recruitment application has this identifier (`crmhr.recruiting.application-not-found`).

post.summary: Schedule or update an interview of a recruitment application.
post.description:
The interview is found by `id`; without `id`, or when no interview has it, a new interview with a new identifier is created. All interview fields are overwritten with the values sent, including the application it belongs to. `scheduledAtUtc` is required and is stored in UTC. The interviewer, when set, must be an existing person party. Saving an interview or its outcome does not change the application's stage or decision.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

requestBody.description: The application, schedule, interview type, interviewer, outcome and feedback.

200.description: The interview was saved. The body is the interview identifier as a JSON string (a GUID); read it back in `interviews` of `GET /api/crm-hr/recruiting/applications/{applicationId}`.

400.description: The interview was not saved: `crmhr.recruiting.interview.application-required`, `crmhr.recruiting.interview.schedule-required` or `crmhr.recruiting.interview.interviewer-invalid`. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

404.description: The recruitment application does not exist (`crmhr.recruiting.interview.application-not-found`).

post.summary: Create or update an onboarding, offboarding or training task of a CRM/HR party.
post.description:
A lifecycle task is a recruiting checklist item for a party, owned by a person and optionally linked to a project. It is not a canonical Project Structure task and does not appear in a project plan. The task is found by `id`; without `id`, or when no task has it, a new task with a new identifier is created. All task fields are overwritten with the values sent.

Required: `partyId` of an existing party, a non-blank `title`, `ownerPartyId` of an existing person and `dueDate`. `relatedProjectId`, when set, must identify an existing project.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

requestBody.description: The party, kind, title, owner, due date, status and optional project of the task.

200.description: The task was saved. The body is the lifecycle task identifier as a JSON string (a GUID); read it back in `lifecycleTasks` of the recruitment workspace.

400.description: The task was not saved: `crmhr.recruiting.task.party-required`, `crmhr.recruiting.task.title-required`, `crmhr.recruiting.task.owner-required`, `crmhr.recruiting.task.due-date-required` or `crmhr.recruiting.task.owner-invalid`. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

404.description: The party (`crmhr.recruiting.task.party-not-found`) or the related project (`crmhr.recruiting.task.project-not-found`) does not exist.

post.summary: Replace the manager, buddy and mentor of a CRM/HR party.
post.description:
Support assignments are stored as party relationships and replaced together: all ManagedBy relationships in which the party is the source and its Supports relationships labelled Buddy or Mentor are deleted, then one relationship is created for each of `managerPartyId`, `buddyPartyId` and `mentorPartyId` that is set. An omitted or null value removes that assignment. This also deletes ManagedBy relationships saved through `PUT /api/crm-hr/parties/{partyId}/relationships`, and a later relationship replacement can delete these assignments. The `managerPartyId` of the workforce profile is a separate value and is not changed.

Each assigned party must be an existing person other than the party itself.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, any valid bearer token issued by this host.

requestBody.description: The party and its complete set of support assignments.

200.description: The assignments were replaced. Read them back in `supportAssignments` of the recruitment workspace or in `GET /api/crm-hr/parties/{partyId}/relationships`.

400.description: Nothing was changed: `crmhr.recruiting.support.party-required`, `crmhr.recruiting.support.self-reference`, `crmhr.recruiting.support.manager-invalid`, `crmhr.recruiting.support.buddy-invalid` or `crmhr.recruiting.support.mentor-invalid`. A body the framework cannot bind is rejected with HTTP 400 without the `errors` envelope.

404.description: The party does not exist (`crmhr.recruiting.support.party-not-found`).

post.summary: Convert the candidate of an approved recruitment application into workforce.
post.description:
Conversion saves the candidate party's workforce profile, then marks the application Hired with decision Approved and sets the party's lifecycle status to Active. Start from `conversion` in `GET /api/crm-hr/recruiting/applications/{applicationId}`.

Prerequisites: the application must not be Rejected or Withdrawn and its decision must be Approved (save it with `POST /api/crm-hr/recruiting/applications` first). An AI agent candidate also needs a bound technical agent with a completed application-specific technical assessment and human approval.

Profile values: an empty `jobTitle` uses the application's desired role, an empty `homeUnitPartyId` the application's target unit, an empty `managerPartyId` the candidate's support manager or else the hiring manager, a capacity of 0 or less 40 hours and an empty status Active. The profile is saved as by `POST /api/crm-hr/workforce/profiles`: profile fields that this request does not carry (employee code, end date, rates, rate unit and rate currency) are saved empty or with their defaults, replacing the values of an existing profile.

The steps are saved separately: when the call fails after the profile was saved, read the workforce workspace and the application before retrying. Converting a converted candidate again saves the profile again and keeps the application Hired.

post.description:
An archived conversation keeps its transcript readable but accepts no turns and cannot be renamed; this API offers no way back. A conversation whose turn is still active or unfinished (including one that requires recovery) cannot be archived: follow that operation until it ends, or settle it with cancel, reconcile or abandon, then retry. Archiving an archived conversation changes nothing and returns it unchanged, provided the concurrency token matches. The concurrency token increases by one; the transcript revision does not change.

Send the concurrency token you read as `expectedConcurrencyToken` in the JSON body or as `If-Match`. A JSON body is required even with `If-Match`; `{}` is then enough.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the exact scope `api.llm-chats.manage`; the broad `api` scope is not accepted. With authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open. Failures use Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` member.

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the conversation, as returned in `id` by conversation creation or `GET /api/llm-conversations`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Strong ETag of the conversation version you read, for example `"2"` including the quotes, as returned in the `ETag` response header. It carries the same concurrency token as `expectedConcurrencyToken` in the body: send at least one of them, and when both are present they must be equal. A weak ETag (`W/`), `*` or a list is rejected with 400.

requestBody.description: JSON object with the expected concurrency token, for example `{ "expectedConcurrencyToken": 1 }`, or `{}` when the token is sent as `If-Match`.

200.description: The conversation is archived. The body is the conversation without messages and the `ETag` header carries its concurrency token.

400.description: `llm-chat.invalid-request`, nothing was changed: the identifier is the empty GUID; the body is missing, is not JSON or has other members; no concurrency token was sent; `If-Match` is not a single strong numeric ETag; a token is negative; or the two tokens differ.

404.description: `llm-chat.conversation-not-found`: no conversation has this identifier.

409.description: Nothing was changed: `llm-chat.storage-conflict` (the conversation changed since your read; read it again), `llm-chat.active-turn-conflict` (a turn is active or unfinished) or `llm-chat.runtime-profile-changed` (the host's active database profile changed; read the conversation before repeating the request).

500.description: `llm-chat.storage-corrupted`: the conversation's transcript, definition or pinned revision is missing from storage; nothing was changed.

post.summary: Admit one user message as a new conversation turn; the model's reply is produced asynchronously.
post.description:
Records the user message in the transcript, queues the turn as a durable operation and returns HTTP 202 at once. The provider is called later by a background dispatcher, never by this request: HTTP 202 means the turn was admitted, not that a reply exists. Follow the operation with `GET /api/llm-chat-operations/{operationId}` (the `Location` header) or its event stream (`eventsUrl`) until `status` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `recoveryRequired`. On success the reply is in `assistantMessage` and in the transcript.

Preconditions: the conversation is not archived, its definition is `active`, no other turn of the conversation is active or unfinished, and `expectedTranscriptRevision` equals the conversation's current `transcriptRevision` (from `GET /api/llm-conversations/{conversationId}`, or `resultingTranscriptRevision` of the previous successful turn). The turn uses the definition revision the conversation is pinned to.

Idempotency: `operationId` is a GUID you generate, and it identifies both the operation and the turn. Repeating the request with the same `operationId` and an identical body never calls the provider again; it returns the recorded operation with `replayed` true, whatever its status. Reusing an `operationId` with a different body is rejected with 409 `llm-chat.operation-id-conflict`. After a lost or ambiguous response, resend the identical request. To try again after a failed or cancelled turn, read the conversation for its current `transcriptRevision` and send a new turn with a new `operationId`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the exact scope `api.llm-chats.execute`; the broad `api` scope is not accepted. With authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open. Failures use Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` member; failures after the body was read also carry the requested `operationId` and `retryable`.

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the conversation, as returned in `id` by conversation creation or `GET /api/llm-conversations`.

requestBody.description: The turn as a JSON object (`application/json`) with a new `operationId`, the conversation's current `transcriptRevision` as `expectedTranscriptRevision`, and the user `message`.

202.description: The turn was admitted, or an identical earlier request was replayed (`replayed` true). The body is the operation, usually in `pending` status; a replay returns its current status. The `Location` header is the operation's status URL.

400.description: `llm-chat.invalid-request`, nothing was admitted: the body is missing, is not JSON or has unknown members; `operationId` or the conversation identifier is the empty GUID; `expectedTranscriptRevision` is negative; or the message is blank or longer than 400,000 characters.

404.description: `llm-chat.conversation-not-found`: no conversation has this identifier.

409.description: The turn was not admitted: `llm-chat.operation-id-conflict` (the `operationId` belongs to a different request), `llm-chat.transcript-revision-conflict` (read the conversation for its current revision), `llm-chat.active-turn-conflict` (another turn is active or unfinished; follow it first), `llm-chat.conversation-archived`, `llm-chat.definition-not-active`, `llm-chat.storage-conflict` (a concurrent change; retryable) or `llm-chat.runtime-profile-changed` (retryable: resend the identical request).

422.description: The provider selection of the pinned definition revision is no longer usable, nothing was admitted: `llm-chat.provider-not-found`, `llm-chat.provider-kind-mismatch` (the profile now has another provider kind), `llm-chat.model-not-supported`, `llm-chat.thinking-effort-not-supported` or `llm-chat.model-settings-invalid`. The conversation stays pinned to its revision, so updating the definition does not repair it: restore the provider configuration, or update the definition and start a new conversation.

500.description: `llm-chat.storage-corrupted`: stored conversation, definition or transcript state is missing or inconsistent, or admission failed unexpectedly. Read `GET /api/llm-chat-operations/{operationId}` before resending: HTTP 404 there means the turn was not admitted.

503.description: Nothing was admitted and `retryable` is true: `llm-chat.dispatcher-unavailable` (this host runs no LLM Chat dispatcher) or `llm-chat.provider-unavailable` (the definition's provider profile is disabled or no longer serves chat). Resend the identical request later.

post.summary: Abandon a turn that requires recovery, removing its user message from the transcript.
post.description:
Use this only for an operation in `recoveryRequired` status whose outcome reconciliation could not prove (`POST /api/llm-chat-operations/{operationId}/reconcile` left it in that status), once you accept that its reply is lost. The operation must belong to the conversation, must be in `recoveryRequired` status, must not be owned by a live execution and must still be the conversation's active turn. The provider is never called.

On success the pending user message is removed, the transcript revision increases by one and the operation ends as `failed`, with its recovery reason (or `llm-chat.operation-recovery-required`) as failure code. The conversation then accepts new turns; read it for its current `transcriptRevision`. If the response still shows `recoveryRequired`, the abandonment did not complete: read the conversation before trying again.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the exact scope `api.llm-chats.execute`; the broad `api` scope is not accepted. With authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open. Failures use Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` member and the requested `turnId` as `operationId`.

parameters.name: conversationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the conversation, as returned in `id` by conversation creation or `GET /api/llm-conversations`.

parameters.name: turnId
parameters.description: Identifier of the turn to abandon, which is its operation identifier: the conversation's `activeOperationId`, equal to the `operationId` sent with the turn.

200.description: The body is the operation: `failed` when the turn was abandoned, still `recoveryRequired` when the abandonment did not complete. The `Location` header is its status URL.

400.description: `llm-chat.invalid-request`: an identifier is the empty GUID.

404.description: `llm-chat.operation-not-found`: no operation has the identifier `turnId`.

409.description: `llm-chat.operation-recovery-required`: the operation is not in `recoveryRequired` status, belongs to another conversation, is still owned by a live execution or is no longer the active turn; nothing was changed. Or `llm-chat.runtime-profile-changed`: the host's active database profile changed; read the operation before repeating the request.

get.summary: Read the current state of an LLM Chat turn operation.
get.description:
Returns the durable state of an operation created by `POST /api/llm-conversations/{conversationId}/turns`: its status, the assistant reply once committed, the recorded failure and up to 100 provider invocation attempts in order. Poll it until `status` is `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`, which are final, or `recoveryRequired`, which needs a decision (reconcile, then abandon if the outcome stays unknown). For live progress, use the event stream (`eventsUrl`) instead of frequent polling.

Invocation attempts are an allowlisted projection of the provider evidence: provider kind, model, delivery mode, finish reason, requested and effective thinking effort, outcome, token usage and failure code. Provider profile identity, correlation identifiers and raw provider errors are not exposed.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the exact scope `api.llm-chats.read`; the broad `api` scope is not accepted. With authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open. Failures use Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` member and the requested `operationId`.

parameters.name: operationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the operation: the `operationId` sent with the turn, also returned as `activeOperationId` by the conversation read.

200.description: The operation.

400.description: `llm-chat.invalid-request`: the identifier is the empty GUID.

404.description: `llm-chat.operation-not-found`: no operation has this identifier.

409.description: `llm-chat.runtime-profile-changed`: the host's active database profile changed while the request ran. Repeat the request.

get.summary: Stream the events of an LLM Chat turn operation as server-sent events.
get.description:
Opens a `text/event-stream` response that first replays the operation's retained events after your cursor, then delivers new events as they are committed, until the operation ends. Use it to show a reply while it is generated; the authoritative result stays `GET /api/llm-chat-operations/{operationId}`.

Every event has an `id` (the event sequence, increasing by one per event of the operation), an `event` (the event type) and one `data` line with a JSON object of contract `candoitall.llm-chat-operation-event.v1`: `schema`, `operationId`, `conversationId`, `sequence`, `occurredAtUtc`, `eventKind` (the event type again), `operationState` (a camel-case operation status; `running` for attempt and delta events) and `payload`, whose members that do not apply are null. Event types:

- `llm.operation.accepted`: the turn was admitted (state `pending`).
- `llm.operation.claimed`: a dispatcher started executing it (state `running`).
- `llm.provider.attempt-started`: a provider attempt began; payload `attemptOrdinal`, `model` and `deliveryMode` (`incremental` or `completedFallback`).
- `llm.response.delta`: a chunk of reply text; payload `attemptOrdinal`, `text` and `aggregateCharacterCount` (characters delivered so far).
- `llm.response.completed` and `llm.provider.attempt-finished`: an attempt succeeded, or ended otherwise; payload adds `finishReason`, `outcome` (`succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`), `usage`, `failureCode` and `retryable`.
- `llm.operation.cancellation-requested`: cancellation was requested; payload `cancellationGeneration` and `cancellationRequestedAtUtc`.
- `llm.operation.succeeded`, `llm.operation.failed`, `llm.operation.cancelled` and `llm.operation.recovery-required`: final events; payload `outputIncomplete`, `usage` (except for recovery), `failureCode` and `retryable` (except for success), and on success `model`, `assistantMessageId` and `transcriptRevision`.

Delta text is provisional: it becomes the reply only when `llm.operation.succeeded` follows. After a failure, cancellation or recovery (`outputIncomplete` true) discard it.

Resuming: send the `id` of the last event you processed as the `Last-Event-ID` header or as the `after` query parameter (a non-negative integer); when both are present they must be equal. Only later events are sent; omit both to start from the first event. When the cursor lies outside the retained events, the stream first sends a `stream.gap` event whose data holds `reason` (`cursorBeforeRetention` or `cursorAheadOfStream`), `requestedAfterSequence`, `firstAvailableSequence`, `lastAvailableSequence`, `resumeAfterSequence` and `snapshotUrl` (the operation's status URL); read that URL to recover what you missed. Events of finished operations are deleted after a retention period, 7 days by default.

While no event arrives, the server writes comment lines (`: heartbeat` and a timestamp), every 15 seconds by default. It closes the stream after a final event; reconnecting after that returns an empty stream that closes at once. The server can also end the stream early, for example when the host's active database profile changes: reconnect with the last `id`. Disconnecting does not cancel the operation; use `POST /api/llm-chat-operations/{operationId}/cancel`.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the exact scope `api.llm-chats.read`; the broad `api` scope is not accepted. Send it in the `Authorization` header; tokens in query parameters are not accepted. With authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open.

parameters.name: operationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the operation: the `operationId` sent with the turn, also returned as `activeOperationId` by the conversation read.

200.description: The server-sent event stream (`text/event-stream`) described above, uncached and unbuffered. It ends after a final event.

400.description: Rejected before streaming. An invalid `Last-Event-ID` or `after` (not a single non-negative integer, or the two differ) returns this general error envelope (`errors` array, `application/json`) with code `llm-chat.stream-cursor-invalid`; start again from the operation's `lastEventSequence`. The empty GUID as operation identifier is rejected differently, with Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) and code `llm-chat.invalid-request`.

404.description: `llm-chat.operation-not-found`: no operation has this identifier.

409.description: `llm-chat.runtime-profile-changed`: the host's active database profile changed while the stream was opened. Reconnect.

post.summary: Request cancellation of an LLM Chat turn operation.
post.description:
Records a durable cancellation request for a `pending` or `running` operation and signals its provider call when this host executes it; a dispatcher on another host notices the request at its next lease heartbeat. Cancellation is asynchronous: while the operation is `pending`, `running` or `cancellationRequested` the response is HTTP 202, and you follow the operation until it is final. It normally ends `cancelled`, with the user message removed from the transcript; depending on what the provider call had already done it can also end `failed` or `recoveryRequired`.

For an operation that is already `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `recoveryRequired`, nothing changes and the response is HTTP 200 with its current state; a committed reply is never withdrawn. Repeating the request is safe.

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the exact scope `api.llm-chats.execute`; the broad `api` scope is not accepted. With authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open. Failures use Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` member and the requested `operationId`.

parameters.name: operationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the operation: the `operationId` sent with the turn, also returned as `activeOperationId` by the conversation read.

200.description: The operation was already final or requires recovery, so nothing changed; the body shows its state. The `Location` header is its status URL.

202.description: Cancellation is recorded and not yet settled; the body shows the operation, usually `cancellationRequested`. Follow the `Location` header until the operation is final.

400.description: `llm-chat.invalid-request`: the identifier is the empty GUID.

404.description: `llm-chat.operation-not-found`: no operation has this identifier.

409.description: `llm-chat.runtime-profile-changed`: the host's active database profile changed while the request ran. Repeat the request.

post.summary: Settle an interrupted LLM Chat turn operation from its durable evidence, without calling the provider.
post.description:
Use this for an operation whose provider call may have started but that is no longer progressing, typically one in `recoveryRequired` status. Reconciliation never calls the provider and never dispatches the turn again. It inspects the stored transcript and invocation evidence and settles the operation only where that evidence proves the outcome: `succeeded` when the assistant reply was committed, `failed` or `cancelled` when the last attempt recorded a failure or cancellation (the user message is then removed from the transcript). Otherwise the operation stays in, or moves to, `recoveryRequired`; if you accept that the reply is lost, abandon the turn with `POST /api/llm-conversations/{conversationId}/active-turns/{turnId}/abandon`.

An operation that is already final, or whose provider call never started, is returned unchanged. An operation still owned by a live execution is rejected with 409 `llm-chat.active-turn-conflict`: a running execution keeps renewing its lease, so retry once the execution has stopped and its lease has expired (10 seconds after its last heartbeat by default).

Authority: when API authorization is enabled, a bearer token with the exact scope `api.llm-chats.manage`; the broad `api` scope is not accepted. With authorization disabled (the development default) the route is open. Failures use Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` member and the requested `operationId`.

parameters.name: operationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the operation: the `operationId` sent with the turn, also returned as `activeOperationId` by the conversation read.

200.description: The operation after reconciliation; check `status`, which is unchanged when nothing could be proven or the operation was already final. The `Location` header is its status URL.

400.description: `llm-chat.invalid-request`: the identifier is the empty GUID.

404.description: `llm-chat.operation-not-found`: no operation has this identifier.

409.description: `llm-chat.active-turn-conflict` (a live execution still owns the operation; nothing was changed) or `llm-chat.runtime-profile-changed` (the host's active database profile changed; repeat the request).

secretId.description: Identifier of the stored secret. Agent saves drop entries with the all-zero identifier; it is not checked against the secret store.

nameSnapshot.description: Display name of the secret when it was allowed, trimmed; a label only.

purpose.description: Purpose label of the allowance; blank is stored as `agent-request`.

AgentAllowedSecretReference.description: Stored secret an agent may use, one entry of its allowed secret references. It carries the secret's identifier and display name only, never the secret value. For agents, the list limits at run time which secrets MCP capability bindings may resolve; in the permissions of a workflow LLM call component it is only stored.

executionRunId.description: Identifier of the reconciled execution run.

chatSessionId.description: Identifier of the run's chat session; the all-zero GUID for a run without a chat session.

hasUnknownEffects.description: True when at least one tool call still has effect state 0 Unknown or a provider request is not in state 1 ResponseAdmitted. Changes may then exist without confirmation: check the affected records with their owners before repeating any work.

outcomes.description: The admitted tool calls of the run, in admission order; empty when there were none.

providerDispatches.description: Model-provider requests that carried approvals of tool calls the provider runs itself, in order; empty when there were none.

AgentCancellationReconciliationApiRespon.description: Result of reconciling a cancelled agent execution run, returned by `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/reconcile-cancellation`. It lists every tool call admitted for the run with what is known about its effect, and every model-provider request that carried approved tool calls.

capabilityId.description: Identifier of the catalog capability, as listed by `GET /api/agents/capabilities`.

capabilityKey.description: Key of the catalog capability at the time of assignment, kept in sync with the catalog.

kind.description: Kind of the capability, as a JSON integer: 0 McpServer, 1 Skill, 2 Tool, 3 Plugin, 4 Rag, 5 AiContext, 6 Memory (retired).

proofStatus.description: Result of the latest verification of this assignment, as a JSON integer: 0 NotRun, 1 Verified, 2 Failed, 3 PendingReview. It is informational: the runtime does not use it to decide whether the capability is attached. A new assignment starts with the catalog capability's current proof state.

lastVerifiedAtUtc.description: Instant, with offset, at which the proof in `proofStatus` was produced; null when never verified.

proofNotes.description: Human-readable notes of the latest verification; empty when none.

AgentCapabilityAssignment.description: Catalog capability assigned to an agent, one entry of the agent definition's `capabilities`. Assignments are changed through the editor form's `selectedCapabilityIds`; this record is read-only. An assignment declares a capability for the agent; a run attaches the corresponding tools only as the agent's permissions and the runtime policy allow.

id.description: Identifier of the agent definition.

roleTitle.description: Role title shown with the agent; may be empty.

summary.description: Short description of the agent; may be empty.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the agent, as a JSON integer: 0 Draft, 1 Active, 2 Suspended, 3 Archived.

model.description: Model identifier set on the agent; empty means the provider profile's default model.

isTemplate.description: True when the agent is a template used to create working agents.

avatarImageUrl.description: Avatar image reference (a bundled avatar path or a `data:` image URL), or null when none is set.

AgentCatalogItemApiResponse.description: Short catalog entry of a technical agent definition, as listed by `GET /api/agents/bootstrap`. It describes the agent definition only, not the CRM party that may represent the agent; read the full definition with `GET /api/agents/{agentId}`.

chatSessionId.description: Identifier of an existing chat session of the agent in the route to continue, or null or omitted to create a new session titled from the prompt. The all-zero GUID is rejected (`agents.request-invalid`).

prompt.description: The message to the agent; it must not be blank (`agents.request-invalid`) and is trimmed. No length limit is applied.

attachmentPaths.description: Optional images to show the model: paths of at most 8 files (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif or .webp, each up to 10 MiB) inside the workspace or a registered external folder, typically the `relativePath` returned by `POST /api/agents/attachments/images`. Blank entries and duplicates are ignored. Null or omitted means none.

activityOperationId.description: Optional identifier of the activity operation for this command, as a GUID string. Choose it to follow the progress with `GET /api/agents/execution-operations/{operationId}/events/stream` while the command runs; when null or omitted the server generates one. It is returned in the `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` header. It is not an idempotency key: an identifier the server still retains is rejected with HTTP 409 `agents.execution-operation-duplicate` or 410 `agents.execution-operation-evicted`, so use a new one for every command. The all-zero GUID or a non-GUID value is rejected before the command runs.

AgentChatApiRequest.description: Chat message to an agent, sent to `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/chat` and to its streaming variant `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/chat/stream`. Each message starts a new chat-backed agent execution run.

relativePath.description: Path of the stored image relative to the managed workspace, with `/` separators, for example `artifacts/chat-attachments/20260919/101500123-3f2504e04f8911d39a0c0305e82c3301-diagram.png`. Send it unchanged in `attachmentPaths` or `inputAttachmentPaths`; it is not a URL.

contentType.description: Image media type derived from the file name extension: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif` or `image/webp`.

sizeBytes.description: Number of bytes stored, at most 10485760.

AgentChatAttachmentStagingResult.description: A stored image attachment, returned by `POST /api/agents/attachments/images`. Attach the image to an agent chat message or execution run by sending `relativePath`.

AgentChatHistoryMode.description: Where an agent's chat history is kept between turns, as a JSON integer: 0 ProviderDefault (kept by the product, except for OpenAI and Azure OpenAI provider profiles on the Responses transport that do not prefer product-managed history, where the provider keeps it), 1 FrameworkManaged (kept and resent by the product), 2 ProviderManaged (kept by the model provider).

id.description: Identifier of the message.

role.description: Author of the message, as a JSON integer: 0 System (written by the product, for example the record of the tool calls made during a run), 1 User (a prompt), 2 Assistant (the agent's reply).

createdAtUtc.description: When the message was added, in UTC.

AgentChatMessageApiResponse.description: One message of an agent chat session transcript.

agents.description: The listed agents as short catalog items; templates only when `includeTemplates` was true.

initialAgentId.description: The agent to select first: the one with the most recently updated chat session, otherwise the first listed agent; null when there are no agents.

oneOf.description: Chat workspace of that agent, or null when there are no agents.

AgentChatPageBootstrapApiResponse.description: Data for opening the agent chat page, returned by `GET /api/agents/bootstrap`.

chatSessionId.description: Identifier of the chat session, including a session created for this message.

assistantMessage.description: The agent's reply message. While the run waits for approvals it holds only the text produced before the approval request, which can be empty.

metric.description: Usage and duration of this run segment.

executionRunId.description: Identifier of the execution run started by the message.

state.description: State of the run when the request returned, as a JSON integer: 5 Completed, 3 WaitingOnTool (decide the pending approvals with `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/pending-approvals`) or 6 Failed (a changing tool call failed without a later successful attempt).

AgentChatRunApiResponse.description: Result of a chat message sent with `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/chat`. The streaming variant sends the same object as `result` of its `agent.command.completed` event, with enum values written as camel-case strings (for example `waitingOnTool`) instead of integers.

agentId.description: Identifier of the agent that ran.

chatSessionId.description: Identifier of the run's chat session, or null for a run without one.

title.description: Title of the run with line breaks replaced by spaces, cut to 117 characters followed by `...` when longer than 120 characters.

state.description: State from the run's latest log entry (or the run's own state when it has no log), as a JSON integer: 0 Idle, 1 Preparing, 2 Running, 3 WaitingOnTool, 4 Persisting, 5 Completed, 6 Failed.

phase.description: Phase label of the latest log entry, for example `Completed`; free text for display.

message.description: Message of the latest log entry, or the run's result summary or title when it has no log; free text for display.

oneOf.description: Final outcome, as a JSON integer, or null while the run is not finished: 0 Succeeded, 1 Failed, 2 Cancelled.

createdAtUtc.description: When the run was created, in UTC.

updatedAtUtc.description: When the run last changed, in UTC.

startedAtUtc.description: When the run started, in UTC, or null.

completedAtUtc.description: When the run finished, in UTC, or null while it is not finished.

duration.description: Wall-clock time from the start to the finish (or to the last change of an unfinished run), as a time span string in the form `[d.]hh:mm:ss[.fffffff]`; null when the start time is unknown.

knownCostUsd.description: Estimated cost of the run in US dollars: the sum of the costs recorded with the run's provider usage or, when none has a cost, of its positive per-segment metric costs; 0 when no cost is known.

hasUnknownCost.description: True when part of the run's usage has no cost or no cost is known at all; `knownCostUsd` is then a lower bound.

AgentChatRunSummaryApiResponse.description: Summary of the latest agent execution run shown in an agent's chat workspace.

executionLog.description: Log entries of the included runs, newest first.

metrics.description: Segment metrics of the included runs, newest first.

AgentChatRuntimeApiResponse.description: Execution log entries and segment metrics of an agent's execution runs, returned by `GET /api/agents/{agentId}/runtime-snapshot`.

id.description: Identifier of the chat session.

agentId.description: Identifier of the agent that owns the session.

title.description: Title of the session: `New exploration thread` for a session created empty, the first prompt (cut to 45 characters followed by `...` when longer than 48 characters) for a session created by a message, or the title set by a rename.

createdAtUtc.description: When the session was created, in UTC.

updatedAtUtc.description: When the session last changed, in UTC.

latestExecutionRunId.description: Identifier of the session's most recent execution run, or null when no run has been started in it.

pendingApprovals.description: Normally empty: waiting tool approvals are reported on the execution run (its `pendingApprovals`). Only sessions stored by earlier product versions can still list approvals here.

autoApprovePendingToolCalls.description: Normally false: automatic approval is reported on the execution run. Only sessions stored by earlier product versions can report true here.

AgentChatSessionApiResponse.description: An agent chat session with its full transcript. The session is the conversation; each message sent in it starts a separate agent execution run, listed by `GET /api/agents/execution-runs?chatSessionId={chatSessionId}`.

id.description: Identifier of the chat session.

agentId.description: Identifier of the agent that owns the session.

createdAtUtc.description: When the session was created, in UTC.

updatedAtUtc.description: When the session last changed, in UTC.

messageCount.description: Number of messages in the transcript, including messages written by the product.

lastMessagePreview.description: Text of the last message, cut to 177 characters followed by `...` when longer than 180 characters, or `No messages yet.` for a session without messages.

pendingApprovalCount.description: Number of tool approvals waiting on the session's latest execution run.

autoApprovePendingToolCalls.description: True when the session's latest execution run approves its tool calls automatically.

AgentChatSessionSummaryApiResponse.description: Summary of an agent chat session for session lists.

agentId.description: Identifier of the agent.

sessions.description: Summaries of the agent's chat sessions, most recently updated first; may be empty.

oneOf.description: The selected session with its transcript, or null when the agent has no sessions.

selectedSessionId.description: Identifier of the selected session, or null when none is selected.

oneOf.description: Summary of the most recently updated execution run of the selected session (of the whole agent when no session is selected), or null when there is none.
The selected session's latest execution run with its pending approvals, or null when no session is selected or the session has no run.

AgentChatWorkspaceApiResponse.description: Chat workspace of one agent, returned by `GET /api/agents/{agentId}/chat-workspace` and inside `GET /api/agents/bootstrap`.

cloneName.description: Name of the new agent, trimmed. Its template key is derived from it (lower-case letters and digits separated by hyphens), so it must contain at least one letter or digit and must not normalize to the key of another agent or template.

AgentCloneApiRequest.description: Name of the agent to create by `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/clone`.

sourceKind.description: Kind of the owner record that holds the change, as recorded by the owner.

sourceId.description: Identifier of that owner record, as recorded by the owner.

AgentCommittedEffectApiResponse.description: Identity of a change that the owning feature's receipt confirms was committed by a tool call of a cancelled run. The change exists even though the run was cancelled: read it back from its owner instead of repeating the call.

id.description: Agent identifier, used by the `/api/agents/{agentId}` operations and by execution runs.

name.description: Display name of the agent; also the name the model runtime gives the agent.

roleTitle.description: Role title shown with the agent, for example `Support engineer`; may be empty.

summary.description: Short description of the agent, also given to the model runtime; may be empty.

instructions.description: System instructions sent to the model on every run of the agent.

status.description: Lifecycle status, as a JSON integer: 0 Draft, 1 Active, 2 Suspended, 3 Archived. Many runtime features, such as the first-party runtime tools, run recovery and process steps, require an Active agent that is not a template; Suspended and Archived agents cannot take part in handoffs.

providerProfileId.description: Identifier of the provider profile (a configured model provider, see `GET /api/agents/providers`) the agent uses, or null when none is selected. It is not a model identifier.

model.description: Model identifier within the selected provider profile, for example a model or deployment name; empty means the provider profile's default model.

workload.description: Kind of work the agent does, as a JSON integer: 0 General, 1 Management, 2 Hr, 3 Sales, 4 Assistant, 5 Qa, 6 Support, 7 Programming, 8 Spreadsheet, 9 Mail, 10 Research. Programming and Research enable conversation compaction under the default policy, and the name is the key of AgentRole memory provider assignments.

chatHistoryMode.description: Where the chat history is kept between turns, as a JSON integer: 0 ProviderDefault (kept by the product, except for OpenAI and Azure OpenAI profiles on the Responses transport that do not prefer product-managed history, where the provider keeps it), 1 FrameworkManaged (kept and resent by the product), 2 ProviderManaged (kept by the model provider).

temperature.description: Sampling temperature sent to the model. The server does not check its range, and it is omitted for models that do not accept it.

requirePerServiceCallChatHistoryPersiste.description: True to persist the chat history after every model call of a run rather than only at the end. The runtime also does this for product-managed history when approval-requiring tools are attached.

enableBackgroundResponses.description: True to request background (long-running) model responses; it takes effect only when the provider profile supports them.

configurationJson.description: Further configuration as a JSON string containing a JSON object: the access settings (keys `projectStructure`, `processes`, `workspaceTools`, `imageGeneration`, `voiceAccess`, `memory`), model parameters such as `modelParameters.reasoningEffort` and other agent options. The editor form exposes the access settings as typed members. It can contain encrypted external-folder bindings; treat it as sensitive.

isTemplate.description: True for a template: an agent definition used to create working agents with `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/clone`.

templateKey.description: Canonical key of the agent, derived from its template key or name: lower-case letters and digits separated by hyphens, unique among all agents and templates.

permissions.description: Runtime permissions of the agent's runs; not HTTP permissions.

capabilities.description: Catalog capabilities assigned to the agent, each with its proof state.

tags.description: Free-form labels, trimmed and unique ignoring case.

createdAtUtc.description: Instant, with offset, at which the agent was created.

updatedAtUtc.description: Concurrency revision of the agent: an instant, with offset, that advances with accepted changes. The editor form returns it as `expectedUpdatedAtUtc` for the next save, and a package import that replaces this agent must send it as `expectedAgentVersion`.

avatarImageUrl.description: Avatar image reference, or null when none is set. The product uses a bundled avatar path (for example `_content/CanDoItAll.Components.BaseLib/assets/identity/avatars/avatar-01.jpg`) or a `data:` image URL; the API stores any trimmed text.

AgentDefinition.description: Stored technical agent definition: the Agents-owned configuration and identity that agent execution runs use. Returned by `GET /api/agents` and `GET /api/agents/teams/{teamId}/agents`. The CRM/HR party that represents an agent is a projection of this record, not another definition. To change an agent, read and save its editor form (`GET /api/agents/{agentId}`, `POST /api/agents`).

id.description: Identifier of the agent. Null for a new agent, which receives a server-generated identifier; the identifier of an existing agent to replace it. An identifier that does not exist yet creates the agent with that identifier. Must be null for the external-key operation.

expectedUpdatedAtUtc.description: Concurrency revision from the latest read (the agent's `updatedAtUtc`), sent back unchanged. When present, the save is rejected with HTTP 400 unless it equals the stored revision exactly, including when the agent does not exist. Null skips the check: use null for a create; for an update it overwrites without protection. Must be null for the external-key operation.

name.description: Display name, trimmed. When `templateKey` is blank the agent's canonical key is derived from it.

roleTitle.description: Role title shown with the agent, trimmed; may be empty.

summary.description: Short description of the agent, trimmed; may be empty.

instructions.description: System instructions sent to the model on every run, trimmed.
