AgentVoiceAccessSettings.description: Voice settings of an agent, the `voiceAccess` member of the agent editor form, stored in the agent's `configurationJson` under `voiceAccess`. A save replaces that section, and an omitted or empty object removes it. They affect the voice features of the chat interface only; they attach no runtime tools.

AgentVoiceDriverKind.description: Voice driver that performs speech-to-text or text-to-speech, as a JSON integer: 0 OpenAi, the only driver, which sends the audio request through the selected provider profile.

speechToText.description: Speech-to-text settings. Transcription is disabled by default.

textToSpeech.description: Text-to-speech settings. Speech output is disabled by default.

sampleText.description: Text spoken when a user previews the selected voice. A blank value falls back to the built-in sample sentence when the settings are applied.

disclosureText.description: Notice shown in the voice settings screen that tells users the audio is AI-generated. Defaults to `Voice output is AI-generated.`; a blank value falls back to that default when the settings are applied.

AgentVoiceSettings.description: Agent voice settings: speech-to-text for voice input, text-to-speech for spoken replies, and the texts the voice settings screen uses. They are stored with the workflow settings. When they are applied, text is trimmed, a blank model, voice or text falls back to its default, and an empty provider profile GUID counts as null.

AgentWorkloadKind.description: Kind of work an agent does, as a JSON integer: 0 General, 1 Management, 2 Hr, 3 Sales, 4 Assistant, 5 Qa, 6 Support, 7 Programming, 8 Spreadsheet, 9 Mail, 10 Research. It labels the agent, is the key of AgentRole memory provider assignments and feeds process-readiness scoring; Programming and Research also enable conversation compaction under the default policy.

profile.description: Permission preset, as a JSON integer: 0 Custom (the default), 1 ReadOnly, 2 SoftwareDevelopment, 3 QualityValidation, 4 ArchitectureReview, 5 SecurityReview, 6 BusinessAnalysis. The preset's permissions are added to the explicit flags below and cannot be switched off by them; see the `AgentWorkspaceToolProfileKind` schema for what each preset grants. An undefined value is stored as Custom.

canReadFiles.description: Allows reading workspace files and folders (listing, search, read, compare, git history and inspection). True by default, and implied by every write, command or external-folder permission.

canWriteFiles.description: Allows creating and writing workspace files (including archives and spreadsheets). Implied by `canManageWorkspacePaths`, `canScaffoldProjects` and `canTransformArtifacts`.

canRunValidationCommands.description: Allows running the .NET restore, build, test, run and stop commands in the workspace.

canRunLocalScripts.description: Allows running Python files and PowerShell scripts from the workspace.

canScaffoldProjects.description: Allows creating projects from .NET templates in the workspace.

canManageWorkspacePaths.description: Allows copying, moving and deleting workspace paths and changing git state (stage, commit, branch).

canTransformArtifacts.description: Allows converting documents and analyzing images; it also enables image analysis of Project Structure assets for agents with Project Structure read access.

allowedExternalTargetAliases.description: External folders outside the workspace that the agent may write under, as external-target aliases of the form `external-target/v1/{rootId}/{encoded path}`. Values that are not aliases are dropped silently; legacy aliases that embed a drive letter are rejected. A plain file-system path cannot be sent here. Send back the values as read.

externalTargetRootBindings.description: Server-issued root bindings that let the aliases in `allowedExternalTargetAliases` resolve to folders on the host. Send back the values as read; bindings that no alias uses are removed on save.

canReadStorage.description: Adds the storage tools that list catalogs, browse and read text files of the permitted catalogs.

canWriteStorage.description: Adds the storage tools that write text files and delete objects in the permitted catalogs (approval required by default); implies `canReadStorage`.

allowAllStorageCatalogs.description: True to permit every storage catalog; `allowedStorageCatalogIds` is then not needed.

allowedStorageCatalogIds.description: Identifiers of the storage catalogs the storage tools may use when `allowAllStorageCatalogs` is false. They are not checked for existence when saved.

AgentWorkspaceToolAccessSettings.description: Workspace file, command and storage tool permissions of an agent, the `workspaceToolAccess` member of the agent editor form, stored in the agent's `configurationJson` under `workspaceTools`. A save replaces that section. When the section is absent, the agent has the default: profile Custom with only file reading allowed; an omitted object in a save therefore resets the agent to that default. The tools also need the agent's `canUseTools` permission, and tools that change files or run commands need approval of each call unless the run suppresses approvals.

AgentWorkspaceToolProfileKind.description: Preset of workspace tool permissions, as a JSON integer: 0 Custom (no preset; only the explicit flags apply), 1 ReadOnly (read files), 2 SoftwareDevelopment (read, write, validation commands, local scripts, scaffolding, path management, artifact transformation), 3 QualityValidation (read, write, validation commands, local scripts, artifact transformation), 4 ArchitectureReview (read, write, artifact transformation), 5 SecurityReview (read, write, validation commands, artifact transformation), 6 BusinessAnalysis (read, write, artifact transformation). A preset is a minimum: its permissions are added to the explicit flags and cannot be switched off by them.

AiResourceBindingStatus.description: State of the link between an AI agent party in CRM/HR and a technical agent definition of the Agents module, as a JSON integer: 0 Unbound (no technical agent is linked), 1 PendingBackfill (a legacy CRM/HR technical profile waits to be linked to an agent definition), 2 Bound (linked to a technical agent definition), 3 Error (the linked technical agent is not available to CRM/HR).

apiEnabled.description: True when `Api:Enabled` is set, which maps the `/api` route families. The Project Structure (`/api/project-structure`) and runtime (`/api/runtime`) routes stay available even when it is false. Always true in a response of `GET /api/access/status`, which exists only while the API is enabled.

openApiEnabled.description: True when the OpenAPI document is served at `/openapi/v1.json` and `/swagger/v1/swagger.json`.

swaggerUiEnabled.description: True when the interactive Swagger UI is served at `/swagger`; false whenever the OpenAPI document is disabled.

authorizationEnabled.description: True when API operations require a bearer token issued by this host (`Api:Authorization:Enabled`). When false, most operations accept calls without a token and tokens cannot be issued; operations that need an authenticated caller (answering workflow external requests, agent recruiting reviews, storage placement recovery) then always fail with HTTP 401 or 403.

signingKeyConfigured.description: True when a token signing key is configured. Only its presence is reported, never its value.

issuer.description: Issuer (`iss` claim) that tokens must carry to be accepted by this host.

audience.description: Audience (`aud` claim) that tokens must carry to be accepted by this host.

defaultTokenLifetimeMinutes.description: Lifetime in minutes given to a token issued without `lifetimeMinutes`.

maxTokenLifetimeMinutes.description: Largest `lifetimeMinutes` accepted when a token is issued.

ApiAccessStatus.description: HTTP API access configuration of this host, returned by `GET /api/access/status`. It reflects the host's `Api` configuration section and never contains the signing key or a token.

ok.description: True: the command completed. A failed command never returns this object.

ApiAck.description: Acknowledgement returned by a command that has no other result. A success response always carries `{ "ok": true }`; failures use an error response instead.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, for example `crmhr.party.not-found` or `agents.run-failed`. Branch on this value, not on the message.

message.description: Human-readable explanation for operators and logs. Its wording can change.

severity.description: Severity of the reason, as a JSON integer: 0 Info, 1 Warning (request validation problems), 2 Error (failed commands). Any item in an error envelope means the request did not succeed.

ApiErrorItem.description: One reason in an error envelope.

errors.description: The reasons the request was rejected or failed, in the order they were detected.

correlationId.description: Server trace identifier of the failed request, for support and log correlation. Present on agent run and agent command failures; omitted otherwise. It is not an idempotency key and does not identify a committed effect.

agentId.description: Identifier of the agent whose run or command failed. Omitted when the failure is not tied to an agent.

executionRunId.description: Identifier of the agent execution run that failed, usable with the agent run read operations. Omitted when no execution run was created.

chatSessionId.description: Identifier of the agent chat session in which the run failed. Omitted when the run was not part of a chat session.

oneOf.description: Category of a model-provider failure when an agent run failed while calling its provider: requestCompatibility is returned with HTTP 400, providerConfiguration with HTTP 422, and quotaOrBilling, rateLimit and providerError with HTTP 503. Omitted for other failures.

ApiErrorResponse.description: Error envelope of the general API families (for example agents, workflows, processes, projects and CRM/HR): an `errors` array with at least one item, plus correlation fields when an agent run or command failed. Project Structure, LLM Chat and shared-provider operations use their own error formats. The HTTP status alone does not prove that nothing was written; check the operation's documentation for its effect guarantees.

subject.description: Subject (`sub` claim) of the token: the caller identity recorded for the token and used by operations that scope records to their caller, for example memory-provider operation status. Surrounding whitespace is removed; a blank value is rejected. Omitted means `api-client`. Tokens with the same subject share that identity.

displayName.description: Human-readable name of the token, shown in token administration. Surrounding whitespace is removed; omitted or blank means `API client`.

lifetimeMinutes.description: Token lifetime in minutes, from 1 through the configured maximum (`maxTokenLifetimeMinutes` of `GET /api/access/status`). Omitted or null means the configured default lifetime.

scopes.description: Scopes to grant, for example `api` or `api.memory-providers.read`. Values are trimmed, blank values are dropped and duplicates that differ only in letter case are merged; at least one scope must remain. Names are not checked against the known scopes, and operations compare them exactly and case-sensitively. Omitted means `["api"]`.

ApiTokenIssueRequest.description: Request of `POST /api/access/tokens`: who the new bearer token represents, how long it lives and which scopes it grants. Every member is optional; an omitted member takes the default stated on it. Do not send null for `subject` or `displayName`: an explicit null is not handled and fails the request, so omit the member instead.

token.description: The signed JSON Web Token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer {token}`; never put it in a URL or log.

tokenType.description: Authorization scheme to use with the token; always `Bearer`.

expiresAtUtc.description: Instant (UTC, with offset) after which the host rejects the token.

subject.description: The normalized subject (`sub` claim) of the token.

displayName.description: The normalized display name of the token.

scopes.description: The scopes granted by the token after normalization, sorted alphabetically without regard to letter case.

ApiTokenIssueResult.description: A newly issued bearer token, returned once by `POST /api/access/tokens`. The token value cannot be read again later; treat it as a secret.

target.description: The run to record. It must exist in the current workspace and show participation of the interview's candidate.

challengeKey.description: Caller-defined key of the challenge given to the candidate, 1 to 200 characters.

challengeVersion.description: Caller-defined version of the challenge, 1 to 100 characters.

rubricVersion.description: Version of the rubric used to evaluate the attempt, 1 to 100 characters.

inputHash.description: SHA-256 of the challenge input: 64 hexadecimal digits, optionally prefixed with `sha256:`. An empty string or null leaves the attempt incomplete (`input-hash`); any other value is rejected with `agent-recruiting.hash-invalid`.

outputHash.description: SHA-256 of the candidate's output, in the same form as `inputHash`.

structuredOutputContractKey.description: Key of the structured-output contract the output had to satisfy, at most 200 characters; an empty string or null when none applies. When set, the attempt is complete only if `structuredOutputValidationStatus` is `succeeded`.

structuredOutputSchemaHash.description: SHA-256 of that contract's schema, in the same form as `inputHash`; an empty string or null when none.

structuredOutputValidationStatus.description: Validation status of the structured output, at most 100 characters; `succeeded` (compared case-insensitively) marks a successful validation. An empty string or null when no contract applies.

oneOf.description: Automated evaluation of the attempt. Send null when there is none; the attempt is then incomplete (`automated-evaluation`).
Optional structured analysis for reviewers; omit it or send null when there is none.

AppendAgentRecruitingAttemptCommand.description: Request to append an attempt to an agent recruiting interview: the finished run whose result is assessed, the challenge and rubric, integrity hashes, the automated evaluation and an optional analysis. Missing evidence does not reject the request; the attempt is then stored as incomplete and lists what is missing. Send every member except `analysis`, using an empty string or null where a value is not available.

attemptId.description: Identifier of the reviewed attempt; it must belong to the interview in the route.

decision.description: Decision of the reviewer, as a JSON string: `Approved` or `Rejected` (the integers 0 and 1 are also accepted).

reviewerActorId.description: Optional check: when not blank, it must equal the bearer token's subject exactly (`agent-recruiting.reviewer-identity-conflict`). The stored reviewer is always the token subject.

reviewerDisplayName.description: Reviewer name, at most 200 characters, used only when the token carries no name claim.

authorizationReference.description: Reference to the authorization behind an approval, at most 500 characters. An approval without it is stored but does not qualify for readiness.

authorizationEvidenceHash.description: SHA-256 of the authorization evidence: 64 hexadecimal digits, optionally prefixed with `sha256:`. An approval without it is stored but does not qualify for readiness; any other non-empty value is rejected with `agent-recruiting.hash-invalid`.

notes.description: Notes of the reviewer, at most 4000 characters.

AppendAgentRecruitingReviewCommand.description: Request to append a human review to one attempt of an agent recruiting interview. The stored reviewer identity is always taken from the authenticated bearer token. Send every member, using an empty string where a value is not available.

ApplicationPurposeRootConfigurationSourc.description: Where the location of an application purpose root comes from, as a string token: `PlatformDefault` (the default location for the operating system), `ExplicitConfiguration` (a configured path), `ActiveDatabaseProfile` (the workspace root stored with the active database profile), `DerivedFromControlPlaneRoot` (a location under the configured control-plane root) or `OwnerResolved` (resolved by its owning component without a reported source).

ApplicationPurposeRootKind.description: Application purpose root, as a string token: `Workspace` (workspace data), `ControlPlane` (host control-plane settings), `DatabaseProfiles` (database profile catalog), `DataProtectionKeys` (ASP.NET Core Data Protection keys), `State`, `Logs` or `RuntimeTemporary` (temporary runtime data).

purpose.description: The root, as a string token: `Workspace`, `ControlPlane`, `DatabaseProfiles`, `DataProtectionKeys`, `State`, `Logs` or `RuntimeTemporary`.

configurationSource.description: Where the root's location comes from, as a string token: `PlatformDefault`, `ExplicitConfiguration`, `ActiveDatabaseProfile`, `DerivedFromControlPlaneRoot` or `OwnerResolved`.

state.description: Whether the root is usable, as a string token: `Ready` or `Unavailable`.

reason.description: Why, as a string token: `Ready`, `InvalidConfiguration`, `AccessDenied`, `UnsafePath` or `IoFailure`.

ApplicationPurposeRootReadiness.description: Readiness of one application purpose root in a runtime host snapshot: which root, where its location comes from and whether the host can use it. The root's path itself is never reported.

kind.description: Kind of the referenced artifact: `project` for the project root node, `prompt` for a prompt node bound to its Prompt Gallery prompt, `test-plan` for the Test command, and otherwise usually the node's object type name, for example `WorkItem` or `File`.

entityId.description: Identifier of the referenced artifact, a GUID, for example the project or the Prompt Gallery prompt; null when the node refers to no separate artifact.

title.description: Display title: the node's title, or `Test Lab` for the Test command.

route.description: Relative web application route to open: for example `/projects/{projectId}/structure` for an ordinary node, the managed file's preview route for a file or media node, or `/test-lab?projectId={projectId}`.

description.description: The node's notes, or a fixed description for the Test command; may be empty.

projectId.description: Identifier of the project the node belongs to.

artifactKey.description: Identifier of the node the reference was resolved for; null for the Test command.

projectName.description: Not set by node commands; always null.

phaseName.description: Not set by node commands; always null.

snapshotJson.description: Not set by node commands; always null.

tabKind.description: Workbench tab that shows the reference: `project-overview` (project root), `prompt-detail` (prompt nodes), `processes`, `workflows`, `validation-run`, `test-plan` (test plans and evidence), `project-structure` or `project-calendar` (nodes shown on those pages) or `page`; null for the Test command.

ArtifactReference.description: Reference to the application page or artifact that a project structure node opens, returned by a node command. Open `route` in the web application to show it.

defaultEffect.description: What happens to candidates no rule decides: `denyAll` (a candidate needs a matching allow or require rule), or `inherit` (the default when blank) and `allowAssigned`, which both allow every candidate that no deny rule matches.

rules.description: The rules of the policy; empty for none.

CapabilityAccessPolicyTemplateDto.description: Capability access policy written with text tokens. Tokens are member names matched ignoring case, hyphens and underscores, so `denyAll`, `deny-all` and `DenyAll` are equal; numbers are not accepted. Every problem is reported as a validation issue with the JSON path of the offending member.

identity.description: Kind and key of the candidate, in the identity numbering.

displayName.description: Display name of the candidate; the key when the name is blank.

isAllowed.description: True when the policy allows the candidate.

diagnostics.description: Reasons the candidate is suppressed; empty when it is allowed.

CapabilityAccessPreviewCapabilityRow.description: Preview result for one candidate capability. An MCP server candidate produces a row for the server and one row per allowed MCP tool.

capabilityIds.description: Identifiers of saved catalog capabilities to use as candidates; empty uses every saved capability.

draftCapabilities.description: Unsaved capability forms to add as candidates. A draft replaces the saved candidate with the same `id`, or with the same key (ignoring case) when its `id` is null. Their `kind` uses the catalog numbering: 0 McpServer, 1 Skill, 2 Tool, 3 Plugin, 4 Rag, 5 AiContext.

policy.description: The access policy to compile and evaluate against the candidates.

requiredCapabilities.description: Capabilities the policy is expected to allow; a Require rule that matches no candidate produces a diagnostic.

correlationId.description: Correlation identifier to put on the diagnostics; blank generates `access-preview-` followed by a new GUID.

CapabilityAccessPreviewRequest.description: Candidate capabilities and an access policy to evaluate without saving anything, sent to `POST /api/agents/capabilities/access-preview`. Send empty arrays rather than null lists.

validationResult.description: Validation issues of the candidates and the policy.

effectiveSet.description: The candidates the policy allows and the ones it suppresses, with reasons.

capabilities.description: One row per candidate, in candidate order.

CapabilityAccessPreviewResult.description: Result of an access policy preview. When the policy or any candidate is invalid, `validationResult` lists the issues, the effective set is empty and no row is allowed.

id.description: Identifier of the rule in lower kebab case, unique within the policy ignoring case.

effect.description: Effect of the rule: `allow`, `deny` or `require` (allow, and report a diagnostic when no allowed candidate matches). `inherit` is rejected for rules.

scope.description: Level at which the rule is declared: `system`, `agentDefault`, `workflowDefinition`, `workflowNode`, `processDefinition`, `processStep`, `runtimeOverride` or `uiPreview`. When several deny rules match, the scope decides which one is reported.

oneOf.description: What the rule matches; required.

reason.description: Why the rule exists; required, and reported with the capabilities the rule suppresses.

CapabilityAccessRuleTemplateDto.description: One rule of a capability access policy. A matching deny rule wins over any allow rule.

CapabilityAccessScope.description: Level at which a capability access rule is declared, as a JSON integer: 0 System, 1 AgentDefault, 2 WorkflowDefinition, 3 WorkflowNode, 4 ProcessDefinition, 5 ProcessStep, 6 RuntimeOverride, 7 UiPreview.

CapabilityAvailabilityState.description: Whether a capability can be used, as a JSON integer: 0 Available, 1 Retired, 2 Unavailable, 3 FailedSetup (its definition did not pass validation).

id.description: Identifier of the capability; agents select it by this value.

kind.description: Kind, as a JSON integer: 0 McpServer, 1 Skill, 2 Tool, 3 Plugin, 4 Rag, 5 AiContext, 6 Memory (retired).

key.description: Stable normalized key, unique per kind.

description.description: Description; may be empty.

endpointOrPath.description: Endpoint URL, command or path the capability uses, depending on its kind; may be empty.

configurationJson.description: Kind-specific settings as stored, returned without redaction.

proofStatus.description: Result of the latest verification through any agent, as a JSON integer: 0 NotRun, 1 Verified, 2 Failed, 3 PendingReview. It is informational: the runtime does not use it to decide what a run may use.

proofNotes.description: Notes of the latest verification; empty when never verified.

lastVerifiedAtUtc.description: When the latest verification ran, in UTC, or null when never verified.

isBuiltIn.description: True for a capability shipped with the product.

tags.description: Labels of the capability, lower-case and sorted.

CapabilityCatalogItem.description: A capability in the workspace catalog, listed by `GET /api/agents/capabilities`: a declared MCP server, skill, tool, plugin, retrieval source or context message that agents can select. It is a declaration only: a run grants tools from it only as the runtime's permissions and invocation policy allow.

category.description: Category, as a JSON integer: 0 TemplateValidation, 1 SecretBinding, 2 CommandPolicy, 3 ProcessStart, 4 ProcessExit, 5 Timeout, 6 McpHandshake, 7 McpListTools, 8 SchemaValidation, 9 JsonParse, 10 HttpStatus, 11 Cancellation, 12 ImplementationMissing, 13 RuntimeAdapter, 14 ResourceCleanup, 15 AccessPolicy, 16 CapabilityUnavailable, 17 RequiredCapabilityDenied, 18 RuntimeDependency, 19 PackageSetup, 20 WorkingDirectory, 21 UnsupportedPlatform, 22 PermissionDenied.

severity.description: Severity, as a JSON integer: 0 Info, 1 Warning, 2 Error.

oneOf.description: Identity kind of the affected capability, as a JSON integer (0 Skill, 1 Tool, 2 McpServer, 3 McpTool, 4 Plugin, 5 Rag, 6 AiContext, 7 Memory), or null.
Key of the affected capability, or null.
Path of the affected template, or null.

fieldPath.description: JSON path of the affected setting, for example `$.jsonInput`.

oneOf.description: Key of the affected implementation, or null.

How the capability is reached, as a JSON integer (0 InternalHosted, 1 InternalImplementation, 2 ExternalProcess, 3 ExternalHttp, 4 LocalStdio, 5 RemoteHttp, 6 FileSkill, 7 InlineSkill, 8 RegisteredSkill), or null.

exitCode.description: Exit code of a tested process, or null.

httpStatusCode.description: HTTP status code returned by a tested endpoint, or null.

timeout.description: Timeout that was exceeded, as a time span string, or null.

correlationId.description: Correlation identifier of the test or preview.

maskedDetail.description: Description of the problem with secret values masked.

CapabilityDiagnostic.description: A problem found while validating or testing a capability definition. Details are masked so that secret values are not returned.

CapabilityDiagnosticCategory.description: Category of a capability diagnostic, as a JSON integer: 0 TemplateValidation, 1 SecretBinding, 2 CommandPolicy, 3 ProcessStart, 4 ProcessExit, 5 Timeout, 6 McpHandshake, 7 McpListTools, 8 SchemaValidation, 9 JsonParse, 10 HttpStatus, 11 Cancellation, 12 ImplementationMissing, 13 RuntimeAdapter, 14 ResourceCleanup, 15 AccessPolicy, 16 CapabilityUnavailable, 17 RequiredCapabilityDenied, 18 RuntimeDependency, 19 PackageSetup, 20 WorkingDirectory, 21 UnsupportedPlatform, 22 PermissionDenied.

id.description: Identifier of the capability: null to create one (the server assigns the identifier), or the identifier of an existing capability to replace it; an unknown identifier is rejected.

expectedFingerprint.description: Concurrency fingerprint from the editor read. On an update, a value that no longer matches the stored capability rejects the save and null or blank skips the check; on a create it must be null or blank.

kind.description: Kind of the capability, as a JSON integer: 0 McpServer, 1 Skill (the default), 2 Tool, 3 Plugin, 4 Rag, 5 AiContext; 6 Memory is retired and rejected.

key.description: Stable key of the capability, normalized to lower-case letters and digits with other characters collapsed to hyphens; it must contain a letter or digit and be unique per kind.

description.description: Description; trimmed.

endpointOrPath.description: Endpoint URL, command or path the capability uses, depending on its kind; trimmed.

configurationJson.description: Kind-specific settings, normally the text of a JSON object: a Skill's configuration must be a JSON object and other kinds are stored as sent. It is returned without redaction, so never put secret values in it.

isBuiltIn.description: True for a capability shipped with the product. It is stored as sent, but shipped capabilities are restored to their shipped definition whenever the catalog is written.

tags.description: Labels of the capability; trimmed, a leading `#` removed, lower-cased and de-duplicated.

CapabilityEditorModel.description: Editable form of a catalog capability, read from `GET /api/agents/capabilities/{capabilityId}/editor` and sent whole to `POST /api/agents/capabilities`. A save replaces the capability's definition and keeps its proof fields. A catalog capability is a declaration: agents use it only when selected in their `selectedCapabilityIds`, and each run still grants tools only as the runtime's policies allow.

identity.description: Kind and key of the capability, in the identity numbering.

displayName.description: Display name.

description.description: Description.

oneOf.description: Key of the implementation behind the capability, or null.
Name of the runtime tool the capability exposes, or null.
Key of the MCP server the capability belongs to, or null.
Name of the MCP tool, for an MCP tool capability; otherwise null.

operationClassifications.description: Kinds of operation the capability performs, as JSON integers: 0 Read, 1 Write, 2 Mutation, 3 Validation, 4 ScriptExecution, 5 BrowserAccess, 6 ProjectStructure, 7 DocumentProcessing, 8 ProviderNative, 9 ExternalAction, 10 McpTool, 11 RuntimeLaunch, 12 ResourceCleanup.

sideEffectProfile.description: Declared side effect of the capability.

availabilityState.description: Whether the capability can be used, as a JSON integer: 0 Available, 1 Retired, 2 Unavailable, 3 FailedSetup (its definition did not pass validation).

oneOf.description: Path of the template the capability comes from, or null.

CapabilityExposureDescriptor.description: A capability as a candidate for exposure to a run, with the properties that access policies match on.

kind.description: Identity kind, as a JSON integer: 0 Skill, 1 Tool, 2 McpServer, 3 McpTool, 4 Plugin, 5 Rag, 6 AiContext, 7 Memory (the identity numbering, not the catalog numbering).

CapabilityIdentity.description: Kind and key identifying a capability in setup tests and access previews.

kind.description: Identity kind, as a JSON integer in the identity numbering (not the catalog numbering): 0 Skill, 1 Tool (the default), 2 McpServer, 3 McpTool, 4 Plugin, 5 Rag, 6 AiContext, 7 Memory.

key.description: Capability key in lower kebab case, for example `release-notes`; an invalid key is reported as a validation issue.

CapabilityIdentityEditorModel.description: Kind and key identifying a capability that an access policy is expected to allow.

value.description: The key: groups of lower-case ASCII letters and digits separated by single hyphens.

CapabilityKey.description: Capability key in lower kebab case, for example `release-notes`. It is serialized as an object whose `value` member holds the key.

CapabilityKind.description: Kind of a catalog capability, as a JSON integer: 0 McpServer (an MCP server whose tools a run can use), 1 Skill (a skill or inline skill instructions), 2 Tool (for example an external process or HTTP tool), 3 Plugin (plugin tools), 4 Rag (retrieval context), 5 AiContext (a context message), 6 Memory (retired; rejected when saved). Used by catalog capabilities, capability editors and agent capability assignments. The schema name `CapabilityKind` is shared with the capability identity kind of setup tests and access previews, which numbers kinds differently (0 Skill, 1 Tool, 2 McpServer, 3 McpTool, 4 Plugin, 5 Rag, 6 AiContext, 7 Memory); each member's description states the numbering it uses.

capability.description: The MCP server capability form to test; the server is read from its `configurationJson` and its kind is ignored.

correlationId.description: Correlation identifier to put on the diagnostics; blank generates `mcp-setup-` followed by a new GUID.

CapabilityMcpSetupTestRequest.description: MCP server capability definition to test by starting or connecting to the server and listing its tools, sent to `POST /api/agents/capabilities/setup-tests/mcp`. The definition does not have to be saved; nothing is written to the catalog.

CapabilityOperationClassification.description: Kind of operation a capability performs, as a JSON integer: 0 Read, 1 Write, 2 Mutation, 3 Validation, 4 ScriptExecution, 5 BrowserAccess, 6 ProjectStructure, 7 DocumentProcessing, 8 ProviderNative, 9 ExternalAction, 10 McpTool, 11 RuntimeLaunch, 12 ResourceCleanup.

CapabilityProofStatus.description: Result of a capability verification, as a JSON integer: 0 NotRun (never verified), 1 Verified (the verification's checks passed), 2 Failed (a blocking problem was found, for example a missing file, an unreachable endpoint or raw secrets in the configuration), 3 PendingReview (recorded, but it cannot be proven by a local check). It is informational: the runtime does not use it to decide whether a capability is attached to a run.

value.description: The identifier: groups of lower-case ASCII letters and digits separated by single hyphens.

CapabilityRuleId.description: Identifier of a capability access rule in lower kebab case, serialized as an object whose `value` member holds the identifier.

CapabilitySelectorKind.description: What a capability access rule matches on, as a JSON integer: 0 All, 1 Kind, 2 CapabilityKey, 3 Tag, 4 OperationClassification, 5 RuntimeToolName, 6 McpServerKey, 7 McpToolName, 8 ImplementationKey.

kind.description: Selector kind: `all`, `kind`, `capabilityKey`, `tag`, `operationClassification`, `runtimeToolName`, `mcpServerKey`, `mcpToolName` or `implementationKey`.

value.description: Value to match, in the form the selector kind needs: a capability kind name such as `tool` or `mcpServer` for `kind`; a lower kebab-case key or tag for `capabilityKey`, `tag` and `mcpServerKey`; an operation classification name such as `read` or `externalAction`; a lower snake_case name for `runtimeToolName`; the MCP tool name for `mcpToolName`; an implementation key for `implementationKey`. Ignored for `all`.

serverKey.description: Lower kebab-case key of the MCP server; required for `mcpToolName` selectors and ignored otherwise.

CapabilitySelectorTemplateDto.description: What a capability access rule matches.

isSuccess.description: True when the definition was valid and the test call succeeded.

identity.description: Kind and key of the tested capability, in the identity numbering.

diagnostics.description: Problems found; empty when the test succeeded.

CapabilitySetupTestResult.description: Result of a tool capability setup test.

CapabilitySideEffectKind.description: Main side effect of a capability, as a JSON integer: 0 None, 1 WorkspaceRead, 2 WorkspaceWrite, 3 LocalProcessExecution, 4 RuntimeLaunch, 5 RuntimeProofCapture, 6 ProcessMutation, 7 ProjectStructureMutation, 8 ExternalAction, 9 MediaGeneration, 10 DocumentConversion, 11 ProviderNative, 12 McpTool, 13 InternalDataRead, 14 InternalStateMutation.

kind.description: Main side effect, as a JSON integer: 0 None, 1 WorkspaceRead, 2 WorkspaceWrite, 3 LocalProcessExecution, 4 RuntimeLaunch, 5 RuntimeProofCapture, 6 ProcessMutation, 7 ProjectStructureMutation, 8 ExternalAction, 9 MediaGeneration, 10 DocumentConversion, 11 ProviderNative, 12 McpTool, 13 InternalDataRead, 14 InternalStateMutation.

requiresApprovalByDefault.description: True when calls need an approval unless a policy says otherwise.

isStateChanging.description: True when calls can change state.

CapabilitySideEffectProfile.description: Declared side effect of a capability.

value.description: The tag: groups of lower-case ASCII letters and digits separated by single hyphens.

CapabilityTag.description: Capability tag in lower kebab case, serialized as an object whose `value` member holds the tag.

capability.description: The tool capability form to test; the tool is read from its `configurationJson` and its kind is ignored.

jsonInput.description: Input to send to the tool, as the text of a JSON object; blank is treated as `{}`. Any other JSON value is reported as a diagnostic.

correlationId.description: Correlation identifier to put on the diagnostics; blank generates `tool-setup-` followed by a new GUID.

CapabilityToolSetupTestRequest.description: Tool capability definition to test once, sent to `POST /api/agents/capabilities/setup-tests/tool`. The definition does not have to be saved; nothing is written to the catalog.

CapabilityTransportKind.description: How a capability is reached, as a JSON integer: 0 InternalHosted, 1 InternalImplementation, 2 ExternalProcess, 3 ExternalHttp, 4 LocalStdio (a local MCP server process), 5 RemoteHttp (a remote MCP server), 6 FileSkill, 7 InlineSkill, 8 RegisteredSkill.

category.description: Category, as a JSON integer: 0 TemplateValidation, 1 SecretBinding, 2 CommandPolicy, 3 ProcessStart, 4 ProcessExit, 5 Timeout, 6 McpHandshake, 7 McpListTools, 8 SchemaValidation, 9 JsonParse, 10 HttpStatus, 11 Cancellation, 12 ImplementationMissing, 13 RuntimeAdapter, 14 ResourceCleanup, 15 AccessPolicy, 16 CapabilityUnavailable, 17 RequiredCapabilityDenied, 18 RuntimeDependency, 19 PackageSetup, 20 WorkingDirectory, 21 UnsupportedPlatform, 22 PermissionDenied.

severity.description: Severity, as a JSON integer: 0 Info, 1 Warning, 2 Error.

oneOf.description: Identity kind of the affected capability, as a JSON integer (0 Skill, 1 Tool, 2 McpServer, 3 McpTool, 4 Plugin, 5 Rag, 6 AiContext, 7 Memory), or null.
Key of the affected capability, or null.
Path of the affected template, or null.

fieldPath.description: JSON path of the affected setting.

message.description: Description of the problem.

CapabilityValidationIssue.description: A validation problem of a capability definition or an access policy.

issues.description: The problems found; empty when there are none.

isValid.description: Set by the server: true when no issue has severity 2 Error.

CapabilityValidationResult.description: Validation result of capability definitions or an access policy.

CapabilityValidationSeverity.description: Severity of a capability diagnostic or validation issue, as a JSON integer: 0 Info, 1 Warning, 2 Error; only Error makes a result invalid.

agentId.description: Identifier of the agent from the request route.

capabilityId.description: Identifier of the catalog capability from the request route.

outcome.description: Why no proof was published, as text: `Rejected` (HTTP 400; the agent, the capability, its single assignment or the agent's provider could not be resolved) or, with HTTP 409, `InfrastructureUnavailable`, `DiagnosticInterrupted`, `Superseded`, `PublicationNotStarted`, `Unconfirmed` (the proof may have been stored), `CanceledBeforeDiagnostic` or `PublicationCanceled`. `Committed` never appears in this response.

proofAttemptId.description: Server-generated identifier of this verification attempt, present once the diagnostic has produced a proof (outcomes `Superseded`, `PublicationCanceled`, `PublicationNotStarted` and `Unconfirmed`); null when the attempt stopped earlier. It identifies the attempt only; it is not a retry key.

proofCheckedAtUtc.description: Instant, with offset, at which the diagnostic produced its proof; present together with `proofAttemptId`.

automaticReplaySafe.description: Always false: do not repeat the verification automatically. Read the agent's capability assignment (`GET /api/agents`) to see whether a proof was stored, and start another verification only as a deliberate new request.

CapabilityVerificationApiResponse.description: Typed failure of a capability verification request (`POST /api/agents/{agentId}/capabilities/{capabilityId}/verify`), returned with HTTP 400 when the attempt was rejected before the diagnostic and with HTTP 409 when it did not publish a proof. It replaces the general `errors` envelope for this operation and never contains internal exception details. A successful verification returns `{ "ok": true }` instead.

CapabilityVerificationDisposition.description: Outcome of one capability verification attempt, written in HTTP responses as the text name of the member. Rejected: the agent or capability does not exist, the capability is not assigned exactly once to the agent, or the agent's provider profile cannot be resolved; no diagnostic ran. CanceledBeforeDiagnostic: the request was cancelled before the diagnostic started. DiagnosticInterrupted: the diagnostic failed or was interrupted without a proof; nothing was published. Superseded: the agent, the capability or the agent's provider changed while the diagnostic ran, so its proof was not published. PublicationCanceled: the request was cancelled after the diagnostic and before publication. PublicationNotStarted: the current catalog could not be read after the diagnostic, so nothing was published. Committed: the proof was published on the agent's capability assignment and on the catalog capability. Unconfirmed: the publication write failed and the proof may or may not have been stored. InfrastructureUnavailable: the catalog or provider state could not be read before the diagnostic.

id.description: Identifier of the capacity block; send it as `id` to update the block.

blockKind.description: Reason for the block, as a JSON integer: 0 Leave, 1 Unavailable, 2 Reserve, 3 Tentative.

endDate.description: Last day of the block, inclusive (`yyyy-MM-dd`).

percentage.description: Share of the party's capacity that the block takes, in percent (above 0, at most 100).

relatedProjectId.description: Identifier of the project the block relates to; null when none.

relatedProjectName.description: Name of the related project; empty when none or when the project no longer exists.

notes.description: Free-text notes; empty when not set.

isActive.description: True when the current UTC date is within the block; active blocks count in `activeBlockedPercent`.

isFuture.description: True when the block starts after the current UTC date.

CapacityBlockItemModel.description: A capacity block of a party as returned in the workforce workspace: a date range in which a percentage of the party's capacity is not available. It is not a task or a project assignment.

CapacityBlockKind.description: Reason for a capacity block, as a JSON integer: 0 Leave, 1 Unavailable, 2 Reserve, 3 Tentative. The kind is descriptive: every active block reduces the party's available capacity by its percentage, whatever its kind.

id.description: Identifier of the block to update, from `capacityBlocks[].id` of the workforce workspace. Omit it to create a block; an unknown identifier creates a new block with a new identifier.

partyId.description: Identifier of the party whose capacity is blocked; required and must exist.

blockKind.description: Reason for the block, as a JSON integer: 0 Leave, 1 Unavailable, 2 Reserve, 3 Tentative; every kind reduces availability in the same way. Omitted means Leave (0).

startDate.description: First day of the block (`yyyy-MM-dd`); required.

endDate.description: Last day of the block, inclusive (`yyyy-MM-dd`); required and not before `startDate`.

percentage.description: Share of the party's capacity that the block takes, in percent: greater than 0 and at most 100. Omitted means 100.

relatedProjectId.description: Project the block relates to, from `GET /api/projects`; it must exist. It is informational and changes no project allocation. Null or omitted means none.

notes.description: Free-text notes; trimmed. Omitted means empty.

CapacityBlockSaveApiRequest.description: Request of `POST /api/crm-hr/workforce/capacity-blocks`: a date range in which a percentage of a party's capacity is not available. All fields are overwritten.

ChatMessageRole.description: Author of a chat message, as a JSON integer: 0 System (system instructions or messages written by the product), 1 User, 2 Assistant. Server-sent event streams write it as camel-case text: `system`, `user`, `assistant`.

title.description: The title. Runs of white space become single spaces and text beyond 96 characters is cut. It must not be blank.

ChatSessionRenameApiRequest.description: New title of an agent chat session, sent to `POST /api/agents/{agentId}/chat-sessions/{chatSessionId}/rename`.

key.description: Key of the field in the settings JSON object, for example `label`; settings keys are compared case-insensitively.

fieldType.description: Value type, as a JSON integer: 0 Text, 1 Url, 2 Number, 3 Boolean, 4 Json, 5 SecretReference, 6 Select, 7 MultilineText, 8 Guid.

isRequired.description: True when the field must have a non-blank value.

helpText.description: Help text shown with the field.

options.description: Allowed values of a Select field; empty for other field types.

numberKind.description: Number format of a Number field, as a JSON integer: 0 Int32, 1 Int64, 2 Decimal, 3 Double. 0 by default; ignored for other field types.

ConfigurationFieldDescriptor.description: One field of a settings form.

value.description: The value to store.

acceptedValues.description: Other values accepted as equivalent to `value` (compared case-insensitively); empty when there are none.

ConfigurationFieldOption.description: One allowed value of a Select settings field.

ConfigurationFieldType.description: Value type of a settings field, as a JSON integer: 0 Text, 1 Url (absolute http or https URL), 2 Number (see `numberKind`), 3 Boolean (`true` or `false`), 4 Json (JSON text), 5 SecretReference (identifier of a stored secret, a non-empty GUID), 6 Select (one of the field's options), 7 MultilineText, 8 Guid (a non-empty GUID).

ConfigurationNumberKind.description: Number format of a Number settings field, as a JSON integer: 0 Int32, 1 Int64, 2 Decimal, 3 Double (finite values only).

version.description: Version label of the form, for example `1.0`.

fields.description: The fields, in display order; empty when there are no settings.

ConfigurationSchema.description: Description of a settings form: the fields of a flat JSON settings object, with their value types and whether they are required. Plugins use it for connection, plugin and workflow executor settings. It is not a JSON Schema document.

candidateAgentId.description: Identifier of the candidate agent in the current workspace, as listed by `GET /api/agents`; not the empty GUID.

candidateConfigurationVersion.description: The candidate's current configuration version, as returned in `currentConfigurationVersion` by `GET /api/agent-recruiting/candidates/{agentId}/readiness` (64 hexadecimal digits, compared case-insensitively). Any other value is rejected with `agent-recruiting.candidate-version-conflict`.

purpose.description: What the assessment must establish, 1 to 500 characters, stored trimmed.

recruitmentApplicationId.description: Optional identifier of the CRM/HR recruitment application the interview supports, from `GET /api/crm-hr/recruiting/applications`. Stored as sent without an existence check; the candidate interview list and readiness can be filtered by it. Omit it or send null when there is none; the empty GUID is rejected.

projectId.description: Optional identifier of a project the interview relates to, stored as sent without an existence check. Omit it or send null when there is none; the empty GUID is rejected.

CreateAgentRecruitingInterviewCommand.description: Request to open an agent recruiting interview for a candidate agent. The interview is fenced to the candidate's current configuration, so the request must name that configuration version.

title.description: Title of the new conversation. Trimmed, at most 200 characters; null, empty or blank becomes `New chat`.

CreateLlmChatConversationApiRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/llm-chats/{definitionId}/conversations`. Only `title` is accepted: the definition comes from the route and the origin is always `api`.

value.description: The generation number; never negative.

DatabaseProfileGeneration.description: Generation of the active database profile within the running host, as an object whose `value` is a non-negative integer. It starts at 0 and increases each time the host switches its active database profile.

description.description: Description reported by the server; may be empty.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the tool's input as reported by the server, or null.

DiscoveredMcpTool.description: A tool reported by an MCP server during a setup test.

diagnostics.description: Reasons for suppressed or missing capabilities.

EffectiveCapabilitySet.description: Capabilities an access policy allows and the reasons for the ones it suppresses.

ErrorSeverity.description: Severity of an error, as a JSON integer: 0 Info, 1 Warning (for example a rejected request value), 2 Error (a failed command or operation).

ExecutionApprovalStatus.description: Status of a tool approval request of an agent execution run, as a JSON integer: 0 Pending, 1 Approved, 2 Rejected. Query parameters accept the member name or the integer; server-sent event streams write camel-case text such as `pending`.

sourceKind.description: Kind of source that started the run, for example `manual` or `chat-session`; blank becomes `manual`.

sourceId.description: Identifier of the source record; with source kind `chat-session` a blank value becomes the chat session identifier.

correlationId.description: Correlation identifier chosen by the caller; free text.

causationId.description: Identifier of what caused the run; free text.

requestedBy.description: Who requested the run; free text.

requestedByKind.description: Kind of requester, for example `interactive`; free text.

metadataJson.description: Additional metadata as the text of a JSON object, for example `{}`; text that is not a JSON object is replaced by `{}`. Keys whose names start with `agent` are reserved for the product and must not be sent.

processRunId.description: Identifier of the owning process run; set only by process automation.

processStepId.description: Identifier of the owning process step; set only by process automation.

schedulerRunId.description: Identifier of the scheduler run that started the run; free text.

messageId.description: Identifier of the message that started the run; free text.

oneOf.description: Optional structured-output policy stored in the run metadata. It applies only to runs with a built-in typed output contract, which runs started through the HTTP API do not have, so it has no effect on them.

ExecutionInvocationContext.description: Origin labels of an agent execution run, sent as `context` when a run is started. The caller chooses them; they are stored with the run as sent, without length limits, and can be used as filters of `GET /api/agents/execution-runs`. Process automation sets them too: a run whose source kind is `process-step` or that carries a process run or process step identifier is handled as a governed process run, with different validation, approval and tool rules, so other clients must not send those values.

oneOf.description: How a typed final answer must be submitted, as a string: `Disabled`, `Shadow` or `Required`; null keeps the default.

maxStructuredOutputRepairAttempts.description: Number of repair attempts for an invalid typed answer, clamped to 0 through 2; null keeps the default.

requireStructuredOutputValidation.description: True (the default) to validate the typed answer.

allowRequiredFinalizerStructuredOutputRe.description: True to recover the typed answer from the model's text when the required finalizer tool call is missing; the default is false.

ExecutionInvocationPolicy.description: Structured-output policy of an agent execution run, stored in the run metadata. It applies only to runs with a built-in typed output contract started by process automation; runs started through the HTTP API have no such contract, so the policy has no effect on them.

ExecutionState.description: State of an agent execution run, as a JSON integer: 0 Idle (no state; a log entry with it does not change the run), 1 Preparing, 2 Running, 3 WaitingOnTool (stopped until the pending tool approvals are decided), 4 Persisting (storing the result), 5 Completed, 6 Failed (also used for cancelled runs, whose outcome is Cancelled). Query parameters accept the member name or the integer; server-sent event streams write camel-case text such as `waitingOnTool`.

rootId.description: Root identifier used inside external-target aliases: 24 lower-case hexadecimal characters.

hostPlatform.description: Platform of the host the folder belongs to: `windows`, `macos`, `linux` or `other`. A binding only resolves on a host of the same platform.

protectedRootToken.description: Encrypted token holding the folder location, readable only by the issuing host's data protection keys. Opaque; do not change it.

ExternalTargetRootBinding.description: Server-issued binding of an external-target root identifier to a folder on a host, used by agent workspace access to resolve external-target aliases. The folder path is not readable in the binding: it is encrypted in the protected token. Treat bindings as sensitive and send them back exactly as read; clients never create them.

GanttScheduleGesture.description: How a planned task interval is edited, as a JSON integer: 0 Move (shift the whole interval), 1 ResizeStart (change only the start), 2 ResizeEnd (change only the end), 3 SetInterval (set an explicit start and end).

value.description: String node identifier of the task, as returned in `nodes[].id` by the Project Structure read.

GanttTaskId.description: Gantt task identifier object. Its `value` member holds the task's string node identifier.

HistoryAuthenticationKind.description: How the caller of a recorded operation authenticated, as a JSON integer: 0 Unknown (not recorded, for example work started by a background owner), 1 TrustedLocalOperator (the local operator of this host), 2 ManagedCredential (a managed API credential issued by this host), 3 LegacyAuthenticated (a valid bearer token that is not a managed credential), 4 AuthenticationDisabled (API authorization was disabled for the request).

kind.description: How the caller authenticated, as a JSON integer: 0 Unknown, 1 TrustedLocalOperator, 2 ManagedCredential, 3 LegacyAuthenticated, 4 AuthenticationDisabled.

oneOf.description: Managed API credential that authenticated the caller; null for every other kind.

issuer.description: Issuer of the caller's credential or token; null when unknown.

subject.description: Subject of the caller's token; `api-authorization-disabled` when API authorization was disabled for the request; null when unknown.

displayName.description: Display name of the managed credential, or `Local operator` for the local operator; null otherwise.

HistoryCaller.description: Caller recorded for an operation: how it authenticated and, for a managed API credential, which one. It identifies the caller for audit and grants nothing.

HostCapabilityAvailability.description: Current availability of a host capability, as a string token: `Available`, `Unavailable` (a dependency is missing or failing), `Unsupported` (the host profile does not support it), `Misconfigured` (its configuration is invalid or unsafe) or `Unverified` (its probe has not completed).

HostCapabilityCriticality.description: Whether the host needs a capability to be ready, as a string token: `Mandatory` (the host is ready only when the capability is available) or `Optional` (the host can be ready without it).

id.description: The capability: `ControlPlanePaths`, `PhysicalFileSystem`, `SecretVault`, `FileToolsDesktop`, `DesktopFileOpen`, `InteractiveTerminal` or `NativeProcessDiscovery`.

criticality.description: `Mandatory` when the host is ready only while the capability is available, otherwise `Optional`.

remediation.description: Human-readable action that would make the capability available, or `None.` when nothing is needed. Its wording can change and must not be parsed.

supportLevel.description: Support level on this host: `Stable`, `BasicLocal`, `DevelopmentOnly`, `ActualHostUnverified` or `Unsupported`.

implementationRegistration.description: `Registered` when this build contains an implementation, `NotRegistered` when it has none.

implementationId.description: Name of the implementing component, for example `CanDoItAll.Infrastructure.ControlPlane` or the secret-vault provider name; null when there is none.

implementationVersion.description: Assembly version of the implementing component; null when unknown.

supportProfile.description: The resolved host profile the entry was evaluated for, for example `WindowsHeadless`; the same as `profile` of the snapshot.

observedAtUtc.description: Instant (UTC, with offset) at which the snapshot was taken.

HostCapabilityDescriptor.description: Availability of one host capability in a runtime snapshot, with the reason and the remediation an operator can apply. Every enumerated member is written as a string token.

HostCapabilityExecutionBoundary.description: Where the implementation of a host capability runs, as a string token: `ManagedProcess` (inside the host process), `OperatingSystem` (operating-system services), `ExternalProcess` or `ExternalService`.

HostCapabilityId.description: Host capability reported by the runtime snapshot, as a string token: `ControlPlanePaths` (control-plane and application purpose-root paths, mandatory), `PhysicalFileSystem` (safe native file system access under those roots, mandatory), `SecretVault` (the configured secret vault, mandatory), `FileToolsDesktop` (desktop file tools, optional), `DesktopFileOpen` (opening files with desktop applications, optional), `InteractiveTerminal` (interactive terminal, optional, not implemented in this build) or `NativeProcessDiscovery` (native process discovery, optional, not implemented in this build).

HostCapabilityImplementationRegistration.description: Whether this build contains an implementation of a host capability, as a string token: `Registered` or `NotRegistered`.

HostCapabilityReasonCode.description: Reason for the availability of a host capability, as a string token: `Ready`, `ProbePending` (the startup probe has not completed), `DisabledByProfile` (the host profile, for example a headless one, turns it off), `DependencyUnavailable`, `UnsupportedByProfile`, `InvalidConfiguration`, `PermissionDenied` (the operating-system account lacks access), `UnsafePath` (a configured path failed the path safety checks), `IoFailure` or `ActualHostValidationDeferred` (available, but support on this kind of host is not yet validated).

profile.description: The resolved host profile, as a string token: `WindowsInteractive`, `WindowsHeadless`, `LinuxInteractive`, `LinuxHeadless`, `MacOsInteractive`, `MacOsHeadless` or `Test` (development test hosts only).

operatingSystem.description: Operating system of the host, as a string token: `Windows`, `Linux` or `MacOs`.

isInteractive.description: True for an interactive (desktop) profile; false for a headless service or container profile, on which desktop capabilities are unsupported.

isReady.description: True when every mandatory capability is available. Optional capabilities do not affect it.

observedAtUtc.description: Instant (UTC, with offset) at which the snapshot was taken.

purposeRoots.description: Readiness of each application purpose root (workspace, control plane, database profiles, Data Protection keys, state, logs and runtime temporary data). Empty when the path probe produced no result.

capabilities.description: One entry per host capability, in a fixed order.

HostCapabilitySnapshot.description: Snapshot of the runtime host: its resolved profile, whether it is ready, the readiness of each application purpose root and the availability of each host capability. Returned by `GET /api/runtime/capabilities` and inside `GET /api/runtime/operations`; each read takes a new snapshot. It contains no paths or secret values.

HostCapabilitySupportLevel.description: Support level of a host capability on this host, as a string token: `Stable`, `BasicLocal` (works with basic local protection only, such as a local user-file secret vault), `DevelopmentOnly` (acceptable for development only), `ActualHostUnverified` (works, but is not validated on a real host of this kind) or `Unsupported`.

IFormFile.description: Binary content of one file part in a `multipart/form-data` request.

value.description: The key: groups of lower-case ASCII letters and digits separated by single periods, underscores or hyphens.

ImplementationKey.description: Key of the implementation behind a capability, for example `tool.release-notes`, serialized as an object whose `value` member holds the key.

JsonElement.description: Any JSON value. The member that uses it describes the expected shape.

id.description: Identifier of the lifecycle task; send it as `id` to update the task.

partyId.description: Identifier of the party the task is for.

taskKind.description: Kind of task, as a JSON integer: 0 Onboarding, 1 Offboarding, 2 Training.

ownerPartyId.description: Identifier of the person responsible for the task.

ownerName.description: Display name of the responsible person; empty when unknown.

dueDate.description: Date by which the task should be done (`yyyy-MM-dd`).

status.description: Progress of the task, as a JSON integer: 0 NotStarted, 1 InProgress, 2 Completed, 3 Cancelled.

relatedProjectId.description: Identifier of the project the task relates to; null when none.

relatedProjectName.description: Name of the related project; empty when none or when the project no longer exists.

notes.description: Free-text notes; empty when not set.

isOverdue.description: True when the due date is before the current UTC date and the task is neither Completed nor Cancelled.

LifecycleTaskItemModel.description: A lifecycle task of a party (an onboarding, offboarding or training checklist item) as returned in the recruitment workspace. It is not a Project Structure task.

LifecycleTaskKind.description: Kind of lifecycle task of a party, as a JSON integer: 0 Onboarding, 1 Offboarding, 2 Training.

id.description: Identifier of the task to update, from `lifecycleTasks[].id` of the recruitment workspace. Omit it to create a task; an unknown identifier creates a new task with a new identifier.

partyId.description: Identifier of the party the task is for, for example the candidate of an application; required and must exist.

taskKind.description: Kind of task, as a JSON integer: 0 Onboarding, 1 Offboarding, 2 Training. Omitted means Onboarding (0).

title.description: Title of the task; required and trimmed.

ownerPartyId.description: Person responsible for the task; required and must be an existing person.

dueDate.description: Date by which the task should be done (`yyyy-MM-dd`); required. A task past this date that is neither Completed nor Cancelled is reported as overdue.

status.description: Progress of the task, as a JSON integer: 0 NotStarted, 1 InProgress, 2 Completed, 3 Cancelled. Omitted means NotStarted (0).

relatedProjectId.description: Project the task relates to, from `GET /api/projects`; it must exist. The task does not become part of the project's plan. Null or omitted means none.

notes.description: Free-text notes; trimmed. Omitted means empty.

LifecycleTaskSaveApiRequest.description: Request of `POST /api/crm-hr/recruiting/lifecycle-tasks`: an onboarding, offboarding or training checklist item of a party. It is not a Project Structure task. All task fields are overwritten.

LifecycleTaskStatus.description: Progress of a lifecycle task, as a JSON integer: 0 NotStarted, 1 InProgress, 2 Completed, 3 Cancelled. Completed and Cancelled tasks are never reported as overdue.

id.description: Identifier of the component.

providerProfileId.description: Provider profile the component calls, from `providerProfileId` of `GET /api/workflows/provider-options`; null leaves the provider to the node or the host default.

model.description: Model name within the provider, for example one of the provider's `modelOptions`.

modality.description: Input modality, as a JSON integer: 0 Text, 1 Vision, 2 Audio, 3 Image, 4 Multimodal. Audio and Image are not supported by the current runtime.

modelSettings.description: Temperature, output limit and JSON output settings.

instructions.description: System instructions of the model call, taken from the bound Prompt Gallery prompt version.

inputShape.description: Shape of the value the component receives.

resultShape.description: Shape of the value the component produces.

permissions.description: Permissions granted to the model call, such as tools and secrets it may use.

createdAtUtc.description: Time the component was first stored, as an instant with offset.

updatedAtUtc.description: Time the component was last stored.

promptArtifactId.description: Identifier of the Prompt Gallery item that holds the component's instructions; null for a component that was never bound, which a save binds.

promptVersionId.description: Identifier of the Prompt Gallery prompt version whose content is the component's instructions.

LlmCallComponent.description: Reusable LLM call component: a model call (provider, model, instructions, input and result shapes, permissions) that LLM call nodes reference by `settings.componentId`. Its instructions are stored as a Prompt Gallery prompt version. Returned by the component operations; create or replace it with `POST /api/workflows/components`.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the component to replace; null creates a new component.

providerProfileId.description: Provider profile to call, from `providerProfileId` of `GET /api/workflows/provider-options`; it must exist, be enabled and be a chat provider. Null leaves the provider unset.

model.description: Model name within the provider, for example one of its `modelOptions`; required and trimmed. The provider must have a price row for it.

modality.description: Input modality, as a JSON integer: 0 Text, 1 Vision, 2 Audio, 3 Image, 4 Multimodal. Audio and Image are rejected; Vision and Multimodal need a provider with vision support.

modelSettings.description: Temperature, output limit and JSON output settings.

instructions.description: System instructions; required and trimmed. They are stored as a new Prompt Gallery prompt or prompt version, unless `promptVersionId` is set, whose content is used instead.

inputShape.description: Shape of the value the component receives.

resultShape.description: Shape of the value the component produces.

permissions.description: Permissions granted to the model call, such as tools and secrets it may use.

promptArtifactId.description: Prompt Gallery item to bind the instructions to; null keeps the existing binding, or creates a new prompt for a component that has none.

promptVersionId.description: Prompt Gallery version whose content becomes the instructions; it must belong to `promptArtifactId` when both are set. Null records the sent instructions instead.

LlmCallComponentSaveRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/workflows/components`: the complete LLM call component to create or replace.

items.description: The items of this page in list order; at most the requested `take`, possibly none.

nextCursor.description: Opaque continuation value for the next page, or null when no further items exist. Send it unchanged as `cursor` with the same filters; it is not a page number or an offset.

LlmChatApiPageOfLlmChatConversationApiRe.description: One page of a cursor-paged LLM Chat list: definitions (`GET /api/llm-chats`) or conversations (`GET /api/llm-conversations`). Request the next page by sending `nextCursor` back as `cursor`.

items.description: The items of this page in list order; at most the requested `take`, possibly none.

nextCursor.description: Opaque continuation value for the next page, or null when no further items exist. Send it unchanged as `cursor` with the same filters; it is not a page number or an offset.

LlmChatApiPageOfLlmChatDefinitionApiResp.description: One page of a cursor-paged LLM Chat list: definitions (`GET /api/llm-chats`) or conversations (`GET /api/llm-conversations`). Request the next page by sending `nextCursor` back as `cursor`.

id.description: Identifier of the conversation, assigned by the server on creation.

definitionId.description: Identifier of the definition the conversation was created from.

definitionRevision.description: Definition revision the conversation is pinned to, fixed at creation. Its turns always use the settings of this revision, even after the definition is updated.

definitionName.description: Current display name of the definition.

status.description: Lifecycle status as a camel-case string: `active` (accepts turns) or `archived` (read-only).

origin.description: Where the conversation was created, as a camel-case string: `application` (product UI) or `api` (this HTTP API).

transcriptRevision.description: Revision of the conversation's transcript: 0 on creation, or 1 when the definition has a system prompt. It increases by one whenever the transcript changes (a turn's user message is admitted, its reply is committed, or a failed, cancelled or abandoned turn is rolled back) and with every rename. Send it as `expectedTranscriptRevision` with the next turn or rename. It is neither the definition revision nor the concurrency token.

hasActiveTurn.description: True while a turn holds the conversation, from its admission until its reply is committed or the turn is rolled back. No other turn can start while it is true.

concurrencyToken.description: Optimistic-concurrency token of the conversation: starts at 0 and increases with every rename and archive; turns do not change it. The response also carries it as the strong `ETag` header. Send it back as `expectedConcurrencyToken` or `If-Match` to rename or archive.

createdAtUtc.description: Instant the conversation was created, in UTC.

updatedAtUtc.description: Instant of the last change to the conversation or its transcript, in UTC.

activeOperationId.description: Operation identifier of the active turn, which is the `operationId` sent with it; omitted when no turn is active. Follow it with `GET /api/llm-chat-operations/{operationId}`.

messages.description: One page of the transcript's user and assistant messages, oldest first; system messages are never included. Present, possibly empty, only in `GET /api/llm-conversations/{conversationId}`; omitted elsewhere.

nextMessageCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page of messages; send it back as `messageCursor`. Omitted when no further messages exist or no messages were requested.

LlmChatConversationApiResponse.description: An LLM Chat conversation: its identity, the definition revision it is pinned to, its lifecycle status and the state of its transcript. `GET /api/llm-conversations/{conversationId}` adds one page of transcript messages; list items and the create, rename and archive responses carry no messages.

LlmChatConversationOrigin.description: Where an LLM Chat conversation was created, written in HTTP responses as a camel-case JSON string: `application` (in the product UI) or `api` (through the HTTP API, which always records `api`).

LlmChatConversationStatus.description: Lifecycle status of an LLM Chat conversation, written in HTTP responses as a camel-case JSON string: `active` (accepts turns and renames) or `archived` (read-only; the transcript stays readable).

id.description: Identifier of the definition, assigned by the server on creation.

summary.description: Short description of the definition; empty when none was given.

avatarImageUrl.description: Image URL or bundled avatar path of the definition; empty when none was given.

status.description: Lifecycle status as a camel-case string: `draft`, `active`, `suspended` or `archived`. Only an `active` definition starts conversations and turns.

currentRevision.description: Number of the current immutable revision: 1 after creation, increased by one by every successful update. The settings in this object belong to it. It is not the concurrency token.

providerProfileId.description: Identifier of the provider profile used by the current revision.

providerName.description: Display name of that provider profile, recorded when the revision was saved.

providerKind.description: Provider kind as a camel-case JSON string: `openAi`, `azureOpenAi`, `ollama` or `comfyUi`. It is written as a string, not as the integer of the shared `ProviderKind` schema (0 OpenAi, 1 AzureOpenAi, 2 Ollama, 3 ComfyUi).

model.description: Model identifier used by the current revision.

oneOf.description: Typed thinking effort of the current revision as a camel-case JSON string: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `extraHigh` or `max`, not the integer of the shared schema (0 None, 6 Minimal, 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High, 4 ExtraHigh, 5 Max). Null means the provider's default for the model applies when a turn runs.

tags.description: Tags of the definition, trimmed and lower-cased; empty when it has none.

concurrencyToken.description: Optimistic-concurrency token of the definition: a non-negative integer that starts at 0 and increases with every update and lifecycle change. The response also carries it as the strong `ETag` header, for example `"3"`. Send it back as `expectedConcurrencyToken` or `If-Match`.

createdAtUtc.description: Instant the definition was created, in UTC.

updatedAtUtc.description: Instant of the last update or lifecycle change, in UTC.

oneOf.description: Model settings of the current revision. Omitted in list items.
Structured-output settings of the current revision. Omitted in list items and when the revision has none.

revisionReason.description: Reason recorded with the current revision; empty when none was given. Omitted in list items.

LlmChatDefinitionApiResponse.description: An LLM Chat definition: reusable chat configuration with its lifecycle status and the settings of its current revision. Returned by `GET /api/llm-chats/{definitionId}`, by the create, update and lifecycle operations and, as a summary without `modelSettings`, `responseFormat` and `revisionReason`, by the definition list. It never contains the system prompt or provider credentials.

id.description: Identifier of the definition.

summary.description: Short description of the definition; empty when none was given.

avatarImageUrl.description: Image URL or bundled avatar path of the definition; empty when none was given.

status.description: Lifecycle status as a camel-case string: `draft`, `active`, `suspended` or `archived`. An `archived` definition cannot be updated.

revision.description: Number of the revision these values belong to, which is the definition's current revision.

systemPrompt.description: System prompt of the revision, exactly as stored; empty when none. Treat it as sensitive configuration.

providerProfileId.description: Identifier of the provider profile used by the revision.

providerName.description: Display name of that provider profile, recorded when the revision was saved.

providerKind.description: Provider kind as a camel-case JSON string: `openAi`, `azureOpenAi`, `ollama` or `comfyUi`, not the integer of the shared `ProviderKind` schema (0 OpenAi, 1 AzureOpenAi, 2 Ollama, 3 ComfyUi).

model.description: Model identifier used by the revision.

oneOf.description: Typed thinking effort of the revision as a camel-case JSON string: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `extraHigh` or `max`, not the integer of the shared schema (0 None, 6 Minimal, 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High, 4 ExtraHigh, 5 Max). Null means the provider's default for the model applies.

modelSettings.description: Model settings of the revision; always present.

oneOf.description: Structured-output settings of the revision, or null when it has none.

tags.description: Tags of the definition, trimmed and lower-cased; empty when it has none.

revisionReason.description: Reason recorded with the revision; empty when none was given.

concurrencyToken.description: Optimistic-concurrency token of the definition, also sent as the strong `ETag` header. Send it back as `expectedConcurrencyToken` or `If-Match` with the update.

createdAtUtc.description: Instant the definition was created, in UTC.

updatedAtUtc.description: Instant of the last update or lifecycle change, in UTC.

LlmChatDefinitionEditorApiResponse.description: The editable current revision of an LLM Chat definition, returned by the manage-scoped `GET /api/llm-chats/{definitionId}/editor`. It holds every value an update needs, including the system prompt, and never provider credentials, endpoints or local paths.

name.description: Display name of the definition. Required: not blank, trimmed, at most 200 characters.

summary.description: Short description of the definition. Trimmed, at most 2,000 characters; null or empty stores no summary.

avatarImageUrl.description: Image shown for the definition: an absolute `http` or `https` URL, or a bundled avatar path such as `_content/CanDoItAll.Components.BaseLib/assets/identity/avatars/avatar-01.jpg` (avatars 01 to 08). At most 2,048 characters; null or empty stores no image.

systemPrompt.description: Instructions sent to the model as the system message of every turn, stored exactly as sent. Send it on every create and update: null is rejected, an empty string means no system prompt. At most 400,000 characters. Only the manage-scoped editor read returns it.

providerProfileId.description: Identifier of the provider profile to use, from `providerProfileId` in `GET /api/llm-chats/provider-options`. The profile must exist, be enabled and serve chat.

model.description: Model identifier offered by that profile (`models[].model` in the provider options), matched exactly after trimming. Required.

oneOf.description: Typed thinking (reasoning) effort as a JSON string, matched case-insensitively: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `extraHigh` or `max`, for example `"low"`. These are the names of the shared schema's integer values (0 None, 6 Minimal, 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High, 4 ExtraHigh, 5 Max), but a JSON number is rejected here. Null or omitted uses the provider's default for the model when a turn runs; `"none"` explicitly disables thinking. A value must be one of the model's `allowedEfforts`, otherwise the request fails with 422 `llm-chat.thinking-effort-not-supported`; it is never silently downgraded.
Sampling, model-parameter and timeout settings. Null or omitted stores no temperature, an empty parameter object and no per-invocation timeout.

tags.description: Labels of the definition. Each tag is trimmed and lower-cased; at most 20 tags of at most 100 characters, unique after that normalization. Null or an empty array stores no tags; on update the list replaces all existing tags.

revisionReason.description: Reason recorded with the new revision, for example `Shorter answers`. Trimmed, at most 500 characters; null or empty records no reason.

oneOf.description: Structured-output settings for the model's replies. Null or omitted stores none, so replies are free text.

expectedConcurrencyToken.description: Update only: the definition's `concurrencyToken` from your last read, the number inside its `ETag` header. Send it here or as `If-Match`; when both are present they must be equal. Ignored on create.

LlmChatDefinitionMutationApiRequest.description: Request body of `POST /api/llm-chats` (create) and `PUT /api/llm-chats/{definitionId}` (update): the complete editable configuration of an LLM Chat definition.
