On update every member replaces the stored value, so read `GET /api/llm-chats/{definitionId}/editor` first and send back the values you do not intend to change. Take the provider profile, model and thinking effort from `GET /api/llm-chats/provider-options`. Members not listed here are rejected.

LlmChatDefinitionStatus.description: Lifecycle status of an LLM Chat definition, written in HTTP responses as a camel-case JSON string: `draft` (created, cannot start conversations yet), `active` (starts conversations and turns), `suspended` (temporarily starts neither; can be reactivated) or `archived` (final and read-only). Draft can become active or archived, active can become suspended or archived, and suspended can become active or archived.

expectedConcurrencyToken.description: The resource's `concurrencyToken` from your last read, the number inside its `ETag` header; not negative. Null or omitted is allowed only when `If-Match` carries the token; when both are present they must be equal.

LlmChatExpectedConcurrencyApiRequest.description: Body of the definition lifecycle operations (`activate`, `suspend`, `archive`) and of conversation archiving: the concurrency token from your last read. A JSON body is required even when the token is sent as `If-Match`; `{}` is then enough. Members not listed here are rejected.

ordinal.description: Position of the attempt within the operation, starting at 1.

providerKind.description: Provider kind as a JSON integer: 0 OpenAi, 1 AzureOpenAi, 2 Ollama, 3 ComfyUi.

model.description: Model reported for the attempt.

deliveryMode.description: How the reply was obtained, as a JSON integer: 0 Incremental (streamed in parts), 1 CompletedFallback (the provider could not stream, so the reply was obtained in one piece).

finishReason.description: Finish reason of a successful attempt as reported by the provider driver, at most 100 characters; null for failed or cancelled attempts.

oneOf.description: Thinking effort set by the definition revision, as a JSON integer: 0 None, 6 Minimal, 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High, 4 ExtraHigh, 5 Max. Null when the revision leaves it to the provider default.

Thinking effort applied to the attempt: the requested value or, when none was requested, the provider default for the model, as a JSON integer: 0 None, 6 Minimal, 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High, 4 ExtraHigh, 5 Max. Null when neither exists.

outcome.description: Result of the attempt, as a JSON integer: 0 Succeeded, 1 Failed, 2 Cancelled.

usage.description: Token usage reported for this attempt; zeros when the provider reported none.

oneOf.description: Failure of a failed or cancelled attempt; null for a successful one.

startedAtUtc.description: Instant the attempt started, in UTC.

completedAtUtc.description: Instant the attempt ended, in UTC.

LlmChatInvocationAttemptApiResponse.description: Evidence of one provider invocation attempt of an LLM Chat turn: an allowlisted projection that omits the provider profile identity, correlation identifiers and raw provider errors. Unlike the definition resources, this object writes its enum members as JSON integers.

LlmChatInvocationOutcome.description: Outcome of one provider invocation attempt of an LLM Chat turn. In the operation resource (`invocationAttempts[].outcome`) it is a JSON integer: 0 Succeeded (the provider returned a complete reply), 1 Failed (see the attempt's failure code), 2 Cancelled (the attempt was cancelled). In the operation event stream (`payload.outcome`) the same values are camel-case strings: `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`.

entryId.description: Identifier of this message entry, assigned by the server.

turnId.description: Identifier of the turn the message belongs to, which is the `operationId` of that turn's operation.

role.description: Author of the message as a camel-case string: `user` or `assistant`. System messages are never returned.

content.description: Text of the message, as stored in the transcript.

createdAtUtc.description: Instant the message was recorded, in UTC.

model.description: Model reported for an assistant reply; empty for user messages.

oneOf.description: Token usage of the provider call that produced an assistant reply; null for user messages.

LlmChatMessageApiResponse.description: One message entry of a conversation transcript: the user message of a turn or the assistant reply to it. The user message and the reply of one turn share its `turnId`.

model.description: Model identifier; send it as `model` when creating or updating a definition.

thinkingEffort.description: Which typed thinking-effort values a definition may set for this model.

LlmChatModelOptionApiResponse.description: A model offered by a provider profile to LLM Chat definitions.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature from 0 through 2. Null leaves it to the provider.

modelParameterConfiguration.description: Provider-neutral model-parameter overrides as a JSON object, not a string containing JSON, for example `{ "maxOutputTokens": 1024 }`. Null or omitted stores an empty object. Any other JSON type is rejected, and so is a member named `thinkingEffort`, `reasoningEffort` or `think` (any case) in the object or in a nested object: set thinking effort only through the typed `thinkingEffort` member of the definition. The values are interpreted by the provider driver when a turn runs; saving the definition does not validate them.

timeoutSeconds.description: Deadline of each provider invocation of a turn, in seconds: a finite number greater than 0 and at most 1,800 (30 minutes); fractions are allowed. Null sets no per-invocation deadline. An invocation that exceeds it fails with `llm-chat.deadline-exceeded`.

LlmChatModelSettingsApiRequest.description: Model settings of the definition revision written by a create or update request. Members not listed here are rejected.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature from 0 through 2, or null when the provider decides.

modelParameterConfiguration.description: Stored model-parameter overrides as a JSON object (not a string containing JSON); `{}` when none.

timeoutSeconds.description: Deadline of each provider invocation in seconds, or null when none is set.

LlmChatModelSettingsApiResponse.description: Model settings stored with an LLM Chat definition revision.

schema.description: Contract identifier of this object, always `candoitall.llm-chat-operation.v1`.

operationId.description: Identifier of the operation: the client-supplied `operationId` of the turn, which is also the turn identifier.

conversationId.description: Identifier of the conversation the turn belongs to.

status.description: Current status as a camel-case string: `pending` (admitted, waiting for a dispatcher), `running` (being executed), `cancellationRequested`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `recoveryRequired` (interrupted with an unknown outcome). `succeeded`, `failed` and `cancelled` are final; `recoveryRequired` needs reconciliation or abandonment.

replayed.description: True only in a turn response that returned an existing operation for a repeated identical request instead of admitting a new turn; false in all other responses.

expectedTranscriptRevision.description: Transcript revision the turn was admitted against, as sent with it.

resultingTranscriptRevision.description: Transcript revision after the assistant reply was committed; null unless the operation succeeded. Use it as the next turn's `expectedTranscriptRevision`.

lastEventSequence.description: Sequence number of the operation's latest event when this snapshot was read. Open the event stream with `after` set to this value to receive only later events.

eventsUrl.description: Relative URL of the operation's server-sent event stream.

cancelUrl.description: Relative URL for requesting cancellation with `POST`.

invocationAttempts.description: Provider invocation attempts in ascending `ordinal` order; at most 100, empty before the first attempt starts.

oneOf.description: The assistant reply this turn committed to the transcript; null until one is committed.
The recorded failure: present when the operation failed, was cancelled or requires recovery; null otherwise.

startedAtUtc.description: Instant the turn was admitted, in UTC.

completedAtUtc.description: Instant the operation became `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`, in UTC; null before that, including while it requires recovery.

LlmChatOperationApiResponse.description: An LLM Chat turn operation: the durable, asynchronous execution of one turn created by `POST /api/llm-conversations/{conversationId}/turns`. It carries the operation status, the committed assistant reply once there is one, the recorded failure, links for following the operation and up to 100 provider invocation attempts. Returned by the turn, operation read, cancel, reconcile and abandon operations.

code.description: Stable failure code starting with `llm-chat.`, for example `llm-chat.provider-unavailable`, `llm-chat.deadline-exceeded`, `llm-chat.cancelled` or `llm-chat.operation-recovery-required`. Branch on this code.

retryable.description: True when the cause is transient (provider or dispatcher unavailable, deadline exceeded, database profile changed, concurrent storage change), so a new turn with a new `operationId` can succeed. Resending the same `operationId` only returns the recorded operation.

LlmChatOperationFailureApiResponse.description: A failure recorded for an LLM Chat operation or for one of its provider invocation attempts.

LlmChatOperationStatus.description: Status of an LLM Chat turn operation, written in HTTP responses and events as a camel-case JSON string: `pending` (admitted, waiting for a dispatcher), `running` (claimed by a dispatcher; the provider call may be in progress), `succeeded` (final: the assistant reply is committed to the transcript), `failed` (final: the turn ended without a reply), `cancellationRequested` (cancellation was requested and is being applied), `cancelled` (final: cancelled without a reply) or `recoveryRequired` (not final: execution was interrupted after the provider may have been called, so the outcome is unknown until the operation is reconciled or abandoned).

providerProfileId.description: Identifier of the provider profile; send it as `providerProfileId` when creating or updating a definition.

providerName.description: Display name of the provider profile.

providerKind.description: Provider kind as a camel-case JSON string: `openAi`, `azureOpenAi`, `ollama` or `comfyUi`, not the integer of the shared `ProviderKind` schema (0 OpenAi, 1 AzureOpenAi, 2 Ollama, 3 ComfyUi).

models.description: Models a definition may select with this profile: the profile's default model first, then its other allowed or suggested models, without duplicates.

LlmChatProviderOptionApiResponse.description: A provider profile that LLM Chat definitions can use, with the models it offers. Returned by `GET /api/llm-chats/provider-options`; it contains no endpoint, credential or local path.

requireJson.description: True asks the model for a JSON reply, constrained by `schema` when one is given and the provider supports it. False sends no response-format instruction; the other members are then stored but not used.

schema.description: JSON Schema that the model's reply should follow, as a JSON object (not a string containing JSON). Null or omitted means no schema. Any other JSON type is rejected. It describes the model's reply, not a schema of this API.

schemaName.description: Name given to the schema in the provider request. Null or blank lets the provider driver choose a name.

schemaDescription.description: Description of the schema passed to the provider. Null or blank sends none.

LlmChatResponseFormatApiRequest.description: Structured-output settings of the definition revision written by a create or update request. They change the provider request only when `requireJson` is true. Members not listed here are rejected.

requireJson.description: True when replies are requested as JSON; false when no response-format instruction is sent to the provider.

schema.description: Stored JSON Schema for the reply as a JSON object (not a string containing JSON); `{}` when no schema is stored.

schemaName.description: Name given to the schema in provider requests; empty when none.

schemaDescription.description: Description of the schema; empty when none.

LlmChatResponseFormatApiResponse.description: Structured-output settings stored with an LLM Chat definition revision.

status.description: Support status as a camel-case string: `supported` (a definition may set one of `allowedEfforts`), `unsupported` or `unknown` (only null is accepted). It is written as a string, not as the integer of the shared schema (0 Supported, 1 Unsupported, 2 Unknown).

controlMode.description: How the model exposes thinking, as a camel-case string: `effortLevels` (graded levels), `booleanToggle` (on or off, offered as `medium` and `none`) or `unspecified` (no control declared, as for models without support). It is written as a string, not as the integer of the shared schema (0 Unspecified, 1 BooleanToggle, 2 EffortLevels).

allowedEfforts.description: Values accepted as `thinkingEffort` for this model, as camel-case strings from `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `extraHigh` and `max`, not the integers of the shared schema (0 None, 6 Minimal, 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High, 4 ExtraHigh, 5 Max). Empty when thinking effort is not supported.

oneOf.description: Effort the provider applies when a definition leaves `thinkingEffort` null, as a camel-case string (`none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `extraHigh` or `max`, not the integer of the shared schema: 0 None, 6 Minimal, 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High, 4 ExtraHigh, 5 Max). Null when no default is configured.

LlmChatThinkingEffortOptionApiResponse.description: Thinking-effort capability of one model: whether a definition may set `thinkingEffort`, and to which values. All members are camel-case JSON strings, not the integers shown by the shared enum schemas.

inputTokens.description: Tokens counted for the prompt, including the transcript sent as context.

outputTokens.description: Tokens counted for the generated reply.

cachedInputTokens.description: Input tokens the provider reported as served from its prompt cache.

LlmChatUsageApiResponse.description: Token counts reported by the model provider. They are quantities of model tokens, not money and not API bearer tokens; a count the provider did not report is 0.

LlmMessageRole.description: Author of a chat message: System (instructions, such as a definition's system prompt), User (text sent by the person or client) or Assistant (the model's reply). HTTP responses write it as a camel-case JSON string (`system`, `user`, `assistant`); the LLM Chat transcript reads never return system messages.

LlmStreamingDeliveryMode.description: How a provider attempt delivered its reply. In the LLM Chat operation resource (`invocationAttempts[].deliveryMode`) it is a JSON integer: 0 Incremental (the provider streamed the reply in parts as it was generated), 1 CompletedFallback (the provider could not stream, so the reply was obtained in one piece). In the operation event stream (`payload.deliveryMode`) it is a camel-case string: `incremental`, `completedFallback`.

value.description: The credential's GUID.

ManagedCredentialId.description: Identifier of a managed API credential issued by this host.

value.description: The key: groups of lower-case ASCII letters and digits separated by single hyphens.

McpServerKey.description: Key of an MCP server capability in lower kebab case, serialized as an object whose `value` member holds the key.

isSuccess.description: True when the definition was valid, the server started or connected, its tools were listed and matched the allowed tools, and the server was stopped cleanly.

identity.description: Kind and key of the tested capability, in the identity numbering.

serverKey.description: Key of the tested MCP server.

discoveredTools.description: Tools the server reported; empty when listing did not happen.

allowedTools.description: Reported tools that the definition allows; empty when the test failed.

diagnostics.description: Problems found; empty when the test succeeded.

cleanupCompleted.description: True when the server was stopped cleanly after the test; false when stopping failed or the test ended before the server was started.

McpSetupTestResult.description: Result of an MCP server capability setup test.

value.description: The name: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, periods, underscores or hyphens.

McpToolName.description: Name of a tool exposed by an MCP server, serialized as an object whose `value` member holds the name.

operationId.description: Identifier (GUID) of the accepted operation; read it with `GET /api/memory-providers/operations/{operationId}`.

statusPath.description: The operation identifier in text form (the same value as `operationId`), not an address. Build the polling address from `operationId`.

expiresAtUtc.description: Instant (UTC, with offset) at which the provider's acceptance expires; after it the host's memory background workers record an unfinished operation as timed out.

pollAfterSeconds.description: Minimum number of seconds to wait between status reads, as requested by the provider; greater than 0 and may have a fractional part.

callbackAvailable.description: Always false: this API delivers no callbacks; poll instead.

MemoryAcceptedOperationApiResponse.description: How to follow an asynchronous memory operation that a provider accepted.

value.description: Capability identifier text, for example `context.query.sync`, `context.query.async` or `operations.status`.

MemoryCapabilityId.description: Identifier of a memory protocol capability, serialized as an object whose `value` member holds the identifier, for example `{ "value": "context.query.sync" }`. The text is lower-case tokens separated by dots or hyphens and must start with a letter; an invalid value makes the request fail.

sourceRef.description: Provider-defined reference to the source; never blank. Treat it as opaque.

label.description: Human-readable label of the source; can be empty.

MemoryCitationApiResponse.description: A source cited by a section of memory context.

summary.description: Summary of the retrieved context; never blank.

sections.description: Sections of retrieved context; at most `maxContextSections` of the provider.

warnings.description: Warnings about the result, for example partial or policy-limited context; can be empty.

providerConfidence.description: The provider's confidence in the whole pack, from 0 through 1.

feedbackHandle.description: Host-issued opaque handle for later feedback about this context. Null when the provider does not accept feedback, which is always the case for a profile saved through `PUT /api/memory-providers/{providerId}`.

MemoryContextPackApiResponse.description: Context retrieved from a memory provider by a completed query: a summary and sections with citations, as validated by the host against the provider's limits.

title.description: Title of the section; never blank.

text.description: Text of the section; never blank.

citations.description: Sources that support the section; can be empty.

confidence.description: The provider's confidence in this section, from 0 through 1.

MemoryContextSectionApiResponse.description: One section of retrieved memory context with its sources.

id.description: Identifier of the note. Null or omitted creates a note with a new identifier; a value replaces that note or, if none exists, creates it with this identifier.

agentId.description: Identifier of the agent the note belongs to. The agent must exist; otherwise the save fails.

kind.description: Category of the note, as a JSON integer: 0 Fact, 1 Preference, 2 Context (the default), 3 FollowUp, 4 Architecture. It only labels the note.

title.description: Short title of the note; trimmed. Must not be null.

content.description: Text of the note; trimmed. Must not be null.

source.description: Free-text origin of the note, trimmed; `manual` when omitted. Must not be null.

importance.description: Caller-assigned importance, stored as sent; 3 when omitted. The server applies no range check.

metadataJson.description: Optional metadata as a JSON string containing JSON, trimmed and stored as sent; its content is not validated. Must not be null; send an empty string when there is none.

MemoryEditorModel.description: Workspace memory note to create or replace through `POST /api/agents/memory`. A save replaces the whole note. These notes are kept in the agent catalog and listed per agent; they are not injected into agent runs and are separate from the memory providers configured in the agent's `memoryAccess` settings.

MemoryKind.description: Category label of a workspace memory note, as a JSON integer: 0 Fact, 1 Preference, 2 Context, 3 FollowUp, 4 Architecture. It only labels the note; no runtime behavior depends on it, and undefined integers are not rejected.

MemoryLedgerStatus.description: State of an operation in the host's memory operation ledger. In the memory-provider HTTP API it is a PascalCase string token. In progress: `Pending` (recorded, not yet dispatched), `Accepted` (accepted by the provider as an asynchronous operation) and `Running`. Final: `Completed`, `Failed`, `TimedOut`, `Cancelled`, `Expired` (its retention period ended) and `Forgotten` (its data was removed under the retention policy).

MemoryOperationHandlerStatus.description: Outcome of a memory operation request. In the memory-provider HTTP API it is a PascalCase string token and the response status follows it: `Completed` 200; `Accepted` 202; `ProviderNotFound` and `NotFound` 404; `CapabilityDenied`, `ProviderDenied` and `AccessDenied` 403; `DriverUnavailable`, `DriverFailed`, `SourceCaptureFailed` and `Failed` 502; `TimedOut` 504; every other value 409. Values: `Completed` (finished), `Accepted` (accepted as an asynchronous operation), `NoProviderConfigured`, `NoEnabledProvider`, `ProviderNotFound`, `ProviderDisabled`, `CapabilityUnavailable` (the provider does not advertise the capability), `CapabilityDenied` (policy denies the capability), `CapabilityMismatch` (the request does not include its required capability), `DriverUnavailable` (no usable driver for the provider), `SourceCaptureFailed`, `NotFound` (the operation does not exist), `Cancelled`, `Failed`, `TimedOut`, `UnsupportedOperation` (the provider reported the operation as unsupported), `ProviderDenied`, `ProviderSelectionRequired`, `AccessDenied` (the operation belongs to another caller), `ProviderConfigurationFailed` and `DriverFailed` (the provider call failed or returned an invalid result).

MemoryOperationKind.description: Kind of memory operation. In the memory-provider HTTP API it is a PascalCase string token: `ContextQuery`, `Ingestion`, `Feedback`, `SourceRequest`, `EventAcknowledge`, `OperationStatus`, `CapabilityExchange` or `Health`. Queries through that API are `ContextQuery`.

MemoryProviderAssignmentScope.description: What the key of a memory provider assignment identifies, as a JSON integer: 0 Agent (the agent identifier), 1 AgentRole (the agent's workload name), 2 Workflow (the workflow identifier), 3 WorkflowNode (the workflow node identifier), 4 Process (the process identifier).

supportsSynchronousQueries.description: True to advertise synchronous context queries (`context.query.sync`).

supportsAsynchronousQueries.description: True to advertise asynchronous context queries (`context.query.async`). Requires `supportsOperationStatus` and the `Mcp` driver.

supportsOperationStatus.description: True to advertise operation status (`operations.status`), which the host needs to poll asynchronous operations. Only the `Mcp` driver supports it.

MemoryProviderCapabilitiesApiRequest.description: Query and status capabilities to advertise for a memory provider profile. Each driver supports only some of them: `Http`, `NativeRemote` and `Mock` only synchronous queries; `Mcp` all three. Asynchronous queries require operation status. Send all three members.

supportsRclUi.description: True when the profile advertises an embedded user-interface panel (`ui.rcl`). This API does not change it.

supportsIframeUi.description: True when the profile advertises an embedded provider console page (`ui.iframe`). This API does not change it.

MemoryProviderCapabilitiesApiResponse.description: Capabilities a memory provider profile advertises, as stored by the host.

MemoryProviderDriverKind.description: Driver that connects the host to a memory provider. In the memory-provider HTTP API it is a PascalCase string token: `Http` (a provider speaking the host's HTTP memory protocol), `Mcp` (a remote Model Context Protocol server), `NativeRemote` (a remote Cognitive Memory service reached over HTTP), `Mock` (a deterministic built-in provider for tests and demonstrations) or `InProcessMigration` (an internal migration driver that the HTTP API cannot configure).

MemoryProviderDriverKindApiRequest.description: Driver that connects the host to a memory provider, as a PascalCase string token: `Http` (a provider speaking the host's HTTP memory protocol), `Mcp` (a remote Model Context Protocol server), `NativeRemote` (a remote Cognitive Memory service, configured with the HTTP transport) or `Mock` (a deterministic built-in provider for tests and demonstrations).

MemoryProviderFallbackBehavior.description: Whether a memory provider may be used as the implicit default provider. In the memory-provider HTTP API it is a PascalCase string token: `DenyImplicitFallback` (only when chosen explicitly or by an assignment) or `AllowDefaultProviderWhenNoAssignment` (also as the default when no assignment applies).

MemoryProviderFallbackBehaviorApiRequest.description: Whether a memory provider may be used as the implicit default, as a PascalCase string token: `DenyImplicitFallback` (only when it is chosen explicitly or by an assignment) or `AllowDefaultProviderWhenNoAssignment` (also as the default provider when no assignment applies). Queries through `POST /api/memory-providers/{providerId}/queries` always name the provider, so this setting does not affect them.

MemoryProviderHealthState.description: Last recorded health of a memory provider. In the memory-provider HTTP API it is a PascalCase string token: `Unknown` (not checked yet), `Healthy`, `Degraded` or `Unreachable`.

baseUrl.description: Base address of the provider, for example `https://memory.example.com/api`: an absolute HTTPS address, or HTTP only to a loopback host, without user information, query or fragment.

queryPath.description: Path of the query endpoint relative to `baseUrl`, for example `/memory/query`: it starts with `/` and has no `//`, backslash, query, fragment or control character.

healthPath.description: Path of the health endpoint relative to `baseUrl`, for example `/memory/health`, with the same rules as `queryPath`.

apiKeyEnvironmentVariable.description: Name of the host environment variable that holds the API key, for example `MEMORY_PROVIDER_API_KEY`: ASCII letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit. Empty means the provider is called without a credential. A value that is not a variable name, such as a key itself, is rejected.

authHeaderName.description: Name of the request header that carries the credential, for example `Authorization`; must be a valid HTTP header name.

authScheme.description: Authorization scheme placed before the credential when `authHeaderName` is `Authorization`, for example `Bearer`; must then be a valid HTTP token.

timeoutMilliseconds.description: Timeout of one provider request in milliseconds; at least 1.

maxRetryAttempts.description: Number of retries after a failed provider request; 0 or more.

MemoryProviderHttpTransportApiModel.description: HTTP transport of a memory provider that uses the `Http` or `NativeRemote` driver. In a request, send every member. The credential is referenced by the name of an environment variable of the host; the secret value itself is never sent or returned.

value.description: Identifier text of the memory provider instance, for example `team-knowledge`.

MemoryProviderInstanceId.description: Identifier of a memory provider instance, serialized as an object whose `value` member holds the identifier text, for example `{ "value": "team-knowledge" }`. The text is trimmed and must be non-blank, at most 256 characters and free of control characters; an invalid value makes the request fail.

supportsSynchronousQueries.description: True when the provider answers queries within the request.

supportsAsynchronousOperations.description: True when the provider accepts operations that are completed later.

MemoryProviderInteractionSupportApiRespo.description: Interaction styles of a memory provider, derived from its advertised capabilities.

maxContextSections.description: Largest number of sections the host accepts in one context pack from this provider; a larger pack fails the query.

maxSourceItems.description: Largest total number of citations the host accepts in one context pack from this provider.

maxInFlightOperations.description: Declared largest number of concurrent operations of the provider. Informational: the host does not enforce it.

operationTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds after creation at which the host's memory background workers record an unfinished operation of the provider as timed out; may have a fractional part.

MemoryProviderLimitsApiResponse.description: Limits the host applies to a memory provider's results and operations. This API does not change them; a new profile gets the host defaults (12 sections, 100 source items, 4 operations in flight, 120 seconds).

descriptorKind.description: Kind of MCP server; only `remote-http` is accepted.

serverKey.description: Key that identifies the MCP server within the host. Required.

displayName.description: Display name of the MCP server. Empty means the profile's display name.

description.description: Description of the MCP server. Empty means a generic description.

remoteEndpoint.description: Address of the MCP server, for example `https://mcp.example.com/memory`: an absolute HTTPS address, or HTTP only to a loopback host, without user information, query or fragment.

authHeaderName.description: Name of the request header that carries the credential, for example `Authorization`; must be a valid HTTP header name. It is stored only when `authHeaderEnvironmentVariable` is set.

authHeaderEnvironmentVariable.description: Name of the host environment variable whose value is sent in `authHeaderName`: ASCII letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit. Empty means no credential header. A value that is not a variable name is rejected.

contextQueryTool.description: Name of the MCP tool that answers context queries. Required when a query capability is enabled.

operationStatusTool.description: Name of the MCP tool that reports operation status. Required when asynchronous queries or operation status are enabled.

MemoryProviderMcpTransportApiModel.description: Model Context Protocol transport of a memory provider that uses the `Mcp` driver: the remote MCP server and the tools the host calls. In a request, send every member, using an empty string for values that do not apply. The credential is referenced by the name of an environment variable of the host; the secret value itself is never sent or returned.

operationId.description: Identifier (GUID) of the operation; use it with `GET /api/memory-providers/operations/{operationId}`.

providerId.description: Identifier of the provider profile that runs the operation.

requestedCapability.description: Capability the operation used, for example `context.query.async`.

operationKind.description: Kind of operation, as a PascalCase string token: `ContextQuery` for the queries of this API; the other values (`Ingestion`, `Feedback`, `SourceRequest`, `EventAcknowledge`, `OperationStatus`, `CapabilityExchange`, `Health`) come from other memory features.

status.description: Ledger state, as a PascalCase string token: `Pending`, `Accepted` and `Running` are in progress; `Completed`, `Failed`, `TimedOut`, `Cancelled`, `Expired` and `Forgotten` are final.

retryCount.description: Number of times the host retried the operation.

transitionCount.description: Number of state changes recorded for the operation.

createdAtUtc.description: Instant (UTC, with offset) at which the operation was recorded.

updatedAtUtc.description: Instant (UTC, with offset) of the last change to the record.

completedAtUtc.description: Instant (UTC, with offset) at which the operation reached a final state; null before.

statusReason.description: Human-readable reason for the current state. Its wording can change and must not be parsed.

MemoryProviderOperationApiResponse.description: A memory operation as recorded in the host's operation ledger. The record reflects what the host knows; it is updated by the host, not read live from the provider.

status.description: Outcome of the read, as a PascalCase string token; see the `MemoryOperationHandlerStatus` schema for every value. `Completed` (HTTP 200) means the record was read, whatever state the operation itself is in; read `operation.status` for that. `AccessDenied` or `ProviderDenied` (403), `NotFound` or `ProviderNotFound` (404) and outcomes such as `ProviderDisabled` or `CapabilityUnavailable` (409) mean it could not be read.

diagnostic.description: Human-readable explanation of the outcome. Its wording can change and must not be parsed.

selection.description: How the host checked the provider that ran the operation.

oneOf.description: The operation's ledger record when `status` is `Completed`; otherwise null.

MemoryProviderOperationStatusApiResponse.description: Result of `GET /api/memory-providers/operations/{operationId}`: whether the caller may read the operation and, if so, its ledger record. The HTTP status follows `status`.

displayName.description: Human-readable name of the provider. Surrounding whitespace is removed; must not be blank.

driverKind.description: Driver of the provider, as a PascalCase string token: `Http`, `Mcp`, `NativeRemote` or `Mock`. It decides the required transport and which capabilities can be enabled.

isEnabled.description: True to make the provider selectable. A disabled provider keeps its configuration but queries to it are refused.

fallbackBehavior.description: Whether the provider may serve as the implicit default provider, as a PascalCase string token: `DenyImplicitFallback` or `AllowDefaultProviderWhenNoAssignment`. It has no effect on queries through this API, which always name the provider.

providerKind.description: Kind of memory service behind the provider, as a lowercase dotted token such as `memory.mock`: a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters and digits, in segments separated by `.` or `-`. Surrounding whitespace is removed.

selectionTags.description: Free-form labels stored with the profile and shown in provider management; provider selection does not use them. Blank entries are dropped and the others trimmed. Null means no tags.

capabilities.description: The query and status capabilities to advertise. Required; they must be supported by the driver kind.

oneOf.description: HTTP transport settings. Required for the `Http` and `NativeRemote` drivers and rejected for the others; send null when not required.
Model Context Protocol transport settings. Required for the `Mcp` driver and rejected for the others; send null when not required.

MemoryProviderProfileApiRequest.description: Complete configuration of a memory provider profile, sent to `PUT /api/memory-providers/{providerId}`. The request replaces the configuration it covers; send every member, using null for `selectionTags`, `http` or `mcp` when they do not apply. Unknown members are rejected. The driver kind decides which transport is required: `http` for `Http` and `NativeRemote`, `mcp` for `Mcp`, neither for `Mock`.

providerId.description: Identifier of the profile, chosen when it was saved with `PUT /api/memory-providers/{providerId}`. Use it in the other memory-provider routes.

displayName.description: Human-readable name of the provider.

driverKind.description: Driver of the provider, as a PascalCase string token: `Http`, `Mcp`, `NativeRemote`, `Mock` or `InProcessMigration` (an internal migration driver that this API cannot configure).

isEnabled.description: True when the provider can be selected; false when queries to it are refused.

healthState.description: Last recorded health of the provider, as a PascalCase string token: `Unknown` (not checked yet), `Healthy`, `Degraded` or `Unreachable`. Reading the profile does not check the provider.

workspaceScope.description: Workspaces the provider serves, as a PascalCase string token: `AllWorkspaces` or `SingleWorkspace`. Profiles saved through this API always use `AllWorkspaces`; the host refuses to select a `SingleWorkspace` provider because it cannot verify the workspace.

fallbackBehavior.description: Whether the provider may serve as the implicit default provider, as a PascalCase string token: `DenyImplicitFallback` or `AllowDefaultProviderWhenNoAssignment`.

providerKind.description: Kind of memory service behind the provider, as a lowercase dotted token.

protocolVersion.description: Memory protocol version the profile uses, currently `memory-protocol.v1`.

selectionTags.description: Free-form labels of the profile; provider selection does not use them.

interactionSupport.description: Interaction styles derived from the advertised capabilities.

limits.description: Limits the host applies to results and operations of this provider.

oneOf.description: HTTP transport settings of an `Http` or `NativeRemote` provider; null for other drivers.
Model Context Protocol transport settings of an `Mcp` provider; null for other drivers.

MemoryProviderProfileApiResponse.description: A memory provider profile as stored by the host, returned by the memory-provider operations. It carries the configuration, the advertised capabilities and limits, and the last recorded health. Credentials appear only as environment-variable names, never as values.

query.description: Text to look up. Surrounding whitespace is removed; the rest must be 1 to 32,768 characters (UTF-16 code units).

mode.description: How to run the query, as a PascalCase string token: `Synchronous` (answer within the request) or `Asynchronous` (start an operation to poll).

MemoryProviderQueryApiRequest.description: Request of `POST /api/memory-providers/{providerId}/queries`: the text to look up in the provider's memory and how to run the query. Send both members; unknown members are rejected.

status.description: Outcome, as a PascalCase string token; see the `MemoryOperationHandlerStatus` schema for every value. `Completed` (HTTP 200) and `Accepted` (HTTP 202) are the successes. Selection outcomes such as `ProviderNotFound` (404), `ProviderDenied` (403) or `ProviderDisabled` and `CapabilityUnavailable` (409) mean nothing was dispatched; `DriverUnavailable`, `DriverFailed` and `Failed` (502) and `TimedOut` (504) mean dispatch failed.

diagnostic.description: Human-readable explanation of the outcome. Its wording can change and must not be parsed.

selection.description: How the host selected, or refused, the provider.

oneOf.description: The operation recorded in the host's ledger for this query; null when the query was refused before an operation was recorded (selection failures).
The retrieved context when `status` is `Completed`; otherwise null.
How to poll the operation when `status` is `Accepted`; otherwise null.

feedbackHandle.description: The same value as `contextPack.feedbackHandle`; null when no context was delivered or the provider does not accept feedback.

driverDispatchAttempted.description: True when the host called the provider. False means the query was refused before dispatch and the provider was not contacted.

MemoryProviderQueryApiResponse.description: Result of `POST /api/memory-providers/{providerId}/queries`. The HTTP status follows `status`; which of `operation`, `contextPack` and `acceptedOperation` are present depends on how far the query got.

MemoryProviderQueryMode.description: How a memory provider query runs, as a PascalCase string token: `Synchronous` (the provider answers in the same request; requires the `context.query.sync` capability) or `Asynchronous` (the provider accepts an operation to poll; requires `context.query.async`).

status.description: Selection result, as a PascalCase string token: `Selected`, `NoProviderConfigured`, `NoEnabledProvider`, `ProviderNotFound`, `ProviderDisabled`, `CapabilityUnavailable` (the provider does not advertise the required capability), `CapabilityDenied`, `ProviderDenied` (for example a single-workspace provider, or an operation owned by another caller), `ProviderSelectionRequired` or `ProviderConfigurationFailed` (the provider configuration could not be loaded).

reason.description: Why this provider was considered, as a PascalCase string token: `None`, `ExplicitProvider` (named by the request; the usual value for this API), `AssignmentOverride` or `DefaultProvider`.

requiredCapability.description: Capability the operation needed, for example `context.query.sync`, `context.query.async` or `operations.status`.

dispatchAllowed.description: True when the host may call the selected provider.

diagnostic.description: Human-readable explanation of the selection. Its wording can change and must not be parsed.

selectedProviderId.description: Identifier of the selected provider profile; null when none was selected.

candidateProviderIds.description: Identifiers of the provider profiles the selection considered; can be empty.

MemoryProviderSelectionApiResponse.description: How the host selected, or refused, the memory provider for an operation. `dispatchAllowed` is true only when `status` is `Selected`.

MemoryProviderSelectionReason.description: Why a memory provider was considered for an operation. In the memory-provider HTTP API it is a PascalCase string token: `None`, `ExplicitProvider` (named by the request), `AssignmentOverride` (assigned to the agent, workflow or process) or `DefaultProvider`.

MemoryProviderSelectionStatus.description: Result of choosing a memory provider for an operation. In the memory-provider HTTP API it is a PascalCase string token: `Selected`, `NoProviderConfigured`, `NoEnabledProvider`, `ProviderNotFound`, `ProviderDisabled`, `CapabilityUnavailable` (the provider does not advertise the required capability), `CapabilityDenied` (policy denies the capability), `ProviderDenied` (policy or workspace scope excludes the provider, or the caller may not access the operation), `ProviderSelectionRequired` (no provider was named and no default applies) or `ProviderConfigurationFailed` (the provider configuration could not be loaded).

MemoryProviderWorkspaceScope.description: Workspaces a memory provider serves. In the memory-provider HTTP API it is a PascalCase string token: `AllWorkspaces` or `SingleWorkspace` (never selected, because the host cannot verify the workspace).

MemorySourceScope.description: Source scope of memory, as a JSON integer: 0 Workspace, 1 Project, 2 Process, 3 Workflow, 4 Agent, 5 Crm, 6 Resource, 7 Manual.

kind.description: Kind of warning, as a PascalCase string token: `PolicyLimited` (policy limited the context), `ProviderPartial` (the provider returned partial context), `CapabilityUnavailable` or `SourceUnavailable`.

message.description: Human-readable warning; never blank. Its wording can change and must not be parsed.

MemoryWarningApiResponse.description: A warning attached to a memory context pack.

MemoryWarningKind.description: Kind of warning attached to memory context. In the memory-provider HTTP API it is a PascalCase string token: `PolicyLimited` (policy limited the context), `ProviderPartial` (the provider returned partial context), `CapabilityUnavailable` or `SourceUnavailable`.

addressType.description: Kind of address as free text, for example `Billing` or `Office`.

line1.description: First address line, usually street and number.

line2.description: Second address line, for example a building or floor.

countryCode.description: Country as free text, for example a two-letter code such as `CZ`.

isPrimary.description: True marks the party's main address; not checked for uniqueness. Omitted means false.

PartyAddressCreateApiRequest.description: A postal address of a new party. Every text field is free text, trimmed and not validated; omitted means empty.

PartyContactType.description: Kind of contact value of a party's contact point, as a JSON integer: 0 Email, 1 Phone, 2 Website, 3 Messaging, 4 Social, 5 Other.

partyType.description: Kind of party to create, as a JSON integer: 0 Person, 1 Organization, 2 OrganizationUnit, 3 AiAgent. Omitted means Person (0).

lifecycleStatus.description: Initial lifecycle status of the party, as a JSON integer: 0 Draft, 1 Active, 2 Inactive, 3 Archived, 4 Former, 5 Candidate, 6 Prospect. Omitted means Draft (0).

displayName.description: Name shown for the party in lists and lookups; required and trimmed. It is returned for sensitive parties too.

legalName.description: Registered legal name, for example of a company; trimmed. Omitted means empty.

preferredName.description: Name the party prefers to be addressed by; trimmed. Omitted means empty.

externalCode.description: Business reference from another system, for example an ERP or customer number; trimmed. It is not checked for uniqueness, so it is not an idempotency key. It is searchable and returned only while the party is not sensitive.

summary.description: Short description of the party; trimmed. Withheld from directory reads while the party is sensitive.

tags.description: Free-text labels used by tag filters. Trimmed; blank tags and case-insensitive duplicates are dropped. Omitted means no tags. Withheld from directory reads while the party is sensitive.

region.description: Region or state of the party as free text; trimmed, not validated.

countryCode.description: Country of the party as free text, for example a two-letter code such as `CZ`; trimmed, not validated.

timeZone.description: Time zone of the party as free text, for example an IANA name such as `Europe/Prague`; trimmed, not validated.

isSensitive.description: True marks the party for restricted handling: directory reads return its external code, summary and tags empty and the party is kept out of the application search index. Omitted means false. Other reads, such as the workforce and recruitment workspaces, still return some of its data.

roles.description: Business roles of the party, for example customer, employee or recruiter. Omitted means none. These are CRM/HR classifications, not authorization roles.

publicContacts.description: Contact points of the party, such as email addresses and phone numbers. Each is stored with the public flag, a data classification that grants no access. At most one contact point per contact type can be primary. Omitted means none.

addresses.description: Postal addresses of the party. Omitted means none.

PartyCreateApiRequest.description: Request of `POST /api/crm-hr/parties`: a new CRM/HR party with its roles, public contact points and addresses. A party is always created, never updated. Every member is optional except `displayName`; an omitted member takes the default stated on it, and null text or lists are treated as empty.

PartyLifecycleStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a CRM/HR party record, as a JSON integer: 0 Draft, 1 Active, 2 Inactive, 3 Archived (party lists include archived parties only on request), 4 Former, 5 Candidate (given to candidate parties created by recruiting), 6 Prospect. Converting a recruitment candidate sets Active.

contactType.description: Kind of contact value, as a JSON integer: 0 Email, 1 Phone, 2 Website, 3 Messaging, 4 Social, 5 Other. Omitted means Email (0).

label.description: Label of the contact point, for example `Work` or `Mobile`; trimmed. Omitted means empty.

value.description: The contact value, for example `jordan.lee@example.com` or `+420 555 010 010`; trimmed and stored as sent. Its format is not validated.

isPrimary.description: True marks the party's primary contact point of this contact type; at most one per contact type. Workspace and list reads prefer the primary email and phone. Omitted means false.

tags.description: Labels of the contact point; trimmed, blank values and case-insensitive duplicates dropped. Omitted means none.

PartyPublicContactCreateApiRequest.description: A contact point of a new party, such as an email address or a phone number. It is stored with the public flag set; the flag classifies the contact data and does not make it readable without authorization. A contact point is not itself a party or a contact person.

items.description: Parties on this page, ordered by display name and then party identifier.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of parties per page that was applied.

totalCount.description: Number of parties matching the filters across all pages.

totalPages.description: Number of pages at the applied page size; 0 when no party matches.

PartyRecordPage.description: One page of parties matching a party query.

id.description: Party identifier, used by the other party operations.

displayName.description: Name shown for the party. Always returned, also for sensitive parties.

partyType.description: Kind of party, as a JSON integer: 0 Person, 1 Organization, 2 OrganizationUnit, 3 AiAgent.

lifecycleStatus.description: Current lifecycle status of the party record, as a JSON integer: 0 Draft, 1 Active, 2 Inactive, 3 Archived (party lists include archived parties only on request), 4 Former, 5 Candidate, 6 Prospect.

externalCode.description: Business reference supplied by the organization, for example an ERP or customer number. It is not guaranteed to be unique. Empty for sensitive parties.

summary.description: Short description of the party. Empty for sensitive parties.

tags.description: Tags attached to the party. Empty for sensitive parties.

isSensitive.description: True when the party is marked for restricted handling; its external code, summary and tags are then withheld.

PartyRecordQueryItem.description: Summary of one CRM/HR party in a party list or lookup.

PartyRecordScope.description: Party types included by a party query, as a bit flags value: 1 People, 2 Organizations, 4 OrganizationUnits, 8 AiAgents, 15 All. It filters records; it is not an authorization scope.

PartyRelationshipKind.description: Kind of a directed relationship between two parties, read as source, kind, target (for example a person MemberOf an organization), as a JSON integer: 0 MemberOf, 1 PartOf, 2 ReportsTo, 3 CustomerOf, 4 PartnerOf, 5 VendorTo, 6 Represents, 7 ManagedBy, 8 OwnedBy, 9 Supports. Recruiting support assignments use ManagedBy (the party is managed by its manager) and Supports (a buddy or mentor supports the party).

id.description: Identifier of the relationship record. The same relationship listed for the other party has the same identifier. Every relationship replacement stores the party's relationships again with new identifiers, so do not keep this value across replacements.

relatedPartyId.description: Identifier of the other party of the relationship.

relatedPartyDisplayName.description: Display name of the other party, also when that party is sensitive.

relatedPartyType.description: Kind of the other party, as a JSON integer: 0 Person, 1 Organization, 2 OrganizationUnit, 3 AiAgent.

relationshipKind.description: Kind of relationship, read as source, kind, target, as a JSON integer: 0 MemberOf, 1 PartOf, 2 ReportsTo, 3 CustomerOf, 4 PartnerOf, 5 VendorTo, 6 Represents, 7 ManagedBy, 8 OwnedBy, 9 Supports.

isOutgoing.description: True when the requested party is the source (for MemberOf: the requested party is a member of the related party); false when the related party is the source.

isPrimary.description: True when the relationship is marked as primary.

startDateUtc.description: Start of the relationship in UTC; null when no start was stated.

endDateUtc.description: End of the relationship in UTC; null when no end was stated.

notes.description: Free-text notes. A Supports relationship whose notes are exactly `Buddy` or `Mentor` is a recruiting buddy or mentor assignment.

PartyRelationshipListItemModel.description: A relationship of a party, seen from the party whose relationships were requested with `GET /api/crm-hr/parties/{partyId}/relationships`. Copy its fields into a relationship replacement to keep it.

relatedPartyId.description: Identifier of the other party, as returned by `GET /api/crm-hr/parties`; required. It must exist and must differ from the route party.

relationshipKind.description: Kind of relationship, read as source, kind, target, as a JSON integer: 0 MemberOf, 1 PartOf, 2 ReportsTo, 3 CustomerOf, 4 PartnerOf, 5 VendorTo, 6 Represents, 7 ManagedBy, 8 OwnedBy, 9 Supports. Omitted means MemberOf (0).

isOutgoing.description: True when the route party is the source (for MemberOf: the route party is a member of the related party); false when the related party is the source. Omitted means true.

isPrimary.description: True marks the relationship as primary; not checked for uniqueness. Omitted means false.

startDateUtc.description: Start of the relationship as an instant with an offset; converted to UTC before saving. Null or omitted means no stated start.

endDateUtc.description: End of the relationship as an instant with an offset; converted to UTC and not checked against the start. Null or omitted means no stated end.

notes.description: Free-text notes; trimmed. Supports relationships whose notes are exactly `Buddy` or `Mentor` are the recruiting buddy and mentor assignments, so keep these notes when you copy such a relationship.

PartyRelationshipReplaceItemApiRequest.description: One relationship of a relationship replacement, described from the point of view of the party in the route. Copy the fields of an item of `GET /api/crm-hr/parties/{partyId}/relationships` to keep a relationship.

relationships.description: Every relationship the party should have after the call, described from the route party's point of view. An empty array, or omitting the member, removes all relationships of the party. Do not send null.

PartyRelationshipsReplaceApiRequest.description: Request of `PUT /api/crm-hr/parties/{partyId}/relationships`: the complete intended list of the party's relationships. It replaces every existing relationship in which the party is the source or the target.

roleKind.description: Kind of role, as a JSON integer: 0 Customer, 1 CustomerContact, 2 Partner, 3 Vendor, 4 Employee, 5 Contractor, 6 Freelancer, 7 DeliveryUnit, 8 Candidate, 9 AiSteward, 10 AccountManager, 11 Recruiter, 12 Stakeholder. Omitted means Customer (0).

title.description: Title of the role for this party, for example `Key account`; trimmed. Omitted means empty.

isPrimary.description: True marks the party's main role; not checked for uniqueness. Omitted means false.

validFromUtc.description: Start of the role's validity as an instant with an offset. Null or omitted means no stated start.

validToUtc.description: End of the role's validity as an instant with an offset; not checked against the start. Null or omitted means no stated end.

PartyRoleCreateApiRequest.description: A business role of a new party, for example customer, employee or recruiter. It classifies the party in CRM/HR; it is not an authorization role or a task assignment.

PartyRoleKind.description: Business role of a CRM/HR party, as a JSON integer: 0 Customer, 1 CustomerContact, 2 Partner, 3 Vendor, 4 Employee, 5 Contractor, 6 Freelancer, 7 DeliveryUnit, 8 Candidate, 9 AiSteward, 10 AccountManager, 11 Recruiter, 12 Stakeholder. A role classifies the party in CRM/HR; it is not an authorization role or a task assignment.

id.description: Identifier of the party skill record; send it as `id` to update the record.

skillCategory.description: Category of the skill definition; empty when not set.

proficiency.description: Proficiency level, lowest first, as a JSON integer: 0 Basic, 1 Working, 2 Strong, 3 Expert.

yearsExperience.description: Years of experience with the skill; 0 or more.

certificationStatus.description: Certification state as free text; empty when not set.

lastValidatedOn.description: Date the proficiency was last checked (`yyyy-MM-dd`); null when never.

notes.description: Free-text notes; empty when not set.

PartySkillItemModel.description: A party's recorded proficiency in one catalog skill, as returned in the workforce workspace.

id.description: Identifier of the party skill to update, from `skills[].id` of the workforce workspace. Omit it to update the record of the same party and skill, or to create one. An unknown identifier is never used for a new record.

partyId.description: Identifier of the party that has the skill; required and must exist.

skillId.description: Identifier of the skill definition from `GET /api/crm-hr/workforce/skills`; required and must exist.

proficiency.description: Proficiency level, lowest first, as a JSON integer: 0 Basic, 1 Working, 2 Strong, 3 Expert. Omitted means Basic (0).

yearsExperience.description: Years of experience with the skill, a whole number; negative values are saved as 0. Omitted means 0.

certificationStatus.description: Certification state as free text, for example `Certified`; trimmed. Omitted means empty.

lastValidatedOn.description: Date the proficiency was last checked (`yyyy-MM-dd`). Null or omitted means never.

notes.description: Free-text notes; trimmed. Omitted means empty.

PartySkillSaveApiRequest.description: Request of `POST /api/crm-hr/workforce/party-skills`: a party's proficiency in one catalog skill. All fields are overwritten.

PartyType.description: Kind of CRM/HR party, as a JSON integer: 0 Person (a human), 1 Organization (a company or other legal entity), 2 OrganizationUnit (a department or team of an organization), 3 AiAgent (an AI agent recorded in the CRM/HR directory; its executable agent definition is kept by the Agents module).

PathFoundationReadinessReason.description: Reason for the readiness of an application path, as a string token: `Ready`, `InvalidConfiguration` (the root could not be resolved from the configuration), `AccessDenied` (the operating-system account cannot write it), `UnsafePath` (the path failed the path safety checks, for example link traversal) or `IoFailure` (an input/output error while probing it).

PathFoundationReadinessState.description: Readiness of an application path, as a string token: `Ready` (the root resolved, is writable and passed the path safety checks) or `Unavailable`.

approved.description: Answer applied to every approval pending when the request is handled, used only when `decisions` is null or empty: true approves them all, false rejects them all. Always send it; it is ignored when `decisions` is given.

autoApprovePendingToolCalls.description: True to approve this run's later approval requests automatically as well; it takes effect only when every pending call is approved, and any rejection clears it. Always send it (false when not wanted).

activityOperationId.description: Optional identifier of the activity operation for this command, as a GUID string; when null or omitted the server generates one. It is returned in the `X-CanDoItAll-Agent-Operation-Id` header. Use a new identifier for every attempt.

decisions.description: One decision per approval currently pending on the run, identified by the `approvalId` values read from the run's approvals. When present and not empty it replaces `approved`, and it must name every pending approval exactly once (compared exactly, including case); a missing, unknown or repeated identifier rejects the whole request, with HTTP 400 `agents.approval-decision-mismatch` on the JSON route and a failed-command event (`agents.command-failed`) on the streaming route. Null or omitted applies `approved` to all.

PendingApprovalApiRequest.description: Decisions on the pending tool approvals of an agent execution run, sent to `POST /api/agents/execution-runs/{executionRunId}/pending-approvals` and to its streaming variant. Prefer `decisions` with one entry per pending approval; `approved` is the older form that applies one answer to everything pending.

approvalId.description: Identifier of the pending approval, copied exactly from `approvalId` of the run's approvals or of an `agent.approval.required` stream event; an opaque string.

approved.description: True to approve the tool call; false to reject it.

PendingApprovalDecisionApiRequest.description: Decision on one pending tool approval of an agent execution run.

capability.description: The capability, as a JSON integer (a single flag): 1 WorkflowExecutor, 2 SettingsRenderer, 4 SecretReference, 8 WorkspaceFiles, 16 Storage, 32 ProjectStructure, 64 HttpClient, 128 OAuth2, 256 ExecutionEvents, 512 HostCommand.

oneOf.description: Host tool recipe that the grant covers, for HostCommand (512) grants of a single recipe; null for a capability-level grant.

scopeKind.description: Scope of the grant, as a JSON integer: 0 Plugin (evaluated), 1 Connection, 2 Workflow (stored, not evaluated).

scopeKey.description: Key within the scope; empty for plugin-scope grants.

state.description: Decision, as a JSON integer: 0 Requested (undecided), 1 Granted, 2 Denied, 3 Revoked, 4 Unavailable (unreadable saved state). Only 1 allows the capability.

riskKind.description: Risk rating, as a JSON integer: 0 Low, 1 Medium, 2 High. Informational.

reason.description: Reason recorded with the decision.

updatedBy.description: Actor that made the decision, for example `api`; empty for an undecided entry.

createdAtUtc.description: When the decision was first saved; null for an undecided entry.

updatedAtUtc.description: When the decision last changed; null for an undecided entry.

concurrencyToken.description: Version stamp that changes with every save; null for an undecided entry. The API does not use it for concurrency checks.

PluginCapabilityGrantItem.description: A capability grant of a plugin: the saved decision whether the plugin may use one capability, or a synthesized undecided entry for a declared capability without a decision.

PluginCapabilityKind.description: Capabilities that a plugin declares, as a JSON integer bit mask (add the values of the flags): 0 None, 1 WorkflowExecutor (provides workflow executors), 2 SettingsRenderer (custom settings user interface), 4 SecretReference (uses stored secrets), 8 WorkspaceFiles (reads and writes workspace files), 16 Storage (places files in storage), 32 ProjectStructure (reads project structures), 64 HttpClient (calls external HTTP services), 128 OAuth2 (uses OAuth 2.0 connections), 256 ExecutionEvents (records execution events), 512 HostCommand (runs reviewed host commands). For example 193 means WorkflowExecutor, HttpClient and OAuth2. Grants are evaluated per single flag, so a grant for a combined value never takes effect.

PluginCatalogAvailabilityKind.description: Availability of a plugin's manifest, as a JSON integer: 0 Available (a current source, bundled or an installed package, provides it), 1 Unavailable (the plugin is recorded as installed, but no current source provides its manifest, for example after its package was removed).

pluginId.description: Identifier of the plugin; use it in the `/api/plugins/{pluginId}` operations.

displayName.description: Display name of the plugin.

description.description: Description of the plugin.

version.description: Version text declared by the plugin, for example `1.0.0`.

sourceKind.description: Where the plugin comes from, as a JSON integer: 0 Bundled (compiled into the host), 1 LocalPackage (installed from a package), 2 RemotePackage, 3 ShopCatalog.

trustLevel.description: Trust level, as a JSON integer: 0 Application, 1 Bundled, 2 LocalPackage, 3 RemotePackage, 4 Untrusted.

capabilities.description: Declared capabilities, as a JSON integer bit mask: 1 WorkflowExecutor, 2 SettingsRenderer, 4 SecretReference, 8 WorkspaceFiles, 16 Storage, 32 ProjectStructure, 64 HttpClient, 128 OAuth2, 256 ExecutionEvents, 512 HostCommand; 0 for none.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the plugin's package, for example `gmail.mail.bundled`; null when it declares none.

installationState.description: Installation state, as a JSON integer: 0 NotInstalled, 1 InstalledEnabled, 2 InstalledDisabled.

availability.description: Whether a current source provides the manifest, as a JSON integer: 0 Available, 1 Unavailable.

unavailableReason.description: Why the plugin is unavailable; empty when it is available.

installedAtUtc.description: When the plugin was first installed; it survives reinstallation. Null when it is not installed.

updatedAtUtc.description: When the plugin was last installed, enabled or disabled; null when it is not installed.

oneOf.description: Icon of the plugin; the default icon when the plugin declares none.

descriptor.description: Full manifest of the plugin: workflow executors, settings, connection kinds, package and OAuth metadata. For an unavailable plugin it is the manifest saved at installation, or a minimal placeholder when that cannot be read.

isInstalled.description: True when the plugin is installed, enabled or disabled (derived from `installationState`).

isEnabled.description: True when the plugin is installed and enabled (derived from `installationState`).

PluginCatalogItem.description: A plugin in the plugin catalog: its manifest summary, installation state and availability. Returned by `GET /api/plugins/catalog` and by the install, enable and disable operations.

PluginConnectionAuthKind.description: Authentication method of a plugin connection kind, as a JSON integer: 0 None, 1 ApiKey, 2 Basic, 3 BearerToken, 4 OAuth2, 5 Custom. A plugin must declare the SecretReference capability for 1, 2, 3 and 5, and the OAuth2 capability for 4.

key.description: Key of the connection kind, for example `gmail`; saved connections refer to it.

displayName.description: Display name of the connection kind.

description.description: Description of the connection kind.

authKind.description: Authentication method, as a JSON integer: 0 None, 1 ApiKey, 2 Basic, 3 BearerToken, 4 OAuth2, 5 Custom.

settingsSchema.description: Form of the connection settings (`settingsJson` of a saved connection).

isRequired.description: True when the plugin needs a connection of this kind to work.

PluginConnectionDescriptor.description: A connection kind that a plugin declares: how a saved connection of this kind authenticates and which settings it has.

PluginConnectionId.description: Identifier of a saved plugin connection: on the wire a JSON string containing a non-empty GUID, for example `"5b0f3c1e-7d2a-4c9b-8e61-2f4a9d0c7b13"`. Request bodies may also send the object form `{"value":"GUID"}`; responses always use the string.

id.description: Identifier of the connection.

connectionKey.description: Key of the connection kind, for example `gmail`.

displayName.description: Display name of the connection.

settingsJson.description: Connection settings as JSON text (a string that contains a JSON object), returned exactly as saved; for example OAuth connections read `clientId` and `redirectUri` from it.

isEnabled.description: False excludes the connection from automatic selection by workflows and from token use.

healthStatus.description: Health text of the connection; `Not checked` by default, and the plugin API does not update it.

updatedBy.description: Actor of the last change, for example `api`.

createdAtUtc.description: When the connection was created.

updatedAtUtc.description: When the connection last changed.

concurrencyToken.description: Version stamp that changes with every save. The API does not use it for concurrency checks.

PluginConnectionItem.description: A saved connection of a plugin: which connection kind it uses and its settings. OAuth tokens are not part of it.

PluginConnectionKey.description: Key of a connection kind that a plugin declares, for example `gmail` or `office365`. On the wire it is a JSON string of letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`; the server trims and lower-cases it. Request bodies may also send the object form `{"value":"gmail"}`; responses always use the string.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the connection to update; null creates a new connection. An identifier that no connection of this plugin has creates a connection with that identifier.

connectionKey.description: Key of the connection kind, for example `gmail`. Used only when the connection is created; an update keeps the saved key.

displayName.description: Display name; required, must not be blank.

settingsJson.description: Settings as JSON text: a string that contains a JSON object such as `{"clientId":"example-client"}`, not a nested object. It is stored as sent (surrounding whitespace removed; blank means `{}`) and not checked against the connection kind's settings form. Do not put secrets in it: it is returned unredacted.

isEnabled.description: True (default) makes the connection usable; false disables it.

PluginConnectionSaveRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/plugins/{pluginId}/connections`: creates a connection or replaces the settings of an existing one.

id.description: Identifier of the plugin.

displayName.description: Display name of the plugin.

description.description: Description of the plugin.

version.description: Version text declared by the plugin, for example `1.0.0`.

sourceKind.description: Where the plugin comes from, as a JSON integer: 0 Bundled, 1 LocalPackage, 2 RemotePackage, 3 ShopCatalog.

trustLevel.description: Trust level, as a JSON integer: 0 Application, 1 Bundled, 2 LocalPackage, 3 RemotePackage, 4 Untrusted.

minAppVersion.description: Minimum application version declared by the manifest; informational, the server does not check it.

capabilities.description: Declared capabilities, as a JSON integer bit mask: 1 WorkflowExecutor, 2 SettingsRenderer, 4 SecretReference, 8 WorkspaceFiles, 16 Storage, 32 ProjectStructure, 64 HttpClient, 128 OAuth2, 256 ExecutionEvents, 512 HostCommand; 0 for none. A capability must be declared here before it can be granted.

workflowExecutors.description: Workflow executors that the plugin provides; empty when it provides none.

settings.description: Plugin-level settings form and settings renderers.

connections.description: Connection kinds that the plugin can use.

oneOf.description: Package metadata; null when the plugin declares no package.
OAuth 2.0 configuration of the plugin; null when it uses no OAuth connection.
Icon of the plugin; null means the default icon.

tags.description: Free-form tags of the plugin, for example `email`, `oauth` or `workflow`.

PluginDescriptor.description: Manifest of a plugin: identity, declared capabilities, workflow executors, settings, connection kinds, package and OAuth metadata. It is returned as `descriptor` of a plugin catalog item.

PluginGrantRiskKind.description: Risk rating of a plugin capability grant, as a JSON integer: 0 Low, 1 Medium, 2 High. Informational: it does not change how the grant is evaluated.

PluginGrantScopeKind.description: Scope of a plugin capability grant, as a JSON integer: 0 Plugin (the whole plugin; the only scope the runtime evaluates), 1 Connection, 2 Workflow. Grants with scope 1 or 2 are stored and listed but not currently evaluated.

PluginGrantState.description: Decision state of a plugin capability grant, as a JSON integer: 0 Requested (not decided yet; reported for declared capabilities without a saved decision), 1 Granted (allowed), 2 Denied (refused), 3 Revoked (withdrawn after being granted), 4 Unavailable (the saved state could not be read). Only Granted allows the capability.

capability.description: The capability, as a JSON integer; send a single flag: 1 WorkflowExecutor, 2 SettingsRenderer, 4 SecretReference, 8 WorkspaceFiles, 16 Storage, 32 ProjectStructure, 64 HttpClient, 128 OAuth2, 256 ExecutionEvents, 512 HostCommand. A combined value is stored but never matches at runtime.

state.description: Decision, as a JSON integer: 1 Granted, 2 Denied or 3 Revoked. 0 Requested and 4 Unavailable are rejected.

recipeId.description: Host tool recipe identifier, for example `docker.list-containers`, to decide one recipe of HostCommand (512); a recipe also needs the capability-level HostCommand grant. Omitted or null for a capability-level grant.

scopeKind.description: Scope, as a JSON integer: 0 Plugin (default; the only scope evaluated at runtime), 1 Connection, 2 Workflow.

scopeKey.description: Key within the scope; leave it empty (the default) for plugin-scope grants.

riskKind.description: Risk rating to record, as a JSON integer: 0 Low, 1 Medium (default), 2 High.

reason.description: Reason for the decision; optional.

PluginGrantUpdateRequest.description: Body of `PUT /api/plugins/{pluginId}/grants`: one grant decision. The grant is identified by `capability`, `recipeId`, `scopeKind` and `scopeKey`; saving creates it or replaces the decision of the existing grant with the same identity.

recipeId.description: Identifier of the recipe, for example `docker.list-containers`.

displayName.description: Display name of the recipe.

description.description: What the recipe does.

riskKind.description: Risk rating, as a JSON integer: 0 Low, 1 Medium, 2 High.

mutatesHost.description: True when the recipe changes the host, for example by starting a container.

PluginHostToolRecipeDescriptor.description: A host tool recipe: a reviewed host command that a plugin with the HostCommand capability may run once it is granted.

PluginHostToolRecipeId.description: Identifier of a host tool recipe, a reviewed host command that a plugin may run, for example `docker.list-containers`. On the wire it is a JSON string of letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, lower-cased by the server.

PluginId.description: Identifier of a plugin, for example `gmail.mail`, `office365.mail` or `candoitall.docker`. On the wire it is a JSON string of letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`; the server trims and lower-cases it. Request bodies may also send the object form `{"value":"gmail.mail"}`; responses always use the string.

PluginInstallationStateKind.description: Installation state of a plugin, as a JSON integer: 0 NotInstalled, 1 InstalledEnabled, 2 InstalledDisabled.

actor.description: Ignored: the API records `api` as the actor.

PluginInstallationUpdateRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/plugins/{pluginId}/enable` and `POST /api/plugins/{pluginId}/disable`. The JSON object is required; send `{}`.

enable.description: True (default): the plugin is installed enabled. False: it is installed, or reinstalled, disabled.

actor.description: Ignored: the API records `api` as the actor.

PluginInstallRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/plugins/{pluginId}/install`. The JSON object is required; send `{}` for the defaults.

id.description: Identifier of the log entry.

streamKind.description: Stream, as a JSON integer: 0 Installation, 1 Runtime.

operationKind.description: Recorded operation, as a JSON integer: 0 PackageUpload, 1 PackageValidation, 2 PackageInstall, 3 PluginInstall, 4 PluginEnable, 5 PluginDisable, 6 RestartRequired, 7 RuntimeActivation, 8 ExecutorStarted, 9 ExecutorCompleted, 10 ExecutorFailed, 11 PluginEvent.

severity.description: Severity, as a JSON integer: 0 Information, 1 Warning, 2 Error.

status.description: Short status text, for example `Installed`, `Failed`, `Enabled` or `Completed`; at most 80 characters.

message.description: Log message with secrets redacted; at most 1,200 characters.

detailsJson.description: Details as JSON text (a string) with secrets replaced by `[REDACTED]`; at most 8,000 characters, and text cut at that limit ends with `...[TRUNCATED]` and may not parse as JSON.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the plugin concerned; null when the entry concerns none.
Identifier of the package concerned; null when the entry concerns none.
Identifier of the workflow executor concerned, for example `gmail.messages-by-label`; null when none.

correlationId.description: Correlation identifier of the operation that wrote the entry, for log searches.

createdAtUtc.description: When the entry was written.

PluginLogItem.description: One entry of the plugin installation and runtime log, returned by `GET /api/plugins/logs`.

PluginLogOperationKind.description: Operation recorded by a plugin log entry, as a JSON integer: 0 PackageUpload, 1 PackageValidation, 2 PackageInstall, 3 PluginInstall, 4 PluginEnable, 5 PluginDisable, 6 RestartRequired, 7 RuntimeActivation, 8 ExecutorStarted, 9 ExecutorCompleted, 10 ExecutorFailed, 11 PluginEvent.

PluginLogSeverity.description: Severity of a plugin log entry, as a JSON integer: 0 Information, 1 Warning, 2 Error.

PluginLogStreamKind.description: Stream of a plugin log entry, as a JSON integer: 0 Installation (package and plugin lifecycle), 1 Runtime (workflow executor runs and plugin events).

connectionKey.description: Key of the connection kind that uses OAuth, for example `gmail`.

authorizationEndpoint.description: Authorization endpoint of the identity provider (absolute URL).

tokenEndpoint.description: Token endpoint of the identity provider (absolute URL).

scopes.description: Scopes requested by default and expected on a connected account.

usesPkce.description: True when the authorization uses PKCE (proof key for code exchange).

clientId.description: Public OAuth client identifier used when the connection settings do not provide `clientId`; empty when every connection must provide its own.

clientSecretEnvironmentVariable.description: Name of the server environment variable that holds the client secret, for example `CANDOITALL_GMAIL_SECRET`. Only the name is exposed, never the secret.

redirectPath.description: Relative path of the OAuth callback on this host, by default `/api/plugins/oauth/callback`. The start operation appends it to the request's base address when neither the request nor the connection settings give a redirect URI.

authorizationParameters.description: Additional query parameters added to the authorization request, for example `prompt`: `consent`.

PluginOAuth2Descriptor.description: OAuth 2.0 configuration of a plugin, used by `POST /api/plugins/{pluginId}/oauth/start` and the callback. It contains no secret: the client secret is read on the server from the named environment variable.

connectionKey.description: Key of the connection kind, for example `gmail`.

status.description: OAuth state, as a JSON integer: 0 NotConnected, 1 Connected, 2 ReconnectRequired, 3 Error. A connection whose stored token lacks a scope that the plugin requires is reported as 2 with `lastErrorCode``oauth-scope-missing`.

accountDisplay.description: Display text of the connected account; currently always empty.

accessTokenExpiresAtUtc.description: When the stored access token expires; the server refreshes it when needed. Null when unknown.

refreshTokenExpiresAtUtc.description: When the refresh token expires; currently always null.

lastErrorCode.description: Code of the last error, for example `oauth-scope-missing` or an error code of the provider; empty when there is none.

lastErrorDescription.description: Description of the last error; empty when there is none.

updatedAtUtc.description: When the OAuth state last changed; null when unknown.
